subject: 3code
title: dmail: the model reverts its own conversation to a [checkpoint N] marker mid-turn and carries a self-addressed note forward; filesystem deliberately NOT reverted
evidence: src/threecode/prompts.nim:2983-2987 (tool schema), prompts.nim:2629 (usage rules), src/threecode/session.nim:705,923,1201 (dispatcher + wire record), tests/core/test_dmail.nim (26 tests)

subject: 3code
title: Zero-token flailing detector: call fingerprints over a bounded window with four signals (identical-consecutive, spaced A-B-A-B, no-progress repeats, Jaccard near-duplicate streak clustering), escalating SYSTEM notes x3 then turn abort, every intervention visible in scrollback
evidence: src/threecode/turns.nim:16-60 (thresholds + signal design), turns.nim:652 (detector in loop), docs/manual.md:634-648, tests/core/test_flail.nim (26 tests), tests/flail_replay.nim
one_why: Detection spends no model tokens and no judge model; the near-duplicate clustering (avg pairwise Jaccard over a ring, FlailStreakJaccard/NearDup/Cluster) catches paraphrased thrash that exact-fingerprint detectors miss, while successful idempotent polls are explicitly exempted from false flags.

subject: 3code
title: Default-on kernel fence with zero approval prompts: Landlock/Seatbelt/restricted-token FS policy on every tool call, dual enforcement (in-process checks reload policy on mtime before each restricted op AND the bash subprocess re-loads the policy file itself), hidden guard rules no policy file can weaken, host rules routed through a CONNECT+SOCKS5 egress allowlist proxy

subject: 3code
title: Three context tiers with the model holding two: dmail checkpoint fold, then the clear tool ending a chunk with written handoff instructions for the next session (chunked/cybernetic modes over plan files + worktrees), auto-summarize kept as the last-resort fallback at 0.8 window, keep-8, at-most-once-per-turn

one_why: The ladder prefers discarding spent context over repeatedly re-summarizing it - 'this loses less information than repeatedly summarizing all the old work' - and the published per-task cost table shows the bet measured against five rival harnesses on the same model.

subject: 3code
title: Byte-reproducible agent binary as a CI gate: container pinned by sha256 digest, apt frozen to a snapshot.ubuntu.com timestamp, sha256-pinned Nim toolchain, clean-rebuild byte-equality check, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH double-pack check with perturbed mtimes

subject: 3code
title: Self-built cross-platform PTY expect harness in Nim: one TtySession API over openpty (POSIX) and ConPTY (Windows kernel32 declarations hand-rolled), driving the real binary through a ttty grid with frame-snapshot artifacts on failure - 53 functional tty specs

subject: 3code
title: Patient retry sized to outlive subscription caps: exponential backoff to a 2048s ceiling for ~36 hours on 429/5xx/network, retries after the initial window printed into the transcript as numbered rows, separate rate-vs-server backoff ledgers, Esc cancels

subject: 3code

subject: 3code
title: Skills priced at zero when unused: system prompt carries only a one-bullet-per-skill catalog, the model reads a skill file with the normal read tool when the task smells like it, filename is the trigger, four-tier override dirs including the vendor-neutral .agents/skills/ - and an explicit anti-MCP rationale

subject: 3code
title: Sessions persist the verbatim wire bytes of every request (key order, extra fields, raw argument bytes) so a resumed session re-sends byte-identical history and the provider prompt cache stays hot; stable conversation-id header per session for provider-side cache/routing affinity

subject: SWE-agent

subject: SWE-agent
title: Tools as self-contained bundles (bin/ + install.sh + config.yaml) uploaded and installed into the runtime at setup
evidence: sweagent/tools/tools.py:252-275 (_upload_bundles, install); sweagent/tools/commands.py (generate_command_docs from config.yaml); tools/search/{bin,config.yaml,install.sh}

subject: SWE-agent

subject: SWE-agent

subject: SWE-agent
title: Pluggable cache_control marks plus per-thread API-key affinity to keep provider cache partitions stable
evidence: sweagent/agent/history_processors.py:261-300 (CacheControlHistoryProcessor); sweagent/agent/models.py:172-190 (choose_api_key_by_thread)

subject: SWE-agent
title: LLM reviewer/chooser retry loop with cost-aware budget allocation across attempts
evidence: sweagent/agent/agents.py:257,307-310 (attempt cap clamped to remaining budget); sweagent/agent/reviewer.py:499-559 (ScoreRetryLoop/ChooserRetryLoop, min_budget_for_new_attempt)
one_why: Retry isn't just 'run again': a reviewer scores each submission and the per-attempt cost limit is recomputed from the instance's remaining budget, so retries can never overrun the instance cap - codex's guardian pool guards actions, this guards whole attempts.

subject: SWE-agent

one_why: Turns a hard stop into partial-credit preservation, with a fallback to the last-trajectory-step diff if the runtime already died - the graceful-degradation counterpart to context-overflow-failopen, aimed at batch yield rather than interactive UX.

subject: SWE-agent

subject: SWE-agent
title: Command filter is prefix/exact-match startswith - ACI hygiene, trivially bypassable, and labeled as such

subject: aeon
title: One Claude-Code-shaped headless contract over nine rival coding-agent CLIs

subject: aeon
title: Dispatcher applies its own bwrap sandbox around whatever harness runs, because no harness enforces read-only reliably
evidence: harness-adapter/lib/sandbox.sh:1-15,47-67; .github/workflows/aeon.yml:303-322; harness-adapter/run-harness:133-157

subject: aeon
title: Per-skill requires: secrets resolved from an allowlisted blob that is unset before the agent starts
evidence: .github/workflows/aeon.yml:679-692,966-982; .github/workflows/aeon.yml:748-753; .github/workflows/aeon.yml:880-884
one_why: Only secrets declared in a skill's frontmatter reach its env; the ALL_SECRETS blob is unset before any agent code runs; notify channel tokens were removed from the run env entirely (./notify is a queue writer, delivery is post-run); ./secretcurl keeps credentials off the agent's command line - a graduated trust model per credential blast-radius rather than one token for everything.

subject: aeon
title: Content-addressed skill lockfile (eyebrow) gating post-admission capability drift, incl. egress host sets
evidence: docs/skill-integrity.md:18-28; .github/workflows/ci-skill-integrity.yml:10-29; eyebrowlock.json
one_why: Targets the skill supply-chain rug pull: skills.lock pins provenance but never content, so an admitted skill that later gains an exfil endpoint passes every existing check; eyebrowlock fingerprints each SKILL.md hash AND the declared egress hosts, and CI fails only on escalation-class drift rather than every edit.

subject: aeon
title: Scheduling as the whole architecture: debt-ledger cron catch-up designed around GitHub delivering ~10% of ticks
evidence: .github/workflows/scheduler.yml:5-16,63-72; scripts/cron-due.sh:10
one_why: Converges with cline's scheduled-agent-runs but pushes further: last-dispatch is treated as a debt ledger so missed slots fire once within a CATCHUP_HOURS window that doubles as max-lateness (a daily slot can never double-fire), plus an external cron-tick pinger hook - the honest way to build on a scheduler the platform under-delivers.

subject: aeon
title: Auto-recovering circuit breaker (closed/open/half-open probe) as the single source of the dispatch decision
evidence: scripts/breaker.sh:1-49; scripts/tests/test_breaker.sh; .github/workflows/scheduler.yml:69-80
one_why: A skill failing N consecutive times is an outage, not a flake: the breaker trades a run-per-tick burn for one probe per cooldown, resets on probe success, and lives in one tested script the scheduler calls rather than inline copies - directly portable to any long-lived agent runner loop.

subject: aeon
title: Signed run manifests via GitHub artifact attestation, with proof re-runs against a PR's attested head
evidence: .github/workflows/aeon.yml:1364-1470; docs/attestation.md; .github/workflows/aeon.yml:1936-1940 (prove- dispatch gate)
one_why: Extends gptme's model-provenance-attestation into a full signed chain: a run-scoped immutable snapshot plus manifest {skill, model, mode, trigger, commit, sha256} attested with pinned attest-build-provenance, a tiered opt-in gate, and dev-loop proof runs that must not move the attested head - convergent evidence attestation is becoming a corpus theme.

subject: aeon
title: The core loop is a 2,231-line YAML workflow with a ~500-line inline Run step that nothing unit-tests

one_why: Same shape as crush/prime-agent's fused loop+policy+wiring file, in GitHub Actions YAML: the repo's own discipline extracts logic into tested scripts precisely because the inline step is untestable, but the extraction is partial - model/harness precedence, MCP gating, and the gateway cascade still live only in the workflow, where CI can't reach them.

subject: aeon
title: Three-layer read-only enforcement is opt-in: default tier is write with broad GH token and open network
evidence: scripts/skill_mode.sh:12; .github/workflows/aeon.yml:752-753; harness-adapter/lib/sandbox.sh:10-12; harness-adapter/run-harness:150
one_why: Honest, documented gaps rather than hidden ones: mode:write is the default, read-only deliberately leaves egress open ('read-only is about the repo, not egress'), GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_GLOBAL stay in-run ('deferred, broad gh surface' per their own comment), and with no OS sandbox available the mode degrades to advisory with only a stderr warning.

subject: agentless
title: Anti-agent three-stage funnel: hierarchical localize -> top-N one-shot sampled repair -> test-arbitrated rerank, chained by JSONL artifacts
evidence: agentless/fl/localize.py:100 (localize_instance file/class-function/edit-location stages); agentless/repair/repair.py:431-473 (top-N sampling); agentless/repair/rerank.py:156 (majority_voting) + :13 (_load_results folding reproduction+regression test outcomes); patch gates in agentless/util/postprocess_data.py:11 (ast check_syntax), :52 (lint_code)
one_why: The historically field-shaping result, implemented and inspectable: candidate arbitration by generated-reproduction + selected-regression test outcomes with majority-vote tie-break replaces the whole agent loop; MIT so the funnel shape and the test-arbitrated rerank are directly adoptable concepts for our validation stage.

subject: agentless
title: Sampling-aware cache discipline: first sample sent cold, remaining N-1 re-requested with cache_control ephemeral on the leading message so a fat localized-file context is billed once
evidence: agentless/repair/repair.py:431-435 (prompt_cache=args.max_samples>1) and :469-473 (num_samples=max_samples-1, prompt_cache=True); agentless/util/api_requests.py:145-151 (cache_control ephemeral on messages[0], comment 'cache mainly the reused content at the beginning'); agentless/util/model.py:71-77 (prompt_tokens counted once per batch by design)
one_why: N-sample fan-out is exactly where harnesses silently re-bill a fat prefix N times; keying the cache mark to 'samples > 1' rather than always-on is a small, deliberate policy worth lifting as a concept (distinct from SWE-agent's per-thread key affinity and agentty's quantized anchors).

subject: agentless
title: Python eval() executed on strings parsed out of LLM output -- prompt-injected issue text reaches host RCE in the pipeline process
evidence: agentless/repair/repair.py:188 (edited_file = eval(edited_file_key) with comment 'convert \'file.py\' to file.py'); agentless/util/postprocess_data.py:849 (changed_content = eval(...) on comma-split model edit command)
one_why: The pipeline runs against untrusted third-party issue text (SWE-bench repos), so any injection that steers the model's edit_file command syntax executes arbitrary Python on the host -- there is no sandbox at this layer; ast.literal_eval is the one-line fix; cautionary benchmark for any of our parsers that round-trip model output through eval-adjacent idioms.

subject: agentless
title: Entire evidence base is SWE-bench runs reproducible only by manual README steps; zero CI and zero self-tests, evidence culture lives in release-artifact dumps
evidence: no .github/ in repo (find over tree); only .pre-commit-config.yaml (formatting); README.md:74-78 (complete runs shipped on v1.5.0 release); agentless/test/*.py are benchmark-run harnesses, not package tests (run_tests.py:10,19 imports docker + swebench harness)
one_why: Worst corner of the eval-outside-CI space: not merely unenforced evals -- nothing at all checks the code itself, and 21 months of API drift make even the published claims unreproducible without archaeology; shipping full run artifacts out-of-band is better than nothing but enforces nothing.

subject: agentless
title: Cheapest resume form: append-only JSONL per-instance journal + --skip_existing + config/input snapshot written before the run starts
evidence: agentless/fl/localize.py:399-401,564-566 (load_existing_instance_ids + skip_existing flag); agentless/repair/repair.py:540 (prev_o reload) and :536-545 (config.json dump + used_locs.jsonl input snapshot before processing)
one_why: For batch fan-out pipelines a per-instance skip-set over append-only JSONL is a whole resume system in ~10 lines, and the pre-run config/inputs snapshot gives per-result provenance for free; nuance vs the seeded id: no ordering or replay semantics, just idempotent skip -- sufficient at batch scale.

subject: agentty
title: Three-trigger doom breaker with an always-on identical-SUCCESS-repeat cap that catches unknown local models
evidence: src/runtime/app/cmd_factory.cpp:1699-1810; consult before each continuation :2011; tests/doom_loop_test.cpp:1-13
one_why: Beyond crush's single breaker: failing-repeat x3 (always), byte-identical succeeding-repeat x6 (EVERY model, motivated by a measured 80-repeat loop of a 22GB model behind a private gateway that the weak-model heuristic could not name), and a 25-turn runaway cap deliberately gated to weak models only; the break surfaces as a corrective final assistant turn, not a kill.

subject: agentty
title: Permission policy as a constexpr pure function with an exhaustive 48-cell compile-time proof - the build is the test runner
evidence: include/agentty/tool/policy.hpp:37-53 (pure constexpr (EffectSet x Profile) -> Decision), :66-90 (spec fn + static_assert loop over all 16x3 cells); single-source-of-truth doc :5-8
one_why: No other subject proves its trust matrix: a policy edit that breaks any cell fails the build at the breaking line, so the table can never silently drift from its spec - the cheapest correctness mechanism in the corpus, portable to any language with const-eval.

subject: agentty
title: Sandbox availability is a capability probe that runs the exact namespace the real command will use, not a `which`
evidence: src/tool/util/sandbox.cpp:66-98 (bwrap_can_sandbox unshares --user/--pid against /bin/true; fixes issue #21 false 'sandbox: active' on Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor-restricted hosts), :24-35 (SBPL escape fail-closed); tests/sandbox_escape_test.cpp, tests/sandbox_parity_test.cpp; docs/SANDBOX.md:26-31
one_why: forge-norvialabs has the refuse-startup half; agentty adds the probe-fidelity half - `bwrap --version` proves only the binary exists, so the probe must replicate the real run's unshare set, and Auto-vs-On decide whether failure degrades or aborts; the SBPL path-escaping-with-fail-closed is a tested injection guard nobody else shows.

subject: agentty
title: Deep-ride compaction trigger justified in-cache: fire at ~95% because the retained prefix is a prompt-cache hit and every compaction resets it
evidence: src/runtime/app/update/stream.cpp:1062-1070 (threshold min(95%, window-20k) + cache rationale), :1086 max(tokens_in, est); cmd_factory.cpp:532-543 (summary slice capped at 150k so the summary request stays cheap on 1M windows)
one_why: Compaction cadence is reasoned about as total token burn (cache-hit prefix ~= free, compaction = summary request + cache reset), not as overflow fear - the trigger policy itself is cache-monotonic, and CompactionRecord stores before/after token counts so a compaction that reclaimed ~nothing is detectable (conversation.hpp:897-914).

subject: agentty
title: Reversible wire-only soft-trim under compaction: transcript never mutates, so overflow degrades to truncation instead of wedging the agent
evidence: src/runtime/app/cmd_factory.cpp:382-460 (soft_trim_to_ceiling: protects head, latest User, newest result; 'trim is REVERSIBLE ... no CompactionRecord is mutated'); stream.cpp:1057-1060 (compaction fails -> next turn ships via soft-trim); stream.cpp:405-428,794-799 (rapid-refill breaker, temporarily disabled, re-arms after ~10 quiet turns)
one_why: The loop never observes a wedge: mid-tool-burst overflow is handled by silently trimming the wire payload, LLM compaction stays a strictly-better optimization the user (or the idle trigger) runs at leisure, and the livelock breaker that disables auto-compact is temporary with a documented re-arm.

subject: agentty
title: Hooks and skills share one trust shape: content-hash-bound explicit approval that revokes on any byte change, and execution inside the same OS sandbox
evidence: include/agentty/tool/hooks.hpp:28-48 (unseen/changed hooks file does not run; `hooks approve` stores SHA-256; approved hooks run through the bwrap/sandbox-exec wrapper), skills.hpp:286-345 (body screened for documented injection patterns, approval keyed to body+declared-effects bytes)
one_why: There is no 'approve forever': modification invalidates consent, and the screening cites the arXiv 98k-skill study - even approved-but-compromised extension code stays workspace-confined, closing the auto-shell-on-first-read exfil vector the hooks surface normally implies.

subject: agentty
title: Air-gapped mode: agent runs on an offline host, bytes relay over `ssh -R 1080` SOCKS5 with TLS pinned end-to-end so the relay cannot MITM
evidence: src/airgap/airgap.cpp:1-30 (reverse SOCKS5, AGENTTY_SOCKS_PROXY injection, no per-host enumeration, exec() into ssh on POSIX); main.cpp:852,1210; README 'Air-gapped mode'
one_why: One command covers the whole air-gap workflow (dial, credential ferry with --setup + chmod 600, proxy env) without trusting the relay with plaintext - no other subject in the corpus addresses disconnected-host agenting at all.

subject: agentty
title: Quantized 1-hour cache anchor + one rolling 5-minute pin, capped at Anthropic's 4-breakpoint budget because a 5th evicts the system pin
evidence: tests/cache_anchor_test.cpp:1-13 (shape locked: anchor doesn't move when one turn is appended; <=2 message pins; short threads = rolling pair only); src/provider/anthropic/transport.cpp:87,346-401 (ttl 1h, silent-drop note, tools-array pin)
one_why: The quantization is what makes the anchor pay: a breakpoint that moves every turn is a cache miss every turn, and the <=4 discipline exists because exceeding Anthropic's breakpoint budget silently evicts the front (system-prompt) pin - a failure mode most subjects do not know they have.

subject: agentty
title: Byte-based token estimate is calibrated online by EMA against the provider's real usage counts before it gates compaction
evidence: src/runtime/app/update/stream.cpp:1729-1732 (next = 0.65*est_calibration + 0.35*sample), :1085 threshold compare uses est*calibration; include/agentty/domain/session.hpp:497; single estimator basis everywhere per include/agentty/domain/conversation.hpp:958-963
one_why: The raw bytes/3.5 guess fired compaction with 60k+ headroom on tool-heavy threads; one shared estimator plus a learned correction factor keeps the proactive (lagging-tokens_in problem) trigger honest without shipping a tokenizer.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Scripted JSONL provider streams plus scripted per-tool-use approval decisions drive end-to-end session tests in both stacks
evidence: crates/agent/tests/mod.rs:12-60 with crates/agent/tests/mock_responses/{builtin_tools,context_window_overflow}.jsonl; crates/chat-cli/src/cli/chat/mod.rs:4032,4550-4567
one_why: Nuance vs pi-8/codex-5: the harness scripts approvals as first-class inputs (SendApprovalResultArgs lists), so approval-gated tool pipelines are testable without a human or model - the approval-script channel is the portable part; chat-cli variant mocks at the client-API layer and asserts hook stdout files.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: New agent framework returns unconditional Allow for ExecuteCmd/SpawnSubagent/Grep/Mkdir - no per-call approval path exists
evidence: crates/agent/src/agent/permissions.rs:62-69; allowed_tools only gates tool exposure at crates/agent/src/agent/mod.rs:1498; no requires_acceptance in crates/agent/src/agent/tools/execute_cmd.rs
one_why: The framework has a full approval protocol (AgentRequest::SendApprovalResult, mod.rs:598-723) but shell execution never enters it; a host embedding this crate gets silent shell by default - exposure-gating is not execution-gating.

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Read tools (ls, image_read) are permission-checked against fs_write allowed/denied path lists while the code comment claims fs_read reuse

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Token-level bash auto-approval: shlex split, dangerous-token scan, per-pipe-segment readonly allowlist, find -exec and grep -P special cases, anchored-regex user allowlist

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli
title: Char-based degradation: 600K-char warning nags /compact, auto-compaction fires only reactively on ContextWindowOverflow, hard-fail menu as last rung, all disable-able

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli

subject: amazon-q-developer-cli

subject: atomic-agent
title: GBNF grammar-constrained tool calls for local models: array-only root kills first-token bias into single-object form, per-request grammar narrowing (tool-name set rewritten, every other byte identical, cached by sorted list) travels outside the KV-cached prefix, and a bounded think-body rule (think-char{0,N}) forces runaway reasoners to close the block and emit the call

subject: atomic-agent
title: KV-cache-monotonic prompt architecture: stable prefix pinned byte-identical per session (tests assert byte-equality), everything a step can change placed AFTER ### conversation in the variable tail, per-request grammar kept out of the prefix, conversation pack holds a 0.65 low-water hysteresis, and cache hits are measured server-side (cacheHitTokens) and surfaced per step in traces

subject: atomic-agent

Roadmap-fit: copy the gate-owns-the-value rule.

subject: atomic-agent

subject: atomic-agent

subject: atomic-agent

subject: auto-code-rover

subject: crab-code

subject: crab-code
title: Deny-wins-as-security-boundary invariant, cross-layer tested, plus quote-aware per-segment deny for chained bash

subject: crab-code
title: Transform-style prepare_command with per-platform backends: Landlock fail-closed, seatbelt PATH-hijack-hardened, Windows honestly fail-open
evidence: crates/sandbox/src/lib.rs:1-16; crates/sandbox/src/backend/landlock.rs:57-67,137-142; crates/sandbox/src/backend/seatbelt.rs:19-29,57-66

subject: crab-code

subject: crab-code

subject: crab-code

subject: crab-code

subject: crab-code

subject: crab-code

subject: deepagents
title: LLM classifier batch-reviews tool calls behind deterministic allow/deny, failing to a human on unavailability with a latched bad spec
evidence: libs/code/deepagents_code/auto_mode.py:467-491 (DecisionDisposition), :154-156 (_CONSECUTIVE_DENIAL_FALLBACK=3 / _CONSECUTIVE_UNAVAILABLE_FALLBACK=2), :449-456 (classifier_config_failed_spec latch), :2370 (AutoModeHITLMiddleware subclasses HITL)
one_why: Approvals get a second, model-agnostic adjudicator between 'policy allows' and 'ask the human', and every failure mode (classifier down, bad model spec, repeated denials, oversized context) is engineered to fail toward a human, not toward auto-approve - distinct from codex's guardian-reviewer-pool which reviews actions in-process rather than as a batched classifier with escalation counters; tests assert the fail-closed branches (test_auto_mode.py:742,2339,3012).

subject: deepagents
title: DeltaChannel messages reducer with periodic snapshots cuts LangGraph checkpoint growth from O(N^2) to O(N)
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/graph.py:74-77 (DeltaChannel(_messages_delta_reducer, snapshot_frequency=50)); libs/deepagents/deepagents/_messages_reducer.py:31-60 (dedup by id, RemoveMessage tombstones, id assignment deliberately deferred to LangGraph replay hook)
one_why: Long-horizon agents rewrite the whole message list into every checkpoint superlinearly; the reducer's fast-path skips convert_to_messages on already-typed state and refuses to assign ids because 'a reducer runs on replay too, where a randomly-assigned ID would differ from the one stored in the checkpoint' - a replay-determinism insight most session-journal designs miss.

subject: deepagents
title: Filesystem permissions enforced per-tool with conservative recursive-delete semantics, and construction fails closed when paired with an execute-capable backend
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware/filesystem.py:502-587 (deny blocks ancestor/wildcard-overlapping delete), :1792-1801 (NotImplementedError on permissions+SandboxBackendProtocol); middleware/_fs_interrupt.py:24-46 (pathless bulk grep fires unconditionally for any interrupt rule)
one_why: Two honesty moves over the standard tested-approval 6-rung: a deny pattern anywhere in the ancestor chain blocks a recursive delete even when the leaf is unlisted, and the permissions story does NOT silently claim to cover `execute` - it refuses to build rather than ship a policy the shell tool bypasses. Gap is real and documented: permissions bind at the tool layer only, not on direct backend use (graph.py:454-457).

subject: deepagents
title: Three tiers (tool-arg truncation -> fraction-triggered summarization -> provider-overflow recovery with one budgeted retry) plus reversible backend offload
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware/summarization.py:171-196 (TruncateArgsSettings), :257-286 (model-profile-driven fraction vs conservative fixed defaults), :1542-1548 (context-overflow catch -> summarize+clip, exactly one retry, else ContextOverflowError), :1571-1580 (offload to backend BEFORE summarizing so eviction is reversible)

Trigger defaults switch to fraction-based only when the model profile advertises max_input_tokens.

subject: deepagents

subject: devon

subject: devon

subject: devon

subject: devon

subject: dvalincode
title: Narrowing-monotone org policy with canonical source-order-independent hash, enforced at a single tool chokepoint
evidence: src/core/policy.ts:9-20,152-157,198-231; src/tools/registry.ts:111-131; src/agent/session.ts:203-279; tests/core/policy.test.ts:36-49
one_why: Every resolution combinator only restricts (allowlists intersect, denylists union, caps take min, network takes the strictest level), so a repo-committed policy can never widen the machine policy -- tested property; sorted canonical resolution makes the resolved-policy hash source-order independent, which is exactly what a tamper-evidence hash needs; enforcement lives in one registry.run() chokepoint (tool deny -> per-target command/path checks -> approval -> audit) plus the MCP spawn path applying checkCommand itself because the chokepoint doesn't cover it.

subject: dvalincode
title: Un-raisable hard-block command class + allowlist-disqualifying shell constructs, matched per quote-aware command segment
evidence: src/core/policy.ts:249-290 (HARD_BLOCKED), :293-307 (ALLOWLIST_DISQUALIFIERS), :310+ (splitCommandSegments); tests/core/policy.test.ts (splitCommandSegments/checkCommand imports)
one_why: Nuance on the permission-policy cluster: rm-rf-of-root, raw device writes, curl-pipe-shell and fork bombs are refused whatever the policy says -- no allowlist escape -- and any command containing substitution or redirection is disqualified from ever satisfying an allowlist because matching the visible text proves nothing about what executes; segmentation is quote-aware so 'ls && rm -rf ~' is caught as its segments.

subject: dvalincode
title: Hash-chained per-run audit log seeded with the policy hash, plus an offline verify command and an install-specific `trust` self-report
evidence: src/audit/log.ts:19-40,81-88,191; src/audit/hash.ts:12-30; src/agent/loop.ts:196-215 (run_start); src/core/trust.ts:22-90; src/commands/report.ts:37
one_why: run_start records the resolved-policy hash + per-source hashes + git HEAD, each record chains prevHash over canonical JSON, verifyChain re-derives offline, and `dvalincode trust` prints the install's own posture (policy, per-surface network enforcement, MCP permissions, deps) so an approver verifies claims instead of trusting them; honest boundary stated in code: tamper-evident, not tamper-proof against a hostile local admin; shell_exec events deliberately carry the executable, never the arguments.

subject: dvalincode
title: Verified Fix Record: verdict from observed exit codes + independent re-scan, carrying its own gate rule so a third party can re-reach it; v1 keeps verifying under v1 rules forever
evidence: src/security/fixRecord.ts:13-58 (FIX_RECORD_SCHEMA_V1/V2, FixRecordGate, executor list)
one_why: Inverts the standard 'ask the model that wrote the patch whether it is good': the record is executor-agnostic (dvalin/codex/claude-code/copilot/human), states narrowly (finding gone from this scan + checks observed to pass, never 'vulnerability-free'), and embeds the threshold+mode the verdict was reached under because two producers without it answered the regression question differently; the schema-versioning discipline -- v1 records permanently verify under v1 rules, since a record that stops re-deriving because the rules moved breaks the only promise the format makes -- is the corpus's most rigorous artifact-evolution stance.

subject: dvalincode
title: Append-only turn journal with idempotent replay and dangling-turn recovery, linked to the audit chain by ids and checkpoint hash only
evidence: src/sessions/journal.ts:5-46; src/agent/session.ts:124,155-157; tests/sessions/journal.test.ts:53-55
one_why: Nuance on the seeded journal id: the journal is session state that may hold raw user text (so a crashed turn survives), while the audit chain never receives that content -- the two planes link only via runId/sessionId/audit-head hash, a clean separation most subjects blur by replaying through the same log.

subject: dvalincode
title: Triple-condition stall detector (exact-repeat, same-check-failing-without-edit, N-unverified-edits) with a one-nudge-then-stop escalation, plus first-edit investigation gate
evidence: src/agent/runner.ts:34-48,305-365,425-480 (observeAction); tests/agent.test.ts:81,110
one_why: Beyond crush's single breaker: three distinct stall signatures (consecutive identical action; the same focused check failing N times inside one write-generation; N consecutive writes with no read/diff/validation), each first answered by a single corrective nudge and only then a hard stop with a human-readable summary; the failed-test counter resets on any intervening source edit via a write-generation counter, which kills the retry-blind-backoff pattern without punishing legitimate re-runs.

subject: dvalincode
title: Trigger estimates the full outgoing request (messages + system + tool defs) at turn entry AND every iteration boundary, with a monotonic +1k-token anti-thrash guard between compactions
evidence: src/agent/compact.ts:10-17; src/agent/runner.ts:176-190; src/agent/loop.ts:151-162; tests/agent.test.ts:287,541,575
one_why: Nuance on the measured-input id: estimating includes serialized tool definitions so the number approximates the provider bill rather than chat text, the mid-tool-loop check keeps long turns from dying at the provider limit, and lastCompactionAtTokens + 1000 prevents summarize-thrash where compaction barely shrinks below the trigger; no usage feedback loop calibrates the char/4 estimate (mocode's edge), which is why this is nuance, not a new peak.

subject: dvalincode
title: Cache discipline as loop constraint: nudge messages append-only so every prior message stays cacheable, plus ephemeral cache_control on system/last-tool/last-block
evidence: src/agent/runner.ts:231-233,247-252; src/providers/anthropic.ts:49,70,77,220-234; src/agent/loop.ts:266-280 (cached/cache-miss/cache-write split in run_end)
one_why: Nuance on prompt-cache-marking: the interesting half is not the breakpoints but the loop-level rule -- the pending-work nudge is documented as appended specifically to keep the request prefix append-only -- and run_end records the cached/cache-miss/cache-write token split so cache behavior is observable per run, not just asserted.

subject: dvalincode
title: CI drives the built binary with the reference MCP client over a real pipe, with a require-flag that turns a missing build into a failure; a separate weekly job re-verifies against current real harness CLIs
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml (mcp-interop job + DVALIN_REQUIRE_MCP_INTEROP); tests/mcp/clientInterop.test.ts:11-33; .github/workflows/harness-interop.yml:1-21
one_why: In-process tests that build their own request strings cannot catch a protocol misread -- both sides would be wrong in the same way (a real regression here echoed the client's protocol version back); the fix is CI running an independent reference client against dist/, failing loudly if the build step was reordered away, plus a deliberately CI-external weekly job so interop claims carry a date instead of decaying silently in a PR comment.

subject: dvalincode
title: Offline meta-test asserting every third-party action's commit digest and its version comment never contradict each other across workflows
evidence: tests/actionPinning.test.ts:7-20 and assertions below
one_why: Dependabot moves digests and never the human-trusted version comments, so drift is silent; this test catches the repo contradicting itself -- one digest described two ways, or one version resolving to two digests -- which was the actual failure mode behind real breakages where two jobs of the same action landed on different commits and rejected each other at runtime; cheap supply-chain hygiene any MIT subject can copy today.

subject: ferrum
title: Tree-sitter-bash rejection policy with three enforced tiers; docs capability table IS the regression test
evidence: src/tools/shell_guard.rs:82,1267-1305; src/tools/shell_policy.rs:5-39; src/tools/mod.rs:223
one_why: Nuance vs kimi-code/smelt: there is no approval prompt at all -- grammar verdicts are the authority, tiers are low/medium/high, and tier_capability_contract_is_table_driven asserts the exact allow/deny matrix published in docs/security.md, so docs and policy cannot drift.

subject: ferrum
title: Compaction re-appends immutable system/repo policy AFTER the generated summary so summarized text can never carry system authority
evidence: src/agent/mod.rs:4666-4669; test src/agent/mod.rs:7016
one_why: Most compaction implementations splice the summary into position 0 of the surviving list, letting attacker-seeded text inside the summarized range inherit whatever role the head message had; ferrum makes ordering an explicit invariant with a named test.

subject: ferrum
title: Trigger projects provider-reported context_tokens + estimated tail, checked before every request AND mid-loop, and refuses to send if the post-compaction projection still exceeds budget
one_why: Nuance vs mocode/zot: max(local_estimate, usage_projection) keeps the estimate as floor, and the hard bail after compaction converts a silent provider overflow into a diagnosable local error; compaction is skipped outright unless it strictly reduces tokens (mod.rs:4675).

subject: ferrum

subject: ferrum

subject: ferrum
title: 477 tests including whole-binary protocol conformance with zero CI to run any of them

subject: ferrum

subject: ferrum
title: Per-spawn delegated cgroup-v2 with pre_exec attach and cgroup.kill for bash and MCP children

subject: ferrum

subject: ferrum

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Kernel confinement is the boundary, not approvals: shell is deliberately NOT HITL-gated, and on a host that cannot confine (no bwrap, nested-sandbox sandbox_apply failure) the CLI refuses to start rather than running unconfined

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Per-session deny-by-default egress proxy: nothing pre-allowed (crates.io/npmjs/pypi/github asserted 403 in tests), only PERSONAL permissions.toml host rules open it -- repo-committed allows never do; denied hosts escalate as typed approval kinds with host_grant_stays_filesystem_sandboxed
evidence: crates/forge-core/src/permission.rs:36-48 (repo allows never loosen), :61-84 (proxy start, socket outside workspace, failure leaves network off), :143-167 (refuses former ecosystem hosts), :308-330 (only personal allows open), :470-511 (subagent inherits parent grant, never a second proxy); crates/forge-cli/src/main.rs:205-221 (denied_host / sandbox_escalation / governance_approval JSON kinds); socat relay into the bwrap netns at crates/forge-tools/src/sandbox.rs:404-420
one_why: Same direction as codex's separate network approval but with a sharper trust split: a poisoned repo cannot widen its own network policy, and proxy-start failure degrades to offline rather than to open network -- the three failure modes are each pinned by a test.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Protected-facts gate inside a fully transactional compaction: user-authored constraints/corrections/decisions/irreversible-actions are extracted from canonical history, fed to the checkpoint prompt as must-keep, and the candidate is REJECTED (MissingProtectedFacts) before install; compaction commits-or-rolls-back with a new cache epoch
evidence: crates/forge-context/src/compaction/facts.rs:1-40; crates/forge-context/src/compaction/engine.rs:1-5,35-47 (pure proposal, never mutates; NotSmaller/StillOversized/InvalidStructure/MissingProtectedFacts); crates/forge-core/src/session/compaction.rs:7-18 (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK), :282-311 (install journals + opens cache epoch); crates/forge-context/src/compaction/policy.rs:105-106 (trigger includes next-turn projection so it fires before overflow)
one_why: Same survival-gate idea grinta found, but wired as a hard install precondition with deliberately shallow extraction (user text only, no intent classifier) and paired with the runway gate that refuses compactions too small to pay for breaking the cached prefix.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Permission model tested as a behavior contract: permission_contract.rs spawns real processes and asserts what the kernel did, written around four historical defects a unit test missed (inert rule from /var vs /private/var, --tmpfs symlink abort, bind/mask ordering, cross-layer gap); sandbox_is_available_on_linux_in_ci fails the build if CI loses bubblewrap so skips can't silently untest the suite
evidence: crates/forge-tools/tests/permission_contract.rs:1-40 (design comment + three properties), :104-127 (Expect::Denied rows); crates/forge-tools/tests/sandbox_enforcement.rs:1-47,1177; .github/workflows/ci.yml:24-35 (apt-get bubblewrap socat 'worth spending an apt-get on', installer tested)
one_why: The anti-silent-skip machinery is the portable part: loud skip reasons locally, a test that asserts the CI runner can confine, and a table someone can scan to see exactly what the sandbox promises.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: Cache epochs as first-state: a cache_epoch counter bumped on compaction/transport change, journal-restored; prompt-wire snapshots diff common prefixes and log CACHE PREFIX INVALIDATED naming the diverging part -- gated off the production hot path unless DEBUG; cross-provider usage normalization so Anthropic's uncached-only vs OpenAI's total prompt_tokens mean one quantity
evidence: crates/forge-core/src/session/turn_ops.rs:713-800 (record_prompt_snapshot, begin_cache_epoch); crates/forge-core/src/session/compaction.rs:292,310; crates/forge-durable/src/lib.rs:126-127 (epoch survives replay); crates/forge-model/src/prompt_cache.rs:20-47 (cache_write_tokens, InputTokens::Total|UncachedOnly)
one_why: Below smelt's fuzzed cache-invariance and pi's warming, but the epoch model makes every cache invalidation an attributable event (reason + journal entry) instead of a hope, and the usage-semantics normalization fixes hit-rate math every cross-provider harness silently gets wrong.

subject: forge-norvialabs
title: MCP schema deferral is budget-gated against the SAME window arithmetic as compaction: full schemas are sent until they exceed 10% of usable context (tool_schema_budget), then replaced by a SearchToolsTool catalog
evidence: crates/forge-context/src/compaction/policy.rs:38-44,132-136; crates/forge-core/src/session/turn_ops.rs:113-134; crates/forge-mcp/src/lib.rs:507-588 (SearchToolsTool, install_search_tools)
one_why: Maki's deferred-catalog idea, with the missing bit maki lacks: an explicit, tested token budget tied to the real usable window so the switch is arithmetic, not a setting.

subject: forge-norvialabs

subject: forge

subject: forge

subject: forge
title: Accept-and-Remember stores whole-string glob grants: 'git push' becomes git push*, which also admits 'git push && curl evil.sh' since glob * spans shell metacharacters; write grants become *.ext everywhere (one accepted .rs edit allows all .rs writes system-wide)

subject: forge

title: Reactive overflow ladder: peel API-round groups, shrink giant outputs, trim old errors, then breaker

one_why: On ContextLimitError the loop peels one oldest API-round group if it saves >=500 tokens, retries; at the consecutive-error breaker it truncates largest non-error tool outputs and drops old error observations before one final condense-retry, raising AgentRuntimeError only when even that overflows - graceful steps down instead of failing open or dead.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Stuck detector with intent-diversity, cost-acceleration, token-repetition and think-only signals
evidence: backend/orchestration/stuck/detector.py:339-455,512,541,583; backend/tests/unit/orchestration/test_stuck_detector.py
one_why: Nuance vs crush/kimi-code loop-detection: beyond repeating action/observation patterns it classifies each command's shell intent, computes intent diversity and failure rate to catch semantic loops, and flags escalating prompt-token cost or pure-thinking churn as stuck states.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Composite TaskValidator blocks premature FINISHED declarations
evidence: backend/validation/task_validator.py:1-6,149,166,249,430,564,711
one_why: Inverse of cursor-agent's heuristic-task-completion anti-pattern: completion requires passing pluggable validators (test-passing, meaningful-diff, file-exists, LLM evaluator) over the task's acceptance criteria, so 'done' is an enforced claim rather than a model assertion.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: DeepSWE eval workflow in CI with frozen model policy and explicitly bounded paired Codex case study
evidence: .github/workflows/run-eval.yml:4-10,41; evaluation/deepswe/README.md:1-10
one_why: Nuance vs 6 prior evals-in-ci: runs on release-publish and label-triggered PRs (not a mandatory per-PR gate), uses the external DataCurve Pier harness with Grinta as the agent under test and an external verifier - and the README forbids presenting the 8-task paired Codex comparison as a leaderboard score; clears the anchor errata verification-9 bar alongside every-PR mutmut (mutation-testing.yml:38).

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Command policy is shlex+regex heuristics but de-obfuscates before classifying
evidence: backend/security/command_analyzer.py:1-4,42-51
one_why: Still pattern heuristics, not AST (bashlex is a dep but used elsewhere), yet it collapses $(printf %s rm) / $(echo rm) substitutions and takes the worst-of raw vs normalized risk - one notch above the corpus's naive regex deny-lists, and the reason the safety score sits above nanocoder.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: ChatGPT-subscription Codex OAuth as the harness's own model transport
evidence: backend/inference/clients/codex_app_server.py:1-8,29
one_why: Reuses Codex App Server only for managed OAuth and the model catalog, then drives the subscription Responses endpoint directly so Grinta owns loop, tools, approvals and transcript - a genuinely novel interop shape (rival harness as provider plane, not as agent), but it rests on an unofficial chatgpt.com backend-api URL with unexamined ToS surface; port the shape only with eyes open.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Durable event stream: WAL-first enqueue, flush retry policy, persistence-health states, session lock
evidence: backend/ledger/stream/durable_writer.py:13-18,155-188; backend/ledger/stream/event_stream.py:98,434,617-647
one_why: Nuance vs kimi-code entry: durability machinery is the finding - write-ahead before dispatch, batched flush with transient-failure retry, ok/degraded/failed health exposed at runtime, and a cross-process session lock; crash-window loss is reduced-until-flushed, documented rather than denied.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Manifest-based workspace checkpoint with quarantine instead of silent delete
evidence: backend/execution/rollback/workspace_checkpoint.py:72,109,219-263; pyproject.toml shadowgit pinned dep
one_why: Nuance vs seeded id: restore moves unexpected workspace extras into a quarantine directory rather than deleting them, and a companion pinned ShadowGit dependency handles git-level history; no git-stash GC story like cline's.

subject: grok-cli
title: 253 property tests exist but no CI workflow runs vitest
evidence: .github/workflows/typecheck.yml:31-41 (format/lint/typecheck/build only); release.yml has no test step; 48 src/**/*.test.ts (5,379 LOC)
one_why: Tests assert real semantics (compaction cut-points, shuru wrap escaping) yet nothing enforces them on push, so regressions merge silently — the single cheapest fix on this subject.

subject: grok-cli
title: No approval gate for bash, file writes, or MCP tools in default host mode
evidence: src/grok/tools.ts:901 (only needsApproval in tree, for paid_request); no approval path in src/tools/bash.ts or file tools
one_why: The one approval mechanism built exists solely for payments; destructive host commands run unattended by default because sandboxMode defaults to off (src/tools/bash.ts:42) and is macOS-arm64-only.

subject: grok-cli
title: Hooks loaded from user settings only, with explicit anti-repo-committed-hook rationale
evidence: src/hooks/config.ts:5-11
one_why: Deliberately excludes repo-committed project settings so a malicious repo cannot execute unsandboxed host commands via hook definitions — a documented, copyable trust boundary.

subject: grok-cli
title: Shuru microVM sandbox is fail-closed and trust-prompted, but platform-gated and off by default
evidence: src/utils/workspace-trust.ts:23-25 (darwin+arm64 only); src/tools/bash.ts:411-413 (unsupported => error, no host fallback); src/index.ts:196-211 (default-Y first-run prompt)
one_why: Fail-closed-when-unsupported plus a default-Y per-workspace trust prompt is a stronger posture shape than nanocoder's fail-open jail, but the off default on non-Apple-Silicon guts it for most users.

subject: grok-cli
title: Context-overflow retry halves keep-recent budget down to a 4k floor
evidence: src/agent/agent.ts:1908,2134-2140; src/agent/compaction.ts:342-347 (relaxCompactionSettings, MIN_KEPT_TOKENS_ON_RETRY=4000)
one_why: On a context-limit error with no assistant output it re-compacts more aggressively and retries once instead of dying — a small bounded recovery ladder worth lifting.

subject: grok-cli
title: x402 wallet payments with BRIN security pre-scan hard-blocking low-score URLs
evidence: src/payments/service.ts:103-123 (brin.score<25 => blocked_by_brin); src/agent/agent.ts:2043-2076 (402-header probe feeds approval prompt)
one_why: Only corpus subject with agent-initiated crypto payments; the security-scan-before-pay gate with a human approval step is the transferable pattern (scoring service itself is third-party).

subject: grok-cli
title: Telegram remote control of a live CLI session: pairing codes, voice STT, streamed previews
evidence: src/telegram/pairing.ts:27 (expiring pair codes); src/telegram/audio-input.ts:53; src/telegram/preview-stream.ts
one_why: Driving the running agent from a phone with audio input is a distinctive interop surface no anchor or sibling subject has, though it widens the unattended-approval attack surface noted in grok-cli-2.

subject: grok-cli
title: Encrypted-reasoning marker detection hides opaque reasoning from display and summary inputs
evidence: src/agent/reasoning.ts:4-9 (PGP/AGE/encrypted_content markers); src/agent/agent.ts:1977-1986; compaction.ts:113-127 filters it from summarization
one_why: Grok returns PGP/AGE-encrypted reasoning blocks; stripping them from compaction/summary serialization avoids feeding garbage ciphertext back into summarizer prompts.

subject: grok-cli
title: agent.ts fuses interactive loop, batch loop, delegation and recap; App is 5.9k LOC
evidence: src/agent/agent.ts:535 (class Agent, 2830 LOC); src/ui/app.tsx:597 (App, 5862 LOC)
one_why: Both fusions trip the pi-errata docking rule (>5k product-surface file); loop/batch separation would make headless modes independently testable.

subject: groq-code-cli
title: Never-auto-approvable dangerous tier separated from session-auto-approvable tier
evidence: src/core/agent.ts:583; src/tools/tool-schemas.ts:385-394; default-deny fallback src/core/agent.ts:610
one_why: canAutoApprove requires !isDangerous, so session auto-approve can never silently unlock execute_command/delete_file, and a missing approval callback denies by default; small, clean policy shape worth mirroring, though it is untested here.

subject: groq-code-cli
title: No path containment on read/create/edit; delete guard bypassable via sibling prefix
evidence: src/tools/tools.ts:123,185,222 (path.resolve only); src/tools/tools.ts:264 (targetPath.startsWith(currentWorkingDir))
one_why: With session auto-approve on, the model can read_file then edit_file any absolute path (~/.bashrc, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys); delete_file's startsWith check admits /work/proj-evil when cwd is /work/proj -- approvals bind by tool name, never by path scope.

subject: groq-code-cli
title: ava files glob orphans 3 of 4 test files; no CI ever runs tests
evidence: package.json:53-56 (files: ["src/**/*.test.ts"]) vs test/agent-context-load.test.ts, test/context-generator.test.ts, test/init-command.test.ts; only .github/workflows/stale.yaml exists
one_why: npm test runs only src/tests/proxy-config.test.ts; the loop, approval gate, and tool dispatch have zero coverage and no CI job would catch regressions even in the tests that do exist.

subject: groq-code-cli
title: Unbounded message history; overflow surfaces as generic retry-forever error overlay
evidence: src/core/agent.ts:266-541 (messages array only grows; no compaction anywhere in src/), retry path src/core/agent.ts:487-517
one_why: No compaction, trim, or context-window check exists; a context-length 400 enters the same onError retry loop and 'retry' re-sends the identical oversized payload -- worse than codel's crude >30k-chars ask-the-user because there is no detection at all, only usage display.

subject: groq-code-cli
title: Deterministic no-LLM /init project-context generator with env-var overrides
evidence: src/utils/context.ts:35-80 (walk maxDepth 3 / maxEntries 1500, language histogram, package facts, tree -> .groq/context.md + .json); auto-load + GROQ_CONTEXT_FILE/DIR/LIMIT trim src/core/agent.ts:66-86
one_why: Seeds a repo-map context file without spending a model call, keeps a machine-readable JSON twin, and the GROQ_CONTEXT_* env trio makes it testable (test/agent-context-load.test.ts) -- a cheaper alternative to LLM-summarized AGENTS.md bootstrapping.

subject: groq-code-cli
title: Debug mode writes masked curl repro plus full request JSON per API call
evidence: src/core/agent.ts:664-680 (generateCurlCommand, key masked to 8+8 chars) invoked at src/core/agent.ts:325
one_why: Every request becomes a runnable curl against a saved body file, making provider-side bug reproduction trivial without a proxy; note the request JSON dumps the full conversation to cwd, so it should ship with a redaction pass if adopted.

subject: hax
title: Summarization request advertises the full live tool set so the provider's cached prompt prefix survives; tool calls in the summary response are answered with [rejected] results, never executed, up to 4 attempts
evidence: src/compact.c:240-266 (comment: 'Advertising the normal tools preserves the provider's cached request prefix. Calls are rejected rather than executed because compaction must not mutate task state'), src/compact.c:208-210 (TOOL_CALL_REJECTION), src/compact.c:102 (COMPACT_MAX_ATTEMPTS)
one_why: The usual way to stop a compaction call from running tools is to send an empty tool list -- which changes the request prefix and blows the prompt cache on the very next request; keeping the tools advertised and rejecting calls instead is strictly cheaper and reuses the seeded concept from the execution side.

subject: hax
title: Aggregate image budget enforced at ingestion by dropping the just-read image, not degrading older ones, so all prior serialized requests stay byte-stable and the prefix cache survives
evidence: src/agent_loop.c:227-235 (comment: 'Dropping the just-read image (rather than degrading older ones at serialization) keeps prior requests byte-stable, so the provider prefix cache survives'), src/agent_tool.h agent_tool_result_enforce_image_budget call site
one_why: Monotonicity applied to multimodal content: budget decisions taken at append-time on the newest item only, so history bytes never mutate retroactively -- the cache-safe alternative to trim-on-serialize schemes.

subject: hax
title: No permission gate by explicit doctrine with a correct threat model: an in-process approval gate is declared 'not a security boundary' and isolation is delegated to container/VM, while the README repeats the omission to users
evidence: docs/philosophy.md:74-83 ('because it runs inside the process it guards, it is not a security boundary ... run hax in a container or VM'), README.md:33 ('per-command permission prompts, other agents build exactly that -- hax deliberately doesn't'), src/agent_core.c:51-53 (prompt-only git prohibitions), src/tools/bash_classify.h:6-7 (classifier 'never changes execution')
one_why: Same delegation posture the corpus flags as safety-hole (cline-7, pi), but stated up front instead of discovered -- the honest-minimalist pole of the permission design space; note the display-only classifier is explicitly NOT a phantom control.

subject: hax
title: Mock provider compiled into the shipped binary, scripted from plain-text files via env vars, so Python e2e tests drive the real CLI end-to-end under meson and C tests script loop/compact paths with in-process provider fakes
evidence: src/providers/mock.c (638 LOC), tests/e2e/harness.py:68-108 (HAX_PROVIDER=mock, HAX_MOCK_SCRIPT=scripts/mock/*.txt), tests/meson.build:151-166 (e2e registration), scripts/mock/{tool_roundtrip,tasks,interrupt_stall}.txt, tests/test_agent_loop.c:171-386
one_why: Zero-network deterministic e2e of the actual binary including interrupt and background-task scenarios; the script-file format doubles as the fixture language for --json output tests (test_oneshot_json.py).

subject: hax
title: Bash commands outliving their foreground window are adopted into a task registry owning the process tree, a drainer thread, a spool file, and a per-task cursor of what the model has already seen; completion notes inject at the earliest loop seams
evidence: src/tools/task_registry.h:8-30 (adoption contract), src/tools/task_registry.h:44-58 (task_wait_stream with kill escalation SIGTERM-grace-SIGKILL), src/agent_loop.c:292-300 (task_collect_notes delivered before the request is built)
one_why: Turn-start note injection plus a delivery cursor means long builds never block the loop and the model never re-reads output it has seen -- no other subject has an adoption (rather than launch) model for background work.

subject: hax
title: Append-only versioned JSONL journal where /undo appends a cut record instead of truncating, files flush per newline for tail -f, and torn final lines after a crash are repaired on resume with a test
evidence: docs/sessions.md:22-24 ('append-only and flushed at each newline ... /undo appends a record rather than truncating'), tests/test_session.c:505-529 (test_resume_repairs_torn_final_line), tests/test_session.c:389-402 (resume appends only new items)
one_why: Undo-as-journal-entry (not file rewrite) keeps the same bytes a third-party tail saw, and the crash contract is stated for readers ('skip lines that do not parse') then tested -- nuance on the seeded journal id centered on append-only undo semantics.

subject: hax
title: A philosophy doc answering 'why not X' for each shipped-elsewhere feature (MCP, hooks, permission prompts, slash commands, deps), including an explicit statement of what the design cannot express
evidence: docs/philosophy.md:39-113; honest-gap line at :47-72 ('What outside scripts cannot express is in-turn interception ... hax omits that deliberately rather than claiming a substitute')
one_why: The written answer converts scope-minimalism from a README claim into a reviewable design record, and the admission of the uncovered gap (no veto/rewrite between tool call and next request) is what keeps it honest rather than marketing.

subject: hotdog
title: Per-session CSPRNG aliasing of every protected wire marker: tool-call/thinking/summary tags, WireFormat-owned names, and model control tokens are rewritten to random m_<16-char> aliases before the model ever sees them, so untrusted text cannot forge a tool call or harness message even when it guesses the real tag name
evidence: src/core/marker-mangler.ts:16-46 (protected list, unbiased alias generation), src/core/llm-client/serialize.ts:61-98 (escape at wire incl. tool-call name/args), :110-112 (provenance decides trust: only system/harness exempt)
one_why: Injection defense structural rather than screening: the model never observes the real marker bytes, so a poisoned file quoting  or <tool_call> matches nothing; aliases are unescaped once on assembled stream output so deltas can't fossilize them (src/core/agent.ts:744-756); tests include alias-fossil and mangler-union suites.

subject: hotdog
title: Two-arm spoof defense: the mangler protects the model's eyes, spoof.ts protects the human's - bidi overrides/isolates, zero-widths, C0/C1, BOM become visible counted [U+XXXX] tokens at every human render boundary (approval prompts, tool display, webui), never at storage
evidence: src/utils/spoof.ts:1-20 (invariant), :37-40 (codepoint set), :56-67; choke points src/extensions/user-gate/index.ts:108, src/extensions/ui-interactive-cli/index.ts, src/extensions/webui/ui/utils.ts, src/utils/cli/cli.ts; tests tests/utils/spoof.test.ts, tests/extensions/user-gate.test.ts:87
one_why: The git-di<U+202E>ff class makes an approval prompt read differently from what runs; no other corpus subject neutralizes terminal control at display while keeping original bytes in the audit log; counting (not stripping) makes presence itself the alert.

subject: hotdog
title: Machine-wide provider-concurrency as a filesystem counting semaphore: atomic exclusive-create slots, rename-onto reclaim with read-back, mtime heartbeat leases provable from any host, WeakRef missed-release watchdog, and a capped phantom lane so unplaced traffic cannot bypass caps
evidence: src/core/session/lane-ledger.ts:1-60 (protocol incl. argued residual race), src/core/session/model-resolver.ts:56-80 (bare-name lane conservatism), src/core/session/turn-lanes.ts:1-30 (top-level turns hold the same slots, incl. mid-turn question holds), tests/core/lane-ledger.test.ts, lane-unplaced-capacity.test.ts
one_why: Local-first reality: an interactive session, a CLI workflow, and any other hotdog process hit the same llama.cpp endpoint; no other subject bounds subagent concurrency at machine scope with crash-reclaimable leases; deliberate fail-open on ledger FS errors prevents deadlock-by-state-dir.

subject: hotdog
title: Workflow runs journal state transitions to append-only run.jsonl, claim the run dir with a pid+host+heartbeat owner file (live-owner refusal, stale reclaim), and resume by reconciling completed claims against the filesystem (size+mtime freshness), reusing only what verifies
evidence: src/extensions/workflows/engine.ts:6-14 (design), :270-311 (claim + all-exit-path release), :1177+ (#resume workflow-name guard), tests/extensions/workflows-engine.test.ts:1095-1177 (reconcile validates/flags, resume reuses valid claims, refuses wrong workflow)
one_why: Crash recovery without a daemon: a killed run re-admits only unverified nodes, and double-driving is refused by liveness-checked ownership; this is the orchestrator this very field study runs on (t3-giant-review) - dogfooded durability at the same bar as codex journals.

subject: hotdog
title: Node acceptance is machine-checked: declared output files must exist and be fresh for the run, plus a <node>.verdict file whose first line is pass|fail|reject; an optional judge node re-gates with critique spliced verbatim into the producer's warm retry
evidence: src/extensions/workflows/engine.ts:662-700 (#evaluateGate freshness+verdict), :706-830 (#runJudge per-producer-attempt budget, deadlock-analyzed deps :540-560), :186-196 (spliced model-authored critique rides untrusted parts), tests workflows-engine.test.ts:325-346,805-1015
one_why: Converges with the validated-finish-gate cluster but adds the file-freshness claim (stale outputs from a prior run fail) and judge-verdict routing (reject vs fail selects retryOn buckets); a poisoned run-dir file cannot impersonate harness framing because splices are provenance-tagged.

subject: hotdog
title: Scheduler optimizes KV-cache warmth: spawn candidates are ordered by a cached llama-swap /running peek (loaded models beat all), gate-failed retries run as warm follow-up turns on the same parked session, and lane slots are held across mid-turn question waits so a swap cannot thrash the cache the user returns to
evidence: src/core/session/model-resolver.ts:11 ('cache warmth beats all'), :236 (warmSortCandidates), :426-455 (/running peeker, failures degrade), src/extensions/workflows/engine.ts:449-470 (warm retry comment 'KV cache stays warm'), src/core/session/turn-lanes.ts:12-15
one_why: pi warms caches; nobody else schedules a multi-model fleet around cache residency - on local hardware a cache miss is a minutes-scale stall, and CONTEXT.md:38 names cache invalidation 'can mean 20s vs 5m' as the critical perf concern the placement layer exists to serve.

subject: hotdog
title: Bash triage is a bail-based hand tokenizer, not a deny-list: tracks quoting at character level, segments on operators, follows cd, and BAILS to ask/deny on expansions, substitutions, globs, heredocs, eval/env/xargs, inline-code flags, find -exec - 'when it is unsure it asks'
evidence: src/utils/approvals/bash.ts:1-10 (scope statement incl. 'not a security boundary'), :52-146 (tokenizer bail rules), :210-229 (bail sets), src/extensions/user-gate/extension.json (default-deny: 'unverifiable is not allowed'), tests/utils/approvals/
one_why: Converges with the ferrum/kimi grammar-policy cluster without a parser dependency; the key soundness move is that every un-analyzable construct escalates rather than matches, and under default=deny a bail denies outright - the opposite polarity of the regex-denylist family.

subject: hotdog
title: Approvals are off by default: stock hotdog mediates no tool call - userGate.enabled=false means bash runs unconfirmed - and the always-on Workspace containment covers only file tools, so a single echo > ~/.ssh/x bypasses every default guard
evidence: src/extensions/user-gate/extension.json:10-14 (enabled default false), src/utils/approvals/bash.ts:9 ('Nothing below it enforces any boundaries'), src/utils/workspace.ts:285-355 (containment scope: file tools via resolveSafe only), src/core/tool-executor.ts:155-163 (gate pipeline exists but registers nothing when disabled)
one_why: This is why safety scores 5 and not the 6 of pi/cline/crush: their approval binds by default; hotdog's machinery is the best-tested fail-closed gate in the corpus (tests/extensions/user-gate.test.ts:245-388) and the honesty is exemplary, but real machinery + off-by-default is below the tested-approval rung, per the nanocoder precedent minus the deception.

subject: hotdog
title: Context-overflow rescue is LLM-free and self-guarding: on a provider overflow, trim drops the minimum that the same local estimate says fits; when the estimate itself lost the race, the blunt drop fires only if canCompact passes - so a misclassified overflow cannot silently eat a young session's history - then the single core retry ships the mutated params
evidence: src/extensions/compaction/index.ts:376-430 (PROVIDER_ERROR handler + canCompact gate comment), :400-410 (params.messages mutation), src/core/llm-client/retry.ts (isContextOverflowError)
one_why: The ladder deliberately avoids a summarize pass on a backend that just rejected a conversation-sized request; rung selection (trim vs drop) is decided by the very estimator that failed, with an explicit second-guess rule - converges with overflow-degradation-ladder with a novel misclassification guard.

subject: hotdog
title: Compaction trigger estimates the outgoing request at the session's wire size: tool-result parts are measured through the resolved WireFormat renderer, not at rest, so the projection approximates what the model actually receives including wrappers and mangling
evidence: src/extensions/compaction/utils.ts:63-70 (shouldCompact), :91-94 (estimatorFor renders parts via wire format), src/extensions/compaction/index.ts:357-362 (CONTEXT-hook trigger)
one_why: Same family as the x10 usage-measured cluster; the wire-size twist matters most on local backends where wrapper verbosity differs per format, and chars/4 stays honestly a heuristic with a documented misclassification guard in the overflow rung.

subject: hotdog
title: Tool-call/result pairing integrity is enforced at every truncation seam: finish_reason=length refuses to execute any call (args may be silently truncated) and synthesizes re-issue results for all of them; stopLoop mid-batch answers every stranded call; compaction boundaries back up over tool results so a kept window never starts orphaned
evidence: src/core/agent.ts:43-56,641-666 (length-stop + per-iteration cap), src/core/tool-executor.ts:93-106 (stopLoop skip-answers), src/extensions/compaction/utils.ts:42-58 + index.ts:174-183 (orphan safety net aborts compaction)
one_why: Strict OpenAI-compatible backends 400 a request containing an unanswered tool_call, so one truncation wedges the whole session; treating pairing as an invariant at every cut (including refusing unsafe execution rather than running truncated args) is the discipline most subjects rediscover via bricked histories.

subject: hotdog
title: tool-call-repair recovers local-model output: leaked Hermes/antml/chatML call markup in content or reasoning is grammar-parsed into real tool calls mid-loop, and a corrupt stored tool call (interrupt-truncated args that 400 every subsequent request) is dropped from history with one retry - unbricking the session
evidence: src/extensions/tool-call-repair/index.ts:1-14, grammar.ts:37-66 (Hermes/antml tag synonyms), src/core/agent.ts:329-339 (PROVIDER_ERROR one-retry repair seam)
one_why: Local backends leak template markup constantly; only the agent loop's own response is scanned (model-origin, not injection-origin), and the bricked-history path fixes the classic 'interrupted a hung call, session now permanently 400s' failure no cloud-first subject handles.

subject: hotdog
title: Zero runtime dependencies by construction with a written supply-chain posture: no install step, no build, no lifecycle hooks, bun.lock pins only @types/bun; the Bun runtime itself is named as the remaining trust boundary
evidence: package.json:5 ("dependencies":{}), docs/supply-chain.md:9-24, README.md:7-12
one_why: Strongest supply-chain posture in the corpus (stronger than any anchor); minor nuance: docs/supply-chain.md:3 says 'no published artifact' while package.json:26 carries publishConfig.provenance for an npm publish path - one of three minor doc drifts, not a capability gap.

subject: hotdog
title: Loop breaker over canonicalized call signatures: JSON args re-serialized with sorted keys so cosmetic variants share a hash, detecting consecutive repeats and strict ping-pong, escalating nudge -> stronger nudge -> stop at t/2t/3t with per-episode state reset when the tail stops looping
evidence: src/extensions/loop-detect/detector.ts:1-16,60-109, src/extensions/loop-detect/index.ts:6-15,106-112, tests/extensions/loop-detect.test.ts
one_why: Converges with crush's breaker (only anchor with one) and joins it in the corpus; the argument-canonicalization and level-ladder (intervene early and weakly before stopping) are the refinements worth counting toward convergence.

subject: hotdog
title: Loop driven in-process by programmable stream-event mocks plus an independent-oracle conformance tier: OpenAI wire-shape fixtures vendored from the official openai-openapi repo with declared derivation provenance ('never from hotdog output'), alongside MCP/SSE/retry-after conformance and golden-request suites
evidence: tests/mocks/llm.ts:1-14, tests/conformance/openai-wire-conformance.test.ts:1-10, tests/conformance/mcp-conformance.test.ts, tests/core/llm-client/golden-request.test.ts
one_why: The oracle-independence declaration is the differentiator vs the x33 faux-provider cluster: protocol assertions are checked against captured third-party fixtures rather than regenerated from the implementation's own output; still in-process only - no subprocess/PTY e2e of the real CLI, which keeps verification at 7.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Embedded offline-trained linear risk classifier scores every tool call in shadow mode by default, logging disagreements with the permission policy while blocking nothing
evidence: internal/risk/shadow.go:40-92; cmd/agent/risk.go:19,33-57; internal/risk/call.go:22-48; scripts/train_risk.py:1-30
one_why: Unlike gptme's deterministic shadow guardrail, the scorer is a real 768KB SGD model trained offline (stdlib-only Python, byte-reproducible, embedded via go:embed), on unless IPS_RISK=off because 'a signal nobody enables collects none'; per-workspace learned delta corrections live beside project state and are dropped if they no longer match the base model's positional labels; end-of-session stats line reports calls/flagged/disagreed so promotion to enforcement is a data decision, not a vibe decision.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Monthly model-retrain CI refuses to open its own PR if held-out precision/recall regresses >0.05, with cross-language feature parity pinned by shared hash constants
evidence: .github/workflows/risk-vocab.yml:20-27,70-95; .github/workflows/ci.yml:33-46; scripts/train_risk.py:20-30; internal/risk/features_test.go
one_why: The whole ML loop is offline and deterministic (vendored vocab, fixed python pin so 'byte-identical model.bin' is meaningful), the feature extractor is duplicated in Python and Go purely so no runtime dep ships, and the duplication is guarded both ways: HASH_VECTORS asserted against Go-produced values in the trainer, pinned again in Go tests; the refresh job can only propose - an automated retrain that can merge itself will one day ship a worse model.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Reflection-distilled pitfalls injected into tool-error results on error-pattern match, with a distinct 'avoid' kind for dead ends and generic-pattern guards
evidence: internal/knowledge/pitfall.go:12-44; internal/agent/agent.go:2238,2263-2284; internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:263; internal/agent/agent_test.go:336-440
one_why: Lessons are keyed (domain, error-pattern) and surface only in the failed tool result they match - not the system prompt - so a weak model isn't buried; a dead-end lesson renders differently ('this never works') because telling a model 'this worked: the thing that never worked' is worse than silence; five spec tests pin that hints never present a dead end as a fix, never cross actions sharing error text, and never surface generic 'exit N' patterns; age-based pruning via LastSeen keeps the store fresh.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: One-sample calibration of the 4-bytes/token estimate against the server's prompt_tokens measured on the as-sent request, clamped 0.5-4, with a trim pass that preserves the failure-signal lines
evidence: internal/agent/agent.go:592-616,632-688; internal/agent/agent_test.go:129-335
one_why: Nuance on mocode's usage-feedback trigger: instead of an EWMA, a single clamped ratio from the just-sent turn corrects the estimate, deliberately computed on messages-as-sent because dividing an old reading by the now-larger estimate produced a sub-1 ratio that shrank the number it was meant to correct (documented live blowout: 32.8k window went 5k->20k->44k because HTML tokenizes at half assumed density); trimming also keeps the exit-status + reason lines so mid-task trims don't erase the failure signal the lesson store later keys off.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Compaction keeps a deterministic verbatim actions-digest alongside the LLM prose recap, re-harvested by a shared marker so it survives N successive compactions
evidence: internal/agent/agent.go:473-557; internal/agent/agent_test.go:814,846
one_why: Caught live: a weak model's prose summary blurred 'go.mod already exists' and the next task re-ran the exact command that had always failed; so file-touch/command/failure records are appended after the model answers - no user focus steer can drop them - and the digest block is written with the same marker the next Compact's reader scans for, making the audit trail idempotent across repeated compaction; the FAILED-entry wording also warns against re-running unchanged while explicitly NOT forbidding re-verification after a fix.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Hard floor is argv-aware and wrapper-transparent; allow-globs require every chained segment to match and refuse command substitution and redirections; deny-globs re-checked after async approval
evidence: internal/policy/policy.go:114-157,160-212,234-249; internal/policy/policy_test.go:160,186,206,320; internal/tool/run.go:97-100
one_why: Beyond glob matching: 'xargs rm -rf' and 'env FOO=1 rm -rf' hit the floor because it looks through wrappers and is reorder-proof on recursive flags; an allow-glob never spans && chains (git * can't smuggle a second command), never auto-allows $(), backticks or redirections whose target the glob can't see; DeniedWrite is re-run against the freshly re-resolved path after an approval wait closes a symlink-swap TOCTOU; the secret-read floor (.env, *secret*) can't be disabled by config, and the jail chases dangling symlink targets with a chain-depth limit (tested).

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Goal ends only on explicit DONE, TTL expiry, or the user: judge verdicts of 'unclear' re-feed rather than end, and every give-up path (turn failure, stuck-stop, step exhaustion) gets a judge pass with a persisted gap note for resume
evidence: internal/agent/agent.go:1013-1044,1221-1237,1287-1300,1767-1810; internal/agent/agent.go:29-50
one_why: 'Silence is not acceptance' - a judge that can't answer (its own reasoning ate the output budget) had silently abandoned a goal with 254/255 returns unspent; the fix makes judgeDone the sole early terminator, treats unclear as more, and runs judgeOnGiveUp on all three give-up paths fed by a deterministic actionsDigest because the isolated judge call never sees the transcript; the judge's 'still missing' text persists into the standing goal with the run's Progressed flag so a later /goal go resumes with a real hint instead of amnesia.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Per-turn file+history checkpoints with unified-diff revert preview, but session-lifetime in-memory only - a crash loses all rewind state
evidence: cmd/agent/main.go:448-450; cmd/agent/rewind.go:14-60; cmd/agent/rewind_test.go
one_why: Preview-before-revert is the good part: the picker shows per-file restore/delete/toobig deltas plus the conversation-trim count computed against the checkpoint's history length; but unlike cline's git-stash checkpoints (anchor 8) nothing is persisted, and external-CLI sub-agent edits are explicitly outside rewind's view - honestly documented rather than silently missed.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Clean loop/product split undermined by cmd/agent/main.go at 5,981 LOC plus tui.go at 3,375 (and main_test.go at 9,469)
evidence: cmd/agent/main.go (5,981); cmd/agent/tui.go (3,375); cmd/agent/main_test.go (9,469)
one_why: Per the pi errata a >5k product-mode file docks architecture on both sides: the testable core (internal/agent over an interface) is genuinely well separated, but wiring, sessions, spawn planning, risk hookup, config commands and flags share one file, and the matching test god-file signals the same coupling at the test surface.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Kernel write-jail (Seatbelt / Landlock re-exec shim that fails CLOSED) sits under the policy engine and is tested on a real macOS runner - but ships default-off and auto-mode runs unconfined with only a warning
evidence: internal/sandbox/sandbox.go:60-86; internal/sandbox/wrap_linux.go:24-41,56-61,68-77; .github/workflows/ci.yml:60-68; internal/config/config.go:222-226; cmd/agent/main.go:2728-2729
one_why: Landlock restricts the calling process, so the wrapper re-execs the agent binary with a hidden __landlock-exec argv and self-confines before exec'ing the real command - and if the kernel probe misses on that leg it exits 126 rather than running free; network deny is ABI-gated with the offline flag as the primary gate; the docking point is the default: sandbox='off', and on kernels without Landlock, 'auto' logs a warn and runs unconfined, so containment-under-approval is opt-in.

subject: ipsupport-code
title: Whole-binary and whole-TUI e2e against httptest fake OpenAI providers, including a session-persist-across-restart test driven through teatest
evidence: internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:312-380; cmd/agent/tui_e2e_test.go:72,106,354-573; go.mod:15 (charmbracelet/x/exp/teatest)
one_why: Nuance on the seeded id: not just scripted chats at unit level - TestE2E_Binary builds and drives the real binary end-to-end, and the TUI specs assert stream rendering, no-race semantics between config reload/MCP connect and concurrent UI reads, and that the context meter reads the agent's main-turn figure rather than a side call's - UI and loop paths are covered, which the nanocoder anchor's 7 was docked for lacking.

subject: jazz
title: Four-rung context ladder (offload+clear 0.50 / warn 0.70 / LLM-compact 0.80 / trim 0.95) applied cheapest-first, with per-rung telemetry
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/context/context-window-manager.ts:21-41; packages/core/src/agent/execution/agent-loop.ts:1052-1105,1119-1125,1434-1440; packages/core/src/agent/context/summarizer.ts:76-97
