one_why: Trim is explicitly demoted to a floor keyed to 0.95 of the model window with a comment documenting the bug its old constant caused (trim preempting compaction and rewriting the cacheable prefix every turn); the clear rung persists large tool bodies to disk and can be delegated to a plugin keep/truncate/drop decision that falls back deterministically and never deletes a message.

subject: jazz
title: Every pressure nudge is an ephemeral request-only suffix; the prompt-cache breakpoint targets the last persisted message so nudges never move the cached prefix
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/execution/agent-loop.ts:1176-1201,231-252; packages/adapters/src/llm/ai-sdk-service.ts:521-523,550-565,366-369
one_why: Budget/context warnings exist on many agents but are persisted into history, spending tokens exactly when scarce and getting summarized into the compaction they warned about; jazz also adds a post-compaction counter-nudge that reverses its own wrap-up advice once space is freed, and accounts attachment aging-out as exactly one cache miss.

subject: jazz
title: Meltdown window measures uniqueness on name:arguments, plus a second mechanism: byte-identical read-only calls collapsed inside a single batch before anything executes
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/execution/agent-loop.ts:354-366,382-417,788-799; packages/core/src/agent/execution/agent-loop.test.ts:2219-2269,2283
one_why: Composite-key uniqueness keeps alternating productive tools (search->fetch->search-new-query) from tripping the 40% threshold, and in-batch dedupe catches the same-turn triple-read that a cross-turn window can only notice after paying for it; dedupe is gated on declared riskLevel read-only because two identical mutating calls may legitimately be two effects; the recovery message's placement invariant (after results, never between call and result) is directly tested.

subject: jazz
title: Capability boundary enforced at execution, not prompt: no effective tool set = refuse, hidden execute-half tools refused when the model names them, refusal returned as a model-actionable tool result
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/execution/tool-executor.ts:96-121,142-143,254,321-446; packages/core/src/agent/execution/tool-executor.test.ts:859-1060
one_why: Mutating tools are approval pairs (proposal + hidden execute half the model cannot call directly), 'always approve' is re-checked at dequeue so parallel grants apply, picker approvals are never auto-approved even under yolo, and the whole boundary has ~10 property tests including the adversarial 'model names the hidden tool directly' case.

subject: jazz
title: Single-token LLM command-risk classifier for execute_command with 8s/16-token budget, fail-closed to high-risk, overridable by a plugin hook that is denied escalation authority
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/tools/command-risk.ts:29-45,49-68,73-82; packages/core/src/agent/execution/tool-executor.ts:347-375; docs/security/threat-model.md:34-40
one_why: Only an exact 'read-only'/'low-risk' token lowers risk; timeouts, errors and ambiguity stay high-risk; conversation evidence is withheld when the approver isn't the conversation author (bot bridges); the docs explicitly bound the plugin hook - it can lower a verdict but cannot expand the tool set, override allowlists, the tier, or the shell denylist.

subject: jazz
title: Parking: a run blocked on approval persists transcript + pending tool calls + TTL as a durable record answerable from another process, and resume finishes the parked tool call before iterating
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/run/run-recorder.ts:29-60; packages/core/src/agent/execution/agent-loop.ts:1573-1590,617-640; packages/core/src/agent/run/park-resume.integration.test.ts; docs/concepts/daemon.md:51-52
one_why: Multi-surface reality (bot, webhook, unattended) means the approver is often in a different process; parking refuses to fire mid multi-call batch because replaying siblings would repeat their effects, failed turns hand their transcript to the caller before unwinding, and a parked run's tool call stays unanswered so resume is exactly-once - integration-tested across the process boundary.

subject: jazz
title: External doors (peers, webhooks) share one authorization model: a disclosure tier intersects the toolset down, and anything riskier than read-only must be named per caller
evidence: packages/core/src/types/disclosure-tier.ts:1-50; packages/adapters/src/daemon/webhook-authorization.test.ts; packages/adapters/src/daemon/token.test.ts
one_why: Because enforcement is toolset intersection rather than runtime approval, an injected payload at an external door is never even offered a way out - and the read-what-you-may-learn axis (none/public/internal/private) is kept deliberately separate from the may-act axis so raising disclosure cannot silently grant mutation; no other corpus subject models peer/webhook entry this way.

subject: jazz
title: Strong eval harness (pass@1/Pass^k, A/B attribution, cost guardrails, ambient-LSP and memory-journey acceptance tasks) is not wired into any CI workflow
evidence: evals/runner.ts:19-42; evals/README.md; .github/workflows/ci.yml (no evals step); grep of all workflows for 'evals' returns nothing
one_why: The harness already isolates a private JAZZ_HOME per rollout and gates cost, so a nightly scheduled job on the free-model SUT would catch harness regressions the unit tests cannot; this is the one rung separating jazz's verification from the anchors' observed ceiling of 8.

subject: jazz
title: ask_peer forces the outbound question through a single string parameter and types the reply as a quotation, not a fact
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/tools/peer.ts:1-15,36-40
one_why: The egress control is structural: a model left to compose a request volunteers calendar/personal context into a body nobody reads, so the parameter shape is the whole reason this is a tool rather than an http_request; the reply gets web_fetch-grade framing because 'Sam's agent says X' and 'X' are different claims.

subject: keen-code
title: TurnMemory: future-turn history carries placement-tagged tool ACTIVITY records, not results - raw outputs are json:"-" excluded and survive only in-session under /tool-history full
evidence: internal/llm/core/message.go:19-32; internal/llm/tool_execution.go:17-31,146; docs/turn-memory.md:52-58
one_why: A fourth state layer between the provider-native active loop and the session transcript: cross-turn projection keeps 'what ran, where in the prose, did it succeed' and drops stale contents by default, with a user-visible opt-in for full retention - closest cousin is memcode's thrash-aware-tool-eviction (reactive dedup) but this is a structural projection layer, not an eviction policy

subject: keen-code
title: Ephemeral breakpoints at stable-prefix end AND last message, and mode switches never change the tool-definition prefix: plan-mode denial wraps tools instead of removing them
evidence: internal/llm/anthropic.go:228-257; internal/llm/tool_execution.go:90-104; internal/appstate/state.go:188-190,229
one_why: The denyWriteToolRegistry trick keeps tool definitions byte-stable across build/plan mode toggles purely to preserve cache hits - most subjects re-send a changed tool list on mode switch and silently bust the cache

subject: keen-code
title: Auto-compact trigger estimates tokens of the ACTUAL serialized outgoing request (json.Marshal of provider params) at 90% of input budget, mid-tool-loop, and the compaction call is user-cancellable mid-flight
evidence: internal/llm/anthropic.go:593-644; internal/llm/core/context.go:30-35; internal/llm/auto_compaction.go:13-54
one_why: Nuance on zot's measured-input trigger: keen re-serializes the pending request per loop iteration rather than reusing last-turn reported usage, and exposes a Cancel handle on the AutoCompactionEvent so a runaway summarize is interruptable; replacement is transactional (empty-summary and incomplete-stream rejected, tested at auto_compaction_test.go:63,90)

subject: keen-code
title: Each connected MCP server auto-generates a managed skill (mcp:<server>) containing a tool table; full JSON schemas load on demand - no tool-search-tool needed
evidence: internal/mcpskills/mcpskills.go:15-49,51-63; docs/mcp-skills.md
one_why: Converges with crab-code's prompt-to-skill conversion and the lazy-tool-catalog intent (forge-norvialabs), but keen's unit is the whole server's TOOL catalog expressed as ordinary skill docs, reusing the skills loader rather than adding a catalog mechanism

subject: keen-code
title: Guard: system-path denylist + blanket block of every $HOME dotfile + gitignored paths, with per-agent artifact allow-dirs that explicitly reject symlinks via Lstat
evidence: internal/filesystem/guard.go:31-41,44-79,117-133,155-186
one_why: Component-safe prefix checks on cleaned absolute paths (no sibling-prefix escape like claii's), and the IsInKeenBashDir/MCPArtifactsDir/WebFetchArtifactsDir allow-dirs refuse to trust paths whose final component is a symlink - a small hardening most prefix-based guards skip

subject: keen-code
title: Five-step approval ladder (yolo -> headless autoApprove -> project allow -> session allow -> prompt) where 'allow session' deliberately never sticks to dangerous commands, but the project allow-list can skip even the dangerous-bash prompt
evidence: internal/cli/repl/permissions/requester.go:64-101,112-119; docs/permission-system.md (lookup order + yolo section); internal/tools/bash.go:156
one_why: The session-scope anti-sticky rule for dangerous actions is a good least-privilege default; its mirror is the foot-gun: allow:["bash"] in .keen/permissions.json also mutes the danger prompt - documented honestly in permission-system.md, which itself earns the honesty credit

subject: keen-code
title: /adversary: user-launched second-model reviewer on a SEPARATE provider client whose tool registry is stripped of write_file/edit_file/bash/call_mcp_tool/delegate_task
evidence: internal/appstate/state.go:259-283; internal/agentcore/adapter.go:67-76; docs/cli-usage.md
one_why: No pool/prewarm (contrast codex guardian_review.rs) - on-demand instead - but the enforcement is registry intersection, so the reviewer physically cannot mutate anything regardless of what its model decides

subject: keen-code
title: /btw side-question runs a tool-less one-shot over a last-10-message window alongside the main stream, bypassing the 5-item input queue
evidence: internal/appstate/state.go:243-258; internal/appstate/state.go:288-303 btwContext; docs/queuing.md (btw row)
one_why: Same shape as kimi-code's btw feature - convergent design; keen's nuance is the bounded history slice (btwContext trims the trailing user msg, keeps 10) so side questions never serialize behind busy turns or pollute main history

subject: keen-code
title: The tool-loop scaffold (maxToolTurns loop, proactive-compaction hook, incomplete-exit, pending-state injection) is re-implemented in all six provider clients
evidence: internal/llm/anthropic.go:673; bedrock.go:277; openai.go:516; genkit.go:26; openai_responses.go:214; openai_codex.go:81
one_why: tool_execution.go, auto_compaction.go and the compaction package prove the shared seam exists, yet each client copies the control flow around it - six places to fix any loop-semantics bug; protocol differences justify provider encoding, not loop duplication

subject: keen-code
title: Dangerous-bash classifier is segment- and subshell-aware (splits pipelines, extracts $(...), flags privilege escalation and secret-exposure env reads like cat $AWS_SECRET) rather than a flat regex list
evidence: internal/tools/bashclassifier.go:10-79,84-120
one_why: Stronger convergent variant of the regex-denylist family (nanocoder, bash-ast-rule-matching subjects), including a secret-exposure dimension few denylists have - still fundamentally bypassable (find -delete, interpreter-mediated writes) and should be read as prompt-elevation for the approval UI, not enforcement

subject: keen-code
title: GA4 session start/end telemetry is on by default at build time, with opt-out only via KEEN_TELEMETRY / DO_NOT_TRACK / CI env vars
evidence: internal/telemetry/telemetry.go:81-92; cmd/main.go:17-20,38-46
one_why: Payload is minimal (session start/end, version, OS, random client ID persisted in ~/.keen/state.json) and honors DO_NOT_TRACK, but a solo OSS coding agent phoning home by default is still a posture note users should find themselves

subject: kimi-cli
title: D-Mail: the model folds its own context by reverting to a named checkpoint with a model-authored payload, at zero LLM cost
evidence: src/kimi_cli/tools/dmail/dmail.md; src/kimi_cli/soul/denwarenji.py; src/kimi_cli/soul/kimisoul.py:1315-1335 (BackToTheFuture), :1100-1105 (revert+recheckpoint); src/kimi_cli/soul/context.py:137-190 (revert_to with journal rotation)
one_why: Second compaction tier that needs no summarizer call: agent rewrites its own history at a step where it notices waste (huge file read, dead-end debugging), and the tool text is explicitly honest that filesystem state is NOT reverted -- unlike pi's branch summaries this is agent-initiated, not system-initiated.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Graduated repeat-call ladder (reminders at 3/5/8, hard turn-stop at 12) plus same-step dedup that awaits the original task and copies its result
evidence: src/kimi_cli/soul/toolset.py:117-167 (ladder), :176-199 (canonical-JSON arg keys), :370-375 (same-step await-and-copy), :430-452; src/kimi_cli/soul/kimisoul.py:1330-1337 (force_stop_turn); tests/core/test_kimisoul_repeat.py
one_why: Most complete loop breaker found: streaks survive across steps via canonicalized args, escalation is prompt-side before the circuit trips, and parallel identical calls within one step are collapsed instead of double-executed -- crush's breaker is a single-shot abort by comparison.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Agent flows declared as D2/Mermaid fenced blocks in SKILL.md, parsed into task/decision graphs; the ralph loop is just a synthesized 2-node flow
evidence: src/kimi_cli/skill/__init__.py:645-660; src/kimi_cli/skill/flow/d2.py, mermaid.py; src/kimi_cli/soul/kimisoul.py:1787-1845 (FlowRunner.ralph_loop), :1862-1963 (edge-choice execution + re-prompt); klips/klip-10-agent-flow.md
one_why: Deterministic multi-turn control flow that end users can author as pictures; decision nodes re-prompt on invalid <choice> instead of crashing, and the notorious ralph-loop is expressed as data (BEGIN->R1->R2 self-loop->END) rather than a separate runner.

subject: kimi-cli
title: ChaosChatProvider: a fault-injection decorator wrapping any real provider, deterministic-configured, used to test retry/recovery paths in the live loop
evidence: packages/kosong/src/kosong/chat_provider/chaos.py:115; tests/core/test_kimisoul_completion_budget.py:260,305; kosong echo scripted-DSL provider (chat_provider/echo/dsl.py) + mock.py; tests/core/test_kimisoul_retry_recovery.py
one_why: Beyond scripted responses: transient-connection/auth failures are injected into a real Kimi provider and the test asserts the loop's 401-refresh-once / connection-recovery-once ladder (kimisoul.py:1657-1730) actually unwinds correctly.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Approvals are action-name session-cached and ContextVar-sourced: approving an action retroactively resolves same-action pending requests, and turn end cancels orphaned approvals
evidence: src/kimi_cli/soul/approval.py:200,354-366; src/kimi_cli/approval_runtime/runtime.py:171-194 (cancel_by_source), multi-waiter refcounting :96-140; kimisoul.py:673-676,812-817
one_why: Approval identity travels with the execution context (foreground turn vs subagent), so backgrounded work can surface approvals on the root wire hub without leaking them past the turn that created them; feedback-aware rejections get anti-bypass instruction text for subagents (approval.py:76-100).

subject: kimi-cli
title: All fs+exec tools go through a kaos backend interface with local, SSH, and ACP-host implementations -- in ACP mode the agent's shell and file tools run on the IDE host's terminal APIs
evidence: packages/kaos/src/kaos/local.py, ssh.py:61,276; src/kimi_cli/acp/kaos.py:44-165 (ACPProcess over terminal_create/wait/output), :165-259; src/kimi_cli/acp/session.py:159 (set_current_kaos); klips/klip-2-acpkaos.md
one_why: The whole tool surface is host-agnostic by construction: the same Shell/Read/Write tools transparently execute in an SSH box or inside the editor's own terminal/filesystem bridge, which no other reviewed subject does -- rival IDE integrations re-implement tools per surface.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Background tasks run as detached worker processes with heartbeats, control-file polling, stale reconciliation, and Windows process-tree kill
evidence: src/kimi_cli/background/worker.py:21-40; src/kimi_cli/background/manager.py:422-483 (stale_after, reconcile); background/store.py; kimisoul.py:1131-1146 (notification injection with pre-delivery reconcile); tests/core/test_background_agent_kill.py
one_why: Crash-aware durability for bg bash+agent tasks: after a CLI restart, reconcile() marks orphaned workers stale before notifications are claimed, so the model never waits on a phantom task -- amazon-q's delegate tool has the spawn half but none of the reconciliation half.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Two cooperating JSONL journals: versioned wire.jsonl (protocol-versioned envelope header) for UI replay and context.jsonl with inline _checkpoint/_usage markers that turn-aware truncation slices for /undo and /fork
evidence: src/kimi_cli/wire/file.py:19-30; src/kimi_cli/soul/context.py:124-135,271-340 (marker records, tolerant replay); src/kimi_cli/session_fork.py:1-30; tests_e2e/test_wire_sessions.py; tests/core/test_session_fork.py
one_why: Token accounting is embedded in the journal itself (_usage records reset the pending-estimate on restore) so crash-resume reconstructs near-exact context usage, and malformed lines are skipped rather than failing the load -- the journal doubles as the compaction trigger's source of truth.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Four host contracts off one soul: single+multi-session ACP server, versioned wire JSON-RPC with host-provided external tools, stream-json headless, and an OpenAPI web backend -- and kimi term dogfoods its own ACP server
evidence: src/kimi_cli/acp/AGENTS.md:13-49; src/kimi_cli/wire/server.py:26-33 (HookRequest/ToolCallRequest); KLIP-12 (klips/klip-12-wire-initialize-external-tools.md); docs/en/reference/kimi-term.md:9-13; docs/en/reference/kimi-command.md:98-106; sdks/kimi-sdk + .github/workflows/release-kimi-sdk.yml
one_why: External hosts can inject their own tools mid-turn (KLIP-12) and receive hook callbacks over the wire -- nanocoder proved ACP dogfooding for one plugin; kimi-cli spread the same event stream across four contracts plus a published SDK.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Hooks exist with the full Claude-shaped event vocabulary but can only come from the global config file, so a cloned repo cannot plant hook commands
evidence: src/kimi_cli/config.py:276-278 (get_config_file = share dir only); src/kimi_cli/hooks/config.py:5-19; src/kimi_cli/hooks/runner.py:78-81 (permissionDecision deny); src/kimi_cli/hooks/engine.py:244-246 (PreToolUse block is fail-closed)
one_why: Not advertised as a security feature, but the config-scoping accident means repo-borne hook RCE -- the hole several rivals have -- is structurally absent; PreToolUse denial is honored before the approval prompt and telemetry failure cannot downgrade the block.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Canonicalized workspace containment on read/glob with an explicit /add-dir escape hatch persisted in session state, and a distinct approval action for edits outside the workspace
evidence: src/kimi_cli/tools/file/read.py:86-94; glob.py:87-101; tools/file/__init__.py:13 (edit-file-outside action); src/kimi_cli/soul/agent.py:243-261 (prune stale additional_dirs on restore); tests/test_additional_dirs_state.py
one_why: Containment is canonical-path based (no sibling-prefix escape), out-of-workspace edits are not silently allowed but mapped to their own approval action name -- so per-action session caching degrades to least-privilege by default.

subject: kimi-cli
title: Graceful sunset engineering: final releases convert the CLI's own entry points into a redirector that downloads and runs the successor's installer, plus a tested tombstone package
evidence: CHANGELOG.md 1.51.0/1.52.0 entries ('Running kimi with no arguments now directly downloads and runs the Kimi Code install script'); HEAD commit 9ab1286 'short-circuit entry points to a Kimi Code installer (#2666)'; packages/kimi-code/src/kimi_code/__init__.py; tests/core/test_kimi_code_tombstone.py; SECURITY.md:1
one_why: A field template for killing a live product: no-fix SECURITY banner, tombstone package that prints migration instructions and exits 1, and the binary itself funnels stragglers to the successor -- archived:true remote-verified, which is also why this review's band is capped at B by rule (b).

subject: kimi-code
title: Composable first-match permission policy chain evaluated in the executor's before-tool hook
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/permissionPolicy/permissionPolicyService.ts:39-57; permissionGate/permissionGateService.ts:30,40-63
one_why: 13 named policies (user deny/ask/allow, dangerous-command, sensitive-file, git-path, session-history, yolo, fallback-ask) resolve in explicit constructor order, each emitting telemetry with the winning policy name; easy to adopt wholesale and far more debuggable than one monolithic canUseTool.

subject: kimi-code
title: Dangerous-command detection over a tree-sitter-bash AST, not regex
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/permissionPolicy/policies/dangerous-command-ask.ts:15-50; packages/tree-sitter-bash/
one_why: Inverts the corpus's regex-denylist anti-pattern: parses the command via a real grammar with nested-shell depth cap (4), unsafe-operand bail-out, and sudo/doas wrapper unwrapping before deciding ask; the grammar ships as its own package with tests.

subject: kimi-code
title: No OS-level sandbox: approved tools execute with full user privileges
evidence: repo-wide grep for seatbelt/sandbox-exec/bwrap/landlock/seccomp in src: zero hits (only pi-tui/src/terminal.ts false positive)
one_why: Approval is the entire enforcement story; a prompt-injected but approved command, or any allow-rule hit, runs unconfined - codex-tier safety needs a kernel layer under this otherwise strong gate.

subject: kimi-code
title: Dangerous-command guard silently dropped in non-interactive mode
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/permissionPolicy/permissionPolicyService.ts:42-44
one_why: bootstrap.args.nonInteractive splices DangerousCommandAsk out of the chain, so headless runs where the user configured allow-rules lose the extra dangerous-command check with no deny/fallback of its own (mitigated somewhat by fallback-ask and the --prompt/--yolo conflict, cli/options.ts:79-80).

subject: kimi-code
title: Graduated repeat breaker: reminders at streak 3/5/8, hard force-stop at 12
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/toolDedupe/toolDedupeService.ts:63-66,536-550; test/agent/toolDedupe/toolDedupe.test.ts
one_why: Stronger than crush's binary breaker: escalating in-result reminders then a terminal force-stop result that refuses further tool calls for the step, with dedup of identical parallel calls in the same step folded into the same streak accounting.

subject: kimi-code
title: Agent state is a replayable event fold with undoable keys and journal repair migrations
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/src/state/eventDispatcherService.ts:169-267,564-594; src/wire/repair.ts:20-29; test/wire/resume.test.ts; test/wire/migration/
one_why: Session resume, conversation undo, and permission-mode history all fall out of one replayable/undoable state model over a repairable wire journal - the deepest state model in the corpus after codex's rollout journals, and tested across migrations.

subject: kimi-code
title: Fork governance: UPSTREAM.md intent cards pin the vendor delta against a fixed upstream commit
evidence: packages/pi-tui/UPSTREAM.md:1-60 (Last Sync Point 53816d7dcc5ebe3a0eedec3cd07196c3a66d83fd + keep/absorbed intent cards)
one_why: A reusable recipe for carrying a vendored upstream library: every local behavior change must map to an intent card that says why it cannot live in the app, and the fork must reconstruct cleanly against the pinned upstream ref - worth copying for any vendor decision, license-independent.

subject: kimi-code
title: minidb: pure-Node embedded KV store (WAL group-commit, skip-list indexes, torn-tail truncation) backing agent persistence
evidence: packages/minidb/README.md:8-30; packages/minidb/src/mini-db.ts (1470 LOC); test coverage 15k LOC
one_why: Zero-native-addons durable store (Redis AOF policies + SQLite WAL ideas) so sessions/tasks survive crashes without shipping sqlite natives; crash-torn tails are CRC-detected and truncated on recovery.

subject: kimi-code
title: AGENTS.md late-reminder and instruction drift injection
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/agentsMdReminder/agentsMdReminderService.ts:355,363
one_why: Instead of eagerly stuffing every nested AGENTS.md into the prompt, kimi detects instruction files applying to paths a tool call just touched and queues a reminder - and re-flags files that changed on disk after injection; solves both token economy and stale-instruction correctness.

subject: kimi-code
title: btw: side-question agent on a lightweight instance, read-only tools, tool defs kept visible to preserve prompt cache
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/src/features/btw/btw.ts:3-20
one_why: Users can ask side questions without interrupting the running turn; disabled tool definitions are deliberately retained in the request because removing them would break the provider prompt cache - explicit cache-aware prompt construction, rare in the corpus.

subject: kimi-code
title: Scripted streaming provider harness drives loop, compaction, and permission tests
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/test/harness/scripted-generate.ts; test/agent/loop/loop.test.ts (61 it); test/agent/fullCompaction/fullCompaction.test.ts (95 it)
one_why: A fake generate() that emits real stream part sequences (text/think/tool_call_part with stream indices) lets ~16.7k tests exercise full turn semantics offline across the whole monorepo - the strongest faux-provider corpus found after codex's mock SSE suites.

subject: kimi-code
title: 357k LOC of tests and 9 workflows, but zero model evals or fuzz targets
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-160 (build/smoke, 5-shard vitest, lint, tsgo; grep 'eval' across workflows: no matches); Windows matrix disabled at :93
one_why: Shares the corpus-wide verification ceiling: nothing measures model-behavior quality (compaction fidelity, loop-breaker effectiveness against real trajectories), so model/prompt regressions ship silently.

subject: kode-cli
title: Anthropic-internal USER_TYPE branches ('ant', 'SWE_BENCH') in readable TypeScript prove Claude-Code-internals origin, contradicting the cline-lineage lore
evidence: packages/core/src/engine/query-executor.ts:22 (process.env.USER_TYPE !== 'ant' gates dual-response binary feedback); packages/core/src/ai/llm/anthropic/client.ts:97; packages/core/src/ai/llm/retry.ts:5,49 (USER_TYPE === 'SWE_BENCH'); packages/core/src/logging/log/jsonLog.ts:173
one_why: No public bundle or independent clean room needs env branches on Anthropic's internal user-type values; combined with claude-shaped internals (canUseTool, ToolUseQueue barrier, PreToolUse permissionDecision) the v1 codebase almost certainly descends from deobfuscated Claude-Code source (the org's anon-kode route) -- the repo's self-granted Apache-2.0 cannot clear that origin, so treat all portables from this subject as concepts-only until provenance is clarified.

subject: kode-cli
title: Two-tier compaction: disk-offload micro-compact of stale tool results, then snapshot-enriched auto-compact with a fit-aware compression-model fallback
evidence: packages/core/src/utils/microCompactCore.ts:19-22,306-360 (persist old tool_results to disk keeping 400-char refs, keep last 3, fire only when >=20k tokens saved past the warning margin); packages/core/src/utils/autoCompactCore.ts:215-241 (task/skills/MCP/plan-file snapshots inside the summarization prompt), :251-276 (use 'compact' model unless its 90%-context budget can't fit history, else fall back to 'main'), :333-355 (compaction boundary + summary persisted as JSONL record for resume)
one_why: Nuance vs deepagents' reversible-offload tier: the offload is disk-backed with preview refs and a minimum-savings gate so it never churns small results, and the summarizer itself is told which model will have to read the summary -- neither appears in cline's or gptme's tiers.

subject: kode-cli
title: Regex data-loss classifier promotes suspicious Bash commands to a quick-model LLM reviewer; gate failure fails closed only when the command would run unsandboxed
evidence: packages/tools/src/tools/system/BashTool/call.tsx:131-203 (getBashGateFindings -> needsLlmGate -> runBashLlmSafetyGate; on gate error block unless canFailOpen, computed from willSandbox); packages/tools/src/tools/system/BashTool/dataLossRules.ts:355 + 14-category SimpleRule set; packages/tools/src/tools/system/BashTool/llmSafetyGate.ts:138-180 (purpose-built single system prompt, 'quick' model pointer, 300s timeout, </final> stop sequence)
one_why: Because the gate lives in the Bash tool call rather than the permission engine, it still fires under YOLO auto-approval -- a floor that survives the product's own worst default; and tying fail-open to sandbox state makes the two defenses compose instead of both being optional.

subject: kode-cli
title: Single permission chokepoint where deny-rules outrank YOLO and bypassPermissions keeps an explicit opt-out-only write-safety floor
evidence: packages/core/src/permissions/engine.ts:96-133 (bypassSafetyFloor requires KODE_BYPASS_SAFETY_FLOOR opt-in before skipping getWriteSafetyCheckForPath), :344-351 (yolo auto-approves only when shouldPromptUser !== false, so explicit denies still win); packages/core/src/test/unit/bypass-permissions-safety-floor.test.ts; packages/core/src/utils/permissionModeState.ts:7 (ACTUAL_DEFAULT_MODE = 'yolo')
one_why: Most yolo/bypass flags are pure boolean bypasses; kode's precedence ladder (explicit deny > mode auto-approve > safety floor unless env-renounced) is the pattern worth copying -- though the shipped default being yolo (README.md:46 discloses it plainly) is what caps this subject's safety score.

subject: kode-cli
title: YOLO is the factory default: fresh installs bypass all approval prompts; permission checks exist but must be opted into via --safe
evidence: packages/core/src/utils/permissionModeState.ts:7 (const ACTUAL_DEFAULT_MODE: PermissionMode = 'yolo'); README.md:46 ('runs in YOLO mode by default (equivalent to --dangerously-skip-permissions)... we strongly recommend kode --safe')
one_why: Nuance vs gptme's silent fail-open: kode's is loud and documented, and the LLM data-loss gate plus deny-rules give yolo a real floor -- but every unattended first run of the distributed product is still an unapproved shell, and no default mode plus per-feature opt-in can match codex's deny-by-default kernel posture.

subject: kode-cli
title: Trust gate covers only workspace MCP headersHelper; project-defined hooks spawn subprocesses with no trust decision
evidence: packages/core/src/mcp/client/connection.ts:121-124 (checkHasTrustDialogAccepted blocks headersHelper pre-trust); packages/core/src/hooks/executor.ts:31 (spawn(cmd[0], ...) with no trust check); grep -i trust over packages/core/src finds no other gate
one_why: A cloned repo whose .claude/settings.json defines a PreToolUse or SessionStart hook executes attacker-chosen commands on first open -- kode built the right gate (the MCP one) and left the wider hook surface ungated; claurst's fingerprint-keyed project-trust store is the missing piece.

subject: kode-cli
title: No scripted provider drives the loop in CI: provider integration tests silently skip without API keys and the shipped VCR harness has no committed fixtures
evidence: packages/core/src/test/integration/integration-cli-flow.test.ts:17-21 (test.skip when ACTIVE_PRODUCTION_MODELS empty); grep -rln mock.module packages/core/src/test => 2 files; packages/core/src/services/vcr.ts:14-56 (content-hash fixture VCR active under NODE_ENV=test) with no fixtures/ directory in repo
one_why: The unit corps proves permission and hook semantics well, but loop-level properties (approval-iff-policy, parallel tool ordering, compaction mid-loop) have no zero-network end-to-end assertion -- codex/cline/kimi-code's scripted-SSE harness is the ceiling kode is missing, and the half-built VCR shows intent without commitment.

subject: kode-cli
title: CI-enforced zone DAG with a reverse-edge ratchet that may shrink but never grow
evidence: scripts/check-architecture.mjs:12-40 (zone/alias registry), :42-46 ('Known reverse edges are listed separately and may shrink, but new exceptions must not appear unnoticed'); .github/workflows/ci.yml:42-43 ('Architecture boundaries' job step on every push, 3-OS matrix)
one_why: Stronger than openhands' single ban-test: it parses the TS AST against a declared allowed-edge map for nine zones and ratchets legacy violations downward, which is why an agent CLI with 145k LOC has no file over 863 lines and the loop stays host-agnostic.

subject: kode-cli
title: Priority-ranked cache_control allocation inside Anthropic's 4-breakpoint limit, stripping foreign cache markers before placement
evidence: packages/core/src/ai/llm/anthropic/cacheControl.ts:14-85 (system blocks >1000 chars first, then >2000-char documents and the tail block, then forced removal of pre-existing cache_control fields)
one_why: Solves the quiet 'more than 4 breakpoints => provider silently drops caching' failure that most subjects ignore, but placement is length-heuristic with no monotonicity invariant across turns -- unlike smelt's fuzzed cache-prefix stability, so it earns nuance, not a new pattern.

subject: kolega-code
title: license conflict is a census misread: BUSL-1.1 binds now; AGPL-3.0+ is only the post-2030 Change License
evidence: LICENSE:1 ('Business Source License 1.1'), LICENSE:27-29 (Change License AGPL-3.0-or-later, Change Date 2030-08-12), pyproject.toml:14 (license = "BUSL-1.1")
one_why: File and manifest agree - what binds is BUSL-1.1 per version until its change trigger (Change Date or 4y after that version's first distribution), after which that version converts to AGPL-3.0+; census 'AGPL-3.0 (file)' matched the Change-License line, so pipeline consumers must treat this repo as BUSL: concepts-only, clean-room, and even post-2030 copies inherit AGPL derivative obligations.

subject: kolega-code
title: resume matched by content cache_key, not position: replays survive script edits, pipeline order drift, and resume-of-resume
evidence: kolega_code/agent/orchestration/journal.py:18-27 (contract), :44+ (slug/artifacts), tests/agent/orchestration/test_orchestration.py:538-569 (replay/invalidate tests), runtime.py:33-50 (caps around it)
one_why: Nuance vs existing workflow-resume-journal portables: label/phase excluded from the key, same-key calls replay FIFO in issue order, and replays are re-recorded into the new journal so a resume of a resume is exact - the strongest resume identity semantics seen in the corpus; BUSL means clean-room reimplementation of the keying+drift-tolerance idea only.

subject: kolega-code
title: command allow-rules match whole command strings, so an executable/prefix grant admits everything chained after it
evidence: kolega_code/permissions.py:299-305 (exact / startswith(pattern+' ') / first-token match), agent/tool_backend/terminal_tool.py:497-503 (create_subprocess_shell shell=True), default check-off at terminal_tool.py:66
one_why: A persisted 'allow git' rule also passes 'git status && curl evil' because no shell-metacharacter split or per-sub-command approval exists; fails closed on callback errors (baseagent.py:1491-1510) and ASK is the default, so exposure is bounded to user-created rules - converge with the grammar-parsed-bash-policy cluster: rules must parse to per-atom commands to be a grant with meaning.

subject: kolega-code
title: persistent per-session Python/JS eval kernels with an in-kernel tool bridge back through the agent's permission-gated tool path
evidence: kolega_code/agent/eval/kernel.py:1-11 (NDJSON protocol, thread-keyed kernel registry, 'in-kernel tool.<name>(args) calls route through that agent's standard tool path'), permissions.py:33-38 ('eval' in COMMAND_PERMISSION_TOOLS)
one_why: Unlike codex's v8 code-mode, kernel state survives cells, tool calls, and sub-agent dispatches, and code inside the kernel calls tools through the same approval gate as the loop - the bridge keeps the permission model intact instead of bypassing it; kernel itself runs on host, so it inherits the no-OS-sandbox ceiling.

subject: kolega-code
title: skill catalog metadata budgeted as a percentage of the context window with a truncation report instead of silent overflow
evidence: kolega_code/cli/skills.py:33 (SKILL_METADATA_CONTEXT_WINDOW_PERCENT=2), :48-57 (budget from context window), :125-140 (render with report), :199-203 (normalized budget)
one_why: Fixes the scaling hole in fixed-char skill catalogs: on a 32k-context model the catalog can't eat the same tokens as on a 200k one, and when skills are dropped the model is told, so it can ask for the remainder - clean-room-portable budget formula + honesty report.

subject: kolega-code
title: test fake that enforces the production context-budget check inside stream(), reproducing the compaction-request-rejected failure mode
evidence: tests/agent/test_compaction_request_budget.py:1-15 (failure-mode docstring), :55-60 (BudgetEnforcingFakeLLM mirrors LLMClient._enforce_run_context_budget)
one_why: The fake plays the provider renderer on both the gauge path and the enforcement path exactly as production routes them, so the regression (an unfittable compaction request reads as llm_error and permanently disables auto-compaction) fails CI - the pattern 'fake must enforce, not just answer' generalizes beyond compaction.

subject: kolega-code
title: the compaction request itself fits a descending budget ladder with tool-pair-safe middle omission and stall detection
evidence: kolega_code/agent/compression.py:196-203 (why ladder exists), :92-106 (_middle_gap half-head/half-tail), :240-280 (widen_gap_until_fits + snap), :284-303 (rungs 100%->...->10%, no identical re-dispatch)
one_why: Nuance on the overflow-ladder cluster: most subjects degrade the main request but send the summarization request unbounded - at the trigger point it is ~parent-context-sized, so its own fit (omitting whole messages from the middle, never splitting a tool exchange, keeping half the budget for the task statement and half for recent continuity) is what makes auto-compaction robust instead of heroic.

subject: kolega-code
title: no repeated-action breaker in the main loop; guards cover model stalling (silent/truncated turns), runaways only bounded in workflows
evidence: kolega_code/agent/baseagent.py:171-177 (silent/truncated nudge caps), :218+:2571 (max_iterations optional, default None), orchestration/runtime.py:31-33 (DEFAULT_AGENT_CAP=1000 workflow-only backstop)
one_why: An unbounded main loop can burn tokens on repeated near-identical tool calls indefinitely - the silent-turn and truncation guards are about degenerate outputs, not repetition, and the 1000-agent cap lives only in gigacode; crush remains the reference for an in-loop breaker (loop_detection.go:11-40).

subject: kolega-code
title: optional LLM pre-exec shell-safety classifier that fails closed - but off by default
evidence: kolega_code/agent/tool_backend/terminal_tool.py:66 (security_check_enabled = False), :96-153 (fast-model classify, 'Command not executed. Could not verify safety' on any error)
one_why: The classifier's fail-closed-on-error posture is the part to note (every failure path returns not-executed), unlike phantom-safety-control subjects where the check vanishes on error; but default-off plus an unenforced rule layer keeps the whole safety stack at the tested-approval rung.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Subscription-limit continuity: durable pause, token-free lift probe, and mid-turn auto chain-walk across the user's own equivalents (vendor CLIs, gateway, local endpoints)
evidence: internal/engine/resume.go:15-49; internal/engine/agent.go:1455-1470; internal/continuity/pause.go; internal/engine/cooldowns.go; docs/plan/35-continuity.md
one_why: No other subject treats 'one of my four plans hit its cap mid-turn' as a first-class recoverable state: the pause persists in the session, a monitor confirms the lift without spending a token (key-status//models/sign-in checks), and auto mode resumes the pending turn on the next equivalent model - the whole failure mode every multi-subscription user hits is engineered around.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Three-stage sacrificial compaction (tool-results, then collapsed tool traffic, then summary) that stops at the first stage that fits, triggers only on provider-measured prompt tokens, and is undoable via on-disk archive
evidence: internal/engine/compact.go:13-18,61-105,202,205-207,257-291,374-385; internal/engine/context.go:20-58
one_why: Nuance vs seeded id and codex's tiers: the trigger refuses to fire on an unknown or guessed window (compacting on a guess is worse than a readable provider error), it compacts to half the window rather than to the threshold so the next turn does not re-trigger, and tool results are emptied-not-removed to keep call/result pairing provider-valid - plus RestoreCompaction and an archive path make the one lossy operation reversible.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Doom-loop guard keyed on identical call AND identical result bytes, with a 9-slot cycle window for alternating-call loops, checked before the repeat executes
evidence: internal/engine/doomloop.go:13-43,119-127; internal/engine/agent.go:1639-1651; internal/engine/doomloop_test.go:16-154
one_why: Best-reasoned loop detector in the corpus: success is the wrong discriminator (a test failing differently is progress; an identical successful read x3 is waste), fixed threshold that does NOT scale with effort (a bigger budget shouldn't buy longer stalls), and the window catches the remove-and-recreate alternation that resets consecutive counters - their own observed failure. crush remains the anchor but this refines the rule.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Floor-first ordering: hardline refusals bind every tier including full-auto, then user-written rules, then the tier; subagents convert Ask to Deny; 'always' answers land in the visible session rule list, never silently persisted
evidence: internal/engine/permission.go:78-118,126-186; internal/engine/agent.go:967-1041; docs/plan/13-tools-permissions-sandboxing.md
one_why: The ordering is the design and it is documented as such: 'full-auto stops asking, it does not stop refusing'. The subagent Ask->Deny rule (a child that cannot ask must not inherit ask-scoped autonomy, and the refusal names the switch that legitimately widens it) is directly portable to any subject with background agents; kept-rules going into /permissions rather than a private cache closes the 'always that outlived its session' hole.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Escape tests that only pass if the KERNEL refused: refusedByTheOS distinguishes kolk declining (exit -1), the pre-exec child guard (exit 125), and a real sandbox denial (platform refusal phrase)
evidence: internal/shell/sandbox_escape_test.go:13-75; internal/shell/sandbox.go:70-75; internal/shell/sandbox_darwin.go:31-46; .github/workflows/ci.yml (ubuntu+macos test matrix)
one_why: The corpus's sandbox claims mostly die at exactly this ambiguity: a test that asserts 'the command did not happen' passes when the wrapper merely skipped it. Kolkrabbi's fixture plants a credential canary and demands the platform's own refusal string, so pre-enforcer commits fail red; fail-closed everywhere else (Landlock ABI<4 network-deny refused not approximated, !darwin&&!linux refuses all sandboxed commands). Test-honesty pattern every jail claim in this study should adopt.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: mockagent: shell-script fake vendor CLIs that record received signals, proving the SIGINT->SIGTERM->SIGKILL spawn ladder rung-by-rung against deliberately uncooperative children
evidence: internal/mockagent/mockagent.go:1-40; internal/shell/ladder_test.go; internal/enginetest/{fakes.go,router.go}; cmd/kolk-mock/main.go
one_why: Signal escalation is untestable with stock tools - you need a child that traps SIGINT and one that exits on it, and an exit code cannot distinguish which rung fired, so the fake logs the signals it received. Scripts not binaries on purpose (no toolchain, no GOCACHE, seconds not minutes); the reasoning why SIGKILL-first invalidates a vendor session (destroys the result frame) is written down next to the proof.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Architecture as data with a no-escape-hatch ratchet: layer import rules, engine-purity ('the engine touches no OS'), naming, plus ~14 named CI gates; knownViolations fails on both add AND un-removed-fix
evidence: internal/arch/layers.go:1-32; Makefile:58-74; .github/workflows/ci.yml (arch, purity, buildtags, budgets, surface, spec, plan-check, workflow-pin-check)
one_why: Stronger than ouroboros's size ratchet and cline's docs: the ratchet list cannot rot because the test also fails when a listed violation has been fixed but not removed, violations are edited as reviewed data not suppress comments, and 'purity' means the core loop is OS-free by CI, not by convention - which is what makes the 0-god-file, 3-surface tree (tui/cli/serve) actually stay that way at bus factor 1.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Hardline command floor is word-list matching (sudo/mkfs/dd-of-dev/rm-rf-root/curl|sh/force-push) - bypassable by indirection, but explicitly labeled 'not a perimeter' with the jail named as the real control
evidence: internal/engine/permission.go:145-149,188-232; docs/plan/13-tools-permissions-sandboxing.md:106-108
one_why: Convergence entry for the corpus regex-denylist cluster (6 prior): the mechanism itself is the usual weak one ($(HOME) indirection, absolute-path dd, env splitting all slip past), but unlike claii-class subjects the code and docs state the ceiling in the same breath and route real enforcement to tiers + seatbelt/Landlock - the honest-framing half is the transferable artifact, and it pairs with aeon-9's permission-policy nuance.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: Effort as a cross-cutting routing dial: one setting simultaneously selects model tier, per-turn tool-round budget, shell timeout, and orchestration task width
evidence: internal/engine/agent.go:99-148 (MaxRoundsFor, TimeoutForEffort); internal/engine/orchestrator.go:26-43 (maxTasksFor); internal/engine/agent.go:641-660 (modelFor); README.md:44-62
one_why: Everyone has a thinking-budget dial (ultrathink); nobody else's scales the harness instead of the model: low = flash-class model, 4 rounds, 30s shells, 1 task; ultra = frontier tier, 80 rounds, 900s, 8 concurrent tasks - coherent resource posture per level with alias migration tested, and the pairing with per-slot model config makes cost/latency/blast-radius a single user-facing decision.

subject: kolkrabbi
title: KolkBench: pre-registered benchmark methodology that holds the model constant to measure the harness, with the failed local-8B pilot published as its own finding
evidence: bench/methodology.md:5-30; bench/harnesses.md; bench/results/2026-09-05-local-8b-pilot.md; bench/tasks/ with validate-tasks.sh
one_why: The evals-in-CI gap is the corpus's known ceiling and everyone scores models; this is the only pre-registered attempt to score agent loops against each other with model/repo/prompt pinned - and the pilot writeup states the validity condition ('when every harness scores zero the score is measuring the model'). No comparative run yet, so it scores as method + honesty, not as results.

subject: maki
title: Tree-sitter-bash parse derives permission scopes per command segment; 'allow always' generalizes safely, unparseable commands force a prompt
evidence: plugins/bash/init.lua:295-315; maki-agent/src/permissions.rs:933-953, 39-43
one_why: `git diff && rm -rf /` yields scopes git+rm (stored as `git *` and `rm *`, never block-wide wildcards -- SHELL_KEYWORDS guards block-openers); parse failure returns the full command with force_prompt=true instead of defaulting allow, inverting the corpus's regex-denylist anti-pattern.

subject: maki
title: Doom-loop breaker deduplicates identical repeated calls instead of aborting the run
evidence: maki-agent/src/agent/tool_dispatch.rs:25,69-92,916-946
one_why: 3 consecutive calls with identical name+input-hash are skipped with an injected error tool-result while the run continues -- gentler than crush's breaker, and the hash+window design is tested as a matrix (tool_dispatch.rs:1142).

subject: maki
title: Embedded monty Python interpreter exposes every tool as an async function, gated by the same dispatcher, with hook-bypass-proof file access
evidence: plugins/code_execution/init.lua:1-40; maki-interpreter/src/runner.rs:1-12,732-741
one_why: Filter/transform/pipe happens outside the context window; interpreter `open()` is disabled whenever a plugin hooks `read` so the sandbox cannot route around policy, gather() is re-implemented to keep sibling results on partial failure, and time+memory limits bound the interpreter -- a second code-mode shape (vs codex's v8) that is testable in one binary.

subject: maki
title: Summarizer overflow retry ladder: strip images/thinking, collapse tool results to placeholders, then drop oldest round with orphan cleanup

subject: maki

subject: memcode
title: Risk classifier and capability denylist walk the same shell AST through one shared unwrapper, with a bypass battery as the standing regression guard
evidence: internal/agent/permissions/permissions.go:74-77,124-166,433-445; internal/agent/permissions/deny.go:44-47,75-82; internal/agent/permissions/classify_bypass_test.go:6-97; internal/agent/runtime/exec.go:1672-1685

subject: memcode
title: Hot-raw / warm-summary / cold-session-log tiering with budgets derived from learned lane capacity, never absolute constants
evidence: COMPACTION.md; internal/agent/runtime/compact.go:26-37,142-165,262-300; internal/agent/compaction/compaction.go:47-62
one_why: Every prior magic number (45K, 150K) 'aged into a silent clip' as windows grew 5-20x, so budget = served lane capacity x85% with a window-relative fallback; the warm summarizer is force-escalated because 'a wrong summary silently becomes the session's false memory', and the cold layer's marker tells the model precisely what is retrievable vs must be re-run.

subject: memcode
title: Eviction derived from a measured read-evict-reread thrash: superseded-read dedup (range-aware), decaying hot-path pins, budget-scaled keep counts
evidence: internal/agent/compaction/compaction.go:217-311; internal/agent/runtime/compact.go:46-118; internal/agent/compaction/compaction_test.go:238-401
one_why: Audit evidence: fixed keep-counts (6/8) were smaller than real working sets, so the same 9 files were re-read 13-14x per session; now an earlier read of a path+range dies the moment it is re-read (a later FULL read covers ranges), paths observed re-read stay pinned with per-turn decay capped at 12, and keep scales 8..32 with budget — offload pointers are typed and lossless ('re-read that range to restore').

subject: memcode

evidence: internal/agent/runtime/compact.go:150-175,252-256
one_why: Re-summarizing a history that can't get under budget rewrites the whole prefix each crossing — the measured '3 compactions in 8 minutes' signature — burning a summarizer call and busting the prompt cache for a near-identical result; manual /compact resets the baseline because the user asked.

subject: memcode

subject: memcode

subject: memcode

subject: mini-kode

subject: mini-kode

subject: mini-kode

subject: mini-kode
title: 4,851 LOC of behavior-asserting vitest across 32 files, zero CI to ever run them -- tests execute only by developer habit and prepublishOnly

subject: mini-kode

evidence: src/agent/executor.test.ts:13-26 (vi.mock('../llm/client')), :418-503 (permission_denied propagation to ExecutionResult), :126-231 (tool start/complete callback shapes)
