subject: mini-kode
title: Tool batches scheduled by consequence class: all-readonly runs concurrently, any mutating tool forces sequential LLM order, results re-indexed to LLM order, denial cascades to the remainder, and a readonly tool requesting permission is a hard bug-throw
evidence: src/agent/toolExecutor.ts:122-145 (strategy choice), :196-207 (requestId->index re-ordering), :214-222 (readonly-permission bug throw), :330-349 (denial cascade)
one_why: Consequence-class batching with an order-preservation guarantee keeps OpenAI tool-message sequences valid under concurrency -- the readonly-claims-permission assertion is a nice tripwire no other reviewed subject has; no loop-level cap or budget alongside it though.

subject: mini-kode
title: fileEdit refuses any update unless a sha256 of the on-disk file matches the cached hash from the last read -- staleness enforced, not just read-before-edit
evidence: src/tools/fileEdit.ts:154-163 (currentHash vs getCacheEntry, 'Please read the file first to confirm context.'), cache write-through on edit :180, guard test src/tools/fileEdit.test.ts:13 ('requires read-before-write')
one_why: Cheaper than checkpointing and kills the whole class of edits against a file changed by hooks/the user mid-loop; tested via fileEdit.test.ts; no reviewed subject enforces the hash (most only require a prior read happened) -- and note autoEdit mode bypasses approval but not this guard.

subject: minicode
title: Filesystem jail and bash-guard run BEFORE mode dispatch and bind even in allow-all, with a realpath double-key against internal symlink escape
evidence: src/policy/permission.ts:379-441 (universal jail pre-mode), :483-497 (allow-all still runs full bash-guard), :443-479 (owned-state .minicode/ write lock, string + isOwnedStateReal realpath check); src/policy/jail.ts:44-60
one_why: The usual failure of 'allow-all' is that it becomes unrestricted host access; here the only thing a mode can disable is the approval prompt, never the path jail, the credential denylist, or the guard against a subagent poisoning minicode's own state (fake 'always' allowlist, malicious MCP config, blinded recovery journal) - and the double-key (logical string + resolved real path) closes the junction/symlink-around hole that string-only checks always have.

subject: minicode
title: Bash denylist done right: normalize-then-match (quotes, simple-var inlining with chained rescan, cmd.exe caret escapes) with honest limits stated and paired must-deny/must-allow oracle probes run in PR CI on Linux and Windows
evidence: src/policy/bash-guard.ts:1-19 (bypass classes that motivated it), :38-46 (stripQuotes), :60-88 (quote-aware caret stripping with reasoned PowerShell non-treatment), :90-120 (inlineSimpleVars 3-pass rescan); experiments/bash-bypass-probe.ts:11-13 (each case paired with must-allow over-block guard); .github/workflows/ci.yml:77-83,158-159
one_why: The corpus's standing anti-pattern is regex-over-raw-string denylists trivially bypassed by `cat .e""nv` or `X=.env; cat $X`; minicode closes the whole equivalence class by canonicalizing before matching, refuses to pretend the residual is solved ('static analysis over a Turing-complete language - raises the cost of attack, does not remove it'), and ties every rule to a two-sided probe that runs per PR on two OSes so neither bypasses nor over-blocks regress silently.

subject: minicode
title: Compaction tiering with anti-thrash circuit breaker, verbatim-pinned prior summary, hard summary budget, and compaction spend booked into the session budget
evidence: src/policy/compaction.ts:44-51 (F3.1 per-session thrash state), :95-120 (2 sub-10% rounds disable LLM path, loop falls to sync-mechanical), :207-217 (prior summary pinned verbatim, never re-summarized - anti semantic drift), :169-215 (composeBoundedSummary 1500-char cap, asymmetric trim directions, lone-surrogate drop), :31-40+:293-305 (compaction usage reported to session bus); loop.ts:336-355 (async compactor can never crash the loop); CHANGELOG.md:5-8 (measured 53.9x growth fix)
one_why: Three failure modes every summarize-and-prepend scheme has - unbounded summary growth (window filled by the summary itself), semantic drift from summarizing summaries, and compaction LLM spend invisible to cost accounting - each has an explicit, tested mechanism here, plus a breaker that notices when compaction stops making progress instead of burning a provider call per turn forever.

subject: minicode
title: Seeded-PRNG bash-guard fuzz plus shadow-git stress and adversarial MCP server on nightly CI
evidence: experiments/extreme-bash-fuzz.ts:17-34 (deterministic LCG, bugs reproducible via --seed); .github/workflows/slow.yml:28-34 (multi-seed multi-round nightly), :35-37 (shadow-git 1500 files x 8 sessions), :39-41 (extreme-mcp-adversarial)
one_why: Not coverage-guided fuzzing, but a reproducible adversarial loop against the exact components that carry the security claims, scheduled nightly so PR CI stays fast; the seed-reproducibility contract (found bug -> replay command) is the piece most harness-less repos skip.

subject: minicode
title: Mutation-intent journal answering exactly one question - is mutation X committed? - with intent issued after permission and before execute, finalize only on durable SQLite, and fail-open-with-degraded on journal write failure
evidence: src/session/journal.ts:1-22 (design, explicit non-goals: not a cross FS+DB transaction, never auto-redo, resume = verify-first), :29-40 (record schema with childOf delegation chain); test/journal-verify.test.ts, recovery-idempotency.test.ts, recovery-side-effects.test.ts
one_why: After a crash the honest answer for FS-vs-DB mutation state is 'unknown', and most subjects either ignore it or overclaim transactions; minicode scopes the artifact to commitment truth, deliberately fails OPEN on journal write failure (killing the turn over a log error destroys more than the gap) while flipping the session to an advisory resume path - the tradeoff is written down instead of hidden.

subject: minicode
title: Shadow-git checkpoints: temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE + write-tree pinned under refs/minicode/ as bare trees, undo = tree-diff restore of changed paths only, user index/HEAD provably untouched
evidence: src/session/shadow-git.ts:12-27 (O(delta) object-store approach replacing the old O(workspace) JSON manifest; trees pinned via refs so gc keeps them; invisible to git log --all / git branch); test/shadow-git.test.ts; slow.yml:35-37 (stress)
one_why: Cline's git-stash checkpoints pollute user stash/reflog and cost a full snapshot; this reuses the existing object store for content-addressed delta checkpoints while making a hard promise - no git add/commit/checkout/reset/stash ever touches user state - and records its honest limit (.gitignore'd files are outside the snapshot, stated at :29-30).

subject: minicode
title: Docs-map drift gate: every git-tracked src/** file MUST appear in docs/ARCHITECTURE.html, kernel pin in the map MUST equal VENDOR.md, plus layer-direction import tests
evidence: test/architecture-map.test.ts:1-29 (two drift incidents cited as motivation: untracked motion.ts file, stale kernel pin); test/ui-boundary.test.ts; AGENTS.md:20-24 (import direction rules)
one_why: 'AGENTS.md says update the map' is a prayer; this makes the living architecture document a build artifact under test - a doc that cannot silently rot is a force multiplier for both humans and agents working the repo, and it caught two real drifts before being written as a test.

subject: minicode
title: Two-repo kernel split: 1.6k-LOC agent kernel frozen, vendored into the product via #minicore subpath imports, seams additive-only, sync hash-pinned and CI-checked
evidence: package.json:44-46 (imports #minicore -> vendor/minicore), vendor/minicore/VENDOR.md:5-14 (source commit 0d33571, file hash, shipped-tarball hash, vendor:minicore workflow), .github/workflows/ci.yml:44-46 (vendor:check per PR), AGENTS.md:41 (do-not-edit rule)
one_why: Distinct from vendoring a third-party fork: this is deliberate kernel/product segregation of the team's own runtime - the loop stays small, deterministic, and reviewable (355-LOC loop.ts) while the product layer churns, and the only permitted kernel edits are backward-compatible additive seams (compactAsync/initialMessages/cwd), enforced by hash check rather than discipline; nobody gets to quietly grow the kernel from the product side.

subject: minicode
title: Evidence-gated task completion: `completed` requires injected verify evidence, failed verify demotes the task to a new `blocked` state, no-verify runs report `unverified` instead of claiming verified
evidence: src/tools/todo.ts:51 (setCompletionEvidence injection point), cli/setup.ts:1184 (composition-root wires last verify verdict in), CHANGELOG.md:5-8 (pre-fix state: no code path prevented marking done while verify red)
one_why: Self-reported completion is the agent's favorite lie; rather than blocking normal no-verify usage, the design makes the claim honest at the state level - completed means evidenced, blocked carries the reason to the model, and unverified is visibly distinct from both.

subject: minicode
title: One-page threat model naming the deterministic execution chain (permission -> jail -> guard -> validation -> executor -> journal) with per-mode tables and a 'no absolute safe' rule
evidence: docs/security-model.md:1-30 (every claim points to a readable/testable mechanism; explicit 'allow-all is not unrestricted host access' callout)
one_why: The doc mirrors the actual gate order in code and states what is NOT protected instead of marketing safety; pi's SECURITY.md honesty is the anchor for this rung and minicode matches it with an unusually concrete mode x mechanism table.

subject: mocode
title: Deterministic intent/constraint ledger survives compaction independently of the summarizer
evidence: src/session/compact.ts:462-495,1068-1069
one_why: extractUserDirectives harvests user intent/constraint lines with rules (not the summary model) and pins them across compaction generations, motivated by measured ~17% summarizer retention of user constraints (compact.ts:54-55,464); no other subject separates user-intent preservation from summarizer goodwill.

subject: mocode
title: Dual-pressure ladder: 60% zero-LLM deterministic cleanup, 80% commits to LLM compact with no per-stage re-check
evidence: src/session/scheduler.ts:114-163; src/context/budget.ts:53
one_why: Nuance vs existing tiering entries: a low-pressure band does only idempotent cost-free rewrites, and crossing 80% deliberately commits the step to compacting rather than re-evaluating after each stage - anti-oscillation rule stated at scheduler.ts:147-149.

subject: mocode
title: Compaction fork reuses the parent request prefix so the summarizer call itself is a cache hit
evidence: src/session/compact.ts:1044-1046; tests/compact-fork.test.ts:74-132
one_why: Summarizer forks parent system+history and appends only the compact instruction; auto-falls back to a standalone compressor when the fork would not fit the window - turns compaction from a guaranteed cache miss into a cache read.

subject: mocode
title: Fingerprint-scoped grants that never migrate legacy tool-wide authority
evidence: src/permissions/index.ts:84-97,112-114,214,251
one_why: Grants bind exact-command/resource-path hashes with once/session/project scopes, off-TTY denies fail-closed, dangerous tools default the panel to DENY, and v2 allowForever is intentionally not migrated so an upgrade cannot silently restore whole-tool authority.

subject: mocode
title: realpath-based jail incl. the new-file nearest-existing-ancestor case, centrally enforced
evidence: src/sandbox/jail.ts:36-62; src/sandbox/policy.ts:39-70; tests/sandbox.test.ts:20-40
one_why: One policy choke point rewrites args.path into the jail for all path tools; symlink-out-of-root and new-file-ancestor-aliasing escapes are covered with real-symlink tests - the completeness checklist ('new path tool must be registered') is explicit.

subject: mocode
title: Project-sourced skills gated by content hash with fail-closed non-TTY
evidence: src/skills/trust.ts:1-11
one_why: Trust is sha256 over SKILL.md+scripts+references, invalidated on content change, user-dir skills exempt, untrusted project skill execution in pipes/CI strictly denied - registry-skill payload threat treated as real.

subject: mocode
title: Hand-shaped SSE chunk stub drives the full stream-tool-refeed loop with byte-level assertions
evidence: tests/agent-core.test.ts:37-57; tests/compact-fork.test.ts:74
one_why: Mock chunks mirror the real provider parse path (delta.content / delta.tool_calls / trailing usage) and assert history structure and hook ordering are reproducible, giving loop-regression safety without any API spend; plus 300-case property tests on the budget evaluator (context-budget.test.ts:164,200).

subject: mocode
title: 61-task coding benchmark exists but CI gates only the offline smoke
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:59-61; evals/README.md:1-12
one_why: The fixture suite (basic/hard/advanced incl. concurrency, atomicity, protocol-parsing tasks) with independent verifiers is exactly what an evals-in-CI rung needs, but it requires a live key and never runs in CI; only the zero-model smoke is gated.

subject: mocode
title: Atomic full-history checkpoint per tool batch with resume-job in a new process
evidence: src/jobs/checkpoint.ts:1-19; src/index.ts:105
one_why: Background jobs tmp-write+rename the entire history after each committed tool batch, so a crash or reboot resumes from the last batch boundary via mocode resume-job - crash recovery scoped to jobs rather than the interactive session.

subject: mocode
title: Immutable per-step tool-policy snapshots with explicit add_tool_groups expansion and an optional small-model router
evidence: src/agent/run-coordinator.ts:166-192; src/tools/policy.ts:148,240; src/tools/router.ts:133
one_why: Schema, runtime backstop, and sub-agent permissions all derive from one per-step non-expansible snapshot; mid-step group expansion only takes effect next step, and a probability-threshold classifier can pre-select groups - expansion is a versioned, traced, tested state transition (tool-policy.test.ts:144-246).

subject: mocode
title: Command denylist and env-secret filter are bypassable by construction - but honestly labeled non-boundary
evidence: src/sandbox/command.ts:1-43
one_why: Source states 'not a security boundary' and lists its own bypasses ($IFS/base64/env concat); the honesty is the model, the mechanism is not - real isolation still needs an OS jailer, which this project defers.

subject: mocode
title: Provider-reported usage calibrates the token estimator (EWMA with outlier rejection) and ephemeral injections count toward pressure
evidence: tests/token-calibration.test.ts:32-61; src/session/scheduler.ts:52-56; tests/context-budget.test.ts:123-162
one_why: Nuance vs existing entries: samples with ratio <0.3 or >3.5 vs estimate are discarded, and out-of-history tail injections are passed in explicitly so fixed overhead is invisible to the 80% pressure line; a real 289k/256k overflow regression is pinned by test.

subject: mocode
title: Sub-agents reuse the parent's exact wire prefix - byte-equality asserted by test
evidence: src/agent/run-coordinator.ts:196-215; tests/spawn-permissions.test.ts:157,204
one_why: Delegation strips only the trailing assistant tool_call message, appends the task text, and keeps identical tools/system prompt, so the sub-agent's first request is a prefix-cache hit on the parent's already-sent bytes; test also forbids added restriction phrasing that would fork the prefix.

subject: molt
title: Completion is a claim the harness refuses or accepts: task criteria are Object.freeze-copied, sealed by hash, and journalled BEFORE the first request, then re-run against disk on every 'done'; refusals get receipts too
evidence: src/engine.ts:3608-3637 (freeze + seal + journal append before first request), :3688-3702 (criteria stated to model as unchangeable, recorded-notes may never be called verified), :3712-3718 (maxProofAttempts + identical-failure tracking)
one_why: Nuance on the validated-finish-gate cluster: the seal makes 'criteria predate the work' a verifiable fact in the journal rather than a promise, and mid-session bar drift is refused with deliberate no-blame wording (engine.ts:2330-2352) after a real false-accusation incident.

subject: molt
title: Shipped builtin check rejects completions whose new tests prove nothing: tautologies (assert.equal(f(x),f(x))), assertion-free its, and new test files that never import the changed module
evidence: src/tests-real.ts:1-24 (three shapes + stated conservatism rule), wired as bar builtin with removedAssertions ledger flag at engine.ts:2216-2226
one_why: Every validated-finish-gate subject trusts that green tests mean something; molt attacks the tests themselves, and documents that three tests in its own suite passed by luck until this existed (docs/testing-charter.md, discipline 2).

subject: molt
title: Repeat-call guard keyed on line-range coverage, not byte identity ('has this already been shown?' vs 'is this identical?'), and cleared whenever a shed archives what was shown
evidence: src/engine.ts:3735-3756 (answered map + shown coverage map, 32-step walk-past incident in comment), :3996-4006 (shown/answered cleared after shed, 29-of-31 false stall-refusals incident)
one_why: Most loop guards compare exact call strings, so asking for line 181 then 182 slips past; the paired detail -- invalidation of the guard's own memory when compaction archives the evidence -- is the bug nobody else has reported having.

subject: molt
title: Superseded-tool-result elision protects the cached prefix once the endpoint has EVER served from cache: mid-conversation rewrites measured 0% cache hit on the next step, so elision defers rather than pay it
evidence: src/engine.ts:3960-3985 (protectCache: this.sessionCached > 0, deferred counter journalled), :1310-1318 (sticky cachingUnsupported flag stops re-offering refused cache_control)
one_why: Compaction and prompt-cache are usually tuned independently; molt gates the cheaper compaction on observed cache state of the specific endpoint, so the saved tokens never cost a full-price re-send.

subject: molt
title: Fully mechanical two-tier shedding with crash-atomic archive: elide superseded results, then shed-to-archive in planShed -> archive.write -> commitShed order, so a failed disk write cannot take context with it
evidence: src/engine.ts:3952-3991, docs/shed.md:26-38 (two-phase diagram + throwing-archive test), archive at .molt/exuviae/ per docs/transparency.md:6-15
one_why: Zero LLM calls in compaction -- no summarization hallucination surface -- and the archived originals are what the proof loop verifies completion claims against, inverting the usual trade: compaction here protects evidence rather than destroying it.

subject: molt
title: Hash-chained session journal with offline `molt verify`, whose header states the honest bound itself: 'tamper EVIDENCE, not tamper prevention' -- silent edits impossible, wholesale rewrite not
evidence: src/journal.ts:1-16 (claim + honest limit), kinds incl. permission/bar_run/bar_skipped at :35-53, redaction before write per redact.ts:1-12, docs/transparency.md:24-28
one_why: Nuance vs dvalincode's chain: molt chains for post-hoc trust in its own receipts ('what did this thing do?'), costs zero tokens (disk only, never enters context), and redacts secrets at the journal boundary because the audit file's whole purpose is to leave the machine.

subject: molt
title: Subscription models ride the vendor's own CLI over documented protocols (ACP to grok/gemini, Claude Agent SDK) instead of lifting OAuth tokens; the agent's built-in tools are stripped and every non-molt permission request is denied at session/request_permission
evidence: src/acp.ts:5-15 (refuses to read ~/.grok/auth.json), :28-40 (MCP-hosted molt tools + builtin stripping + deny-by-molt, 'deliberately no --always-approve'), src/mcp-bridge.ts:1-15 (stdio bridge for MCP-incapable clients)
one_why: grinta reuses Codex OAuth as raw transport; molt draws the ethical line explicitly (entitlement to run their CLI is not a repackaged API) and solves the hard part the other direction: keeping its write-ledger/tree-accounted guarantees complete over a black-box agent it does not run.

subject: molt
title: engine.ts is a 5,452-LOC Engine class fusing the turn loop, budget ceilings, shedding, tool dispatch, ledger, and all three backend paths; runTurn alone spans ~1,400 lines
evidence: src/engine.ts:1228 (class Engine), :3597-~5000 (runTurn with criteria preflight, proof loop, elide/shed, step loop, salvage inline), wc -l = 5,452 (largest single loop in corpus so far)
one_why: Every other boundary in the repo is disciplined (autonomy/journal/receipts/redact/watchdog are clean); the loop is where molt pays the price for that, and per the errata a >5k core file caps architecture regardless of comment quality.

subject: molt
title: No session resume, fork, or rewind anywhere: the hash-chained journal records everything but nothing replays it; a crash or closed window ends the working session permanently
evidence: grep resume/continue over src/cli.tsx yields only keys.ts:137 stdin plumbing; docs/transparency.md:24-28 presents molt log as read-only forensics; no fork/rewind command in cli.tsx:85-153 help surface
one_why: The journal is 90% of a resume journal already (every message, tool call, and decision is replayable JSONL); the forensic strength makes the continuative gap the single biggest operability miss for a 60k-LOC harness.

subject: nanocoder
title: Real OS jail shipped but off by default, silently degrading to plain sh
evidence: source/services/bash-executor.ts:83, source/services/bash-sandbox.ts:6-11
one_why: sandbox-exec/bwrap plans exist with CI-tested profiles yet default config yields plain sh -c; any UI claiming 'sandbox' without checking the flag misleads - fourth convergence on missing/fake enforcement.

subject: nanocoder
title: Dangerous-command detection is a bypassable regex list gating prompts
evidence: source/tools/execute-bash.tsx:189-196
one_why: rm-rf regex rules fall to quoting, $IFS, or cd tricks; deny-lists give false comfort where an allow-list or jail would actually bind.

subject: nanocoder
title: Checkpoint manager with file-snapshot layer and timeline navigation
evidence: source/services/checkpoint-manager.ts, source/services/file-snapshot.ts, source/services/timeline-manager.ts (+specs)
one_why: Snapshot-based checkpointing kept separate from the session store so rewind is a service call, not UI state mutation - contrast cline-3's git-stash approach.

subject: nanocoder
title: Per-project daemon running cron + file-watcher triggered skill runs through a backpressure dispatcher
evidence: source/daemon/daemon.ts:1-12, source/daemon/ipc.ts, source/daemon/lockfile.ts
one_why: Agents as event consumers with backpressure is a distinct orchestration shape (vs cline-5's plain cron); unproven crash semantics but worth watching.

subject: nanocoder
title: Semantic memory with reviewable proposal store and summarizer service
evidence: source/memory/semantic-memory-manager.ts, source/memory/proposal-store.ts, source/memory/summarizer-service.ts
one_why: Memory writes go through a proposal stage instead of silently mutating context files - the write-hygiene nuance the seeded memory-files cluster lacks elsewhere.

subject: nanocoder
title: VS Code plugin drives nanocoder over its own ACP server process
evidence: plugins/vscode/src/acp-client.ts, acp-process-manager.ts; source/acp/acp-agent.ts (1119 LOC) with specs
one_why: Eating own dogfood: making the IDE surface a standard ACP client forces the headless contract to stay complete - the strongest ACP commitment found so far.

subject: nanocoder
title: Agent loop implemented inside React/Ink hooks forces parallel non-UI paths
evidence: source/hooks/chat-handler/conversation/conversation-loop.tsx (1414 LOC), source/acp/acp-conversation.ts, source/message-handler.ts
one_why: Three entry paths (TUI hook, ACP conversation, message-handler) reimplement turn orchestration around the UI-owned loop; every feature must be wired thrice and can drift.

subject: nanocoder
title: PR checks fail on coverage drops and CI runs the bwrap jail spec on real bubblewrap
evidence: .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml:17-21 (fail-on-coverage-drop), :63-95 (jail job with apparmor sysctl)
one_why: Machine-enforced test-quality ratchet + turning a normally-skipped platform test into a real CI job; cheap to copy and hard to argue against.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Agent core is an append-only JSONL ledger: scoped idempotency keys, CAS replacement, content-addressed payloads, enforced event chains
evidence: src/ledger/ledger.ts:323-328 (idempotency scope + conflicting-reuse reject), src/domain/events.ts, test/unit/ledger.test.ts:103,119,213,491 (replay-as-no-op, key-reuse reject, withdrawal CAS, requested->admitted->started chain)
one_why: Crash-resume, fork lineage (ledger.ts:488-495 enforces exactly one run.forked), and audit stop being bolted on - every loop mechanism (compaction, approval, budget charge) is a validated event, which is why test names read as invariants instead of behaviors; heavier lift than any anchor attempted.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Teto: a second cognitive lane that observes only completed owner steps and may interrupt via A2A only when advice could change the next decision
evidence: src/runtime/teto-lane-scheduler.ts:100, src/runtime/run-runtime.ts:537-545 (TetoScheduler/IntentNavigator wiring), docs/runtime-loop-baseline.md:16 (one inference per released batch), CHANGELOG.md:24-26
one_why: Closest corpus analog is codex's guardian pool, but Teto is a continuous per-lane observer with its own context, start/stop authority for the owner, and explicit silence-by-default - a distinct multi-agent primitive, though causal value is still self-claimed pending the arm in nausicaa-harness-3.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Feature shipped with a preregistered experiment: frozen fixture+scorer hashes, four arms including a shadow placebo, per-pair budget envelopes, 95% bootstrap
evidence: test/eval/preregistered-contract.ts:13-27 (CONTROL_ARM teto-shadow, PREREGISTERED_ARMS), :32-57 (BudgetEnvelope, ArmPlan), test/eval/runner.ts, test/eval/teto-live-restraint.ts
one_why: No other subject measures its own flagship feature against a placebo arm with a hash-frozen contract written before the live runs; if the field adopts any causal-eval methodology, copy this shape - the arms are offline-verifiable (preregistered-contract.test.ts) even though live runs need credentials.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Prompt-cache performance is an observed ledger projection and a release gate: recorded live probe artifact with provenance yields pass/hold on shipping
evidence: src/observability/cache-evidence.ts:11-33 (prefixContinuity, providerCache per attempt), test/eval/cache-artifact.ts:21,38-59 (CACHE_PROBE_TASK_ID, releaseDecision pass|hold, evidenceDigest)
one_why: Anchors warm or mark caches (pi, claw-code's broken detector); nobody else ties cache behavior to a release decision or derives prefix continuity from the event journal instead of an in-process counter - and the projection deliberately excludes prompt fingerprints so it is UI-safe.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Two compaction tiers: per-turn selection plus a deterministic pressure gate with predicted-gain floor, contiguous group retention, and output-headroom re-check
evidence: src/runtime/main-loop.ts:668-684 (selectCompaction), :827-870 (compactForPressure adopted only if headroom >= 1 token), src/fukai/compaction-pressure.ts:9-16,53-75 (minimumGainTokens, insufficient-predicted-gain), test/unit/fukai-compaction-pressure.test.ts
one_why: The pressure decision needs no provider call and can say no (skip when predicted gain is below floor), and a candidate summary competes against the live reservation before adoption - avoids the wasted-compact-and-overflow cycle every tier-1 harness hits; closest existing implementations are codex's token-budget tier, so reuse the decision function shape.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Context budget overflow degrades in fixed steps - drop compaction, then drop skill catalog and its paired schema atomically - never fails the turn
evidence: src/runtime/main-loop.ts:742-749 (FukaiBudgetError -> rebuild without compaction), :753-764 (drop skill tool + catalog together and retry), :759-770 (hide schema when catalog not rendered), src/fukai/context-provider.ts:133-136
one_why: The invariant 'an optimization never displaces required context' plus schema/capital coherence (a tool is never advertised for context the provider elided) is a generalizable budget pattern; most subjects either fail-open with truncated required content or crash the turn.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Skill discovery returns immutable metadata-only snapshots; bodies load only on explicit invocation, with changed-during-load rejection
evidence: src/mowe/edges/skills.ts:257-260 (discoverSkills doc), :366-411 (loadSkill with TOCTOU checks :391-403), src/fukai/context-provider.ts:60-62 (bounded catalog: 128 items, 64KB total)
one_why: Converges with the seeded pattern (cline/pi-style catalogs) but adds a per-path sourceId + turn-snapshot generation model so in-flight turns keep the catalog they were built against - the catalog-eviction-vs-in-flight-request race other subjects leave unsolved.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: workspace profile: probed-then-used OS confinement (seatbelt/bwrap) that fails closed by removing the bash tool, hiding secret dirs; default profile remains full-access
evidence: src/tools/workspace-command-sandbox.ts:167-207 (probe never runs the command), :129-134,159-161 (unavailable -> throw), :32-38 (.aws/.ssh/.gnupg/.kube/.nausicaa protected), src/runtime/run-runtime.ts:471-484 (shell enabled only if availability().available), README.md:262, test/unit/workspace-command-sandbox.test.ts:90,163
one_why: Exact inverse of nanocoder's fail-open jail: probe failure means the capability does not exist, and profile refusal is surfaced as unavailable rather than as a command error; the honest caveat is that nothing under the default full-access profile binds - security-posture honesty per SECURITY.md:3-5 keeps it nuance, not safety-hole.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Runs are owned through TTL leases with monotonic fencing tokens; daemon workers persist hash-chained recovery journals and durable writes re-check the lease
evidence: src/runtime/execution-lease.ts:9-15,53-58 (fencingToken, clock-regressed states), src/runtime/file-execution-lease.ts:225 (fence checked under file lock), src/runtime/daemon-worker-recovery-journal.ts:15-37 (uncertain/interrupted statuses, fingerprint-not-payload), src/runtime/session-controller.ts:512-517 (assertExecutionLease durable-write guard)
one_why: Distributed-systems ownership discipline imported into a coding harness: a zombie second instance cannot double-execute because appends fail the fence check - test/protocol/daemon-ledger-fence.test.ts proves it; only codex's daemon comes close, and no other TS subject has fencing at all.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Whole protocol plane tested offline against scripted ports: 20+ daemon/protocol specs, recovery suites, abort-parity tests; live provider suites excluded from npm test and CI
evidence: package.json:61 (--exclude test/live/** test/eval/** test/smoke/**), test/protocol/daemon-worker-recovery.test.ts, test/protocol/agent-loop-abort-parity.test.ts, test/recovery/, test/live/openrouter*.test.ts (credential-gated)
one_why: The seam design (ModelPort/Clock/every dep injectable) makes the daemon restart, fence-loss, and cancellation semantics deterministic to test - the abort-parity test between interactive and one-shot paths is the kind of cross-surface invariant property anchor codex has and pi/cline lack equivalents for.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: session-controller.ts at 6,365 LOC fuses host wiring, permission-mode mutation, model selection, polling, and TUI snapshotting despite the loop itself being separated
evidence: src/runtime/session-controller.ts:563 (class SessionController), :569-600 (sandbox+approval+selection+poll state), :6066 (permissionProfileForCapabilities), 4,718-LOC src/cli/interactive.ts alongside
one_why: Per the errata the >5k product-surface docking factor applies here even though MainLoop is clean - the 8->9 architecture gap is 'loop/state separated from every product surface', and the session host is where policy, selection, and host coordination reconverge; if this one file is decomposed, architecture joins verification at 8.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Every adapted third-party snippet is attributed by upstream commit hash with an explicit not-copied boundary list
evidence: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES:3-5 (pi responsibilities named), :7-13 (Prime Agent commit 7787f074, what was and was not ported), :35-38 (Prime daemon/RPC/IPython explicitly not copied), src/tools/workspace-command-sandbox.ts:94-98 (DeepSeek sandbox-local commit aa6c361a; Codex boundary credited)
one_why: The audit trail synthesis needs for provenance is volunteered by the subject itself - a cheap norm (commit pin + adopted-boundary paragraph per ported file) that would resolve most fork-detection ambiguity in this corpus; MIT compliance intact throughout, no license-risk finding.

subject: neovate-code
title: ACP always-allow is cached per toolName:category and replayed without re-consulting the tool's per-command risk logic, so one grant admits every later bash call including banned ones
evidence: src/commands/acp/session.ts:113-119 (ruleKey = `${toolName}:${category}`), :131-137 (cached decision returned without prompting); risk lives only in tools' needsApproval (src/tools/bash.ts:975-990) which is short-circuited by the cached rule
one_why: Converges with the coarse-grant cluster (cf. kolega prefix-rule bypass): a category is not a grant unit for bash because risk is a function of the command string; the cache must key on command atom, or at minimum re-run needsApproval for high-risk/banned commands even when a category grant exists.

subject: neovate-code
title: Prune-before-summarize: LLM-free tool-output pruning with recency budget, protected tools, and minimum-prune hysteresis, re-measured before escalating to compaction
evidence: src/history.ts:268-300 (step-1 prune, re-check usage, step-2 LLM compact only if still overflowing), src/compression.ts:127-212 (reverse walk, protectTurns=2, protected tools skill/task, 40k recency budget, stop-at-pruned sentinel, >=20k minimum prune), src/constants.ts:101-105
one_why: The re-measure between tiers is the port: most tiered designs fire both tiers from a stale estimate; hysteresis (skip prune unless >=20k freed) prevents churn on borderline sessions; pruned parts keep a prunedAt marker that doubles as the walk-stop sentinel.

subject: neovate-code
title: Turn cap deflated by tool calls: turnsCount -= approvedToolUses.length makes tool-heavy loops effectively unbounded against max_turns
evidence: src/loop.ts:736-737 (turnsCount decremented by number of approved tool uses each turn), cap check src/loop.ts:214-224 (max_turns default 50)
one_why: A model emitting 2 tool calls per turn never consumes budget (1-2=-1), so the only loop guard is disabled exactly in the scenario loops happen; with no loop-identity detection anywhere in the repo, a stuck same-call loop runs until API cost or the user stops it - budgets should count LLM turns only, never be negative-credited.

subject: neovate-code
title: Bash policy is best-of-species among deny-lists (pipeline-segment evaluation credited to codex PR #7544, command-substitution rejection with tested quoting edge cases) but still root-name matching that python -c or find -exec trivially bypasses
evidence: src/tools/bash.ts:18-43 (24 banned roots incl rm/curl/sh), :248-273 (pipeline segment fallback), :283-287 (hasCommandSubstitution reject), tests src/tools/bash.test.ts:14-79
one_why: The banned list only raises needsApproval (bash.ts:975-990) so it fails toward human review, not execution block - which is the honest role for a denylist; but nothing prompts in yolo, and command substitution is rejected outright rather than flagged, an odd asymmetry worth converging with the grammar-parsed-bash-policy cluster.

subject: neovate-code
title: Prompt-cache breakpoints are a static heuristic: model-name substring match (claude|sonnet|opus) gating ephemeral marks on first-2-system + last-2-non-system messages, sliding every turn and never firing for other cache-capable providers
evidence: src/promptCache.ts:12-15 (shouldCache string includes-check), :26-28 (toCache = 2 system + last 2 non-system), applied each turn src/loop.ts:254
one_why: Converges with prompt-cache-marking: capability should come from the provider/model manifest (this repo already has a 1160-LOC modelMap.ts with per-model limit data), and the last-2-messages breakpoint invalidates itself each turn rather than using stable rolling breakpoints one turn apart (kolega pattern) - design-doc 2025-11-12-anthropic-prompt-caching.md shows the team knows, code is still v1.

subject: neovate-code
title: Every product surface - Ink TUI, programmatic SDK, ACP server, web+websocket server - is a thin client of one typed MessageBus/HandlerMap RPC contract generated via api-extractor, with handler slices registered per domain
evidence: src/nodeBridge.ts:3-19 (16 registerXxxHandlers slices), src/nodeBridge.types.ts:1-60 (generated HandlerMap), src/sdk.ts:27-33 (SDKClient = bus.request typed by HandlerMap), src/commands/server/websocketTransport.ts, src/uiBridge.ts:56 (TUI answers toolApproval on the same bus)
one_why: Cheapest full-surface fan-out seen: one loop, zero process boundaries in-process, yet the same request/response contract serializes over websocket for remote hosts; the 1930-LOC generated type file is the seam that keeps UI/SDK/ACP from accreting private copies of core logic (contrast nanocoder's per-entry-path re-implementations).

subject: neovate-code
title: Skills expose only name+description in the tool description; bodies are read at invocation, and the installer can target Claude's skill directories for cross-harness skill sharing
evidence: src/tools/skill.ts:8-27 (metadata-only <available_skills> rendering), :44-56 (readSkillBody on invoke), src/skill.ts:732-741 (SkillSource.GlobalClaude/ProjectClaude), src/commands/skill.tsx:632-650 (--claude install flags)
one_why: Converges with seeded lazy-skill-loading; the nuance worth taking is the interop posture - skills are written once and installed into .claude/skills or ~/.claude/skills so a rival harness reads the same packages, an unusually concrete cross-harness import path in either direction.

subject: ob-1
title: Keyless free-tier provider plane as a first-class architecture: ~20 free cloud providers routed in-process with strategy-ordered selection, 8-hop failover, escalating cooldown ladders, self-learned rate limits from 429s, decay-weighted bandit reliability stats, and a tool-call-repair post-processor for weak free models
evidence: src/providers/free/index.ts:1-35 (contract, MAX_ATTEMPTS=8); src/providers/free/state.ts:3-6,66 (cooldowns, learned limits, bandit succ/fail pseudo-counts); src/providers/free/tool-repair.ts:280 (postProcessResponse); scripts/free-router-smoke.ts (319 LOC, CI-gated)
one_why: Every other subject treats the free tier as a promo; OB-1 makes 'works with zero account/key out of the box' the default provider plane and pays for it with real machinery (health loop, debounced persisted state, keyless endpoints, repair for the weak models that fall out of routing) - the pairing of tool-repair with bandit routing over known-weak free models is corpus-unique; concept-porting only, the 'no account' README framing itself is marketing.

subject: ob-1
title: Escalation decided by an objective signal, not a model: self-fix budget spent AND the check still red -> runTurn returns { escalate } handing the turn to Fusion best-of-N; pure shouldEscalate gate exhaustively truth-table-tested, capped at once per user turn
evidence: src/agent/loop.ts:120-128 (shouldEscalate), :796-804 (signal site); src/agent/loop.test.ts:29-33 (full 3-flag truth table); scripts/escalation-smoke.ts:1-13 (a-e decision surface via injected _callModel/verify seams)
one_why: Most quality loops either silently give up or let an LLM judge whether to keep going; OB-1's trigger is purely the verified-failure signal plus three policy flags (off by default on apply turns so escalation can't cascade), and the whole decision is testable without a model, subprocess, or fs - cleaner than deepagents' classifier ladder because no classifier participates.

subject: ob-1
title: Shipping defaults are no-prompt autopilot AND sandbox off; the on-by-default folder-trust gate downgrades only an IMPLICIT autopilot, so one /trust or any saved setting yields unapproved, unsandboxed writes and shell
evidence: src/config.ts:706 (permissionMode default 'autopilot'), :708 (sandbox default 'off'); src/index.ts:2433-2455 (trust gate scope + OB1_TRUST_GATE=0 escape); src/safety/sandbox.ts:120-125 (wrapCommand -> plain bash when mode off)
one_why: The machinery underneath is genuinely good (hardened bwrap tiers, CI-proven enforcement, loud degradation) which makes the default the whole story: trusted-folder == zero enforcement at every layer simultaneously; nanocoder-5 pattern (real jail, wrong default) mitigated but not resolved by the trust gate.

subject: ob-1
title: MockBrain scripted scenarios drive the REAL runTurn over REAL buildTools in 71 CI-gated no-key smokes, asserting wire behavior (denials, multi-tool, history shape) and invariants like 'cached system prefix stays task-agnostic'
evidence: scripts/parity-harness-smoke.ts:1-55; scripts/ci-smokes.ts:19-88 (suite = single source of truth, run on every push/PR per .github/workflows/ci.yml:36-40); escalation-/delivery-e2e-/subagents-smoke.ts all loop-level
one_why: The antipodal proof to crab-code's closed backend enum: an injectable _callModel dep plus a tmp-dir real tool registry means approval, gate, and cache invariants are property-tested end-to-end on a $0 hermetic CI tier - and escalation/delivery smokes reuse the same seam, so each new gate buys its e2e test cheaply.

subject: ob-1
title: bwrap capability probed with the EXACT runtime argv and tiered hardened->base->none so an old bwrap still sandboxes instead of silently dropping to none; CI proves enforcement live (net denied, writes confined) with a connectivity baseline that makes the denial asserts meaningful
evidence: src/safety/sandbox.ts:26-49 (argv-derived probe, tiers), :57-79 (SBPL quote/newline injection guards on embedded paths), :92-114 (--cap-drop ALL, --new-session vs TIOCSTI); scripts/bwrap-enforce.ts:25-55; .github/workflows/ci.yml:53-73 (installs bwrap, re-enables unprivileged userns)
one_why: Two failure modes other subjects miss are engineered out: subset-probes that pass while the real argv fails, and old-bwrap hosts silently losing their previously-working sandbox; the CI job even flips Ubuntu's AppArmor userns restriction so the test cannot self-skip into vacuous green.

subject: ob-1
title: Gate ordering before every mutating call: declarative deny/allow/warn rules (.ob1/policy.json, highest-priority match) -> finite consumable /allow capability tokens -> interactive approval, with forceAsk tools (public tunnel) prompting even in autopilot and an empty rule condition matching NOTHING
evidence: src/safety/policy.ts:43-45,62-70; src/agent/loop.ts:911-947 (ordering incl. forceAsk at :940-947); scripts/policy-smoke.ts + approval-tokens-smoke.ts (CI)
one_why: The empty-condition-matches-nothing rule kills the classic policy foot-gun (a typo'd condition that allows everything), and finite decrementing tokens are a sharper grant model than standing 'always allow git'; non-TTY denial is honestly reported as 'auto-denied, can't prompt' rather than a fake 'user denied' (loop.ts:948-960).

subject: ob-1
title: Two context tiers on one model-scaled budget: deterministic eviction at 60% of (window - output reserve) with path-aware protection of the freshest read of every file, LLM-summary at 85% whose cut walks past orphaned tool_results that would 400 the next call
evidence: src/agent/context.ts:42-54 (budgetChars, fractions), :96-135 (protected-latest-read eviction), :172-178 (orphan tool_result guard); src/agent/loop.ts:614-619 (thresholds track the RESOLVED model)
one_why: A 1M-window model is no longer compacted at 128k thresholds because the router's resolved model drives the arithmetic; the path-aware protection encodes the lesson that dumb age-based eviction makes the model hallucinate files it already read, and eviction invalidates the read-dedup cache so a pointer can never reference evicted content.

subject: ob-1
title: System prompt split into one cached stable block (instructions, AGENTS.md, skills, repo map) and an uncached volatile tail (per-turn semantic memory, date, model identity), with mid-stream retry hints appended as extra UNcached blocks so the warm prefix survives retries - and a CI test asserting the cached prefix stays task-agnostic
evidence: src/agent/loop.ts:270-312 (stable/volatile split), :688-695 (retry hint as uncached extra block); scripts/parity-harness-smoke.ts:41-49 (cache-boundary invariant test)
one_why: The invariant is pinned by a test rather than convention: per-turn task guidance (quality contract) is verified to land OUTSIDE the breakpoint, which is exactly the drift most subjects reintroduce when adding per-turn context.

subject: ob-1
title: The self-fix loop may not green itself by weakening tests: during a correction round a write to a test-pattern path is REFUSED, after any observed failure it is allowed but flagged loudly in the transcript and quality ledger
evidence: src/agent/loop.ts:889-907 (guard + flag sites), :826-843 (flagged edits printed on the green outcome); src/agent/test-guard.ts:12-15 (refuse|flag|off); src/agent/test-guard.test.ts (97 LOC)
one_why: Closes the one exploit every auto-verify loop has - delete the test to pass the build - with a two-strength posture (hard refuse only where the incentive is acute: mid self-fix; loud flag elsewhere so a human, not the model, decides); no other subject guards the verifier against the verified.

subject: ob-1
title: Weak-model degenerate-turn guards: whole-message prose or serialized-JSON tool calls (anchored, arg-shaped, so explanatory text mentioning tools is not flagged) and false capability refusals get one scripted nudge to re-issue REAL tool calls, then an honest 'nothing was done' outcome
evidence: src/agent/loop.ts:524-545 (looksLikeUnsentToolCall), :548-553 (looksLikeToolCapabilityRefusal), :737-775 (nudge + honest degradation)
one_why: A failure mode unique to cheap/weak free-tier models made first-class - the turn that 'did' work but executed nothing - with the anchoring deliberately conservative (requires kwarg syntax inside parens so 'done (first attempt)' passes); the dogfooding cases are cited inline (web_search x25, task-09).

subject: ob-1
title: 11 src modules carry a first-line 'parity with claw-code's X' header - original Apache-2.0 TypeScript, but the feature list is deliberately modeled on claw-code, which the corpus already flags as a Claude Code derivative (claw-code-1)
evidence: src/safety/policy.ts:1, src/eval/parity.ts:1, src/agent/hooks.ts:1, src/agent/approval-tokens.ts:1, src/agent/claims.ts:1, src/agent/green-contract.ts:1, src/agent/recovery.ts:1, src/config-validate.ts:1, src/context/git-state.ts:1, src/context/lsp.ts:1, src/safety/bash-validation.ts:1
one_why: Not a code fork (no shared code lineage, census 'original' holds), so calibration rule (a) does not bind, but lineage stats should trace concept genealogy claude-code -> claw-code -> ob-1 for approval tokens, policy/trust, hooks, recovery recipes and the mock parity harness itself; unusually honest for a lineage this indirect.

subject: ob-1
title: A real eval product exists (typed task suite, solo/fusion/council/personas modes, report template) but eval.yml is workflow_dispatch + secrets-only, so no model behavior is ever gated on push/PR
evidence: .github/workflows/eval.yml:3-13 (dispatch-only inputs), :23-28 (secrets), :47-51 (self-skips without creds); eval/tasks/*.json (typed tasks); docs/evals.md
one_why: Per the frozen errata the 8-rung verification ceiling needs evals-in-CI; ob-1 is one secrets-policy away from being the corpus's first eval-gated repo - the deterministic hermetic tier is already exemplary, so this is the last missing rung (understanding: free-model evals are nondeterministic, which is likely why it stayed manual).

subject: ob-1
title: TUI tested under a REAL pseudo-terminal in CI with a pyte terminal emulator asserting render persistence and streaming hygiene (no overflow garbage, pinned input), separate from the in-memory ink-testing-library smoke
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:27-49 (pip install pyte; tui-pty.py; stream-pty.py); scripts/tui-pty.py (297 LOC), scripts/stream-pty.py (143 LOC)
one_why: Catches the class of bugs component tests structurally cannot - line-overflow garble, scrollback commit errors, input repaint during streaming - by emulating the actual screen rather than the React tree; pairs with slash-menu-smoke's meta-test that every /help command is reachable in the TUI.

subject: ob-1
title: Project memory as a sqlite graph with depth-capped grounded reflection: a LLM-managed evolution pass (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP with id-validation) plus synthesis of 'reflection' facts at level max(source)+1 that cannot recurse into reflection-of-reflection beyond the cap
evidence: src/memory/store.ts:19-43 (brain seam, reflection_level semantics), :80 (schema); src/memory/reflect.ts (shouldReflect, MAX_REFLECTION_DEPTH); scripts/memory-reflect-smoke.ts + memory-evolve-smoke.ts + memory-rank-smoke.ts (recency/importance/relevance re-rank, CI)
one_why: Most subjects stop at store-and-search or flat scratchpad memory; OB-1 consolidates and distills with bounded abstraction depth and invalidates edges in the exported DOT/HTML graph - the depth cap is the guard against confabulation spirals that unbounded reflection invites.

subject: ob-1
title: Identical-call breaker scoped to NON-mutating tools (exact name+input signature, default 3 strikes, model told the result won't change) with mutations exempt because the diff preview already gives feedback, plus a 1000-step runaway backstop that stops with work kept and a resumable message instead of killing the turn
evidence: src/agent/loop.ts:245-258 (RUNAWAY_STEPS=1000, MAX_IDENTICAL_CALLS), :856-877 (breaker site), :1053-1060 (resume-keeping stop text)
one_why: Smaller than 3code's fingerprint window or dvalincode's triple detector, but the mutating-exempt asymmetry is a thought-through distinction none of them make (a re-applied edit is rare and already visible), and the stop message treats a tripped cap as pause-not-failure ('say continue') rather than an error.

subject: ob-1
title: /rewind on a SHADOW git repo (own GIT_DIR under the data dir, project as work-tree): snapshots the real filesystem state before every prompt so run_bash-made changes (rm/mv/sed) are revertible too, never touching the user's .git, and works in non-git directories - ON by default
evidence: src/agent/checkpoint.ts:1-21 (design + why); src/config.ts:709 (checkpoint default true); scripts/rewind-smoke.ts (real-repo isolation, CI)
one_why: Tool-only file histories (Claude Code's checkpoints) cannot undo shell damage; the shadow-repo shape gets whole-worktree revert without polluting the user's repo, and allow-empty commits mean every prompt yields a restore point even when the diff is empty.

subject: octomind
title: Idle-time cache keepalive: max_tokens=1 ping on a frozen conversation snapshot resets provider cache TTL, with ping costs harvested and folded exactly-once into session cost
evidence: src/session/cache_keepalive.rs:17,51,198; src/session/chat/session/main_loop.rs:76-110
one_why: Extends pi's warmer from pre-emptive warming to TTL extension during human idle; provider-policy gated (Anthropic-only today) so unsupported providers never burn money, and warming cost is accounted, not invisible.

subject: octomind
title: Fold economics gate: compaction fires behind the fire line only when priced profitable in token ratios (cache-read, folder in/out, cache-write vs one uncached input token), with a hard ceiling entered early that no cooldown may cross
evidence: src/session/chat/conversation_compression/decision.rs:31-70; src/session/chat/conversation_compression/mod.rs:88-91
one_why: Most rigorous compaction profitability model in the corpus: ratios instead of dollars keep it provider-agnostic and defined when pricing is missing; depth is computed from measured session growth rate rather than a configured ratio ladder.

subject: octomind
title: PACT attention controller: deterministic evidence selection around the generative fold -- packet kinds, provenance enum (RealUser/ToolObserved/ValidatedSummary), KeepExact/Summarize/ArchiveReference lanes, SHA-256 packet digests
evidence: src/session/chat/conversation_compression/attention/mod.rs:15-19,25-59
one_why: Runtime owns task pins, tool-call atomicity, and attribution checks; the model only folds -- cuts the classic failure where the summarizer silently rewrites provenance.

subject: octomind
title: Task-aware narrowing of oversized tool outputs by ONE cheap-model call selecting line ranges over a numbered copy, reconstructed verbatim from the original after lossless spill to a session file
evidence: src/supervisor/condense.rs:15-33
one_why: Selection-not-generation: the model never retypes tool output, so nothing can be mis-copied or hallucinated into the transcript; irrelevant results become deterministic handles and any cut span stays readable on demand.

subject: octomind
title: Guardrails DSL with temporal capability-history conditions: guards match capability(arg=regex) plus has/when ['+/-capability'] evaluated against the session's tool-call log; denied calls are never spawned and never enter history
evidence: src/config/guardrails.rs:15-36; src/session/guardrails.rs:15-60; src/session/chat/response/tool_execution.rs:291,366-368; src/session/guardrails_tests.rs:58
one_why: 'Use view instead of ls' only when no filesystem-read has happened yet -- policy as code with sequence semantics, bound before spawn and tested, unlike the corpus's static regex denylists.

subject: octomind
title: Supervisor authorizer: bounded tool-free LLM batch admission judged against persisted user-intent state (immutable parent boundary for delegated sessions) surviving compaction/resume; only exact grounded denials memoize, any policy/evidence change invalidates
evidence: src/supervisor/authorizer.rs:15-20,39-56; src/session/chat/response/tool_execution.rs:296-340
one_why: Approval authority is durable session data rather than volatile context, so compression or resume cannot launder a denied intent back into admissible work.

subject: octomind
title: In-process kernel jail applied to self before any child spawn and inherited by shells/MCP/subagents: Landlock (Linux) / seatbelt (macOS), write-only isolation (RW cwd+XDG data home, read-only /), honestly documented limits and fail-open
evidence: src/sandbox/mod.rs:15-40; src/sandbox/linux.rs:20-27,38-79; src/main.rs:249-259; config-templates/default.toml:33
one_why: Only subject applying Landlock to its own process rather than wrapping each spawned command; write containment is cheap and inherited, but it is opt-in, reads stay open (~/.ssh readable), and there is no egress control.

subject: octomind
title: LLM-free capability auto-activation: user intent embedded locally (ONNX muvon/octomind-embed) and matched against hand-authored capability triggers (mean-of-top-K cosine + margin); a hit registers the capability's MCP servers with no extra tool-call turn, LRU-evicted under a soft cap
evidence: src/mcp/runtime/capability.rs:21-33; src/mcp/runtime/skill.rs:15-23
one_why: Lazy tool/skill loading driven by local embeddings instead of model-initiated discovery: saves a routing round-trip per activation and keeps tool definitions out of context until the intent matches.

subject: octomind
title: Verify-gate on self-reported done: independent LLM verifier judges END STATE from typed evidence blocks (recorded actions with mut/read shape, ground-truth diff, read-back rounds), treats narrative as data, checks prohibitions as requirements, bounds re-runs at 2, and a PASS labels the trajectory so only verified work is learned
evidence: src/supervisor/gate.rs:15-19,27-75,660
one_why: Strongest finish gate found: prompt-injection-hardened block typing plus observe-vs-change classification prevents both false gaps on read-only tasks and rubber-stamps on violated prohibitions.

subject: octomind
title: Interactive main loop under test: real binary driven inside a pseudo-terminal via a Python pty driver -- type a prompt, read the streamed answer, exit via /slash-command
evidence: tests/interactive_pty_e2e_test.rs:15-18,46-47
one_why: The only mechanism by which the TUI input layer and terminal rendering ever execute under test; nearly every other subject leaves its interactive loop unexercised.

subject: octomind
title: Self-generated guardrails/skills promote only via counterfactual A/B: turns where a shadow artifact's trigger matched but was not applied form the control arm, live trials the treatment arm, scored on gate pass-rate gap vs a noise margin, retiring regressors -- off by default
evidence: config-templates/default.toml:722-739; src/supervisor/learning/evolution/synthesize.rs
one_why: Self-modification with empirical promotion: the agent cannot bake its own lessons into policy without beating its own shadow, which is the opposite of prompt-baked self-grants elsewhere in the corpus.

subject: octomind
title: Free every-turn detectors (identical-call repetition, no-progress window) fused with the agent's structured <sup>{json}</sup> self-report token before any model is woken; hints are advisory only and thresholds are fixed constants, not knobs
evidence: src/supervisor/detect.rs:15-19,82-95,506-510; src/session/chat/response/tool_execution_tests.rs:41-47
one_why: Second data point for detector-plus-advisory designs (crush rung), with the self-report protocol adding intent signal; deliberately never blocks hand-back, distinguishing polling repetition from true stalls.

subject: open-codex
title: Fork delta is exactly the transport swap Responses-API -> Chat-Completions plus a five-provider key/baseURL/model table; loop and sandbox byte-heritage upstream

subject: open-codex
title: Esc-esc cancellation defended by generation counter, dual stream/exec abort controllers, and synthetic tool outputs replayed for unresolved call_ids so the next request satisfies the API contract
evidence: codex-cli/src/utils/agent/agent-loop.ts:88-92,100-107,371-385,113-127; tests/agent-cancel-race.test.ts:8-36; tests/agent-function-call-id.test.ts
one_why: The 'No tool output found for function call' 400 after a mid-tool cancel is a contract problem every streaming tool-calling loop inherits; keeping call_ids in pendingAborts and emitting {output:'aborted'} tool messages on the next run is the minimal repair, and the FakeStream-yields-before-cancel test pins the exact race window.

subject: open-codex
title: FakeOpenAI vi.mock + hand-built FakeStream assert loop semantics (cancel, terminate, rate-limit backoff, max-tokens, retry) across 14 agent-*.test.ts files
evidence: codex-cli/tests/agent-cancel-race.test.ts:37-56; codex-cli/tests/agent-rate-limit-error.test.ts; codex-cli/tests/agent-max-tokens-error.test.ts; codex-cli/tests/agent-server-retry.test.ts
one_why: With only ~5k test LOC the corpus still proves error-taxonomy behavior (which error yields which user-visible message and whether the loop returns or rethrows) instead of asserting existence - cheap pattern that transfers to any provider-SDK loop.

subject: open-codex
title: SandboxType.LINUX_LANDLOCK declared in the enum but never implemented; full-auto on Linux silently runs the same rawExec path as no-sandbox
evidence: codex-cli/src/utils/agent/sandbox/interface.ts:5; codex-cli/src/utils/agent/exec.ts:40 (seatbelt-or-rawExec ternary); no landlock code anywhere in src/
one_why: The CLI help promises '--full-auto automatically run commands in a sandbox' (cli.tsx:74-77) while Linux gets zero kernel enforcement with no runtime warning; milder than the claurst rung because README:151 honestly states 'Linux - there is no sandboxing by default', but the runtime silently degrades on the dominant server platform - caps safety-enforcement at 4.

subject: open-codex
title: Always-approve cache keys collapse 'bash -lc <script>' to the script's first word, so one 'always approve' on git status mutes prompting for every git invocation for the session
evidence: codex-cli/src/utils/agent/handle-exec-command.ts:36-63 (deriveCommandKey),:86-91 (cache consulted before policy, sandbox skipped)
one_why: 'Always approve this command' silently becomes 'always approve this program' - git push --force inherits consent from git status; the key abstraction discards exactly the arguments that distinguish safe from destructive invocations, and approvals.test.ts does not pin the granularity.

subject: open-codex
title: Zero compaction: full history replayed every request, no usage accounting, overflow is one terminal message telling the user to run /clear
evidence: codex-cli/src/utils/agent/agent-loop.ts:505-512 (messages: [system, ...prevItems, ...staged]),:577-596 (isTooManyTokensError -> 'shorten the conversation, run /clear')

subject: open-codex
title: Pre-AGENTS.md project-doc convention preserved: codex.md/.codex.md/CODEX.md discovered from .git-rooted cwd, 32 kB cap with truncation warning

subject: open-interpreter
title: Apache-2.0 compliant rebrand, but residual provenance/trademark exposure
evidence: diff -q codex/LICENSE open-interpreter/LICENSE clean; codex-rs/product-info/src/lib.rs:12-32 (openai/codex release URLs, chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh shipped as CODEX_* fallbacks)

Study-integrity finding: census 'rename-clone' overstates the legal exposure here.

subject: open-interpreter

subject: openhands
title: Agent-triggered child conversations with isolation enum and a corruption-tolerant local launch ledger

title: Product surfaces render only what an admitted extension manifest declares - no manifest, no nav entries, routes 404

subject: openhands
title: Multi-backend registry: one shell drives local/remote/cloud agent servers and different agents per backend, with version-compat gating

subject: openhands

subject: openhands
title: Stryker mutation testing and an affected-E2E router exist but no workflow invokes either
evidence: stryker.config.mjs:1-12; package.json scripts test:mutation:diff; tests/e2e/mock-llm/test-mapping.json + tests/e2e/mock-llm/scripts/resolve-affected-tests.mjs (no .github/ reference)

subject: openharness
title: Narrowing-only subagent permission clamp via strictness rank table
evidence: src/types/permissions.ts:35,61-68; test src/types/permissions.test.ts:249-253

subject: openharness

evidence: src/utils/bash-safety.ts:12-60, used at src/types/permissions.ts:178,258
one_why: Strips timeout/nice/env-style wrappers and splits compound commands before rule matching, so 'timeout 10 rm x' hits the same deny rule as 'rm x' -- the classic prefix-evasion hole in regex deny-lists, done without a full shell parser.

subject: openharness
title: Workspace-trust gate on hooks/statusline scripts, but soft-rollout leaves it inert by default
evidence: src/harness/trust.ts:87-89 (trustSystemActive = trust file exists); enforced at src/harness/hooks.ts:555,606

subject: openharness
title: oh mcp-server exposes all tools with toolPermission rules unenforced
evidence: docs/ecosystem-compat.md:24 ('toolPermissions is NOT enforced when exposing tools via stdio'); src/mcp/server-mode.ts:12-17 (wires getAllTools() with no permission gate)

subject: openharness
title: OS sandbox fully delegated to @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime: opt-in, Bash-only, fail-open passthrough

subject: openharness
title: SECURITY.md states exactly what the sandbox does not cover, including the fail-open contract
evidence: SECURITY.md:29-58 ('Default: tool execution is not sandboxed... falls back to its unsandboxed path... a future revision will add requireSandbox')
one_why: Names the tool-by-tool sandbox gaps, the platform gaps, and the fail-open semantics in the same file that shows the config to fix them -- the honesty rung pi and cline sit on, and cheaper than any control.

subject: openharness
title: MicroCompact -> importance-scored drops -> LLM summarization, with a 3-failure compaction circuit breaker
evidence: src/query/compress.ts:71-135 (scoreMessage :19-41); trigger + breaker at src/query/index.ts:158-190
one_why: Cheapest tiers run first (truncate, stub old tool results, drop lowest-scored by role/recency/decision-point score respecting pins) and LLM summarization only fires if the cheap pass misses; after 3 consecutive compression failures it stops trying and tells the user to start fresh instead of looping.

subject: openharness
title: DeferredTool wraps tools with name+description-only prompts until ToolSearch or first call
evidence: src/DeferredTool.ts:1-33; hint injection src/query/index.ts:96-101

subject: openharness

evidence: src/providers/anthropic.ts:97-111,132-134,154-156
one_why: Marks the last message each turn so the conversation prefix stays cached and marks the final tool def so the whole tool list caches -- the cheap 90%-off discipline most subjects in this corpus lack entirely.

subject: openharness
title: Full eval harness (orchestrator, pack loader, JUnit scorer) in-repo but no CI workflow runs it
evidence: src/evals/orchestrator.ts, src/evals/scorer.ts (parseJunitXml), 8 eval test files; grep for eval across .github/workflows/ returns nothing

subject: openharness
title: Loop e2e driven by scripted mock providers against real tools

one_why: Deterministic coverage of loop semantics (turn completion, tool_call_end payloads, follow-up feeding) without API keys or nondeterminism -- the pattern that makes 1732 test cases runnable on every push across two OSes.

subject: openharness
title: MetaHarness hill-climbs its own config: benchmark, LLM-suggest change, re-run, revert if worse
evidence: src/services/MetaHarness.ts:1-30,115 (optimizes system prompt, tool selection core-vs-deferred, model router config, compression strategy, permission rules)

subject: openharness

subject: openharness

subject: openlumara
