subject: openlumara
title: Compaction writes a SUMMARIZATION_CUTOFF marker instead of deleting history - model view is cut, user history survives, deletion of the marker reverts
evidence: core/context.py:7,58-68; core/commands.py:385-401
one_why: LLM summary + cutoff signal are appended as ordinary messages; context.get() slices everything before the last cutoff and prepends 'Summarize our chat so far.', so compression is revertible from the UI with no separate checkpoint store.

subject: openlumara
title: At 80% of context the model itself receives a budget warning and is instructed to tell the user to /compress
evidence: modules/token_threshold.py:13-34
one_why: Cost visibility is routed through the agent rather than only the UI: provider usage receipts cached on the chat drive an end-prompt injection, making the AI a stakeholder in its own context budget.

subject: openlumara
title: HTTP module resolves DNS, validates every resolved address (incl. IPv4-mapped IPv6 unwrapping) against a full blocklist, and re-validates on redirects
evidence: modules/http.py:673-723,987-1012
one_why: Unparseable literals treated as unsafe, CGNAT/link-local/metadata ranges covered, plus dangerous-port blocklist, https-only default, and per-minute rate cap - the complete SSRF package for a personal agent (GPL: concepts-only).

subject: openlumara
title: Six-layer regex/Unicode injection screening of web content plus random-delimiter untrusted-data envelopes
evidence: modules/http.py:25-112,816-848
one_why: Zero-width + homoglyph + base64-decode-and-scan + instruction-density layers, then content fenced with a 32-char crypto-random delimiter and doubled security notices; honest nuance: regex layers are bypassable, the envelope fence is the part worth keeping.

subject: openlumara
title: api_bridge defaults api_key_required=False and executes every request with commands_authorized=True
evidence: channels/api_bridge.py:40-44,186
one_why: Enabling the OpenAI-compatible endpoint gives any network caller privileged slash-command execution (framework commands bypass the AI entirely) unless the operator notices one boolean; no SECURITY.md to flag it.

subject: openlumara
title: Shell sandbox ships with internet on: setting default True vs in-code fallback False
evidence: modules/sandboxed_shell.py:20-22,350
one_why: The jail is otherwise solid (cap-drop ALL, read-only rootfs, no-new-privileges, pids/mem/cpu caps, gVisor auto-detect) but the persisted default is internet_access=True, and a config-drift read would silently flip to the opposite fallback - network-egress-off should be the default.

subject: openlumara
title: WebUI session middleware falls back to the literal 'openlumara-default-session-secret-change-me'
evidence: channels/webui.py:328
one_why: Login is rate-limited and constant-time-compared, but session cookies are signed with a publicly-known key unless the user sets session_secret, so forged sessions defeat the login gate on exposed instances.

subject: openlumara
title: Recursive agentic tool loop has no iteration cap, loop detection, or budget
evidence: core/toolcalls.py:94,299
one_why: process() recurses per tool-call round with only a per-tool 10s timeout; a model ping-ponging between tools burns context and spend unbounded - crush is the only anchor with a breaker, and this loop lacks one entirely.

subject: openlumara
title: 1597 commits, 29k LOC, zero automated tests and no CI; the one test-named file is an interactive TTY viewer
evidence: channels/turn_grouping_test.py:1-31; no .github/ or any CI config in tree
one_why: QA is manual-review culture (commit messages say so); nothing in the repo can prove loop, context-trim, or sandbox-flag behavior, which caps verification at 1 regardless of how the code reads.

subject: openlumara
title: Scheduler jobs pick a per-job prompt strategy trading token cost against provider prompt-cache reuse
evidence: modules/scheduler.py:22-33
one_why: Three explicit modes (instruction-only / system+instruction / full-context) with the full-context mode chosen for cache-hit economics - a rare explicit statement of the cache-vs-tokens tradeoff at the scheduling layer (GPL: concepts-only).

subject: ouroboros
title: CI-blocking size ratchet: 1600-line module / 300-line function ceilings with tracked debt, enforced in every job
evidence: ouroboros/review.py:19-23 (MAX_MODULE_LINES=1600, MAX_FUNCTION_LINES=300, MAX_MODULE_BYTES=200_000); .github/workflows/ci.yml:175,293 (pytest -m size_ratchet in each tier); tests/test_size_ratchet_ci_shape.py:17 (every CI job must run the lane); tests/test_size_headroom.py:12-40 (headroom incl. zero/negative surfaced to health)
one_why: Anti-god-file discipline is mechanized rather than cultural -- the mechanism a self-modifying agent needs so its own rewrites cannot bloat past reviewable size; any agent repo can adopt the ratchet+debt-registration shape.

subject: ouroboros
title: AST analysis of inline interpreter code in shell commands resolves write targets, with fail-closed scoped to where danger exists
evidence: ouroboros/tools/shell_guards.py:376 (_python_write_targets_and_unknown), :361 (opaque-call detection), :1447-1480 (_dynamic_write_could_hit_repo: unresolved target blocks only if code names a repo path or cwd is inside repo -- 'Fail-closed is right where the danger exists, not everywhere')
one_why: Goes past regex deny-lists: python -c bodies are parsed for open()/write spellings and only genuinely-unresolvable targets near the protected root are refused, so false-blocks on external deliverables stopped driving whack-a-mole (comment at :1462).

subject: ouroboros
title: Closed profile x resource-root x operation matrix as the single tool-access SSOT, summarized back to parent and child at schedule time
evidence: ouroboros/tool_access_types.py:18-56 (6 profiles x 9 roots x 10 operations Literal vocabulary + _POLICY), ouroboros/tool_access.py:195 (decide_tool_access single seam), :88-117 (summarize_subagent_profile derives child capability from the same matrix to prevent wasted blocked rounds)
one_why: The vocabulary is closed and the matrix is one table -- visibility/residency is explicitly separated from authority ('Residency never grants execution authority', tool_policy.py:1-5), which is the separation most approval-gate agents lack.

subject: ouroboros
title: Append-only byte-prefix transcript invariant: compaction seams stamp a sanction, every other cache break is counted in usage
evidence: ouroboros/transcript_prefix.py:1-16 (invariant + OpenAI-family byte-prefix cache rationale, issue #906 'measured 2026-09-14'), :32 (sanction_rewrite), ouroboros/loop.py:337-355 (_record_transcript_prefix counts prompt_prefix_breaks per unsanctioned break; 'records and never blocks a send')
one_why: Seeded id observed with its strongest mechanism yet: cache monotonicity is a named invariant with sanctioned exceptions AND a per-task counter that makes cache loss a visible, budgetable cost rather than an invisible bill.

subject: ouroboros
title: Live-model lanes wired into CI: nightly paid E2E stand with explicit $30 cap and honest skip, plus real-provider skill-review smoke at $1.2/run
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:9,71 (cron 03:17 paid e2e_live stand, skipped honestly without key), :67 (dispatch input '$30 cap'), :631,657-660 (attempt-reserve math proving the cap arithmetic), :385-456 (skill_smoke live installs + review->grant->enable flow on a cheap reviewer model, split into two pytest processes so only one holds the API key)
one_why: First subject observed past the verification-8 ceiling noted for codex/cline/pi: real models run in CI on a schedule with an enforced money bound; still no scored benchmark gate or fuzzing, which keeps it 9 not 10.

subject: ouroboros
title: Stdlib mock OpenAI-compatible server on 127.0.0.1 drives whole-loop tests, backed by a provider contract catalog
evidence: tests/fixtures_mock_llm.py:16-54 (MockLLMServer ThreadingHTTPServer, /v1/chat/completions, hold/release knob so a browser fixture can keep a task inside its first model call), tests/provider_contract_catalog.py, tests/provider_contract_ci.py
one_why: Zero-dependency faux provider that tests real HTTP transport and concurrency, not just client stubs -- the hold/release trick makes mid-first-call UI states testable.

subject: ouroboros
title: In-loop resume journals restore round index, route, and tool schemas; stale snapshots cannot revive a spent wait
evidence: ouroboros/loop.py:387-420 (load_owner_wait/load_budget_pause restore model/effort/round_idx/tool_schemas; unanswered tool calls closed as execution-unknown WITHOUT replay), ouroboros/owner_wait.py:207-217 (resume refused unless status non-terminal, state=='waiting', and wait_id matches)
one_why: Resume semantics at loop granularity (not session granularity): a paid-but-unanswered model call is treated as an unknown outcome that is closed, never resent -- the resend-honesty discipline most resume designs skip.

subject: ouroboros
title: Delivery acceptance panel: host-forced review with a closed set of typed reasons, per-root paid review-cycle ceiling, and identical-diff refusal
evidence: ouroboros/loop.py:113-119 (closed typed acceptance reasons -- 'none derives from model prose'; unspecified is fail-closed), loop.py:571-574 (acceptance observation + transcript seal before send), ouroboros/tools/commit_gate.py:1-27 (advisory-freshness gate, durable commit-attempt record, free identical-diff refusal, per-root-task paid max-review-cycles, review-contract fingerprint)
one_why: Finish-gate taken to its adversarial extreme: a reviewer model must accept the delivery, the reason vocabulary is host-computed so the model cannot author its own bypass, and money spent on review cycles is capped per root task.

subject: ouroboros
title: Runtime-mode tiers gate which source surfaces the agent may rewrite, with consent-tested elevation and constitution-protected files
evidence: ouroboros/runtime_mode_policy.py:1-6 (advanced may evolve app layer but not core contracts/safety files; pro through triad+scope review), :47+ (argv predicate refusing BIBLE.md deletion and git history rewrites), BIBLE.md:7-14 (constitutional amendment requires reviewed release outside Cyber Pro), tests/test_runtime_mode_elevation.py:87-147 (elevation refused without consent flag, downgrade allowed)
one_why: Self-modification with an enforced protected core: the ladder from ordinary task -> app-layer evolution -> core evolution -> unrestricted agency is code, consent-gated, and test-proven -- no other subject in the corpus models who-may-edit-what at this granularity.

subject: ouroboros
title: No OS-level boundary anywhere; elevated cyber_pro makes internal permission/review checks advisory-only
evidence: grep seatbelt/bwrap/seccomp across ouroboros+supervisor hits only ouroboros/config.py:233-241 (delegated containment mechanism is macOS-only per Claudexor docs; a run reporting no mechanism is DISCLOSED, not refused -- 'Disclose instead of forbid'); ouroboros/runtime_mode_policy.py:33-41 (mode_has_unrestricted_agency: internal mechanisms lose veto authority in cyber_pro)
one_why: In-process policy plus AST guards cannot contain a process that can edit the policy at elevated modes; the honesty about the gap (SECURITY.md names the boundary surfaces for reporters) is exemplary, but the boundary itself is absent off-macOS -- this is what caps safety-enforcement at 6.

subject: ouroboros
title: Refactor leaves preserve ~150-name historical re-export facades because tests and sibling leaves monkeypatch private names through them
evidence: ouroboros/loop.py:686-886 ('Cohesive leaves own the implementations... Keep the full re-export surface: production callers and tests address these historical loop bindings'); ouroboros/tool_access.py:31-34 ('extracted VERBATIM... so historical imports and monkeypatch targets keep working'); ~40 'noqa: F401 -- historical facade surface' import markers across the two files
one_why: The size ratchet keeps files small but the extraction seams are frozen by test coupling: leaf-to-leaf calls resolve through the facade at call time, so the module graph the reader sees is not the dependency graph the code runs -- a cautionary pattern for any refactor-under-tests program.

subject: ouroboros
title: Background consciousness wake: model-chosen next-interval inside owner bounds, rolling-24h cost allowance, exponential backoff, explicit no-re-arm events
evidence: ouroboros/consciousness.py:1-30 (tick order with typed outcomes; unreadable allowance ledger is a disclosed skip 'allowance_unknown', never a silent block; launched wake inherits the day's remaining allowance as its graceful cost ceiling; failures double the interval up to max; owner messages and wake finishes never re-arm), consciousness_allowance.py, consciousness_wake.py
one_why: Autonomous periodic agency budgeted like a wallet: the interval is the model's choice within owner clamps, the day's remaining money is the wake's ceiling so it never dies mid-first-call, and unknown ledger state fails disclosed rather than silently blocking or spending.

subject: pi

evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.ts:289,919

subject: pi

evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/cache-stats.ts, packages/coding-agent/src/core/cache-warmer.ts
one_why: Measures hit economics and pre-warms the stable prefix so the first turn after idle isn't a full-price miss; no other anchor treats cache as an active feature.

subject: pi
title: Project-trust store gates loading of project settings, packages, and extensions before first prompt
evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/project-trust.ts:24-29, core/trust-manager.ts
one_why: Extension code is treated as project-executable content with an explicit per-cwd trust decision incl. session-only option - the cheapest defense against repo-supplied extension RCE.

subject: pi
title: Permission gates, destructive-confirm, repo guards shipped as example extensions over a blocking beforeToolCall
evidence: packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/permission-gate.ts, confirm-destructive.ts, dirty-repo-guard.ts; enforcement at packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts:739-740

subject: pi

evidence: SECURITY.md:50 ("intentionally does not have a sandbox"), packages/coding-agent/src/core/bash-executor.ts
one_why: Documented honestly with containerization recipes, but out-of-the-box a prompt-injected command has full user privileges; acceptable only for users who follow the docs.

subject: pi

evidence: SECURITY.md:8,50; packages/coding-agent/docs/containerization.md; README.md:44-48
one_why: A template for honest threat-modeling copy: scope of protection, what is out of scope, and concrete containment recipes - directly quotable for hotdog.

subject: pi
title: Loop tested by a scripted generation harness driving stream events
evidence: packages/agent/test/harness/runtime/drive-generation.test.ts, packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts
one_why: Nuance vs codex-5/cline-2: harness drives the loop's stream-fn abstraction rather than mocking an HTTP wire format - cheaper but tests less of the transport layer.

subject: pi
title: RPC and JSON app modes with a documented command protocol and client/server packages
evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/project-trust.ts:12 (AppMode rpc), packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc-commands.md, packages/{protocol,server,client}

subject: picocode
title: YAML recipes pin provider/model/persona for non-interactive runs, with error_if output-gating for CI exit codes

evidence: src/tools.rs:34-58 + tests src/tools.rs:405-425

subject: plandex
title: Ellipsis-anchored structured edits resolved against tree-sitter node maps with unique/fuzzy replacement fallbacks
evidence: app/server/syntax/structured_edits_tree_sitter.go:119; app/server/syntax/structured_edits_generic.go; app/server/syntax/unique_replacement.go:7; app/server/syntax/structured_edits_test.go:12
one_why: The '// ... existing code ...' sparse-edit format this project popularized is backed by a real parser-anchored resolver (findNextAnchor walks tree-sitter nodes to match fragments) plus deterministic fallbacks, and it is the corpus's best-tested edit path -- the model emits only changed regions, which is the token-economy lever for large codebases.

subject: plandex
title: Genuine property-table tests exist but nothing runs them in CI
evidence: .github/workflows/ contains only docker-publish.yml; 2,511 LOC in 6 *_test.go vs 74,240 non-test; promptfoo eval POC at test/evals/promptfoo-poc/ unwired
one_why: Test quality is not the problem -- TestStructuredReplacements and TestBufferOrStream assert real behavior -- but zero CI wiring means even those regress silently; a minimal go test workflow would monetize tests that already exist.

subject: plandex
title: Every plan gets its own server-side git repo; rewind/checkout/version are git shas
evidence: app/server/db/git.go:37,95,197; app/server/handlers/plans_versions.go:123; app/shared/plan_config.go:86 (AutoRevertOnRewind)
one_why: Checkpointing agent state as commits in a dedicated per-plan repo (not the user's working repo, not a snapshot dir) gives branch/rewind/diff semantics for free and composes with auto-revert on failed runs; MIT-licensed so the approach is directly liftable.

subject: plandex

title: Product surfaces fuse despite a clean core: tui/app.py 8,642 LOC and session.py 5,095 LOC
evidence: src/tau_coding/tui/app.py (8642 wc -l), src/tau_coding/session.py:405+ (CodingSession owns entries, compaction, provider switching, extensions)
one_why: tau shows the port's disease: the pi core discipline transferred, but the app layer accreted past the errata's 5k docking line (worse than pi's own 6.8k interactive-mode.ts), capping architecture at 7.

subject: tau
title: No default tool-approval layer at all: bash execs directly; enforcement is opt-in via extension hooks, with unusually explicit honesty about it
evidence: src/tau_coding/tools.py:627-646 (create_subprocess_shell, no gate), src/tau_coding/project_trust.py:1-5 ('deliberately not a ... sandbox'), src/tau_coding/tui/project_trust.py:122
one_why: Same posture as pi's rung-6 (nothing underneath, no illusions) -- the disclaimer language at project_trust.py:4,:662 and in the TUI prompt is the model for honest security-posture docs; the finding is the absence, not any misrepresentation.

subject: trae-agent
title: LakeView: post-hoc LLM pass tags each recorded step with a fixed 8-label SWE taxonomy and dual-granularity summary
evidence: trae_agent/utils/lake_view.py:16-56 (EXTRACTOR_PROMPT task/details + WRITE_TEST/VERIFY_TEST/EXAMINE_CODE/WRITE_FIX/VERIFY_FIX/REPORT/THINK/OUTLIER), :101,:153 (two-prompt extract-then-tag), trajectory_recorder.py:191
one_why: Trajectory analysis as a first-class artifact: cheap extractor+tagger turns raw run JSON into browsable phase-tagged digests - no other corpus subject analyzes its own behavior at step granularity; useful for eval triage and failure classification.

subject: trae-agent
title: Docker 'sandbox' mode routes only 3 tools into the container; MCP and ckg tools still execute on the host
evidence: trae_agent/agent/base_agent.py:68 (docker_tools=["bash","str_replace_based_edit_tool","json_edit_tool"]), trae_agent/tools/docker_tool_executor.py:55-66 (name-based routing, everything else to host executor)
one_why: A user who opts into --docker-image for isolation still gets arbitrary stdio MCP servers (and ckg subprocess work) running unsandboxed on the host - allowlist-by-tool-name silently undercuts the isolation the flag promises.

subject: trae-agent
title: No approval layer exists at all: bash is a default tool executing arbitrary commands on the host
evidence: trae_agent/tools/bash_tool.py:41-59 (create_subprocess_shell on host), trae_agent/agent/trae_agent.py:21-27 (bash in default tool set); grep approv|permission|confirm across trae_agent hits only Docker daemon error text (cli.py:78,398)
one_why: Not even the 6-rung 'tested approval, nothing underneath' exists - the only in-loop gate is max_steps; the contrast case for permission-policy alongside codel's prompt-baked policy, minus any claim of safety.

subject: trae-agent
title: Zero conversation compaction; history grows unbounded inside the client and overflow is met by blind retries (random 3-30s sleeps) then run abort
evidence: trae_agent/utils/llm_clients/openai_compatible_base.py:119-123 (message_history += parsed, no trim), trae_agent/utils/llm_clients/retry_utils.py:38-50, trae_agent/agent/base_agent.py:177-180 (exception -> ERROR abort); only mitigation is 16k-char tool-output truncation (trae_agent/tools/run.py:17-26)
one_why: Long tasks deterministically die at the provider context wall, and the retry decorator wastes minutes re-sending the doomed payload - the floor case for compaction-tiering discussions, worse than codel-4 only in that it doesn't even notice prompt size.

subject: trae-agent
title: Conversation history is owned by the LLM client, not the loop: the loop passes only message deltas
evidence: trae_agent/agent/base_agent.py:166 (messages = await self._run_llm_step(...) returns new messages only) vs openai_compatible_base.py:119-123 (client accumulates); history-loss fix landed as HEAD commit e839e55 'fix(openai): persist tool outputs in message history'
one_why: Explains why compaction is structurally hard here: the loop cannot see, rewrite, or trim the context it is charged with managing; a single history-owner design (loop or session) is the prerequisite for any token-economy work on this codebase.

subject: trae-agent
title: Research harness: a separate sandboxed selector agent adjudicates N candidate patches with grouped majority voting
evidence: evaluation/patch_selection/selector.py:22-36 (--num_candidate/--group_size/--majority_voting/--max_turn), evaluation/patch_selection/trae_selector/selector_agent.py, sandbox.py
one_why: Inverts the agent-as-producer frame into agent-as-judge over a patch pool - test-time-compute selection run inside its own tool sandbox; interesting input to evals-in-CI style ranking, though the harness never runs in CI.

subject: trae-agent
title: Tools pyinstaller-frozen on the host, copied into the container at /agent_tools, with host<->container path translation on arguments
evidence: trae_agent/cli.py:101-115 (pyinstaller build of json_edit_tool/edit_tool_cli into dist), trae_agent/agent/docker_manager.py:19,47-66 (CONTAINER_TOOLS_PATH copy on start), trae_agent/tools/docker_tool_executor.py:33-46 (_translate_path)
one_why: SWE-agent's bundle-upload idea specialized for a local Docker sidecar: the agent's tools run natively where commands run, avoiding RPC-per-tool-call, but the tool-name routing list is exactly what finding trae-agent-2 shows can silently leak.

subject: tura
title: One macro tool (command_run) executes a stepped command graph per LLM turn: same-step reads run concurrently, mutating steps are barriers under shared/exclusive locks, later steps bind earlier step outputs
evidence: crates/tools/src/command_run/policy.toml (step_required, same_step_read_concurrency, mutating_commands_are_barriers, locks read=shared/write=exclusive/unknown_mutating_shell=workspace_exclusive); crates/tools/src/command_run/handler.rs:74+ (execute), crates/tools/src/command_run/output_binding.rs
one_why: Collapses the inspect/patch/build/test/lint ReAct cycle into one model round trip; the corpus has no other harness that makes the tool surface one macro graph with an in-turn lock scheduler - clean-room port is an architecture decision, not a feature.

subject: tura
title: command_run steps execute speculatively against the still-streaming provider tool-call arguments, emitting streaming_partial updates and terminating the turn early (early_finish_reason) when a mid-graph apply_patch fails
evidence: crates/runtime/src/provider_flow/command_run_streaming.rs:15,935,1097-1115 (early_finish_reason=apply_patch_failed, test); crates/runtime/src/provider_flow/streamed_command_run.rs:234 (streaming_partial)
one_why: Wall-clock win independent of tokens: the sandbox starts running the graph before the model finishes writing it, and a failed patch aborts the remaining model output rather than burning the turn.

subject: tura
title: Two-tier deterministic compaction with no summarizer LLM turn: agent-authored compact_context handoff from task_status, plus projection-based auto-compact; both rebuild a structured record with workspace snapshot, environment context, retained tool tail, and capability reset
evidence: crates/runtime/src/manas/process.rs:357-424 (handoff applied after persisted tool results), :442-458 and :1026-1047 (projected auto-compact, tested :1345-1375); crates/runtime/src/context/compaction.rs:101-150 (rebuild), :18 (max 2 inherited summaries)
one_why: Removes the extra summarizer round trip entirely and keeps execution state (commands, patches, validation evidence) as structured records instead of prose; the 2-generation cap on inherited summaries stops summary-of-summary drift.

subject: tura
title: task_status makes task state structured session data (task_group/status/task_type/compact_context) that mechanically drives prompt-manual selection, compaction handoff, and a startup gate: while task_type is unset, write-producing apply_patch steps are silently discarded from command_run before dispatch
evidence: crates/runtime/src/tool_flow/execute.rs:37 (require_startup_task_state), :55-102 (apply_patch discarded, empty-result path); crates/runtime/src/tool_flow/task_status.rs:14-75; docs/core/task-status.md
one_why: Sequence policy enforced in the loop rather than asked of the model: no investigation state, no writes; distinct from validated-finish-gate, which gates the end, not the start.

subject: tura
title: TUI renders /approve <id> /deny <id> permission prompts and parses permission.asked/replied events, but no Rust code anywhere emits them; the gateway hardcodes allow:["*"] per agent and the runtime's permission layer always blocks requests it cannot route
evidence: apps/tui/src/tui/render.ts:133-138; apps/tui/src/gateway/events.ts:114-115; crates/runtime/src/tool_flow/permission.rs:8-33 (permission_denial_for_tool, request_command_run_sandbox_bypass always Err); crates/gateway/src/api/agent.rs:126-129 (PermissionRuleset allow vec!["*"] deny empty); grep permission.asked across crates: zero emitters
one_why: Users believe an approval gate exists; in fact TURA_APPROVAL_POLICY unset (the default) means no gating and there is no backend path that could ever ask - worse than absent, because the UI launders it.

subject: tura
title: Command interceptor is on by default and de-obfuscates before classifying (wrapper stripping, nested bash -c/eval recursion, connector chains, base64-to-shell, shell-variable alias following, workspace-aware deletion), but TURA_COMMAND_INTERCEPTOR_DISABLED=1 switches it off wholesale
evidence: crates/tools/src/commands/command_safety.rs:26 (DISABLE_ENV), :30-34 (WRAPPERS), :74-101; wired at crates/tools/src/shell_executor/mod.rs:51,133
one_why: Stronger default than nanocoder's opt-in jail, but a denylist plus a single env kill switch is still prompt-adjacent policy, not an enforced boundary; the workspace jail (--sandbox / TURA_COMMAND_RUN_SANDBOX) that does path-contain workdir and apply_patch (command_run/handler.rs:793; commands/apply_patch/mod.rs:307) is opt-in.

subject: tura
title: Guardrail tests prove effect, not classification: the interceptor e2e actually executes commands under a Docker POSIX harness and asserts the destructive side effect never happened, while safe commands must run for real (verified by their side effect)
evidence: crates/tools/tests/business/command_interceptor_e2e.rs:1-12 (design comment), :48-85 (env hygiene under ENV_LOCK), :324-345 (kill-switch case)
one_why: Static blocked/allowed unit tables only test the classifier; end-to-end effect assertions test the whole wiring from model tool-call to process spawn - the gap where denylists usually fail.

subject: tura
title: Runtime leases make crash recovery a typed protocol: ActivateRuntimeLease with LeaseConflict/StaleLease outcomes, ReplayRuntimeRequest/RuntimeReplay journals, router startup orphan-worker reaping, and runtime-side parent watchdog
evidence: crates/session_log_contract/src/protocol.rs:315,459,467,493-531,584-639; crates/router/src/daemon.rs:12 (recover_after_start), :87-91 (cleanup_orphan_runtime_workers); crates/runtime/src/worker.rs:27,70 (start_router_parent_watchdog)
one_why: Two-process crash recovery where both sides can detect the other died (watchdog up, reaper down) and a spent runtime cannot revive itself via a stale lease - stronger resume semantics than any anchor except codex.

subject: tura
title: Loop e2e drives the full real pipeline - scripted codex-style SSE provider over a loopback TcpListener plus real tool execution in a temp workspace - and asserts final session state, tool results, and absence of stray tool calls
evidence: crates/runtime/tests/business/coding_agent_mock_e2e.rs:24-80; helpers/coding_agent_mock.rs:44,185 (mock bind), write_codex_sse :339+; CI runs per-crate: .github/workflows/ci.yml:95-149
one_why: Codex's mock-SSE suite pattern ported with real tools on the other side of the mock, giving loop-semantics tests without providers; the ceiling it shares with all anchors is that no model evals run in CI (caps verification at 8).

subject: tura
title: A CI job runs a Runtime Session equivalence gate against committed baselines with explicit failure-injection evidence artifacts uploaded each run
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:228-244 (Run Runtime Session equivalence gate; baseline.json, core-e2e.json, failure-injection.json uploads); tests/equivalence/runtime_session/ (runner, reference/, evidence json)
one_why: A refactor-grade behavioral contract that fails the build on drift and ships evidence - close to evals-in-CI in spirit without needing a model; exact gate semantics only partially verified from the runner scripts.

subject: tura
title: Cache discipline is append-only by construction: provider messages stored immutably per log record with stable per-result cache ids, and a stable per-session prompt_cache_key gated by provider support with four property tests
evidence: crates/runtime/src/context/build.rs:440-490 (immutable_context_messages_from_log_entry); crates/runtime/src/context/tool_results.rs:134,385 (stable_context_cache_id); crates/runtime/src/provider_flow/request_options.rs:163-178 and tests :525-596; crates/provider/src/llm/claude_code.rs:410-460 (cache_control ephemeral)
one_why: Compaction rewrites a record boundary rather than reshaping history, so provider-side prefixes stay cacheable across turns and across compaction; no cache warming (pi's edge) and coarse bytes/4 token estimates keep it below codex-9.

subject: tura
title: Internal process boundary is a documented anti-HTTP rule: gateway hosts the router, runtime workers are spawned subprocesses driven over a stdin/stdout JSON line envelope, and child-agent dispatch goes through the router CLI - never a URL - protected by contract crates
evidence: crates/runtime/src/manas/child_dispatch.rs:1-5 (binding rule comment: No internal URL communication may be introduced); crates/runtime/src/worker.rs:1-14 (line protocol envelope); Cargo.toml:26-31 (router_contract, runtime_contract, session_log_contract)
one_why: Removes localhost-port attack surface and makes orphan/process recovery the OS's job (reap + watchdog) instead of a reconnect protocol; contract crates keep the wire types honest across the workspace.

subject: waveloom
title: Monotonic compaction decision set: once a message is snipped/pruned the decision never regresses, so compaction never rewrites the cached prefix
evidence: pkg/compaction/compaction.go:64-115 (compactionDecisionSet canApply/upsert, prune>snip only); pkg/compaction/compactor.go:145-193 (Snapshot/Restore persists decisions across resume)
one_why: Tier cursors + an ordered decision ledger make every compaction choice idempotent per message index; the strongest prefix-cache-safety mechanism found in the corpus, tested by pkg/compaction/compaction_test.go monotonicity specs.

subject: waveloom
title: Four-tier watermarks (snip/prune/summarize/hard-stop) triggered on real API usage and recalibrated from 148 real sessions
evidence: pkg/compaction/compaction.go:1-13 (tier design), 31-47 (45/65/85/98 with written recalibration rationale: old 60/80/95 peaks never reached in 148 sessions)
one_why: Tiers 1-2 are zero-API local transforms; thresholds carry measured-session justification in-code, an evidence-driven calibration practice most subjects lack.

subject: waveloom
title: Forked subagents fire byte-aligned with the parent's cached prefix, tools array included; parent-only tools become explicit error stubs
evidence: pkg/agentloop/execute.go:69-76 (WithParentTools, '同 messages 换 tools → 零命中'); pkg/agentloop/loop.go:100-104,945-951 (ToolsOverride); CHANGELOG.en.md v0.8.2 (error-stub tools + whole-turn truncation + measured 1.44M-refuse guard)
one_why: DeepSeek prefix cache forks on any tools-array difference, so naive subagents drop cache hits to zero; aligning the fork's first request with the parent's last cached payload is a measurable, copyable win.

subject: waveloom
title: Project-directory hook configs (.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, .waveloom/settings.json) load and execute with no trust prompt
evidence: cmd/waveloom/main.go:739-789 (hookSettingsPaths includes repo-relative .claude/settings.json and .waveloom/settings.json; hooks run at startup and PreToolUse/PostToolUse)
one_why: Cloning a hostile repo and running waveloom inside it is arbitrary code execution on first tool use; no grep hit for any trust/confirm gate on hooks anywhere in cmd/ or pkg/hook/.

subject: waveloom
title: Skill allowed-tools bash whitelist is sticky and bypasses the RiskHigh hard-block for all later bash calls until the next skill load
evidence: pkg/permission/guard.go:104-127 (SetSkillBashWhitelist '持续到下一个 skill 加载'), 278-292 (Step 2.5 returns ALLOW before Step 3 hard blocks)
one_why: Whitelists borrowed from an installed skill's allowed-tools outlive the skill invocation, converting a per-skill grant into a session-wide hole under the deny-rules floor.

subject: waveloom
title: LD_PRELOAD/DYLD_*/NODE_OPTIONS commands hard-denied ahead of every short-circuiting allow path
evidence: pkg/permission/guard.go:236-255 (Step 0.5 with written laundering rationale: ask-rules under autoAllow and skill whitelist would let the stripped command pass checks then inject at exec)
one_why: Placement is the finding: the block runs before ask-rule and whitelist short-circuits precisely because those paths would only ever see the sanitized command.

subject: waveloom
title: Parser-differential detectors: 23 checks over mvdan/sh AST flag inputs where naive shell-quote tokenization and bash disagree (CR mid-token, mid-word '#'), routed to ASK
evidence: pkg/bash/security.go:3,135,813-847,1000; pkg/permission/guard.go:429-435 (IsParse issue → DecisionAsk, never silent allow)
one_why: Goes beyond grammar-parsed policy (kimi-code/smelt) by explicitly hunting the differential between the checker's tokenizer and bash's own.

subject: waveloom
title: Backoff ladder 3/5/8 keyed on (error-kind, tool) pairs with tool-specialized recovery text; rate-limit errors exempt from fatal escalation
evidence: pkg/agentloop/execute.go:770-833 (pair tracking, warn thresholds at 3/5, fatal at 8; edit-specific 're-read only' text; rate-limit resets instead of escalating to avoid killing crawl tasks); pkg/agentloop/loop.go:152-166
one_why: Nuance over the familiar 3/5/8 ladder (kimi-code): guidance text differs per failure class and the breaker deliberately declines to fire on shared-host rate limits.

subject: waveloom
title: Session-level per-host ThrottleStore turns 429/403 into model-readable errors carrying earliest-retry time; subagents inherit the store
evidence: pkg/tool/throttle.go:12-22 (session-level per-host state, nested-loop passthrough); pkg/tool/web_fetch.go:269-270 (Retry-After scheduled, in-window requests short-circuit without network); pkg/agentloop/execute.go:806-812
one_why: CHANGELOG v0.8.2 records the behavioral fix: previously the model responded to throttling by switching User-Agent and hammering harder; explicit retry semantics in the error text stopped that.

subject: waveloom
title: Detects 'preview' assistant text ending in a colon/arrow/ellipsis with no tool call and grants exactly one grace turn to re-issue it
evidence: pkg/agentloop/loop.go:737-760 (previewWarned + previewGraceStep through shouldContinue), 1056-1114 (hasPreviewSuffix with 16 Unicode colon-variant codepoints and two written REGRESSION notes)
one_why: Eval-measured DeepSeek behavior ('启动 xxx:' then no tool call) treated as a first-class loop hazard with a one-shot, max-steps-aware repair path; the Unicode-variant regression history is documented in-code.

subject: waveloom
title: Five-layer tool-output pipeline: unicode sanitize, injection-pattern scan with warning prefix, untrusted-source boundary tag, high-risk source escalation, 256KB UTF-8-safe truncation
evidence: pkg/agentloop/execute.go:727-760 (layers 1-5 inline, '[tool_result from X — EXTERNAL UNTRUSTED SOURCE]'); pkg/tool/sanitize.go:30; pkg/tool/scan.go:22
one_why: Layered ordering is explicit and applied to every tool result uniformly; scan hits switch the model from executing instructions to auditing them per the comment.

subject: waveloom
title: 'proplan' routing: plan-mode runs the pro model, everything else flash, with a 200k-context downgrade guard and a never-leak-sentinel invariant
evidence: pkg/agentloop/loop.go:152 (planProMaxContextTokens), 882-935 (resolveModel with fallback chain ensuring the 'proplan' sentinel string can never reach the API)
one_why: Cost-routed model selection with defensive anchor fallbacks (both anchors self-referential → client default); a clean copy of the opusplan idea with an explicit over-window guard.

subject: waveloom
title: Headless entries (ACP/one-shot) auto-activate the OS sandbox even with sandbox.enabled=false, but degrade to fully-unsandboxed auto-allow when bwrap is absent unless failIfUnavailable=true
evidence: cmd/waveloom/acp.go:122-135 (EnableAutoAllow + sandbox auto-activate comment); cmd/waveloom/sandbox_setup.go:55-110; pkg/sandbox/config.go:101-112 (defaults: disabled, fail-open, network on, no read-masking; stderr warning only)
one_why: The right instinct (no-interaction implies sandbox), but the default failure mode of a missing backend is auto-allow + bare execution with a warning; exfiltration of unmasked ~/.ssh in net-on mode is warned about, never prevented.

subject: waveloom
title: Three-layer edit-eval harness exists but no eval job in CI, and the documented Layer-1 suite points at deleted paths
evidence: eval/llmedit/README.md:8-16 (commands reference pkg/hashline/eval and cmd/editbench — neither exists in the tree); .github/workflows/ci.yml has no eval target
one_why: The deterministic layer README itself calls 'CI 回归防线' is unrunnable as documented; evals exist as artifacts, not as gates.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: 378 semantic unit tests plus an eval harness and 14 e2e scripts, none executed by any CI workflow
evidence: .github/workflows/build.yml:70-96 (steps are build/package/release only); grep 'cargo test' .github/ = 0 hits; security-audit.yml:23-24 runs only cargo-audit+cargo-deny
one_why: The tests are real property tests (grant-class cross-talk, trust-gate env handling, cache_control marking at src/llm_client/anthropic.rs:527) so a single cargo-test job on push would convert the subject's biggest paper strength into actual regression defense; today every claim of 'tested' is unenforced.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Compaction trigger projects the tokens of skills that WOULD be injected this turn, not just current context
evidence: src/session/turn.rs:74-93 (projected_skill_tokens computed before ctx_pct check), :121 (auto-compact at projected >= 90%), :107-119 (hard stop at 100% when budget set)
one_why: Fixes the classic hole where a window at '75%' plus a fat skill match overflows the model anyway: the same rank_and_truncate pass that builds the injection is run speculatively first, so the threshold sees the payload the model will actually receive.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Keyword-matched skills are ranked and truncated to a per-turn skill_token_budget, with the effective token cost shown per turn
evidence: src/skill_manager.rs:790-802 (match_skills_scoped with domain scope); src/session/turn.rs:148-158 (rank_and_truncate_skills to config.skill_token_budget), :382-386 (per-turn 'skills Nt' cost line)
one_why: Converges with the lazy-skill-loading cluster (kolega-code's budget idea, maki's index-only prompt); zap's unit is whole skill bodies per matched turn with a default 4000-token cap and visible accounting, which makes the injection decision debuggable turn by turn (skill_trace at turn.rs:160-170).

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Unconnected MCP servers occupy zero tool slots: one synthetic mcp_connect tool names them, and connecting is a model-initiated tool call
evidence: src/tools/mod.rs:221-244 (synthetic mcp_connect appended only when pending servers exist), :138 (load_mcp_lazy), tests :305-385
one_why: Lazy MCP without any search-tool machinery: N servers cost one tool definition instead of hundreds of schemas, and the model pays the connect cost only when a task actually needs that server -- a cheaper cousin of tool-search approaches.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Repo-local hooks.json and .mcp.json are inert until the directory is explicitly trusted (env / .zap/trusted marker / ~/.zap/trusted_dirs)
evidence: src/trust.rs:1-58 (three trust paths, canonicalized path compare), :73+ (unit tests incl. env-lock for parallel-safety)
one_why: Converges with pi's project-trust gate; the framing comment ('cloning and opening an untrusted repo cannot execute its hooks/servers') plus a one-line untrusted_hint() at the point of skip makes the gate discoverable instead of silent -- the skip-then-hint pattern is the portable part.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Two-tier substring patterns: hard-block list rejects even in Auto mode; destructive list forces a confirmation prompt even in Auto mode
evidence: src/tools/shell.rs:14 (BLOCKED_PATTERNS) and :97-115 (DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERNS with per-pattern reason strings), escalation wired at src/session/tools.rs:83
one_why: The interesting wrinkle over the standard denylist anti-pattern is the second tier: Auto mode is not blanket-auto, patterns like force-push or 'drop table' downgrade themselves to NeedsPrompt with a human-readable reason -- partial credit despite the whole thing being bypassable (which SECURITY.md:14-16 admits verbatim).

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: SECURITY.md grades each sandbox mode by whether it is a security boundary and calls its own denylist 'trivially bypassed'
evidence: docs/SECURITY.md:14-16 ('not a security boundary ... trivially bypassed with encoding, variable indirection'), :22-28 (off/workdir/container boundary table)
one_why: Converges with pi's honesty rung; zap goes further by labeling the weak middle mode (workdir = just current_dir, honestly marked 'Weak') instead of letting the word 'sandbox' imply enforcement -- an antipattern-inoculation doc other subjects should copy at the concept level.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Session 'always' grants work on tool-classes: approving edit_file grants write/batch/undo as one semantic unit while shell stays isolated
evidence: src/permission_manager.rs:13-21 (tool_grant_class), tests :250-280 (grant must fill the class and must NOT spill to shell)
one_why: Killstops the prompt-fatigue loop where four names for 'modify a file' each demand their own always-approval, while keeping the read/write-vs-shell boundary intact; the class + negative-spill test pair is the transferable artifact.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: SLM-mode loop breaker: exact equality of the previous round's {name:input} fingerprint set triggers a one-shot anti-loop nudge inside the next tool result, not an abort
evidence: src/session/turn.rs:500-537 (prev_call_fingerprints set compare, nudge appended to tool_msg)
one_why: Converges with crush's breaker but tuned for small chatty local models: identical-argument repetition means the model cannot gain new information, so the fix is an injected conclusion-prompt rather than killing the turn; cheap and falsifiable (set equality, one-shot).

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: MIT declared in Cargo.toml but no LICENSE file anywhere in the tree
evidence: Cargo.toml:10 (license = "MIT"); find . -iname '*license*' (excl. .git) returns nothing
one_why: A manifest SPDX field states intent but is not a grant of rights in most jurisdictions; until upstream adds the text, any reuse assessment must treat the repo as undeclared -- all findings here are concept-only and effort_for_us assumes clean-room implementation.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Per-turn task classifier swaps the provider/model for one turn from user-declared model_routes, then restores on exit -- including on every early-return path
evidence: src/session/routing.rs:12-27 (classify -> route -> save), src/session/turn.rs:68 (route_for_turn) with restore_routing called on budget-stop :119, error :369, and turn end :566
one_why: Routing granularity is the turn, not the session: cheap model for 'what is this repo', frontier model for refactor turns, and the save/restore discipline means a mid-turn error cannot strand the session on the wrong client -- the restore-on-all-paths pattern is what most routing designs get wrong.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: System prompt is chosen per turn class: casual greeting prompt (~12 tokens of persona), ~400-token SLM prompt, or full prompt -- with the compaction projection honoring the same class split
evidence: src/context_manager.rs:5-14 (build_casual_system_prompt, 'Saves ~6-8k tokens'), :20-46 (build_slm_system_prompt targeting ~400 tokens), src/session/turn.rs:78 (is_casual gates projected skill tokens to 0), :300-310 (casual sends last message only, no tools)

subject: cline

subject: cline

evidence: sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/compaction.ts:342-354

subject: codebuff

subject: codebuff

subject: codebuff

subject: deepagents

subject: deepagents

subject: deepagents

subject: ferrum

subject: gptme

subject: gptme

subject: gptme

one_why: Measures tokens of the prepared provider messages, not the raw log, so a compaction that reorganizes without shrinking can never loop into a second guaranteed-overflow call - a cheap anti-wedge invariant most ladder implementations (grok-cli, grinta, maki) lack.

subject: grinta-coding-agent

subject: grinta-coding-agent

evidence: .github/workflows/integration-runner.yml:31-44 (detect requires backend/evaluation/agent_eval_pack.py and evaluation/integration_tests/scripts/run_infer.sh) vs ls evaluation/ = __init__.py + deepswe only; :57-64 runs 'Integration workflow skipped (assets missing)' whenever available != true - the permanent state; same shape self-declared at .github/workflows/vscode-extension-build.yml:4

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Security-analyzer exception falls the effective risk DOWN to the model's own declared level, LOW when undeclared
evidence: backend/execution/aes/security_enforcement.py:526-541 (except Exception -> analyzer_risk=None; declared UNKNOWN -> LOW) vs :543-551 (analyzer can only escalate when it succeeds)
one_why: The classifier normally ratchets upward, but any analyzer crash converts an unclassified shell command into model-self-certified LOW - the exact inverse of deepagents' classifier-unavailable -> require_human fail-closed (auto_mode.py:3542-3546); joins the fail-open family watch (gptme confirm fail-open, nanocoder jail fail-open) as the classifier-exception variant.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: Codex provider rides the user's ChatGPT subscription OAuth from a third-party loop via chatgpt.com/backend-api - ruled ToS/license class, not safety-hole
evidence: backend/inference/clients/codex_app_server.py:1-6 (module docstring: managed OAuth + direct Responses endpoint, Grinta owns loop/approvals) and :34 (_CODEX_RESPONSES_BASE_URL = https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex)
one_why: Boundary taxonomy ruling: no protection mechanism inside Grinta is advertised-but-inert (so not safety-hole); the exposure is the TERMS of credential use - subscription auth licensed for first-party Codex surfaces, account-action risk lands on the end user - which is the same usage-terms bin as kode-cli's Apache self-grant and manifest-only licenses; stays distinct from claurst-2 oauth-client-impersonation (active client/TLS spoofing) because Grinta declares its posture openly and does not evade gates; concepts-only portables.

subject: grinta-coding-agent
title: sandboxed_local profile hard-fails when the OS jail binary is missing (all three platforms incl. a Windows AppContainer path) and offers whole-FS immutability instead of command classification
evidence: backend/execution/sandboxing.py:205-213,222-224 (RuntimeError when bwrap/sandbox-exec absent, no silent fallback); sandboxing.py:4-6 (bubblewrap / sandbox-exec / AppContainer); backend/core/config/security_config.py:71-81 (readonly_workspace mounts the workspace read-only 'rather than classifying shell commands as read or write (unreliable...)')
one_why: The two decisions most harnesses get wrong in one config: no fail-open when the jail is unavailable (vs nanocoder's plain-sh fallback), and encoding read-only delegation as filesystem immutability rather than another regex ladder; still opt-in (execution_profile='standard' default) and interactive terminals bypass isolation by design - honest at sandboxing.py:7-10 - which keeps the subject's safety at 7, not 8.

subject: hax
title: Prompt-only restraint with explicit anti-deception documentation: the reference rung-3 - honesty buys exactly one rung up out of codel's misleading band, no further
evidence: docs/philosophy.md:74-84 ("No permission prompts... it is not a security boundary"; "control and restraint, not enforcement") + README.md:32-34 ("If you want... per-command permission prompts, other agents build exactly that - hax deliberately doesn't") + src/agent_core.c:51-53 (restraint is prompt text) + src/config.c:93 (max_turns default 0 = unbounded)
one_why: Together with kolkrabbi this settles the corpus honesty-credit question: deception cost codel its bottom-of-2 (README contradicted behavior); hax's identical mechanics plus candid labeling land at 3, the ceiling for absent machinery - so honesty is worth one rung upward out of misleading, never a substitute for enforcement; rung 4+ requires binding machinery regardless of disclosure.

subject: hax
title: Push-gating CI carries ASan+UBSan, TSan, AND boot-VM FreeBSD/OpenBSD jobs that run the identical suite - sanitizer and port regressions block the commit
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-5,33-38 (ubuntu-asan/ubuntu-tsan on every push/PR), ci.yml:74-86 (cross-platform-actions FreeBSD 15.1 + OpenBSD 7.9), scripts/check.sh:100-107 (build-asan -> -Db_sanitize=address,undefined; build-tsan -> -Db_sanitize=thread), Makefile:11-12
one_why: Sanitizer builds are common as nightly advisories; hax makes them same-workflow same-event gate jobs, and adds booted BSD VMs running the same tests - the strongest C-language safety-net wiring found in the corpus short of codex's scale, and directly copyable.

subject: hax
title: Python e2e suite drives the built binary through the mock provider and is registered in the same meson suite, so the real executable's full loop runs under ASan and TSan on every push
evidence: tests/meson.build:151-166 (e2e scenarios registered as meson tests driving the binary via tests/e2e/harness.py), scripts/mock/ (8 scripted transcripts incl. interrupt_stall.txt, tool_roundtrip.txt)
one_why: Most subjects keep e2e out of the sanitizer runs (separate nightly or dev-only); wiring the process-level scenarios into the same test target means memory and thread bugs in the actual binary's loop are caught by the same blocking jobs.

subject: hax
title: Zero fuzz targets and no model evals in CI - a wire-parsing C agent that hand-tests SSE/JSON bodies but never fuzzes them
evidence: grep -ri 'LLVMFuzzer|fuzz' across src tests scripts .github = 0 hits; .github/workflows has no eval job; parsing surface is real (src/providers/anthropic_events.c, chat_events.c, responses_events.c, src/transport/sse)
one_why: The errata's 8-ceiling applies, but for a memory-unsafe language parsing untrusted network bytes into malloc'd structures, missing fuzzers is the one verification gap that could actually bite users - ASan without fuzz is a detector with no search.

subject: hax
title: Prefix-cache-stability as an ingestion invariant: the aggregate image budget drops only the just-read image, and compaction keeps normal tools advertised, so prior request bytes never change
evidence: src/agent_loop.c:224-230 ("Dropping the just-read image (rather than degrading older ones at serialization) keeps prior requests byte-stable, so the provider prefix cache survives"), src/compact.c:241 ("Advertising the normal tools preserves the provider's cached request prefix. Calls are...")
one_why: Most cache-aware compaction tunes when to fire (agentty) or marks blocks (prompt-cache-marking); hax encodes a monotonicity rule at the ingestion point - new budget pressure may only evict the newest item, never rewrite history - which is the property the cache actually requires.

subject: hax
title: Subagents are ordinary hax -p background tasks with an env-carried depth guard, not a bespoke runtime: recursion limit shipped as a shell variable
evidence: src/tools/bash_env.c:84,112 (subagent_depth_assignment injected into every tool shell), docs/usage.md:240-243 (presets with descriptions advertised as delegation roles)
one_why: Delegation with zero new machinery - the subagent IS the same binary under the same task registry - but note depth enforcement is env-based (a subagent could unset it), so it is runaway-protection, not a boundary; pair with hax-b1 for the pattern's safety ceiling.

subject: jazz
title: Usage-feedback-calibrated token counter with measured request-overhead gap
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/context/token-counter.ts:342-401
one_why: Pre-call trigger stays an estimate (exact BPE only for OpenAI families) but every provider usage.promptTokens response retrains the per-model chars/token ratio AND measures request overhead as usage-minus-estimated-messages, closing the 10-30k MCP-schema blind spot that cline-style thresholds have; nuance vs pi: estimate-plus-correction rather than measured projection.

subject: jazz

evidence: packages/adapters/src/llm/ai-sdk-service.ts:520-529
one_why: Context/budget/time/cost pressure messages ride the request uncached and the breakpoint walks back to the last persisted message, so per-turn changing guidance never spends the incremental cache write on content guaranteed to miss - tested at ai-sdk-service.test.ts:1979-1998; no other anchor treats nudging and cache-prefix stability as one design problem.

subject: jazz
title: Fail-closed LLM command-risk classifier gates execute_command
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/tools/command-risk.ts:1-29
one_why: A cheap 16-token-classifier model labels read-only/low-risk/high-risk with 8s timeout, and timeouts, errors, and ambiguous replies all stay high-risk; classifier tokens are metered separately from loop totals (agent-run-metrics.ts) so approval gating is observable apart from the conversation.

subject: jazz
title: Per-conversation OS uid + JAZZ_HOME isolation for multi-user bot bridges
evidence: packages/bot-shared/src/chat-sandbox.ts:1-28
one_why: One bridge process serves many strangers; instead of filename-prefix isolation (which every tool call steps past) each conversation gets its own uid and setgid-stamped home so the kernel enforces the split - honest about the ceiling: engages only when the bridge runs as root, degrades to shared dir elsewhere.

subject: jazz
title: Full A/B eval harness never invoked by any CI workflow
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:176-179
one_why: evals/ has tasks, judge, held-model A/B, and memory-judgment calibration (evals/README.md) but zero of the seven workflows reference evals and the only cron builds a plugin catalog (community-plugin-catalog.yml:6); per errata a cost-capped nightly live-eval job would break the verification-8 ceiling that jazz otherwise sits under.

subject: jazz
title: A2A server door on the existing trust model, tested against the official SDK's parser
evidence: packages/adapters/src/peers/a2a.ts:1-27
one_why: A2A wire format (agent card, SendMessageResponse, PascalCase JSON-RPC) is validated by parsing with @a2a-js/sdk classes (a2a.test.ts:70) and authorization reuses jazz's own tier/persona/bearer-token model instead of a second trust system; deliberately minimal (one sync method, no task lifecycle) - the only A2A surface found across all studied subjects.

subject: jazz
title: Parking restricted to lone tool calls so resume replay is exactly-once
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/run/resume.ts:1-8
one_why: A run that parks for a human replays its stopped batch rather than re-entering the executor mid-batch; because parking is only allowed on a lone tool call, replay is exactly one tool running once with its approval already answered - durable RunRecord (run-record.ts:1-12) carries parked-turn snapshots that are dropped on resume.

subject: jazz
title: Four-rung overflow ladder with config-enforced ordering (trim above compact above warn above clear)
evidence: packages/core/src/agent/context/context-window-manager.ts:21-41
one_why: Clear 0.5 / warn 0.7 / compact 0.8 / trim 0.95 with the ordering as a validated property: config resolution rejects a compact ratio at-or-above trim and warn at-or-above compact (context-thresholds.test.ts:36-49), so a user misconfiguration can never silently collapse the ladder into a sliding window.

subject: keen-code
title: Compact trigger measures the actual serialized outbound request before EVERY tool turn - but tokens stay a len/3 heuristic and provider usage never feeds back
evidence: internal/llm/anthropic.go:593-596,553-563; internal/llm/core/context.go:7-12,22-34; internal/llm/auto_compaction_test.go:105
one_why: A mid-ladder rung between history-shape triggers (crush-6) and pi's exact projected context: estimateAnthropicInput JSON-marshals the exact messages about to ship (so pending tool results count immediately), threshold = window - max(4096,w/20) - further 10%, and the boundary is property-tested to the token (85500 fires, 85499 does not) - but usage events incl. cached_tokens (anthropic.go:711-720) are display-only, so unlike cline's token-estimator-feedback the estimator can never self-correct; 5 provider paths re-implement the same trigger inline.

subject: keen-code
title: Dual message cache breakpoints (stable turn-start boundary + last message) cleared/reapplied per turn, with stale-marker stripping asserted at the wire
evidence: internal/llm/anthropic.go:228-258,644,676; internal/llm/anthropic_test.go:984,1030,1063
one_why: Every turn starts from a marker-free clone (clearAnthropicCacheControl), then places system/tools/turn-start/last ephemeral markers; post-compaction the stable boundary resets so breakpoints follow the new prefix; tests capture the actual request params and assert EXACT marker counts (3 normal, 2 one-shot) and that stale pending-state markers are stripped - the test idiom is the portable part, joining the jazz/g3 breakpoint cluster; missing vs 8.5+ rungs: no warming/keepalive and no realized-cache-hit validation.

subject: keen-code
title: Anti-scope-amnesia: session allow-grants are toolName-keyed but structurally never honored for elevated risk, and danger is computed independent of the model's own flag
evidence: internal/cli/repl/permissions/requester.go:73,97; internal/tools/bash.go:151; internal/tools/bashclassifier.go:39-58,133-140; internal/tools/bash_test.go:477
one_why: Direct counterexample to neovate's approval-scope amnesia (same category-level cache key, wrong handling): `if !isDangerous && sessionAllowedTools[toolName]` means an allow-session for bash NEVER covers a dangerous command - the cache cannot ride a risk-class elevation - and bash.go gates on `isDangerous || IsDangerousCommand(command)` so model under-reporting cannot disarm the prompt (bash_test.go:477 proves the classifier binds with no LLM flag; classifier suite covers compound, subshell, redirection, env-secret forms); hotdog rule: caches may key coarse IF the key's scope cannot widen into a higher risk class without re-prompt.

subject: keen-code
title: Subagent registries ship a hard-wired unconditional AutoApprover - delegated bash/write/edit/MCP never surface a user prompt
evidence: internal/subagents/tool_factory.go:13-15,31-45; internal/subagents/runner.go:57
one_why: Negative pole of the opencode non-escalation precedent: child registries are constructed with approver=always-true, so containment is only filesystem.Guard + profile tool-list - a dangerous command inside a subagent classifies, requests, and self-approves silently, splitting the user's threat model between parent and child surfaces; bounded (guard, timeouts) so no score dock at the 6-rung, but delegation must inherit the parent's LIVE requester or narrow, never widen.

subject: keen-code
title: Token-map bash classifier with recursive subshell expansion sits between regex deny-lists and grammar parsing - interpreter payloads remain unreachable
evidence: internal/tools/bashclassifier.go:60-75,114-140; internal/tools/bashclassifier_test.go:211,265,292
one_why: Splits command segments, recurses into subshells, maps base commands + dangerous subcommands + conditional flags + an env-secret regex - meaningfully stronger than substring/regex deny-lists (zot) but, like all corpus deny-lists, `python -c 'shutil.rmtree(...)'` executes unflagged; corpus strictness order: token-map-with-recursion (keen) > regex-denylist > substring; grammar-parsed (maki/codex) still the ceiling.

subject: keen-code
title: Wire-capture test idiom: mock stream seam captures the full outbound request struct and tests assert on the serialized payload
evidence: internal/llm/anthropic_test.go:984-1110; internal/tools/bash_test.go:232-294
one_why: streamImpl captures anthropic.MessageNewParams and tests marshal it to assert cache-marker counts, absence of top-level cache control, and stale-marker stripping - correctness is pinned at the wire contract rather than internal state, which is why this T1 solo project's 35.9k test LOC actually constrain provider-request behavior (all blocking under go test -race, go.yml:29-30); the cheapest verification-shape upgrade path for subjects stuck at existence tests.

subject: kilocode

subject: kimi-code

subject: kimi-code

evidence: AGENTS.md:3 ('Keep runtime dependencies directed from Schema to Core and Protocol...'); no dependency-cruiser or eslint-boundaries config anywhere (find over repo: only .oxlintrc.json and packages/vscode eslint config); packages/core/package.json dependencies: 20 '@ai-sdk/*' entries plus aws/google-auth/gitlab/venice/openrouter provider packages; contrast packages/schema/package.json dependencies: effect only (true leaf)
one_why: The Schema->Core->Protocol layering is real in the leaf packages and DI nodes, but nothing mechanical stops a reverse import; codex's crate graph is compiler-enforced, cline's SDK split is package-enforced - here the law is a comment.

subject: opencode
title: Revert is event-sourced and per-file: each step records a snapshot id, revert plans file-level restores from projected rows and stages a reversible event
evidence: packages/core/src/session/revert.ts:27-57 (plan: walks assistant rows after boundary seq, maps each RelativePath to its snapshot.start tree), :60-96 (stage restores files and publishes RevertEvent.Staged with diff), :98-120 (clear/commit as events); packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts (807 LOC git-dir snapshot engine); packages/opencode/test/session/revert-compact.test.ts (683 LOC)
one_why: Stronger than cline's git-stash checkpoints (checkpoint-revert anchors): the restore target per file is durably recorded in the message projection itself, so revert survives process restart and composes with compaction - but only in V2; V1 keeps its own older revert path (opencode/src/session/revert.ts:37-90).

subject: opencode

subject: opencode

subject: opencode
title: No sandbox of any kind; documented outright, with sandbox escapes declared out of scope

The permission system exists as a UX feature"; Out-of-Scope table row "Sandbox escapes"); grep -riE 'seatbelt|bwrap|bubblewrap|landlock|seccomp' over packages/opencode/src + packages/core/src = zero enforcement hits; boundary code is only path-containment asks (packages/opencode/src/tool/external-directory.ts:17-44 containsPath -> ctx.ask)

subject: opencode
title: Shipped default ruleset is `*: allow`: bash, edit, write, apply_patch, webfetch all auto-approved out of the box; only external_directory, *.env reads, doom_loop and three utility tools gate
evidence: packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:119-135 (defaults = fromConfig({"*":"allow", doom_loop:"ask", external_directory:{"*":"ask",...}, question/plan_enter/plan_exit deny, read:{"*.env":"ask"}})); :143-158 build agent = defaults + user config only; explore subagent adds bash/webfetch allow :205-206; user opt-in required to get asks (cfg.permission merged last :137)

SECURITY.md's honest 'UX feature' line arguably concedes this, but nowhere states the default is allow, and nanocoder's 'real machinery + wrong defaults' was anchored to 5 for less: here defaults at least match the declared threat model.

subject: opencode
title: Zero named prompt-injection defense: web/websearch/MCP output enters history unmarked; webfetch has no SSRF guard; MCP connect auto-enables
evidence: grep -riE 'injection|untrusted|prompt attack' over packages/opencode/src + packages/core/src = only review-prompt template text (packages/opencode/src/command/template/review.txt:49); packages/opencode/src/tool/webfetch.ts:76-126 (fetch arbitrary URL, size/type caps only, no localhost/169.254/private-range check); packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts:650,941 (createAndStore with enabled:true on connect); no output markers or provenance flags on tool results entering durable history
one_why: Combined with s2+s3 this is the real attack chain of the subject: poisoned page or MCP response -> model with default-allow unsandboxed shell. No anchor subject except codel is this open; pi/cline at least ask per command by default so the chain needs a human slip, not just a model slip.

subject: opencode
title: Shell tool parses the command into an AST and issues per-subcommand asks (bash patterns + external_directory globs) before spawning, tested for bash and PowerShell incl. nested and conditional forms
evidence: packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:257-261 (tree-sitter-style bash/ps parse), :263-290 (ask: external_directory globs for scanned dirs, then bash patterns from scan), :627 (ask precedes execution); packages/opencode/test/tool/shell.test.ts:222-475 ("asks for bash permission with correct pattern" :223, nested bash :346, PowerShell conditionals :267, drive-relative and $HOME paths :430-475)

subject: opencode
title: The command-prefix dictionary that decides what an approval *means* was generated by an LLM prompt, prompt preserved in-source, guarded by 33 lines of tests
evidence: packages/opencode/src/permission/arity.ts:14-30 (verbatim generation prompt: 'You are generating a dictionary of command-prefix arities...'); :22-163 (hand-adopted ARITY table); :1-9 prefix(): longest-prefix lookup, unknown commands collapse to first token; tests packages/opencode/test/permission/arity.test.ts:1-33 (5 happy-path tests, no adversarial cases e.g. `python -c` under `python` arity 2)
one_why: Approving 'git *' or 'python *' is defined by an unreviewed LLM's token-count intuition, and edits to the table are cheap; codex anchored the 10 with a purpose-built execpolicy DSL (execpolicy/src/rule.rs:111,149) - a prefix-arity dictionary is the opposite end of the grammar-design spectrum.

subject: opencode

evidence: packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:55-63 (addFinalizer fails all pending with RejectedError), :117-127 (reject cascades to same-session pendings), :137-155 (always persists allow rules and resolves newly-matching pendings); packages/opencode/test/permission/next.test.ts:777,808,843 (always persists / reject cancels session / other session stays pending), :966 (it.live directory isolation), :1019,:1046 (dispose + reload reject), :1149 (abort clears pending)

subject: opencode
title: No fuzzing, no in-CI model evals; tool-permission tests stub ctx.ask, so no end-to-end 'rejected -> process never spawned' spec through the real service

subject: opencode
title: Crash story is V1 snapshot/revert only: no sqlite-corruption recovery, V2 durability explicitly unchecked, interruption is interrupt-only cause swallowing
evidence: grep -rniE 'CORRUPT|recovery|integrity' over packages/core/src/database + packages/opencode/src/storage = zero; packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts:44-60 (TODO checklist: durable busy/retrying/idle/interrupted status, stale-work rejection unchecked); packages/core/src/session/execution/local.ts:23-27 (Cause.hasInterruptsOnly ? Effect.void : log); user-facing recovery = packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts git snapshots + revert; packages/core/src/event.ts:180 (TODO: bind durable projectors to exact type+version); specs/v2/session.md:32 (activity is not durable across process restarts)
one_why: Scoring crash behavior must anchor on V1's snapshot/revert, not V2's aspirational checklist; a mid-run crash inside a permission-parked Deferred relies on the dispose/reload finalizer (index.ts:55-63) tested at :1019/:1046 - which is, at least, a real answer. Crash posture is process-local by the core lane's own admission: between process death and a fresh wake, status is unknowable and a corrupt journal has no documented recovery path - honestly self-declared unchecked, but it is what keeps V2 operability one rung under codex.

subject: opencode

evidence: packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts:232-242 (compactIfNeeded estimates {system,messages,tools} of the built LLMRequest against context - max(output, buffer)); :12-13 DEFAULT_BUFFER 20k / KEEP 8k; V1 contrast packages/opencode/src/session/overflow.ts:22-33 (isOverflow uses provider-returned tokens incl. cache read/write vs usable())

subject: opencode

evidence: packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:28-30 (PRUNE_MINIMUM 20k / PRUNE_PROTECT 40k / protected 'skill'), :273-315 (prune walks backwards, marks part.state.time.compacted), :115-121 preserveRecentBudget = clamp(2k, 25% of usable, 15k), :208-228 select() with splitTurn mid-turn budget split; opt-in gate at :274 (cfg.compaction?.prune)

subject: opencode

evidence: packages/llm/src/cache-policy.ts:1-36 (default 'auto' = tools+system+latest-user-message with the 1.25x-write/0.1x-read math spelled out; implicit-caching protocols skipped :29-31), :56-74 (single-pass substitution, profiled); packages/llm/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts:234-252 (ANTHROPIC_BREAKPOINT_CAP=4, cacheControl drops+counts over-cap hints), :534-537 (warn log naming the drop count); packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts:204,214 (promptCacheKey derived from session id)
one_why: No anchor does this: pi-8 warms caches, codex-9 gates on cache keys, cline-7 has none - opencode budgets and audits breakpoints themselves at the wire layer, then reinforces them with the Context Epoch immutable baseline (context-epoch.ts:39-80).

subject: opencode
title: The shipping V1 path pins cache breakpoints with a static heuristic - first two system messages plus last two messages - fanned across six provider option shapes
evidence: packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts:358-400 (applyCaching: system.slice(0,2) + msgs.slice(-2); providerOptions map for anthropic/openrouter/bedrock/openaiCompatible/copilot/alibaba; message-level vs content-level choice per provider), :483 (call site)
one_why: Cache discipline exists in the shipped binary, not only in unreleased V2 - but it is a fixed-shape heuristic without the cap accounting or TTL buckets of packages/llm, so the 4-breakpoint guarantee rests on the constant '2+2' never exceeding the API cap.

subject: opencode
title: Oversized tool output is offloaded to a managed on-disk directory (2000 lines / 50KB caps, 7-day retention GC) instead of being silently truncated into oblivion
evidence: packages/core/src/tool-output-store.ts:14-18 (MAX_LINES 2_000, MAX_BYTES 50*1024, RETENTION days(7), MANAGED_DIRECTORY); CONTEXT.md 'Managed Tool Output File' concept; V1 truncates only at serialize-time for compaction summaries (core compaction.ts:14 TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS 2k)

subject: opencode
title: Retry policy honors retry-after-ms / retry-after seconds / HTTP-date, adds jittered exponential backoff with caps, and exempts ContextOverflowError from retry
evidence: packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts:26-31 (2s initial, x2, 0.25 jitter, 30s no-headers cap, RETRY_MAX_RETRIES 5), :48-78 (delay() header precedence), :87 (overflow never retried), :193 (attempt bound enforced); retryable message-pattern table :33-40
one_why: Token-economy guardrail: prevents retry storms re-billing a huge prompt while keeping overflow to feed the compaction path instead; V2 checklist admits this bounding is not yet in the durable runner (packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts:53).

subject: opencode

subject: opencode
title: Background jobs and the V2 run coordinator are in-process only; the durable runner's own checklist admits no durable status, no interruption/stale-work rejection, no retry/identical-call bounding
evidence: packages/core/src/background-job.ts:35 (jobs = SynchronizedRef<Map>); packages/core/src/session/run-coordinator.ts:23-30 (plain Map in make()) - clean algebra (run joins, wake coalesces, interrupt awaits cleanup :73-103) but zero persistence; packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts:47-53 (unchecked: durable multi-node ownership, durable busy/retrying/interrupted status, honor interruption / reject stale work, bound retries and repeated identical tool calls)
one_why: Crash mid-background-job silently loses the parent notification; no first-class queue (codex-9 `codex queue`), no durable cron/journal (cline-8 sqlite-cron + hub-event-log), and no loop breaker (crush-7's loop_detection.go is still the only anchor with one) - this is what holds opencode at the 7 rung.
