subject: code
title: TUI product surface is a 44,921-LOC single file with 1,048 methods; single event handler is 2,262 lines and a render function 2,006 lines
evidence: wc -l code-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs = 44,921 with 41 impl blocks / 1,048 methods; handle_code_event :13865 ~2,262 lines; render_ref :42234 ~2,006 lines; submit_user_message :11792 ~600 lines; ~30 submodules exist under code-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/ but do not reduce the parent file; tui crate total 131,439 LOC > core crate 93,055 LOC
one_why: Errata says treat any product/TUI file >5k LOC as a docking factor and the 8->9 gap is loop/state separated from every product surface; here the surface holds more code than the engine (tui > core) and dwarfs pi's 6,852-LOC docking file by 6.5x, so no host-agnostic score above 6 is possible regardless of lineage.

subject: code
title: The documented task/state architecture (SessionTask/ActiveTurn/TurnState, mirroring upstream's turn refactor) is dead code: tasks/ and state/ are not declared in lib.rs and never compile
evidence: code-rs/core/src/tasks/mod.rs (SessionTask trait :47, spawn_task :64) and code-rs/core/src/state/{session.rs,turn.rs,service.rs} exist but lib.rs module list (:9-141) has no `mod tasks`/`mod state`; only reference into either tree is the island edge tasks/mod.rs <- state/turn.rs:13; tasks/mod.rs:147 is a literal empty `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {}`; the shipped loop instead uses AgentTask::spawn (streaming.rs:110) + `state.current_task` behind std Mutex (codex/session.rs:121-141, set_task :1053)
one_why: Two competing loop/state designs, one frozen out of the build, is the worst navigation hazard for humans and AI agents alike: the file layout advertises the architecture that does not run, and the live State struct (:121) is a 20+-field grab bag (approved commands, four pending maps, agent-batch bookkeeping) behind one std::sync::Mutex.

subject: code
title: Session-critical state lives in process-wide singletons that bypass the Session module: agent manager, browser manager, and the submission channel
evidence: code-rs/core/src/agent_tool.rs:396-398 `lazy_static AGENT_MANAGER: Arc<RwLock<AgentManager>>` used directly from submission_loop (streaming.rs:264, :275 cancel_batch/cancel_agent) and run_turn (:3083 has_active_agents); browser/src/global.rs:8 GLOBAL_BROWSER_MANAGER consulted in run_turn (streaming.rs:3079); codex.rs:1091 static TX_SUB_GLOBAL OnceLock set at :1178
one_why: The channel-loop design implies session isolation, but agent and browser registries are shared across any sessions in one process, and no test harness can spin two independent loops; upstream's answer (per-session services, 127 crates) exists untouched in the mirror tree at codex-rs/, so this is fork-tree regression, not lineage.

subject: code
title: JSONL rollout journal with tolerant replay, cursor-paginated listing, catalog bootstrap/reconcile, archive and rename - and it is actually tested
evidence: code-rs/core/src/rollout/recorder.rs:62-66 documented format with jq example, resume :290, get_rollout_history :325-418 (unparseable lines warn+continue :339-344); rollout/list.rs cursor pagination; session_catalog.rs:50 query, :99 find_by_id, :132 set_nickname, :146 archive_conversation (moves rollout + snapshot.json :199-209); rollout/tests.rs:169,285,361,498,538,601,665 and tests/session_catalog_resume.rs:113-277 give 13 behavior tests (resume reconstruction, pagination stability, mtime reconciliation, source filters)
one_why: This is the codex-9 operability spine carried into the fork tree and - unlike most fork deltas - covered by real tests; the tolerant line-skip on replay is the right crash posture for a journal.

subject: code
title: /undo pairs workspace ghost-snapshots with conversation rewind in one picker; snapshots are journaled and archived with the session
evidence: code-rs/tui/src/chatwidget.rs:12426 capture_ghost_snapshot, :12593 enqueue with serial worker (:12601 spawn_next_ghost_snapshot), :12916 handle_undo_command -> :13031 snapshot picker, :13545 restore(restore_files, restore_conversation) with :13605 conversation rewind and :13610 already-matches guard; GhostSnapshot items persisted via rollout/policy.rs:38; snapshot.json moved on archive (session_catalog.rs:199-209); disabled/empty/failure states all handled (:12939, :12962)
one_why: Checkpoint-plus-conversation-rewind in one timeline beats cline's git-stash checkpoints (8-rung) on UX; the caveat is the whole capture/restore machine is TUI-side (~1,200 lines inside the 44.9k file), so exec/app-server surfaces get no undo - a ui-coupled-loop nuance on an otherwise strong feature.

subject: code
title: Session state persistence is hollow: SavedSession serializes a permanently-empty state object, record_state discards its argument, and resume silently drops TurnContext items
evidence: code-rs/core/src/rollout/recorder.rs:45 `pub struct SessionStateSnapshot {}`, :285 `record_state(&self, _snapshot)` returns Ok without writing; get_rollout_history :389-392 skips RolloutItem::TurnContext ("Ignore variants not used by this fork when resuming"), so per-turn approval/sandbox/model context is not restored; forked_from_id never populated (:159 hardcodes None though protocol.rs:1850 carries it)
one_why: The data model advertises resumable state it never captures: a session resumed after a crash reverts to fresh turn settings, and fork (a codex-9 operability feature present in the mirror) is protocol-only in the shipped tree - this is what holds operability at 8 instead of 9.

subject: code
title: Unified panic hook, session end logging, and bespoke forensics commands (doctor, order-replay, sandbox debug runners)
evidence: code-rs/tui/src/lib.rs:766 install_unified_panic_hook -> session_log::log_panic (:781, session_log.rs:373), log_session_end :889; housekeeping panic caught (lib.rs:757); exec/src/lib.rs:1219 separate exec panic hook; cli/src/main.rs:155 `Doctor` (PATH/binary-collision diagnosis), :132 + :377-383 OrderReplay (replays ordering from captured ~/.code/debug_logs/*_response.json + codex-tui.log), :583/:594 debug seatbelt/landlock runners
one_why: Matches pi's crash-log + diagnostics evidence at the 9-rung for the crash/diagnose half of operability; order-replay in particular is a genuinely good debug primitive (codex's `debug prompt-input` peer) that most subjects lack entirely.

subject: code
title: Approval decision defaults to Approved when the approval channel fails: dropped channel runs the command unsandboxed
evidence: code-rs/core/src/codex/streaming.rs:10972 and :11427 (`rx_approve.await.unwrap_or_default()`); code-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs:2576-2580 (ReviewDecision derives Default, first variant = Approved); streaming.rs:11000-11004 (AskUser branch executes approved commands with SandboxType::None)
one_why: Every other failure in the gate is fail-closed (Denied/Abort return before exec at :10995), but a closed channel - killed TUI, app-server disconnect, timeout plumbing bug - silently resolves to the most permissive decision AND skips the sandbox, the one rung codex has since moved away from; invert Default to Denied or match on Err explicitly.

subject: code
title: execpolicy DSL ships with a real negative-example suite but is not wired into the shipped exec path
evidence: code-rs/execpolicy/src/policy_parser.rs, default.policy (202 lines), tests/suite/bad.rs:5-9 (every bad-list invocation must be rejected) + 8 suite files; but zero PolicyChecker/execv_checker/check_exec references anywhere in code-rs/core (grep); only consumer is protocol types: code-rs/protocol/src/models.rs:21 `use codex_execpolicy::Policy` for ExecPolicyAmendment, and code-rs/Cargo.toml:70; the mirror has the wiring (codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs + exec_policy_tests.rs) that the fork tree lacks; assess_command_safety is the sole gate (streaming.rs:10923)
one_why: A policy engine everyone assumes is enforcing because README/docs describe it - enforcement theater risk; tests prove the parser, not any runtime effect; porting the mirror's exec_policy wiring is the cheapest way to make docs true.

subject: code
title: Dangerous-command deny-list is tested dead code: nothing outside its own module ever consults it
evidence: code-rs/core/src/command_safety/is_dangerous_command.rs:4-45 (git reset --hard, rm -rf, sudo-wrapped forms) with 8 unit tests :47-99; grep `is_dangerous` over code-rs returns hits only inside command_safety/ plus one unrelated execpolicy test name; safety.rs:130 gates solely on is_known_safe_command allow-list
one_why: Under Never/WorkspaceWrite a `git reset --hard` auto-approves into the sandbox because the deny-list that exists to force AskUser is never called - green tests for a guard that guards nothing, and the tests actively hide the wiring gap.

subject: code
title: Browser/CDP and Code Bridge inject un-trust-marked page content into model context, including arbitrary JS execution back into the page
evidence: unified browser tool in the live loop (code-rs/core/src/codex/streaming.rs:3078-3079, :5216); code-rs/core/src/bridge_client.rs:732 (tool doc: `action=javascript` runs JS on the bridge client; errors/console streamed into context), :88-89 console/error ingestion; tool outputs written verbatim as FunctionCallOutputBody::Text (streaming.rs:10995-10999 pattern); grep for prompt-injection/untrusted-input framing over code-rs core = zero hits (only browser cursor "injection", a feature, browser/src/hooks/browser_injector.rs:23)
one_why: Fork adds two whole attacker-controlled channels (arbitrary web page text, live app console) on top of inherited MCP with zero of even the trivial defenses - no delimiters, no provenance labels; a page saying "run this command to fix the bug" enters history indistinguishable from user text.

subject: code
title: The honest half: deny-default seatbelt profile pinned to /usr/bin, read-only default, process hardening and exec-subtree OOM containment
evidence: code-rs/core/src/seatbelt_base_policy.sbpl:8 `(deny default)`; seatbelt.rs:17 (only /usr/bin/sandbox-exec honored); code-rs/protocol/src/config_types.rs:60-63 (SandboxMode default = ReadOnly); protocol.rs:370-371 (approval default OnRequest); code-rs/cli/src/main.rs:56 + code-rs/process-hardening/src/lib.rs:1-8 (pre-main: no core dumps, no ptrace, LD_PRELOAD/DYLD stripped); code-rs/core/src/cgroup.rs:11,127-128 (exec subtree oom_score_adj 500 so children die before parent)
one_why: Inherited from codex but genuinely wired and default-on in the shipped tree - this is what lifts the fork above the tested-approval-only 6 rung; the OOM-priority trick is a quiet, cheap crash-containment idea hotdog should copy regardless of the rest.

subject: code
title: No test gate on PRs: CI builds on PR but nextest runs only in the release pipeline on main
evidence: .github/workflows/preview-build.yml:3-6 (PR trigger) with build-only steps (:148 cargo build --release, no test invocation); cargo nextest appears once, in release.yml:145, triggered by push to main (release.yml:3-5); scripts/ci-tests.sh smokes run with SKIP_CARGO_TESTS=1 (release.yml:127-128); no fuzzing (no proptest/cargo-fuzz/libfuzzer in any code-rs Cargo.toml), no cargo-deny/deny.toml, no model or safety evals in any of the 12 workflows
one_why: Even crush (7) and nanocoder (7) gate PRs (-race matrix; coverage-drop + real-bubblewrap jail spec); here a broken approval-gate change can land and only be caught, if at all, at release time on a single ubuntu runner.

subject: code
title: Where fork tests exist they do prove behavior via scripted wiremock SSE - but only 13 core integration files, and enforcement layers have zero denial tests
evidence: code-rs/core/tests/repeated_tool_loop.rs:14-58 (drives a real Codex session against scripted SSE, asserts loop-breaker fires), agent_completion_wake.rs; 13 files in code-rs/core/tests, 58 test files across code-rs, 1,557 #[test] total vs 311k LOC; safety-critical coverage is argv/preflight only: seatbelt.rs tests assert generated args (:69,:163), linux-sandbox landlock tests cover only GPU path filtering (:189-217), exec.rs tests cover preflight rejects (:876-910); no test anywhere executes a sandbox and asserts a denial
one_why: The codex anchor's 440k test LOC are dominated by suite tests that watch real approval/sandbox flows fail closed; the fork kept the mock-SSE pattern but none of the enforcement half, so 'tests exist' proves shape, not safety properties.

subject: code
title: Dual-tree test mirage: ~98% of repo test volume lives in the codex-rs mirror that fork CI never builds or runs
evidence: codex-rs carries 1,035 *_tests.rs/tests files (~816k LOC) including exec_policy/network_policy suites (codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy_tests.rs); code-rs workspace members (code-rs/Cargo.toml:15-94) alias only vendored codex-utils-* crates, never the mirror; nextest runs `cd code-rs` (release.yml:149); justfile:1 sets working-directory to codex-rs so local DX runs the wrong tree's tests

subject: code

evidence: docs/platform-sandboxing.md:13 ("restricted Windows token ... ADS/UNC/device handles proactively denied ... PATH stubs"), :16 ("python windows-sandbox-rs/sandbox_smoketests.py ... 37/41"); no windows-sandbox* crate exists in code-rs/ (ls fails); code-rs/core/src/safety.rs:229-237 get_platform_sandbox returns None on Windows; code-rs/core/src/exec.rs:115-123 SandboxType enum only None/MacosSeatbelt/LinuxSeccomp; upstream implementation sits unconverted in the mirror codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs which release builds never compile (release.yml builds code-rs only) || non-Windows instances of the same drift cluster (from code-e9): docs/getting-started.md:1 still titled 'Getting started with Codex CLI' vs docs/index.md:1 'Every Code Documentation'; code-rs/core/src/codex/compact.rs:52-63 comment asserts 'remote compaction infrastructure is not yet implemented, so this always returns false' while the shipped code takes that branch at compact.rs:191-199 -> compact_remote.rs:82; justfile:1 and code-rs/justfile:1 both `set working-directory := "codex-rs"` driving the mirror while AGENTS.md:7 instructs 'Treat codex-rs as a read-only mirror' and release builds compile only code-rs

Non-Windows drift items dock docs-dx (lane-econ docs-dx 7); the phantom Windows claim docks safety-enforcement (lane-safety 7) and docs-dx - same fact visibly used in two dimensions, neither dimension double-docked within itself.

subject: code
title: Shipped compaction is a degradation ladder, not one summarizer: usage-triggered inline compact -> byte-capped sanitize -> orphan-output prune -> capped overflow-trim loop (32) -> usage-limit retry with parsed Retry-After -> emergency history reset with user-visible warning
evidence: code-rs/core/src/codex/compact.rs:38-45 (COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS=20_000, COMPACT_TOOL_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES=4 KiB, MAX_COMPACT_CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_TRIMS=32); :220-260 apply_emergency_compaction_fallback replaces history with build_initial_context + COMPACTION_EMERGENCY_MESSAGE :47; :306,:349,:476,:519 fallback call sites; :328,:497 trim caps; compact_remote.rs:82+ mirror path with same ladder; invoked from loop at code-rs/core/src/codex/streaming.rs:2665,:2941,:3452; images omitted under compaction at compact.rs:666-677
one_why: crush/nanocoder sit at token-economy 6 with one auto-summarize each; this ladder (degrade stepwise, then reset, and tell the user in both the failure event and the surviving message) is the codex-shaped failure-mode ordering that puts the shipped product in pi/cline territory.

subject: code
title: Auto-context judge: once 150k tokens in a 1M window, a cheap aux model is consulted each turn with a pressure-band + projected-post-turn-risk JSON payload to decide compaction; force threshold = auto-compact limit minus 20k margin; obvious continuations skip the judge
evidence: code-rs/core/src/codex/streaming.rs:58-63 (AUTO_CONTEXT_JUDGE_MIN_TOKENS=150_000, primary judge model gpt-5.3-codex-spark), :1736-1741 (AUTO_CONTEXT_FORCE_COMPACT_MARGIN_TOKENS=20_000), :1742-1757 pressure bands Medium/High/Critical, :1847-1852 estimate_next_turn_context_tokens, :1854-1890 estimate_auto_context_turn_risk clamped 24k-180k blended from last API usage, :2011-2160 judge prompt build with distance-to-limit fields, :2043-2057 forced compaction path
one_why: pi's 8-rung trigger measures what the model would actually receive; this goes one further by paying a cheap model to judge next-turn risk under pressure - genuinely novel among anchors - but it spends judge tokens every turn inside the band and the cost/benefit is nowhere documented or measured.

subject: code
title: Prompt-cache discipline is codex-inherited and intact: session-id prompt_cache_key on chat, compact and compact-history requests, plus a dual underscore/hyphen session-header set for cache/gateway routing; no warming and no fork-side improvement, and the off-API token estimate is a coarse bytes/4 heuristic
evidence: code-rs/core/src/client.rs:936,:1438 (prompt_cache_key = session id on responses payloads), :167 (CompactHistoryRequest.prompt_cache_key), :2119; :440-457 apply_responses_session_headers sending conversation_id/session_id/thread_id + hyphenated variants; code-rs/code-auto-drive-core/src/auto_compact.rs:16 and auto_drive_history.rs:11 (BYTES_PER_TOKEN=4)
one_why: This is exactly the codex 9-rung 'cache-key-gated reuse' mechanism - so the fork neither loses cline's no-cache-dock nor earns pi's cache-warming credit; cache-warming and a real tokenizer remain the gap to 9.

subject: code
title: Auto Drive budgets are real and observable: escalating time-budget nudges, coordinator turn cap that hard-stops runaway runs, HARD_MESSAGE_LIMIT=320 drain with a global trimmed-items counter, drop-oldest capped update queue (24) with drop counter, and an 80%-of-window projected compaction trigger
evidence: code-rs/code-auto-drive-core/src/auto_coordinator.rs:340-366 (time-budget nudge guidance at 50%/120s/30s), :2198-2212 (coordinator_turn_cap stop with user message), :64-65 constants, :2548-2567 (drain to HARD_MESSAGE_LIMIT + HARD_LIMIT_TRIMMED_ITEMS_TOTAL), :2571-2582 (queue_update_capped + QUEUED_UPDATE_DROPS_TOTAL), :4809-4841 (should_compact: projected_total >= 0.8*limit, else trust explicit token budget to avoid compaction loops)
one_why: README's 'hard caps with bounded drop/trim' marketing is verifiably true in code, with counters you can alert on - crush and pi at orchestration 7 have no such budget machinery; this is the strongest evidence the flagship feature is machinery, not prose.

subject: code
title: Subagents are rival harnesses spawned as external processes from a built-in catalog (claude, gemini, copilot, qwen, antigravity, own code CLI) with per-model read-only vs write argv profiles, git worktree isolation for writers, a watchdog, terminal-agent compaction and pruning, and spawn-depth tracking
evidence: code-rs/core/src/agent_defaults.rs:17-34 (argv profiles per family, e.g. CLAUDE_SONNET_READ_ONLY --allowedTools allowlist :14 vs CLAUDE_SONNET_WRITE --dangerously-skip-permissions :22), :43-55 (DEFAULT_AGENT_NAMES 11 slugs across 5 vendors); code-rs/core/src/agent_tool.rs:396-398 (global AGENT_MANAGER), :446 (current_agent_spawn_depth), :484-506 (watchdog), :566-612 (compact_terminal_agent, prune_terminal_agents); worktree/branch fields on Agent struct :379-384
one_why: No anchor federates competitor harness CLIs as its subagent pool; codex's 9-rung subagents are in-family. Note two caveats: the shipped crate embeds the supposedly read-only mirror at compile time (agent_defaults.rs:35 include_str! of codex-rs/models-manager/models.json), and write-mode agents run with the rival's own sandbox disabled - the safety lane should own that half.

subject: code
title: Orchestration has no durability spine: no queue command anywhere in the fork CLI, the Auto Drive transcript is in-memory by design, and crash recovery is an in-process transient-retry state machine rather than journal replay
evidence: grep for queue subcommands across code-rs/cli/src finds only log lines (cli/src/proto.rs:105,137), no Queue command; docs/auto-drive.md:16 'The transcript is kept in memory and compacted automatically'; code-rs/code-auto-drive-core/src/controller.rs:128 in_transient_recovery, :975 test transient_failure_enters_recovery_and_schedules_restart; faults.rs has 0 inline tests; the only durable journal (rollout) covers session resume (lane-core f-code-c5), not coordinator state
one_why: codex's 9 rung includes a first-class queue plus daemon recovery; cline's 8 has durable sqlite cron and an event journal; a killed coordinator loses the entire multi-hour Auto Drive plan, which caps orchestration below the 8 rung regardless of how good the in-run budgets are.

subject: code
title: Both shipped SDK directories are verbatim upstream artifacts that point users at the upstream product: TypeScript SDK's name is still @openai/codex-sdk and its README tells you to install @openai/codex; Python SDK is openai-codex-app-server-sdk at upstream's 0.116.0a1 vs the fork's own 0.6.193; release CI never publishes either
evidence: sdk/typescript/package.json:2 ('name': '@openai/codex-sdk', 'version': '0.0.0-dev'), sdk/typescript/README.md:1-11 ('wraps the codex CLI from @openai/codex... npm install @openai/codex-sdk'); sdk/python/pyproject.toml:6-7 (name = 'openai-codex-app-server-sdk', version = '0.116.0a1'); grep of .github/workflows/*.yml finds no sdk publish step; only @just-every/code is published (codex-cli/package.json:2, version 0.6.193)
one_why: Interop rungs 8-9 require a published SDK that programs THIS product; here the SDK surface is dead weight that actively misroutes fork users to OpenAI's binary - worse than not shipping one, and it is what separates this from cline's genuinely published @cline/* SDK.

subject: code
title: Interop surface is broad but of mixed parentage: MCP client and a maintained 3,733-LOC MCP server live in the shipped tree, app-server protocol has schema export plus TS codegen, headless `code exec --json` is real - but mcp-types is a pure upstream re-export and ACP is never implemented server-side (no acp::Agent anywhere in code-rs), just a client-side fs shim and an alias on the mcp subcommand
evidence: code-rs/mcp-server/src (8 files, 3,733 LOC total), code-rs/rmcp-client/src (1,440 LOC); code-rs/mcp-types/src/lib.rs:1-2 ('Re-export the upstream MCP types so the fork stays in lockstep'); code-rs/app-server/src (8 files) + code-rs/app-server-protocol/src/lib.rs with export/schema_fixtures; code-rs/protocol-ts/generate-ts; headless: code-rs/exec/src/cli.rs:89 (--json), event_processor_with_json_output.rs; ACP: grep 'acp::Agent' over code-rs returns no impl; code-rs/core/src/acp.rs:22-39 (AcpFileSystem client shim), code-rs/cli/src/main.rs:116 (#[clap(visible_alias = "acp")] on Mcp)
one_why: Scouts warning stands: much of interop is inherited or wrapped, so it cannot be scored at codex's 9 (which the fork lacks anyway on SDK publication), but it still exceeds crush-7 (no MCP server, no published CLI package) and reaches cline parity minus published-SDK and IDE surfaces; Zed support is a doc (docs/integration-zed.md), not a plugin.

subject: code
title: Error and onboarding UX is unusually concrete: per-OS agent-not-found errors with config.toml snippets and doc links, usage-limit errors with humanized reset times, a model-facing 600-char prompt rejection that explains why, and npm packaging that preempts PATH collisions with a `coder` alias and refuses to delegate to a foreign `code` binary
evidence: code-rs/core/src/agent_tool.rs:311-344 (troubleshooting blocks for windows/unix with [[agents]] examples); code-rs/core/src/error.rs:276-304 + tests :440-500 (rate-limit messages with 'Try again in 2 days 3 hours 5 minutes'); auto_coordinator.rs:2308 (OVERLONG_MSG teaching 600-char rule); README.md:89-93 (npm install -g @just-every/code; 'our CLI is also installed as coder'); codex-cli/bin/coder.js:17-21 ('Never delegate to another system's `code` binary (e.g., VS Code)'); .devcontainer/ + build-fast.sh + config.toml.example present; AGENTS.md is 152 lines of specific build/test/warning policy
one_why: Few anchors bother below the happy path; this is the cline-8 docs-dx texture (feature docs, real config.md at 1,139 LOC, docs/auto-drive.md stating preconditions honestly) carried into the fork's own deltas - the dock comes from e9's drift, not from thinness.

subject: kilocode
title: Shipping agent loop is an upstream file patched in-place: 69 kilocode_change blocks rewrite loop control flow inside prompt.ts
evidence: packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:2-31 (~23 overlay imports), :1543 while(true), :1560 resume-break replaced by KiloSessionContinuation chronology compare, :1604-1617 loop-exit predicate rewritten (parentID + userBeforeAssistant), :1524 mutable closeReasons Map keyed by sessionID, :1511-1519 10x50ms poll-retry patch for a cancel race; 69 kilocode_change start/end blocks and 266 marker lines in a 2673-LOC loop (upstream same file 1631 LOC); CI (check-opencode-annotations.yml:52 -> script/check-opencode-annotations.ts:5-16) enforces marker presence, not merged semantics. Consequence: loop termination/continuation invariants live inside merge-conflict-prone inline patches; a wrong conflict resolution during the frequent upstream sync silently changes when the agent stops.
one_why: Fork marker discipline scales to files but not to control-flow invariants.

subject: kilocode
title: Two session engines ship simultaneously on one server and one database (v1 prompt loop + v2 Effect runner)
evidence: V1: prompt.ts:1543 free-form while-loop is the product loop (AGENTS.md:49 CLI engine = packages/opencode). V2: packages/core/src/session/runner/index.ts @opencode/v2/SessionRunner + run-coordinator.ts per-key drain/wake/interrupt, wired live into kilo serve via packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:200-207 (serverRoutes from @opencode-ai/server/handlers) and packages/server/src/routes.ts:33,55 (SessionV2.node + SessionExecutionLocal). The same shipped SDK exposes both surfaces: packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/sdk.gen.ts:5047 /session/{id}/prompt_async vs :10030-10077 /api/session/{id}/revert/*. V1 loop reads history from the v2 Effect database: prompt.ts:1548-1550 kilocode_change 'provide the upstream Effect database to Kilo's retained prompt loop'. Consequence: two turn lifecycles mutate one message store, fixes must land twice, and packages/core/test/session-runner*.test.ts green does not cover the shipping loop.
one_why: Migration windows ship products too, and both doors are already open.

subject: kilocode
title: CI-enforced architecture boundaries with a decrementing owner-assigned allowlist
evidence: script/check-architecture.ts:6-17 enforces 5 rules (core/llm/schema import directionality, unclassified InstanceState singletons, direct SQLite constructors, tool process.env reads, httpapi handlers calling node:fs/spawn); script/architecture-allowlist.json records per-file exception counts with owner + reason and instructs 'decrement counts or remove entries to lock in progress'; runs on every PR touching shared code via .github/workflows/check-opencode-annotations.yml:52. Consequence: boundary rot is caught mechanically and legacy debt becomes a bounded, owned, monotonically-shrinking set.
one_why: Boundaries you cannot lint are suggestions.

subject: kilocode
title: Interrupted/failed turns are repaired before the next prompt is accepted, with explicit resume semantics

subject: kilocode

subject: oh-my-pi

subject: oh-my-pi

subject: aider
title: class Coder is a 2,485-LOC / 89-method god object fusing loop, context assembly, cache warming, summarization, git policy, shell exec and cost accounting
evidence: aider/coders/base_coder.py:88 (class Coder), :876 run REPL, :924 run_one reflection loop, :1419 send_message generator, :1783 send, :1340 warm_cache inline worker thread, :1002-1034 summarizer thread lifecycle, :2191 allowed_to_edit policy, :2375 auto_commit, :2434 run_shell_commands; 89 `def` in one class (grep)
one_why: Every loop-adjacent concern shares one mutable object, so any change to context, cache or git policy risks the core loop and none of it can be tested without constructing a near-complete Coder.

subject: aider
title: Edit formats are a tested strategy pattern: Coder.create dispatches over a class registry, each format pairs a subclass with its own prompts module, and ChatChunks is a typed context model with per-chunk cache marking
evidence: aider/coders/base_coder.py:125-201 create() resolves edit_format against coders.__all__ (:190), raising UnknownEditFormat (:196-201); on format switch old assistant history is re-summarized for the new format (:160-168); aider/coders/chat_chunks.py:5-25 typed chunks (system/examples/done/repo/readonly/chat/cur/reminder) with all_messages() composition order and add_cache_control_headers() marking chunk boundaries (:28-44); format-specific tests tests/basic/test_editblock.py, test_udiff.py, test_wholefile.py
one_why: The hardest-to-generalize part of a coder - output edit dialect - is isolated behind one factory seam with prompt and test per dialect, which is the cleanest architectural idea in the tree.

subject: aider
title: Conversation state is four mutable attributes (done_messages, cur_messages, reflected_message, aider_commit_hashes) poked directly by commands, watchers and child coders, with no turn/step context object
evidence: aider/coders/base_coder.py:395-403 state init, :1036-1046 move_back_cur_messages in-place append, :1425/:1576-1583 cur_messages mutated inside send_message incl. interrupt fixups; commands.py has 171 `self.coder.` references (grep -c); watch.py:195 adds files via coder.abs_fnames.add; architect_coder.py:38-46 parent hands 9 fields to the editor child and copies back total_cost/aider_commit_hashes after the child runs; the from_coder handoff dict at base_coder.py:158-171 is an explicit enumeration of the hidden coupling surface
one_why: State transitions are valid only by convention across five modules, so correctness properties like 'history is always alternation-safe' (test_message_sanity_after_partial_response exists precisely because this breaks) cannot be enforced locally.

subject: aider
title: main() is a single ~824-line function wiring config, onboarding, model selection, gui/watch branching and coder construction
evidence: aider/main.py:451 def main, next top-level def at :1187 (is_first_run_of_new_version) so the body spans :451-1274; coder constructed via Coder.create at :973 and :1177; interactive vs --message paths interleaved in the same body
one_why: Any new product surface (gui, watch, strict mode) lands as more branches in one function, which is where entry-path duplication would start the moment a second host wanted to reuse the loop.

subject: aider
title: Session persistence is an append-only human-readable markdown transcript re-parsed on opt-in resume; no session id, store, fork or tree
evidence: aider/args.py:290 --restore-chat-history; aider/coders/base_coder.py:519-522 loads .aider.chat.history.md via utils.split_chat_history_markdown then kicks summarize_start; writer at aider/io.py:1117-1136 appends per message and permanently disables itself on first PermissionError/OSError (:1136); grep over aider/ finds no session database or session-tree code
one_why: Human-greppable transcript-as-state is honest and crash-tolerant for a CLI, but resume fidelity depends on lossy markdown round-tripping, and there is no way back to any earlier session point.

subject: aider
title: /undo is a carefully guarded single-step rewind of aider's own last commit, refusing on every unsafe precondition
evidence: aider/commands.py:560-620: refuses when HEAD is first commit (:566), when the commit is not in the session's aider_commit_hashes (:573), multi-parent merge commits (:581), any changed file dirty (:591), or a changed file absent from the previous tree (:599); suggests `git reset --hard` only with a destructive-command warning (:575-577)
one_why: The guard set is exactly the right defensive property list for rewind, but session-scoped aider_commit_hashes plus single-step depth means recovery stops the moment the session does - nothing like crush's checkpoint infrastructure underneath.

subject: aider
title: The core loop's control flow - run_one, the reflection while-loop, max_reflections, restore-chat-history, the summarizer thread - has zero direct tests
evidence: grep -rn 'run_one|max_reflections' over tests/ hits only tests/fixtures/chat-history-search-replace-gold.txt (a captured source fixture, not an assertion); grep -rn restore_chat_history tests/ likewise fixture-only; tests/basic/test_coder.py covers loop-adjacent surfaces only (:1149 test_keyboard_interrupt_handling, :1172 test_token_limit_error_handling, :1195 test_message_sanity_after_partial_response) with 42 tests mostly on file mentions and edit gating (:25-:1404)
one_why: The one property the loop does defend (reflection bounded at 3, base_coder.py:101, :939) is untested, so a regression there would silently change aider into an unbounded self-correcting loop.

subject: aider
title: Model-suggested shell commands execute as raw shell strings with zero enforcement underneath: no sandbox, no allowlist, no path confinement anywhere in the tree
evidence: aider/run_cmd.py:10-19 (dispatch), :60-70 (subprocess.Popen shell=True), :111 (pexpect.spawn shell -i -c <string>); aider/coders/base_coder.py:2456-2462 (confirm is the only gate, cwd=self.root :2472); grep -i sandbox over aider/ scripts/ docker/ .github/ = 0 hits; grep 'prompt injection' over aider/ = 0 hits
one_why: One explicit_yes confirmation is the entire distance between a hallucinated or injected command and an unsandboxed /bin/sh; the anchors with any real enforcement (codex 10) or even opt-in jails (nanocoder 5) all have machinery, aider has none.

subject: aider
title: --yes-always converts explicit_yes_required prompts to automatic DENY, not automatic yes, and the semantics are pinned by tests
evidence: aider/io.py:866-867 (`res = "n" if explicit_yes_required else "y"`), :918-921 (is_yes only on literal 'y'); aider/coders/base_coder.py:2459,2461 (explicit_yes_required=True, allow_never=True on shell run); tests/basic/test_io.py:180-183 (yes=True + explicit_yes_required -> assertFalse, input never called)
one_why: The blunt instrument that nukes cline/nanocoder-style 'approve everything' risk (codel 2) cannot reach the most dangerous action class: even with every confirmation disarmed, model-proposed shell never runs; this is the single best safety decision in the tree and it is tested.

subject: aider
title: Scraped web pages, clipboard text and command output enter the prompt with at most one plain confirm and no untrusted-content fencing anywhere
evidence: aider/commands.py:244-253 (/web: `Here is the content of {url}:` + raw scrape pushed into cur_messages); base_coder.py:972-979 (URLs auto-detected in user input scraped inline via cmd_web after one confirm); commands.py:1029 (/run output append confirm has NO explicit_yes_required, so --yes-always auto-yeses it); base_coder.py:2479-2481 (same for shell output); grep 'untrusted|prompt injection' over aider/*.py aider/coders/*.py = 0 hits
one_why: A hostile page or tool output gets full authorship of the next prompt - including the part that proposes shell commands - with no delimiters, no source labeling, and an output-append path that --yes-always silently approves; zero anchors in this band even attempt fencing, but aider also doesn't even restrict where ambient text can lead.

subject: aider
title: A few enforcement gates do not depend on approval at all, and the git layer is deliberately built to make every aider change revertible
evidence: base_coder.py:2202-2204 (gitignored file edits refused outright, no confirm offered), :451-457 + repo.py:532-542 (aiderignore/gitignore filter the whole file universe); auto_commits=True default base_coder.py:308; check_for_dirty_commit :2175-2190 ('We need a committed copy of the file in order to /undo'); /undo refuses non-aider commits, multi-parent commits and dirty files commands.py:575-594, guards tested tests/basic/test_commands.py:1176-1279
one_why: This is recovery-as-safety: it cannot prevent a bad write but guarantees a clean rollback for anything aider itself touched, and the refusal conditions are exactly the cases where undo would destroy user work - all three tested.

subject: aider
title: Scripting/API entry silently enables yes-always, auto-approving every edit confirm including create-file and edit-not-in-chat, with no test pinning it
evidence: aider/main.py:546-547 (`if return_coder and args.yes_always is None: args.yes_always = True`); affected confirms base_coder.py:2207 ('Create new file?'), :2226-2229 ('Allow edits to file that has not been added to the chat?'); grep -rn 'yes_always' tests/ = 0 hits
one_why: Embedders get the maximally permissive edit policy by default without any flag or warning line; only the shell fail-safe (aider-s2) keeps this from being total auto-approval, and nothing in CI would catch a regression that removed even that.

subject: aider
title: The shell-approval gate itself has zero test coverage: the gate is mocked away and run_cmd has one echo test
evidence: tests/basic/test_coder.py:994,1004 (handle_shell_commands replaced with MagicMock, only 'was it called' asserted); tests/basic/test_run_cmd.py:6-11 (entire file: one 'echo Hello, World!' smoke test); no test asserts confirm_ask call args (subject, explicit_yes_required, allow_never) for shell or output-append prompts
one_why: The cline 8-rung hallmark is 'approval-iff-policy' asserted end-to-end (agent-runtime.test.ts:2355); aider's most dangerous call site is exactly where its tests stop, so a refactor dropping explicit_yes_required=True would pass all 473 tests green.

subject: aider
title: Real, behavior-asserting test corpus - but 12.4k LOC / 473 tests (not the census 76k), provider fully mocked, no coverage gate, no fuzzing, no evals in CI
evidence: measured: 41 test files, 12,381 LOC, 473 `def test` (tests/basic/*); confirm_ask semantics matrix tests/basic/test_io.py:177-342 (explicit_yes, group all/skip, allow_never); allowed_to_edit allow/deny/dirty matrix tests/basic/test_coder.py:25-101; CI matrix ubuntu-tests.yml:26 + windows-tests.yml:25 (py 3.10-3.14, pytest, AIDER_ANALYTICS=false), pre-commit.yml (ruff/black only); grep hypothesis/atheris/fuzz over tests/ .github/ = 0 hits; benchmark/ runs out-of-band
one_why: Tests assert properties of the approval machinery (inputs -> allowed/refused), not existence - that is the crush/nanocoder 7-rung habit - but 5x thinner corpus, mocked litellm, and no coverage/race/vuln gates put aider under that rung; per the errata, 8 is unreachable without evals-in-CI or fuzzing, which would only be reachable at all if the corpus were crush-scale.

subject: aider
title: Crash handling is interactive-conservative: double-Ctrl-C exit, provider retries with backoff, hard stop on context exhaustion, tracebacks shown and loop survives, bug reports only open a prefilled URL after a y/n
evidence: base_coder.py:986-999 (keyboard_interrupt, 2s window), :1463-1477 (litellm retry/backoff, ContextWindowExceededError -> break -> show_exhausted_error :1545,:1628), :1506-1513 (generic exception: traceback + tool_error, loop continues), report.py:65-77 (input() confirm before browser open, nothing auto-submitted), analytics opt-in gate analytics.py:96-105 with 10% ask-roll (:15, need_to_ask :119-135)
one_why: Nothing auto-transmits (posthog only after asked_opt_in; report is a browser URL gated on stdin) and no error silently kills the REPL - solid crush-8-style recover posture for a CLI, minus crush's boundary-wide recover middleware.

subject: aider
title: No SECURITY.md and no doc states what the approval model does not enforce - silence, not a false claim
evidence: git ls-files | grep -i security = empty; grep -rli security aider/website/docs only legal/privacy.md + troubleshooting/aider-not-found.md; contrast pi SECURITY.md:50 ('intentionally does not have a sandbox')
one_why: Better than codel (2), whose README promises autonomy its policy forbids - aider never claims enforcement it lacks - but users get no written statement that approvals are the whole model, which is the honesty bar pi set at the 6 rung.

subject: aider
title: Single auto-summarize strategy with adaptive budget, weak-model ladder and an equality-guarded publish race: done_messages collapses toward a context-derived budget on a background thread, results adopted only on whole-list equality
evidence: aider/history.py:8 (ChatSummary max_tokens=1024 default), :33-96 (recursive halve-and-summarize, depth cap 3, :46-48), :114-124 (model ladder with per-model try/except); aider/models.py:339,356-358 (max_chat_history_tokens = clamp(max_input/16, 1024, 8192), so the 1024 default is a floor not a ceiling); aider/main.py:949-952 (summarizer built from [weak_model, main_model]); aider/coders/base_coder.py:1002-1022 (summarize_start/spawn worker on every history-too-big), :1024-1033 (join + swap only if `summarizing_messages == done_messages`, discarding a stale summary), :1036-1038 (trigger on every turn end via move_back_cur_messages) ; [merged aider-c4] summarize_worker snapshots list(done_messages) (base_coder.py:1014-1022); summarize_end adopts only `if summarizing_messages == done_messages`, silently discarding otherwise (:1024-1034); no lock anywhere in the file; join deferred to format_chat_chunks (:1278) so worst case is an unsummarized oversized send, not corruption; cache-warm worker shares ok_to_warm_cache/warming_pings_left lock-free (:1343-1390)
one_why: This is the crush/nanocoder 6-rung feature (one standard auto-summarize) done properly -- cheap-model-first, budget scaled to the window, races against new messages detected -- but it stays one strategy with no branching awareness, so it does not by itself reach pi's 8 (branch-summarization + projected trigger).; the equality guard is a deliberate lock-free design with an undocumented silent-drop ceiling
merged_from: lanes core+econ, kept econ record (budget/ladder evidence stronger), core race-guard evidence folded in

subject: aider
title: Context exhaustion is a dead end, not a compaction trigger: provider error sets a flag, aider prints advice and returns; nothing ever auto-retries with a smaller context
evidence: aider/coders/base_coder.py:1464-1465 (ContextWindowExceededError -> exhausted=True, break), :1536-1547 (show_exhausted_error + num_exhausted_context_windows, return), :1628-1676 (diagnostic text: /tokens /drop /clear advice, offer_url :1675); pre-flight check_tokens :1396-1417 measures the fully formatted messages against max_input_tokens and asks 'Try to proceed anyway?' -- advice only, never mutates the context; grep for any auto-retry/compact path after exhausted = none; docs aider/website/docs/troubleshooting/token-limits.md documents the manual escape hatches ; [merged aider-c8] FinishReasonLength without prefill support also exhausts (base_coder.py:1495-1499) -- no retry with smaller context from either path
one_why: Every anchor above the 6-rung converts overflow into action: codex 9 has three tiers incl. a no-LLM token-budget fresh window (compact_token_budget.rs:19-40), pi 8 triggers on projected context before the call; aider's own pre-flight measurement (the pi-like part) is wired to a confirm dialog instead of a compaction, so long sessions end in a wall the user must dismantle by hand.
merged_from: lanes core+econ, kept econ record (impact high vs med, wider anchor evidence)

subject: aider
title: Cache discipline is chunk-aware, provider-aware and cost-correct -- cache breakpoints are placed on a stable message prefix by design, with opt-in keepalive pings
evidence: aider/coders/chat_chunks.py:8-26 (ordered chunks system/examples/readonly/repo/done/chat_files/cur -> stable-prefix assembly), :28-41 (add_cache_control: breakpoints on examples-or-system, repo/readonly, chat_files), :55-63 (cacheable_messages returns the exact warmable prefix); aider/coders/base_coder.py:1334-1337 (headers applied in format_messages only when add_cache_headers), :426-427 (only for cache_control models), :232 (caches_by_default announced); :1340-1394 (warm_cache worker: 5-min delay :1348-1349, env override AIDER_CACHE_KEEPALIVE_DELAY, max_tokens=1 pings :1367-1368, cache-hit accounting :1383-1386); aider/args.py:233-243 (--cache-prompts default False, --cache-keepalive-pings default 0 -- opt-in); cost math :2089-2097 (deepseek hit-rate path; anthropic cache-write 1.25x / cache-read 0.10x)
one_why: This is pi's cache-warmer tier in substance -- a real warming worker and a message layout engineered around the cache boundary -- but pi ships warming as active behavior while aider's is doubly opt-in (flag + ping count) and only correct on 2-3 providers, and docs admit streaming+caching skews cost stats (website/docs/usage/caching.md ~:29, main.py:1120-1121 warning).

subject: aider
title: Repo map is an explicit token-budgeted context component: window-scaled default, empty-chat boost capped by the window, sampled token estimation
evidence: aider/models.py:782-789 (get_repo_map_tokens: max_input/8, clamped [1024, 4096]); aider/repomap.py:49 (map_tokens=1024 ctor default), :115-127 (no-chat-files case: target = min(map*map_mul_no_files, max_context_window - 4096)); :89-102 (token_count samples every Nth line for maps >200 chars instead of full tokenization); aider/main.py:954-955 (--cache-prompts forces map_refresh=files so map churn does not bust the prompt cache), :964-967 (map_tokens resolution order)
one_why: A budgeted, cache-cooperative retrieval component sized against the actual window is the 'budget projection' half of what the cline 7-rung gets credit for, and the map_refresh coupling at main.py:954 is exactly the cache-prefix discipline codex gets 9 for at protocol level.

subject: aider
title: Vision content is unbudgeted: images enter messages with no token accounting or count cap anywhere
evidence: grep -rn 'image_tokens|max_images|image budget' over aider/**/*.py = 0 hits; images ride into chunks as content blocks (aider/coders/base_coder.py format_messages path) and are only reflected in post-hoc usage totals (:1994-2010 calculate_and_show_tokens_and_cost reads usage after the call)
one_why: codex's 9-rung includes image budgets; aider's check_tokens :1399 counts the message list through litellm's tokenizer, which for image blocks under-counts badly -- so the one pre-flight guard it has is weakest exactly where budgets are invisible.

subject: aider
title: The only orchestration is a hard-wired two-model relay: architect spawns an editor Coder in-process, hands off a string plus cost/hashes, and waits
evidence: aider/coders/architect_coder.py:11-48 (reply_completed spawns Coder.create with editor_model/editor_edit_format :22-27, deliberately blank history :36-37, cache disabled :30-31, child.run(with_message=content) blocking :43, cost+commit-hash pullback :46-48); aider/main.py:824-826 (weak_model/editor_model wiring); aider/models.py:622-623 (commit_message_models = [weak_model, main] -- cheap-model delegation for commit messages, used repo.py:343-364)
one_why: Real, tested multi-model delegation with sane economics (weak model for summaries/commit msgs, separate editor), but it is one fixed pipeline with string handoff and no user-spawnable subagents, no parallelism, no budgets -- above codel's no-orchestration 4, nowhere near nanocoder's 6 (daemon + subagents).

subject: aider
title: No queue, no daemon, no journal, no loop detector: resumability is a markdown file reload and crash recovery is single-step /undo of aider's own commits
evidence: grep -rn 'queue|daemon|subagent|loop.detect' over aider/**/*.py hits only voice.py:3,117 (audio queue) and daemon=True threads (base_coder.py:1391 cache warmer, watch.py:169, copypaste.py:42); resume = --restore-chat_history parsing .aider.chat.history.md into done_messages (base_coder.py:519-523, args.py:290); /undo refuses unless last commit is aider's own, single-parent, no unrelated dirty files (commands.py:553-597); mode switches raise SwitchCoder and rebuild the Coder (commands.py:30,112-136,1161,1182-1198); the only loop guard is num_reflections >= max_reflections=3 (base_coder.py:115, :939-941)
one_why: crush holds the 7-rung on three things aider has none of (generic loop breaker with tests, race-tested cancellation, sqlite resume); nanocoder's 6 needs a daemon + subagents; the reflection cap is a narrow stopgap for one loop class, and interruption is a KeyboardInterrupt flag dance (:986-1000, :1575-1582) with nothing durable behind it.

subject: aider
title: Zero protocol interop: no MCP, no ACP, no machine-readable output mode -- headless is human text out
evidence: grep -rin 'mcp|acp|modelcontext' --include=*.py aider/ = 0 hits (scout confirms git log --all -S mcp finds only binary-asset byte matches); no --json/--output-format flag in aider/args.py (grep json = only :129 model-metadata path); headless contract = -m/--message (args.py:639-641) + --exit (:681), output is terminal text; batch path sendchat.py:1-24 is a caller-side script, not a protocol
one_why: Even the 6-rung (pi) earns its place with json/rpc modes and an SDK contract; aider's automation story requires importing Python in-process (scripting.md) -- nothing embeds aider over a wire, and the two dominant industry protocols are absent by inertia rather than the documented philosophy pi has.

subject: aider
title: Interop by surfaces instead of protocols: documented+tested Python API, streamlit GUI, IDE-comment watch mode, clipboard mode, voice, and a 27-provider metadata matrix
evidence: aider/website/docs/scripting.md:63-64,92 (from aider.coders import Coder / from aider.io import InputOutput) pinned by tests/basic/test_scripting.py; aider/gui.py:7 (streamlit) via --gui/--browser (args.py:657-660); watch mode responds to 'ai' comments in any editor (aider/watch.py:145-170, main.py:1028-1036, docs/usage/watch.md 294 lines); clipboard copypaste loop (aider/copypaste.py:24-41, main.py:1038); voice cmd (commands.py:1252); aider/resources/model-settings.yml (3,128 lines) + model-metadata.json (715 lines, 27 provider prefixes) + live OpenRouter model DB (models.py:176-201, openrouter.py); 17 per-provider llms docs pages under website/docs/llms/
one_why: Provider breadth (litellm + fetched metadata) is genuinely best-in-class interop with model backends, and the scripting API is the one thing a program can reuse -- but every surface is human-facing UI, and cline's 8-rung (MCP client + published SDK + four IDE surfaces) is exactly the wire-level half aider lacks.

subject: aider
title: Docs/DX is a first-class product surface: 84 in-repo doc pages incl. 17 provider guides and 7 troubleshooting pages, in-app errors that carry actionable next steps, deprecation shims, and an API-key onboarding wizard
evidence: 84 *.md under aider/website/docs (find count) -- install.md 115 lines + 4 install/ variants (docker, codespaces, replit, optional), troubleshooting/ 7 pages (token-limits.md, edit-errors.md, aider-not-found.md...), faq.md 384 lines, usage/ 14 pages incl. caching.md and watch.md, 30 blog posts under website/_posts; in-app advice: check_tokens prints /drop//clear tactics (base_coder.py:1400-1414), show_exhausted_error itemizes input/output/total vs limits then offers the token-limits URL (:1656-1675, io.py:797 offer_url); aider/deprecated.py:1-21 maps retired shortcut flags to --model with migration text; aider/onboarding.py:46-81 detects API keys, picks a default model, offers OpenRouter OAuth; benchmarks+leaderboards maintained in-tree
one_why: Against the anchors this exceeds pi's 9-rung on volume and matches code on substance (caching.md documents the real chunk order, watch.md documents real comment syntax), and unlike cline's 8 there is no dual-tree confusion -- the caveat is that a chunk of the mass is blog/benchmark prose, so the engineering-docs depth (session format, internals) pi has is thinner here.

subject: bitfun
title: Six-layer crate layout machine-enforced in CI: boundary linter over crate layers, forbidden deps, feature graph, public-API allowlists, and a TUI legacy ratchet
evidence: scripts/core-boundaries/checker.mjs:1-50 (imports crate-layout, crate-rules, feature-rules, source-rules, tui-boundary-ratchet, explicit-test-topology checks); scripts/core-boundaries/rules/crate-rules.mjs:837 LOC + feature-rules.mjs:1837 LOC + generated sources rules/source/required-rules.mjs (10,099) and forbidden-rules.mjs (4,483); package.json:78-79; .github/workflows/ci.yml:577-580 runs check:core-boundaries:test AND check:core-boundaries on every PR; layer table in AGENTS.md:38-48 declares the 6 layers the linter enforces
one_why: Beyond kode-cli/openhands ban-tests: this enforces physical crate layout, per-crate Cargo feature composition, public API surface allowlists, and even integration-test topology, with a self-test gate -- it is why a 43-crate 980k-LOC Rust tree by one contributor has no accidental upward deps, and the closest thing in the corpus to codex's discipline; directly portable as a layer-manifest linter for our repo.

subject: bitfun
title: ConversationCoordinator fuses turn driving, session CRUD, workspace binding, thread goals, subagent lifecycle, compaction gating and persistence finalization in one 21,911-LOC file (~15.5k production LOC before test mod)
evidence: src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/coordination/coordinator.rs total 21,911 LOC with test mod at :15502; struct ConversationCoordinator 24 injected fields :1225-1268; same impl block family holds session create :2519, thread-goal ops :4928-5210, workspace binding :1330+, persist completed/cancelled/failed turn finalization :2972-:3533, subagent timeout watch-loop :10517-10565, fork snapshot :11076; session_manager.rs 18,984 LOC / 457 fns; persistence/manager.rs 8,371
one_why: ~6x crush's fused pair (agent.go 2393 + coordinator.go 1877) and ~5.5x prime-agent's already-flagged agent-session.ts 15,101; the boundary linter keeps the periphery pristine while the center concentrates every subsystem import list in coordinator.rs:1-60 -- this is the single reason architecture cannot score 8, per the >5k-LOC docking erratum.

subject: bitfun
title: Interrupted turns resume only against frozen turn facts: permission mode, resolved model, and a model-binding fingerprint are persisted at interruption and the resume hard-refuses if any changed
evidence: session_manager.rs:8688-8700 ('Interrupted turn has no frozen permission mode; start a new turn instead'), :8750 model-binding-fingerprint mismatch refuses resume; recovery plan with generation guard :8550-8590 ('Interrupted turn generation mismatch'); re-reminder injected to the model '...do not assume that an interrupted tool call had no side effects; verify uncertain external state before acting again' :8648-8652; on resume the permission mode is re-resolved as restrict_recovered_permission_mode(frozen original, current) so recovery can never widen privileges (execution_engine.rs:666-668); coordinator entry recover_interrupted_dialog_turn coordinator.rs:7103; scheduler admission with 30s deadline + armed guard so a failed admission still frees the active turn : scheduler.rs:3239-3300
one_why: No anchor subject does this: codex resumes from rollout journal, crush/pi resume state, but none pins the security-relevant and model-relevant facts of a turn at interruption and refuses resurrection under a changed policy/model -- a cheap invariant worth stealing for any resumable agent (freeze what you will replay against, refuse drift, tell the model side effects are uncertain).

subject: bitfun
title: Runtime concepts exist in two mirrored trees (assembly/core agentic vs execution/agent-runtime) but the direction is enforced: agent-runtime owns session facts and delegates loop calls to core ports
evidence: core/state.rs:5 re-exports SessionState/ProcessingPhase from openbitfun_agent_runtime; core/session.rs is a 7-line facade; state.rs:105-113 records deliberate deletion of a divergent duplicate DialogTurnState copy; agent-runtime/src/runtime.rs:1690-1715 validates request identity and delegates recover_interrupted_turn to the DialogTurn port (core scheduler implements it at coordination/scheduler.rs:3239); mirrored names persist: agent-runtime/src/scheduler.rs 1,225 (owner decisions) vs coordination/scheduler.rs 5,643 (loop owner); docs/architecture/agent-runtime-deployment-design.md:38 asserts '只有一套 Agent Runtime 行为' with Phase 5/6 migration state table
one_why: Like cline's dual-tree dock, but better armed: single-owner direction (facts down, behavior in core) is code-visible and a past divergence was deleted with a comment; residual risk is the mirrored vocabulary drifting for a second contributor -- a watch-list divergence, not yet a fork of behavior.

subject: bitfun
title: Round loop has three bounded-stops (max_rounds, repeated-identical-tool-signature threshold, periodic-window loop detector) all tested, plus a postmortem that deleted a context pre-pass for causing the very loops it fought
evidence: execution_engine.rs:3396-3410 loop with cancellation + reached_fixed_model_round_limit; context-profile trigger has_repeated_tool_loop at :420-428 with repeated_tool_signature_count :445; tests zero/positive max_rounds :5240-5258, periodic_loop_detector_ignores_short_windows :6396, periodic_loop_detector_catches_consecutive_identical_window :6405; incident comment :3415-3423: removed 'microcompact' pass silently rewrote already-sent message prefixes, 'killing provider KV-cache hits on every round' and 'directly drove repetitive tool-call loops in long exploratory subagents (see deep-review subagent loop incident, 2026-05-12)'
one_why: Extends crush's lone loop-detection rung with a second detector and a causal lesson tying cache monotonicity (cache-monotonic-compaction) to loop behavior: mutating the sent prefix both doubles cost and induces repetition -- the postmortem-in-comment practice itself is portable.

subject: bitfun
title: Versioned, per-field-capturable model request/response trace sink wired into every round -- the corpus's strongest analog to codex's debug prompt-input
evidence: execution/model_exchange_trace.rs:22 TRACE_LAYOUT_VERSION=1; ModelExchangeTraceRecord :25-40 (trace_id, sequence, session/turn/operation ids, attempt_number, round_attempt); ModelExchangeTracePolicy :68-77 with per-field toggles (capture_request_body, response_text, reasoning, tool_calls, usage, provider_metadata) driven by user config modes Off/Full; attached per stream attempt in round_executor.rs:385 prepare_model_exchange_trace
one_why: Turn-level debugging of exact provider wire payloads with sequence numbers and retry-attempt lineage is what makes loop/cache regressions debuggable; the per-field capture policy (reasoning/tool-calls optional) also bounds what sensitive payloads land on disk -- codex has the capability, but nobody else in the corpus does, and this versioning+policy shape is copyable.

subject: bitfun
title: Undo/redo/targeted revert is a persisted phase state machine (Applying/Staged/Clearing/Committing) with schema version and recorded per-workspace checkpoint, not an in-memory cursor
evidence: session/revert.rs:9-40 SessionRevertPhase + SessionRevertState {schema_version, boundary_turn, original_turn_end, phase, workspace_checkpoint} with diagnostic_mutation_id :49-56; resolve_undo/redo/targeted :107/:180/:146 with chained-undo tests :275-302; state persisted atomically via persistence/manager.rs:2047 write_json_atomic(session_revert_path); crash-mid-revert handled by phase != Staged check session_manager.rs:5093; per-workspace SnapshotManager service/snapshot/manager.rs:33-48
one_why: crush's revert is live-session only and cline's checkpoints are git-stash side effects; bitfun makes the revert itself a crash-interruptible durable transaction (boundary turn + workspace checkpoint + phase), so a crash between undo steps resumes to a defined phase -- the pattern our rewind path needs.

subject: bitfun
title: Session persistence is keyed-lock-serialized atomic-rename files with schema versions, and the derived FTS index is declared rebuildable rather than authoritative
evidence: persistence/manager.rs:946-959 write_json_atomic/write_text_atomic, :1878/:1921/:1957 write_atomic_strict; save_session takes per-session write lease AND async persistence lock :2496-2514; StoredSessionStateFile carries schema_version :2530-2536; product_runtime.rs:99-156 projected_turn_save_would_overwrite_runtime_state blocks a projection save from dropping persisted text/thinking/tool results or recovery state, tested at :2957; session_search.rs:1 'Rebuildable SQLite FTS index', :13 product-search-v1.sqlite, fts5 tables :281-287
one_why: The write path treats 'two owners may save the same turn' as the failure mode to design against (lease + lock + content-loss predicate with a test), and search is disposable -- a small, high-leverage durability bar between crush's datadir lock and codex's rollout journals.

subject: bitfun
title: Zero OS-level containment: all enforcement is in-process Rust policy, while the tool surface includes computer-use, terminal, remote SSH and relay control
evidence: grep -rniE 'seatbelt|sandbox-exec|bubblewrap|bwrap|landlock|seccomp' over src/**/*.rs returns zero hits; the only kernel primitive is a Windows Job Object used for process-tree lifecycle (src/crates/services/services-core/src/process_manager.rs:52) and sdk-host is contract-tested to not own a second one (src/apps/sdk-host/tests/process_initialization.rs:101); docs/architecture/product-architecture.md:96 marks 'class Sandbox,OpenHarmony planned' and :125 lists Sandbox as the gap in the production Tools&Execution layer; docs/architecture/agent-runtime-services-design.md:373 says allow_in_sandbox may only return true when an actual sandbox exists -- so it never does
one_why: The 6-rung 'tested approval, nothing underneath' ceiling applies at best: any in-process bypass (a bug in policy evaluation, a hook panic, a compromised plugin in-process) reaches the whole machine with no second line of defense; codex's 10-rung kernel enforcement is the gap, and bitfun is at least honest that Sandbox is 'planned' rather than claiming it.

subject: bitfun
title: Shipped config contract defaults to FullAccess: a fresh install with no config file resolves the baseline rule ('*','*')=>Allow, i.e. no approval at all
evidence: src/crates/contracts/product-domains/src/tool_permissions.rs:187-190 PermissionPolicyPreset with #[default] FullAccess; :218 FullAccess baseline_rules => PermissionRule::new("*","*",Allow); src/crates/contracts/config-contracts/src/types.rs:1851 GlobalConfig::default() uses ToolPermissionConfig::default(); the default is locked in by a named contract test src/crates/contracts/product-domains/tests/product_domain_contracts/tool_permission_contracts.rs:57-63 'tool_permission_config_defaults_to_full_access_with_auto_approve_disabled'; PermissionMode::from_config maps that preset to FullAccess (tool_permissions.rs:296-301); CLI surfaces default to Ask instead (src/apps/cli/src/main.rs:553, src/apps/cli/src/runtime/approval.rs:51)
one_why: This is the nanocoder docking pattern -- real machinery, wrong default -- and it is worse where it lands: full-access-without-sandbox on a desktop agent with filesystem, terminal, computer-use and SSH reach; the CLI's Ask default shows the safer default was known, so the config-contract default is a product decision, not an oversight.

subject: bitfun
title: Layered policy resolution with a non-widenable parent runtime ceiling for delegated subagents: ceilings are independently evaluated and typed-reject Allow rules
evidence: resolve_permission_policy fixed layer order product_defaults/baseline/global/project/agent/enforced (src/crates/contracts/product-domains/src/tool_permissions.rs:464-477); resolve_child_permission_policy evaluates the parent ceiling as an independent constraint layer, not merged rules (:481-502); PermissionRuntimeCeiling::try_new rejects any Allow rule with a typed error carrying rule_index/action/resource (:130-147; contract test tool_permission_contracts.rs:259-268); parent-ceiling derivation strips Allow rules (src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/permission_policy.rs:44-65); most_restrictive fold over constraint layers (tool_permissions.rs:750-764); tests: child_profile_allow_cannot_loosen_parent_deny_or_external_directory_ask (permission_policy.rs:285-333), parent_ceiling_overrides_child_agent_allow and parent_ceiling_ask_does_not_loosen_child_agent_deny (tool_permission_contracts.rs:317,345), pipeline-level independent_permission_constraints_tighten_but_never_widen_host_policy (src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/tools/pipeline/tool_pipeline.rs:3741)
one_why: The escalation lattice (session mode cannot widen project/enforced layers, child profiles cannot widen parent deny/ask, enforced stays last) is the cleanest delegation model in the corpus after codex's execpolicy and is tested at resolver, contract, and pipeline level -- directly portable as our subagent permission ceiling design.

subject: bitfun
title: Hook approvals are scoped to waive only the interactive prompt and are structurally checked after policy Deny returns
evidence: hook_preapprovals set keyed by tool_call_id (src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/tools/pipeline/tool_pipeline.rs:666 with doc comment :663-665 'The approval waives the interactive permission prompt only; policy denials still apply'); the set is consulted at :745-750 only after the PermissionIntentPlan::Denied early return at :723-733; preapproval entries cleaned up per batch (:1418-1424); tests hook_approval_does_not_override_a_permission_deny_rule (:3812) and hook_approval_waives_the_permission_prompt (:4170)
one_why: Extension/hook systems tend to become permission bypasses; making the evaluation order (policy deny -> hook waiver -> hook decide -> interactive prompt) a code-structure property plus two named tests is the pattern crush's call-id-scoped grants only half-implement.

subject: bitfun
title: Permission plumbing fails closed on every degraded edge: unmatched rules ask, empty resources ask, closed reply channel cancels execution, audit-write failure aborts request registration, unknown persisted modes degrade to the user default
evidence: unmatched => Ask (src/crates/contracts/product-domains/src/tool_permissions.rs:728-748); empty resources => Ask (:799-801 and src/crates/execution/agent-runtime/src/permission.rs:144-146); oneshot closed => PermissionWaitOutcome::Cancelled -> tool execution returns Err, never proceeds (permission.rs:191-197; tool_pipeline.rs:1369-1377); audit append failure rolls back pending registrations and errors the batch (permission.rs:450-478, error variant AuditStore :221); unrecognized persisted permission mode deserializes to None = follow user-level default rather than failing or trusting the unknown value (tool_permissions.rs:325-340); reply-reject cancels sibling requests in the batch (tool_pipeline.rs:1357-1368)
one_why: This is the failure-mode checklist for any approval system (what happens on restart mid-prompt, corrupt config, audit store down) and bitfun answers each edge with a tested closed direction; our runtime should copy the question list even if we keep our own mechanism.

subject: bitfun
title: Guardrail tests prove absence of side effects: fake tools carry an execution counter and deny-path tests assert the counter never moved
evidence: v2_allow_and_deny_are_enforced_before_tool_side_effects drives the real pipeline with auto_approve_ask=true plus a Deny rule and asserts calls==1, task state Rejected, and result category 'permission_denied' (src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/tools/pipeline/tool_pipeline.rs:3678-3738); the file holds 56 test attributes overall; adjacent suites: 32 evaluator/preset/ceiling contract tests (tool_permission_contracts.rs, 952 LOC), 35 edit_constraint_guard tests (src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/execution/edit_constraint_guard/tests.rs), 9 external-directory intent tests (src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/tools/file_permissions.rs:201-503), permission manager lifecycle + non-interactive-audit tests (src/crates/execution/agent-runtime/src/permission.rs:872,938)
one_why: 'Denied' asserted as a string is weak; asserting the registered tool's side-effect counter stayed at N is the strongest cheap test shape for approval enforcement and matches cline's approval-iff-policy bar.

subject: bitfun
title: No prompt-injection defense anywhere: no screening, no untrusted-content labeling of tool results, and the only sanitizer targets model format bleed, not adversarial content
evidence: grep for prompt-injection defenses finds nothing -- the only 'prompt injection' hits are about injecting memory reminders into prompts (src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/agents/prompt_builder/prompt_builder_impl.rs:398-424); write_content_sanitizer.rs:1-4 documents its target as model-emitted tool-invocation artifacts (DSML/tool_calls markers), not hostile fetched content; a single untrusted-data label exists in the whole tree, for MiniApp context (src/apps/desktop/src/api/miniapp_agent_api.rs:130); webfetch/websearch results are allowed by the Ask preset baseline without any marking (tool_permissions.rs:204-206)
one_why: With terminal, filesystem and (config-gated) computer-use tools all executing model output, web-page content is a live prompt-injection-to-RCE path; the corpus has no subject that solved this well, but bitfun's reach is among the widest and its silence is total.

subject: bitfun
title: Bash rule matching is deliberately asymmetric: Allow needs exact string equality (prefix-glob allow forgery blocked) while deny/ask stay glob-matched on the raw command string, so deny rules remain bypassable by command tricks
evidence: permission_intent_effect: for action 'bash', Allow matches only rule.resource==command or the catch-all ('*','*'), whereas Ask/Deny use wildcard_matches (src/crates/execution/agent-runtime/src/permission.rs:85-103); remembered 'Always' grants for bash are also exact-resource (permission.rs:127-130, grants_for_reply :752-771 saving only request.save_resources); the command string reaching these rules is the raw trimmed input (src/crates/assembly/core/src/agentic/tools/implementations/exec_command/command.rs:731-740); the real shell parser (lexer + bounded AST) is used only by the edit-constraint guard and its own doc says 'not a shell interpreter or a sandbox' (src/crates/execution/tool-execution/src/shell_analysis/mod.rs:1-4)
one_why: The anti-forgery direction (harder to match Allow) is the right asymmetry and worth copying, but a user-written deny of 'rm *' does not see '; rm -rf' or 'sudo rm' -- the analyzer that could fix this already exists one crate over and is wired to the wrong consumer.

subject: bitfun
title: CI never runs the whole test space: every cargo-test invocation is -p-scoped (and often a single test filter or --no-default-features slice), with no coverage gate, no fuzzing, and no in-CI evals
evidence: all test invocations in .github/workflows/ci.yml (682 lines, ~79 jobs) are scoped, e.g. -p openbitfun-cli -p openbitfun-acp (:164-186), single-test filters like -p terminal-core shutdown_returns_only_after_process_exit_is_confirmed (:184-186), feature-sliced core runs (:315-319, :411), no cargo test --workspace / --all-targets / nextest anywhere; grep for coverage|codecov|tarpaulin|llvm-cov, cargo-fuzz|libfuzzer|proptest|quickcheck, and eval workflows all return zero hits across the workflows dir; Rust test-side is ~81k LOC against ~980k Rust LOC (census cross-checked by scout)
one_why: The targeted jobs are deliberate (runner disk limits, ci.yml:195 comment) and the ones that do run are property-grade, but coverage is a hand-maintained list -- a new crate or feature combination can be untested forever without any signal; verification stays capped at 7 (the errata 8-ceiling would hold anyway absent fuzz/evals).

subject: bitfun
title: Honesty about what is not enforced: docs mark Sandbox as Planned, computer-use refuses isolation claims, git ownership trust is never granted implicitly, and relay-server hard-fails on insecure configurations
evidence: docs/architecture/product-architecture.md:96,125 list Sandbox as planned/not-in-production and :129 states design or empty-port does not raise maturity; docs/architecture/computer-use-control.md:34 'no claim of Wayland isolation for legacy X11 calls' and :41; src/crates/services/services-integrations/src/git/trust.rs:19-21 'Trust is never granted implicitly: nothing in this module is invoked as a fallback of a failed operation' while preserving git 2.35.2 ownership protection; relay server refuses to boot anonymous (src/apps/relay-server/src/main.rs:42 'anonymous relay mode is no longer supported'), refuses wildcard CORS with account APIs enabled (:44-48), and 503s all published-page routes until isolated origins are configured (:88-94,:131-146, route-gate test :152-160); SECURITY.md:5 admits broad reach ('filesystem, terminal, Git, MCP, and remote control')
one_why: Per the rubric's 'honesty about what they don't enforce' clause this partially earns back the sandbox absence -- unlike codel whose docs mislead, bitfun's docs match the code and its server prefers failure to a dangerous default; the honesty exception stops at the FullAccess preset, which is documented as a feature, not a risk.

subject: grok-build

one_why: Serializing every mutation through one command channel removes lock discipline from the loop itself and makes each behavior independently testable per concern file.

evidence: xai-grok-shell/src/leader/mod.rs:1-40 (leader process diagram: TUI/IDE/headless over ACP+UDS); grep -rn 'ChatStateActor|process_conversation_turn' crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/src hits only log-parsing test fixtures (xai-grok-pager/src/views/list_pane/render.rs:1022); xai-grok-pager/Cargo.toml:100 (xai-chat-state optional); pager acp client in xai-grok-pager/src/acp/ and src/app/acp_handler/

subject: grok-build
title: The shell crate holds runtime, leader/relay/remote, persistence and wiring in one 436k-LOC compilation unit
evidence: scout census: xai-grok-shell 436k LOC; agent/mvp_agent/agent_ops.rs:5,236 lines with #![cfg_attr(rustfmt, rustfmt::skip)] at :1 and 148 pub fns; leader/, relay/, remote/, session/, upload/ all inside the same crate (src/ tree)

subject: grok-build
title: Session persistence publishes an explicit hard-power-loss contract: awaited acks, barriers, fsync-before-rename, latched write errors
evidence: xai-grok-shell/src/session/persistence.rs:3-14 (Loss contract on hard power loss: fire-and-forget bounded to turn tail; FlushAndAck means on stable media; failed buffered write latches until next barrier which returns the error; atomic rename fsyncs temp and syncs parent dirs); ~20 companion test files session/persistence_*_tests.rs (e.g. persistence_io_error_to_acp_tests.rs, persistence_actor_lifetime_tests.rs)
one_why: No anchor subject states what survives a power cut; codex's rollout journals at the 9 rung have no written durability contract, making this the most portable operability artifact in the tree.

subject: grok-build
title: Reconnect resumes mid-stream via eventId cursors into updates.jsonl, with a replay buffer in the actor loop
evidence: acp_session_impl/updates.rs:481-482 (Must not stamp an eventId: a reconnect cursor pointing at an id absent from updates.jsonl never resolves and forces full replay); run_loop.rs:368 ReplayBuffer, :629-648 consume_chunk/flush arms; interrupted turns closed on the replay rail so clients paint an end marker (interrupted_turn.rs:35-50); pager reconnect suite xai-grok-pager/src/app/acp_handler/tests/reconnect.rs:974 (mid-subagent reconnect replay)
one_why: Every notification is cursor-addressable and durable, so a dropped TUI or IDE client reattaches without a full transcript replay -- crash-adjacent recovery at the protocol level, beyond the resume-only story of codex/pi.

subject: grok-build
title: Dead-process turns are recorded at load with a distinct 'interrupted' stop reason and surfaced to user and model
evidence: session/interrupted_turn.rs:5-11 (INTERRUPTED_STOP_REASON, transcript text 'committed tool results were kept'); :28-31 model_reminder; scanned from events.jsonl tail (:15); xai-grok-active-sessions/src/lib.rs:1-2 (clean exit removes entry, crash leaves it, next register() prunes dead PIDs); session-level crash-restart supervisor with invalidation (leader/mod.rs:823-826; spawn.rs:4 supervisor note)
one_why: Crash is a first-class terminal state distinct from error/cancelled -- the crush-8 rung (recover middleware) upgraded with post-mortem semantics and a restart supervisor.

subject: grok-build
title: Every prompt is a rewind checkpoint with optional file snapshots; history repair is dry-runnable and forks truncate at a prompt index
evidence: acp_session_impl/rewind.rs:20-22 ('Every prompt is a checkpoint: [0..N-1]'), :24-77 (metadata-only picker join with file snapshots); fork.rs:14-49 (ForkSessionRequest.target_prompt_index, worktree session_kind); run_loop.rs:1302 (RepairHistory { dry_run }); updates.rs:6-14 (closes_cancel_rewind_window: hook-gate output keeps the Ctrl+C rewind window open)
one_why: Rewind state is computed from disk metadata rather than in-memory bookkeeping, so checkpoint lists survive restarts, and cancel-window semantics are defined per update type instead of ad hoc.

subject: grok-build
title: One leader process per machine owns all agent state; clients attach/detach over a namespaced UDS protocol
evidence: leader/mod.rs:1-40 (single-leader-per-machine, ~/.grok/leader.sock, request-id namespacing, session-ownership routing); leader/mod.rs:969 (client reattach contract: re-initialize + session/load replay); acp_session.rs:784 (resident session/load re-applies attach policy via UpdateAttachPolicy); fault-injection proxy for leader IPC in xai-grok-test-support/src/uds_proxy.rs:87 (UdsProxy)

subject: grok-build

evidence: run_loop.rs:1124 (InterjectQueuedPrompt { id, expected_version, owner }); run_loop.rs:1017 (InjectNotification { prompt_id, priority, source }); commands.rs:384 (Prompt.send_now cancel-and-send, also derived server-side during interruptible waits); queue arms run_loop.rs:1086-1117 (remove/reorder/clear/edit/hold/release); tests acp_session_tests/interjection_actor_tests.rs, interjection_tests.rs
