subject: jcode
title: Agent loop is process-separated from every product surface, and the dependency direction is CI-enforced
evidence: crates/jcode-app-core/src/agent/turn_loops.rs:53 (run_turn) lives in jcode-app-core, whose Cargo.toml:68-70 states 'jcode-app-core does NOT depend on any jcode-tui-* crate'; .github/workflows/ci.yml:87-89 runs scripts/check_dependency_boundaries.py in CI; the TUI is a socket client of the daemon (crates/jcode-tui/src/tui/backend.rs:325 Stream::connect(server::socket_path())); SDK/ACP/headless/iOS attach to the same daemon (map + src/cli/args.rs Serve/Connect/Acp commands)
one_why: This is the exact property the 8->9 architecture gap names: the loop cannot re-fuse with a UI surface because the build itself forbids the edge, and CI catches the regression, not a code review.

subject: jcode
title: Session journal replay salvages torn/glued lines instead of truncating the transcript at the first bad byte
evidence: crates/jcode-base/src/session/persistence.rs:29-57 salvage_glued_journal_entries scans for '{"meta":' entry starts and stream-parses consecutive complete entries; :60-110 replay_journal_lines counts skipped/salvaged and emits SESSION_PERSISTENCE corruption events; :186-196 checkpoint_snapshot bails on destructive-empty checkpoint replacing a non-empty transcript, with :133-166 pre-wipe .bak copies; tests at crates/jcode-base/src/session_tests/cases.rs:1028 (skip corrupt keep tail), :1091 (salvage glued on torn line), :1148 (heal via checkpoint on next save)
one_why: Crash/full-disk mid-append corruption is the classic way agents silently lose the last prompts; jcode names the failure mode in comments and ships three targeted regression tests, which is defended-and-tested rather than hopeful.

subject: jcode
title: Daemon self-reload execs a new binary in place with per-session recovery records, GC, and restart snapshots
evidence: crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/reload.rs:16-29 unlinks stale socket pair and detaches stdio before exec (SIGPIPE fix), :154-165 finalizes in-process background tasks before exec since exec runs no destructors; server/reload_recovery.rs:6 7-day pending-record GC, per-session records with Initiator/InterruptedPeer/Headless roles and dir fsync (:71-83); restart_snapshot.rs:9-31 auto-restore-on-next-start snapshot; reload_tests.rs 650 lines / 12 tests
one_why: Sessions surviving a binary swap is an operability plane none of the anchors reach (codex/pi resume from journals only); it is also the largest crash-consistency surface in the repo, and the record/GC design plus tests show it was engineered, not stumbled into.

subject: jcode
title: Crash recovery derives recovery sessions per crash-group window, with dedupe against existing recoveries
evidence: crates/jcode-base/src/session/crash.rs:10 60-second RELEVANT_CRASH_GROUP_WINDOW_SECS, :14-16 recover_crashed_sessions is text-only, :20-28 picker-driven variant is 'intentionally stricter' to avoid restoring stale crashes, :43-53 dedupes via existing session_recovery_* parent tracking; detect_crash/recover exercised in crates/jcode-base/src/session_tests/cases.rs
one_why: Restoring the right crashed group after a daemon crash (not every stale Crashed-status session on disk) is a UX-level crash posture beyond crush's recover-middleware rung; the text-only caveat means tool side-effects are not replayed.

subject: jcode
title: Turn-loop retry and cancel budgets are tuned to named production incidents with regression guards
evidence: crates/jcode-app-core/src/agent/turn_loops.rs:26-31 MAX_EMPTY_POST_TOOL_CONTINUATION_ATTEMPTS=5 justified by 'one empty response observed once in 43 turns silently ended a 20-hour benchmark run'; :76-80 cancel check at loop head guards re-entry from recovery paths ('issue #732, regression of #428'); turn_cancel_registry.rs (295 LOC) registers active turns so session-level cancels reach stale control handles, with tests :178-216; agent_tests.rs 41 tokio tests covering soft-interrupt injection, compaction replay, interrupt-before-notify hangs (:891,:904)
one_why: Silent-stop and unkillable-turn are the two loop bugs that destroy trust in long runs; here each has a constant, a comment naming the incident, and a regression test -- the strongest available signal the loop's properties are actually observed in the field.

subject: jcode
title: 217k-LOC jcode-tui is a presentation god-region: 41 files over 2.5k LOC, capped just under the 5k errata trigger
evidence: wc -l over crates/src: largest non-test files crates/jcode-tui/src/tui/app/inline_interactive.rs 4753, ui_messages.rs 4480, app/input.rs 4280, app/commands.rs 3782, ui.rs 3720; exactly one file repo-wide exceeds 5000 LOC incl. tests; CI oversized-file ratchet at .github/workflows/ci.yml:71 caps further growth; app-core mirrors it with server/client_lifecycle.rs 3894 and tool/communicate.rs 3490
one_why: The ratchet holds the region at 'largest file 4753', exactly under the errata's >5k docking trigger; a slightly worse maintainer would already have pi-style 6.8k files, and the process boundary hides how dense this tree is -- it is the main thing keeping architecture at 9 rather than 10.

subject: jcode
title: Opt-in daemon debug socket exposes structured state and prompt-level introspection commands
evidence: src/cli/debug.rs:7-20 debug command client talking to a second *-debug.sock; crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/debug.rs:563-566 debug socket only allows ping, state, and debug_command; debug_help.rs:178-181 documents agent:context, client:frame, set_provider commands; debug_command_exec.rs:647-877 tests for agent:context output; jcode-tui/src/tui/backend.rs:24-48 DebugEvent::StateSnapshot streaming full TUI state
one_why: This is codex's 'debug prompt-input' equivalent (the 9-rung operability differentiator): structured, scriptable introspection into exactly what the provider would receive, gated onto a separate socket so it is not part of the normal client trust surface.

subject: jcode
title: Rewind maps through the rendered-visible index and one-step undo restores provider-session identity alongside messages
evidence: crates/jcode-app-core/src/agent/turn_execution.rs:246-257 doc explains index is against the rendered transcript because counting raw stored messages 'would count tool-result messages the UI never numbers, sending /rewind N far earlier than the on-screen message N (issue #432)'; :268-284 rewind captures RewindUndoSnapshot (messages + both provider_session_ids + visible count), resets provider session so the next request sends truncated context from scratch; :288-303 undo_rewind restores all three; rewind flow also covered in crates/jcode-tui/src/tui/app/tests/remote_events_reload_01/
one_why: Checkpoint-revert systems usually get two things wrong -- off-by-N against what the user sees, and reverting messages while leaving the upstream resumable session pointing at the truncated-away conversation; jcode names both failure modes in code and snapshots around them.

subject: jcode
title: Two-stage blast-radius gate wired unconditionally into the bash tool: deterministic tokenizer-based risk cascade (Safe/Low/Confirm/Catastrophic) classifying by what would be destroyed rather than by command name, with a path-only absolute deny tier that never depends on parsing the command correctly
evidence: crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/bash.rs:878-885 (gate called in execute before spawn, no config toggle); crates/jcode-command-risk/src/lib.rs:93-329 (assess: wrapper unwrapping :160-247, sh -c recursion :253-261, pipe-fed destructive escalation :302-313); crates/jcode-command-risk/src/paths.rs:34-56 (absolute protected-path lists), :130-147 (lexical `..` normalization)
one_why: The deny tier is the one protection that cannot be talked around, and it is deliberately decoupled from parser correctness (`rm -rf ~/../..` normalizes to `/` and dies, paths_tests.rs:44-52); every other subject in the corpus gates by command-name denylist or by user approval, none by computed blast radius.

subject: jcode
title: Reflection gate instead of LLM judge: a Confirm verdict is refused once and only unlocked by a model-supplied `justification` naming the user request; blind retry fails identically, bare affirmations are rejected -- refusal not satisfiable by repetition
evidence: crates/jcode-command-risk/src/gate.rs:77-101 (gate), :46-71 (is_substantive, self-described 'intentionally a low bar'), :75 (MIN_JUSTIFICATION_LEN=25), :104-124 (reflection prompt forces comparison to the user's actual request); gate_tests.rs:68-77 (blind-retry equality property), :57-66 (reflect-on-first-attempt), :79-91 ('yes'/'ok'/'proceed.' rejected); crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/bash_tests.rs:1011-1050 (two-attempt flow through the real tool)
one_why: Spends test-time compute on alignment at the point of action with no second model, and the core property (repetition is not consent) is pinned by a direct test -- portable to any approval design, including ones layered on a sandbox.

subject: jcode
title: No human-approval gate on the default interactive path: the two-tier permission system that classifies bash/write/edit as RequiresPermission is consumed ONLY by ambient sessions; in a normal session the model self-justifies and no user ever sees the command before it runs
evidence: docs/SAFETY_SYSTEM.md:5 ('Currently the only consumer is ambient mode'); crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/ambient.rs:98 ('request_permission is only available to ambient sessions'); crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/tests.rs:1105-1119 (test pins request_permission absent from normal sessions); crates/jcode-base/src/safety.rs:177-183 (classify: bash = RequiresPermission) wired to nothing in tool/mod.rs; crates/jcode-tui-permissions/src/lib.rs:833-866 (run_permissions is a queue reviewer for ambient requests, not a per-call prompt)
one_why: This is what separates the 6-rung (cline/crush/pi: approval binds in-loop and is tested) from jcode: the approval machinery exists, is well built, and is disconnected from the 99% code path; a runaway model in an interactive session faces only the catastrophic deny tier.

subject: jcode
title: Zero kernel isolation, and the absolute-deny tier covers deletion/truncation only: write and edit tools carry no is_catastrophic_target wiring, so the model can overwrite /etc/passwd with the write tool while the bash gate blocks `echo bad > /etc/passwd`
evidence: grep bubblewrap|bwrap|seatbelt|landlock|seccomp over repo: zero hits; crates/jcode-command-risk/src/lib.rs:29-33 (self-declared 'defense in depth, not a sandbox'); crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/apply_patch.rs:182-188 (catastrophic check exists only for DeleteFile); grep is_catastrophic|protected in crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/edit.rs and write.rs: zero hits; contrast crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/bash_destructive_gate.rs:112-124 (bash redirect to /etc/passwd blocked)
one_why: The asymmetry is concrete and exploitable rather than hypothetical: protection follows the verb, not the path, so the same file is guarded through one tool and wide open through another; nothing underneath catches it because there is no sandbox.

subject: jcode
title: No prompt-injection posture at all despite webfetch, browser, computer-control, MCP, native-SSH and gmail/composio surfaces consuming untrusted content; the named 'injection' tests test message ordering of user soft-interrupts, not adversarial content
evidence: grep -i 'prompt.?injection' over *.rs: zero hits; grep -i untrusted|injection|hostile in crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/webfetch.rs and browser_fast.rs: zero hits; tests/test_injection_fix.py:1-11 (docstring: verifies user messages injected after tool_results, not before); tests/test_injection_thorough.py likewise (4 tests, ordering semantics)
one_why: A webpage that steers the model faces exactly the same (thin) controls as the user's own request -- only the catastrophic deny tier -- and the catastrophic tier defends against accidents (issue #604), not adversaries; no anchor except codex has real content-boundary handling.

subject: jcode
title: pre_tool policy hook is the user-side enforcement seam: synchronous, exit-2 blocks with stderr fed back to the model, multi-policy compose, and a deliberately tested fail-open contract ('it is your trust boundary, not jcode')
evidence: docs/HOOKS.md:69-83 (gate semantics + fail-open rationale); crates/jcode-base/src/hooks.rs:373 (run_pre_tool_gate), :19 (module doc fail-open), :668-699 (exit 0 allow / exit 2 block test against `rm -rf /`), :753-779 (hang, odd exit, missing binary all fail open); crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/mod.rs:939-949 (wired in registry execute, skipped when unconfigured); crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/tests.rs:509-568 (registry-level block test)
one_why: Closest thing jcode has to cline's plan-mode guard, but off by default like pi's blocking hook; the fail-open choice is explicit, documented, and tested in all three failure modes, which is more honesty than nanocoder's silent jail fallback.

subject: jcode
title: CI anti-silent-skip discipline: cohorts that would self-skip are fetched-and-forced, then CI greps the log for the skip message and fails the job ('a skipped test still reports ok... only the skip message can' distinguish verified from did-nothing); every cohort step's comment names the incident number it fixes
evidence: ci.yml:240-278 (embedding cohort: downloads model, then grep -q skip -> ::error); ci.yml:221-238 and :280-298 (#651/#660: tests 'compiled and never run' failure modes, cohort steps added); ci.yml:67-99 (ratchet battery: warning budget, oversized-file, oversized-test, panic-prone, swallowed-error, crate boundaries, SDK parity, unused deps); ci.yml:378-383 (cargo-audit + secret-pattern scan strict)
one_why: Every anchor reviewer complained about tests-existence-vs-tests-run; jcode is the only subject that has institutionalized the distinction in CI itself, and it is cheap to copy.

subject: jcode
title: Telemetry honesty check passes with one flag: transcript sharing is genuinely off-by-default, versioned-consent, double-redacted before upload; ordinary usage telemetry however is ON by default (opt-out via marker/env), and TELEMETRY.md's 'anonymous, minimal' framing understates that default
evidence: TELEMETRY.md:5-7 (transcript program 'off by default', consent_versioned), :17-26 (redaction classes, worker re-check), :45 and :428-447 (disable paths); crates/jcode-telemetry-core/src/lib.rs:444-465 (status(): enabled = opt_out_source.is_none() -- default-on)
one_why: Checked the scout's 'verify opt-in claims' flag: the sensitive tier is honest and enforced in code; the usage tier is default-on, which is common but should be named in the report rather than inherited from the README's framing.

subject: jcode
title: Crash behavior is classified, not swallowed: live turns are panic-caught with Crash-vs-Failure stop reasons distinguished without string-parsing error text, crashed sessions are detected and group-recovered, and a CI ratchet caps panic-prone production usage
evidence: crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/live_turn.rs:253-272 (catch_live_turn_panic, TurnStopReason::Crash), :275-297 (test: panic vs provider-text error classified differently); crates/jcode-base/src/session/crash.rs:14-60 (recover_crashed_sessions, 60s crash-group window), crates/jcode-base/src/session_tests/cases.rs:647-663 (recovery preserves debug flag); ci.yml:79 + scripts/check_panic_budget.py (ratchet: existing files may not increase unwrap/expect/panic counts)
one_why: Crash honesty is the operational twin of safety honesty: the system records 'this turn crashed' as a first-class state a user can recover from, rather than the log.Printf-into-the-void pattern that sank codel's operability.

subject: jcode
title: Three compaction modes (reactive 80% / proactive EWMA-growth projection / semantic embedding topic-shift) behind a shared anti-signal guard, with context measured from provider-reported usage under per-provider-family cache accounting
evidence: crates/jcode-base/src/compaction.rs:11-16 (module doc: Reactive/Proactive/Semantic with embedding fallback), :485-500 (anti_signals_block: already-compacting, proactive_floor, min_samples universal guards), :533-553 (should_compact_proactively: EWMA over per-turn token deltas with configurable alpha and lookahead), :583 (should_compact_semantic), :860-876 (mode dispatch incl. Semantic -> proactive fallback); crates/jcode-compaction-core/src/lib.rs:9 (COMPACTION_THRESHOLD 0.80), :13 (CRITICAL_THRESHOLD 0.95 sync hard-compact), :366-394 (effective_context_tokens_from_usage: OpenAI counts cache read/write as input subsets, Anthropic-family adds cache_read+cache_creation, shape-inferred when counters are ambiguous); tests in crates/jcode-compaction-core/src/lib.rs:729-780 (split/subset/zero-uncached accounting cases) + crates/jcode-base/src/compaction_tests.rs
one_why: codex 9 has three tiers and pi 8 has a projected trigger; jcode has both at once -- and the projection runs on the provider's real post-usage numbers corrected per provider cache-accounting family, which is the 'measure what the model actually receives' discipline of pi pushed to multi-provider ground truth, plus an anchor-unseen semantic topic-shift mode with an embedding cache (compaction.rs:202-208).

subject: jcode
title: No-LLM hard-compact above 95% plus a distinct recovery path for provider 413 'request too large' driven by base64 images, with bounded image token cost asserted in tests
evidence: crates/jcode-compaction-core/src/lib.rs:13 (CRITICAL_THRESHOLD triggers synchronous drop-so-the-call-doesn't-fail), :455-518 (build_emergency_summary_text + collect_emergency_summary_hints + extract_file_mentions -- rule-based summary, no model call), :549-711 (emergency_truncate_tool_results / emergency_truncate_large_payloads / emergency_strip_large_images / emergency_truncated_tool_result), :609-642 (is_request_payload_too_large_error with independent-status-code parsing), :30-41 (PAYLOAD_IMAGE_CHAR_BUDGET docstring: Anthropic ~32 MB serialized cap, driven 'almost entirely by inline base64 images, which the normal token-budget accounting deliberately undercounts'), :58 (IMAGE_TOKEN_COST=1600) with test :862-887 (image cost is bounded, not proportional to base64 length); crates/jcode-base/src/compaction.rs:43-44 (hard-threshold pending wait/poll constants)
one_why: This is codex's no-LLM token-budget tier (compact_token_budget.rs:19-40) matched, plus a second failure mode no anchor in the set addresses: the token budget and the payload-byte budget are separate accounting problems, and jcode names that explicitly and recovers from both without spending a summarization call.

subject: jcode
title: Sliding READ/WRITE Anthropic breakpoint strategy with a stated 4-breakpoint budget, per-model-generation OpenAI cache-TTL handling, and a three-layer KV-cache miss observability stack where every miss is classified and attributed or flagged as undocumented
evidence: crates/jcode-provider-anthropic/src/lib.rs:869-878 (strategy docstring: second-to-last assistant = READ marker, last assistant = WRITE marker, 'Budget: system (1) + tools (1) + messages (up to 2) = 4 total, within Anthropic's limit'), :890-921 (two-marker placement), :684-685 (last-tool breakpoint); crates/jcode-base/src/provider/openai.rs:134-230 (supports_extended_prompt_cache_retention / uses_prompt_cache_options: GPT-5.6+ uses prompt_cache_options.ttl not prompt_cache_retention / prompt_cache_ttl_for_model); crates/jcode-base/src/kv_cache_monitor.rs:1-15 (daemon-side so ALL clients get the same classified KvCacheMiss, not just the TUI), :18-20 (MIN_MISSED_TOKENS=1024 noise floor, OPTIMAL_OK_PCT=85), :33-46 (RequestSignature::extends append-only check), :60-71 (MissReason: provider/model/upstream switch, expired, system/tools/prefix changed, zero/low read); crates/jcode-app-core/src/agent.rs:196 emits ServerEvent::KvCacheMiss, surfaced on the public protocol (crates/jcode-harness-api/src/events.rs:166); crates/jcode-base/src/cache_tracker.rs:1-8 (prefix-hash fallback for providers that report no cache metrics, e.g. Fireworks via OpenRouter); crates/jcode-base/src/cache_invalidation.rs:1-12 (documented-invalidation journal; 'An empty journal around a harness-caused miss is itself signal'), record call sites crates/jcode-base/src/config.rs:323, crates/jcode-base/src/skill.rs:623
one_why: codex 9 earns cache credit for key-gated reuse, pi 8 for active warming; jcode's distinct contribution is making cache discipline observable and attributable -- a miss is either matched to a documented harness action or it is by construction a bug report, and the monitor lives daemon-side so SDK/desktop/ACP clients inherit it (the TUI-only detection this replaced is named in kv_cache_monitor.rs:3-5).

subject: jcode
title: agentgrep attenuates results using a harness-built model of what the agent has already been exposed to -- read ranges, prior grep output, trace outlines, shell output paths -- with a file-freshness multiplier, matching the README's adaptive-truncation claim
evidence: crates/jcode-app-core/src/tool/agentgrep/context.rs:107 (collect_tool_exposures walks the persisted session), :158/:214/:291/:444/:609 (per-source collectors: read ranges normalized from tool input at :381, prior agentgrep output, bash output, trace, shell-output path scraping), :659-728 (tune_known_file / tune_known_region / tune_known_symbol), :729-780 (apply_exposure_tuning), :781-828 (file_freshness_multiplier via mtime so stale 'already seen' credit decays when the file changed); :3-26 (per-tool-call harness context JSON consumed by the grep binary, wired at tool/agentgrep.rs:344,416,422); user-facing claim at README.md:688 ('adaptively truncates returns based on what the agent has already seen') verified against this code, not marketing
one_why: No anchor in the frozen set attenuates tool output by seen-content: cline 7 budgets the transcript, crush's loop breaker (loop_detection.go) prevents repeated work but not repeated tokens. This is context economy at the tool-output layer, the layer that actually dominates long sessions.

subject: jcode
title: Swarm state is durable with per-swarm serialization locks, swarm mutations are idempotent via hashed request keys, and a hot binary reload survives via a pending/delivered recovery ledger with GC
evidence: crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/swarm_persistence.rs:13-20 (durable dir under ~/.jcode/state, pre-0.36 tmpfs location migrated away, 7-day dormant-plan retention), :21-31 (SWARM_OPERATION_LOCKS rationale: 'acquire this before reading the independently locked in-memory maps so an older snapshot cannot finish after a newer one' + separate file locks); crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/durable_state.rs:26-40 (hashed_request_key), :46-58 (load_json_state with staleness-based delete); crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/comm_control.rs:1293,1481 (swarm mutation request key guarding replayed mutations), crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/comm_await.rs:337 + await_members_state.rs:139-152 (await-members state machine persisted across restart); crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/reload_recovery.rs:8 (7-day pending-record age), :12-45 (ReloadRecoveryRole Initiator/InterruptedPeer/Headless, Pending/Delivered status persisted before delivery -- crash between write and deliver is a named state), :48-52 GC stats; crates/jcode-base/src/session/crash.rs:14-29 (crash-group recovery with a 60s relevance window, and a stricter picker-based recovery that avoids restoring stale crashes)
one_why: Above cline 8's durable cron + event journal: the odd workload here is the daemon swapping its own binary in place (selfdev) with swarms mid-flight, so the recovery design has to model 'killed after writing the intent but before delivering it' -- and does, with age-bounded ledgers and idempotency keys rather than hope.

subject: jcode
title: Runaway caps and budgets at every orchestration level -- absolute swarm membership cap, configurable live-worker concurrency default 32, adaptive rate-limit backoff for ambient runs, overnight usage projections -- with denial text written so the model knows what to do next
evidence: crates/jcode-swarm-core/src/lib.rs:47-48 (MAX_SWARM_MEMBERS=1000 'absolute cap'; configurable live-worker RAM budget applies first) + crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/swarm.rs:26-32 (deep swarms have no depth limit but budget and cap still apply -- the runaway-prevention comment); crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/comm_session.rs:1383-1393 (machine-safety budget denial: names the limit, the config key agents.swarm_max_concurrent_agents, and the remedy 'Let existing agents finish or stop them'); crates/jcode-base/src/config/default_file.rs:464 (default 32), env_overrides.rs:419 (env override); crates/jcode-app-core/src/ambient/scheduler.rs:168-210 (AdaptiveScheduler, backoff_multiplier doubles on rate-limit hits, calculate_interval consumes RateLimitInfo); crates/jcode-overnight-core/src/lib.rs:142-170 (UsageProjection embedded in overnight run status); gap noted: no first-class queue command -- turn queuing is soft-interrupt persistence (crates/jcode-app-core/src/agent/interrupts.rs:100-107 persists pending interrupts) + TUI queue mode (crates/jcode-tui/src/tui/app.rs:1597)
one_why: nanocoder 6 is docked precisely for 'no budgets'; jcode budgets concurrency, membership, rate, and overnight spend, and the budget-exceeded message is engineered as model-facing guidance (codex's queue primitive has no jcode equivalent at CLI level, which is the one codex-9 orchestration piece missing here).

subject: jcode
title: Stable NDJSON harness API with per-frame version negotiation, Unknown catch-alls, schema/capability snapshot tests, and a published TS SDK whose surface parity with the Rust crate is enforced in CI from both sides
evidence: crates/jcode-harness-api/src/lib.rs:1-16 (design rules: one JSON object per line, every frame carries protocol major, clients must ignore unknown fields via serde(other)-style fallback, additive=minor / breaking=major-negotiated); :46-51 (schema_snapshot + capability_coverage test modules); sdk/typescript/package.json:2-3 (published @1jehuang/jcode-sdk v1.2.0); sdk/typescript/README.md:6-9 ('Schema drift is guarded from both sides: a Rust test fails if a variant is added without mirroring it here, and a Node test fails if the tag sets diverge'); .github/workflows/ci.yml:91-93 ('Enforce Rust and TypeScript SDK surface parity' -- cargo test -p jcode-sdk parity)
one_why: codex 9's interop score rests on a versioned app-server protocol + CI-published SDKs; jcode replicates that contract shape as a solo project, and the parity gate is bidirectional, which is stricter than 'we remember to update the SDK'.

subject: jcode
title: MCP is client-side and stdio-only: HTTP/SSE servers are recognized and skipped, and there is no mode exposing jcode as an MCP server
evidence: README.md:604 ('jcode currently supports stdio (command-based) servers only; HTTP/SSE entries ("type": "http"/"sse") are recognized and skipped with a log line'); grep across crates/ src/ for McpServer/serve_mcp/as_mcp finds only config parsing and the ACP validator (src/cli/acp.rs:1703-1710), no server-mode implementation; src/cli/acp.rs:1703-1710 + test :2015-2020: ACP hosts' non-empty mcpServers params are deliberately tolerated-but-ignored 'until session-scoped MCP is supported'; headless MCP load at src/cli/commands.rs:2503-2512 reads ~/.jcode/mcp.json with a documented cold-schema-cache gap
one_why: The codex-9 rung is 'MCP client AND server'; cline 8 is client-only but with four IDE surfaces. jcode sits at the cline rung on MCP and below it on transport breadth -- remote/HTTP MCP (the norm in 2026 hosted servers) is silently skipped with a log line.

subject: jcode
title: Session import/resume from rival harnesses -- claude-code, codex, opencode, pi, cursor -- with byte-bounded transcript folds so an imported history cannot dominate context
evidence: crates/jcode-base/src/import.rs:1-3 (module purpose), :20-24 (jcode_import_core exports imported_{claude_code,codex,cursor,opencode,pi}_session_id, is_cursor_subagent_transcript), :616,667-670,736,1193 (pi session discovery -> import paths), :35-40 (IMPORT_HISTORY_MAX_MESSAGES=160 / 256 KiB total / 32 KiB per block, comment: prevents 'an imported multi-hundred-message transcript from dominating first paint and every subsequent TUI frame'); crates/jcode-app-core/src/server/client_state.rs:81 (IMPORT_SOURCE_CODES: [opencode, claude-code, openai-codex]); user-facing claim README.md:692 ('Session resume is supported for codex, claude code, opencode, and pi')
one_why: No anchor imports a competitor's sessions; interop is framed as protocol surface (MCP/ACP/SDK) while jcode also treats user migration from rival harnesses as an interop axis -- and applies its own context-economy fold at the import boundary, tying the two lane dimensions together.

subject: jcode
title: 82-file docs tree with an honest current/plans/proposals split and good diagnostics docs, but its own index links two nonexistent desktop docs, the harness-API doc reference is dangling, and the ~2.1k-LOC ACP adapter has zero in-repo documentation
evidence: docs/README.md:5-12 (layout conventions: current-state top level, plans/audits/proposals separated -- a genuinely good practice), :19 ('Desktop app: DESKTOP_APP_ARCHITECTURE.md, DESKTOP_CODEBASE_ARCHITECTURE.md' -- neither file exists in docs/, only DESKTOP_AUTH_SDK.md); crates/jcode-harness-api/src/lib.rs:7 cites docs/HARNESS_API_AND_DESKTOP_REWRITE.md which does not exist; grep -ri acp across docs/, sdk/, README.md returns zero matches while src/cli/acp.rs implements ACP_PROTOCOL_VERSION=1 (:13), three profile tiers (:23-43), and full JSON-RPC handling dispatched at src/cli/dispatch.rs:166; positive controls: docs/PROVIDER_DOCTOR.md:1-9 (tiered offline/catalog/full diagnostics with 'what to try next' hints and --json), README.md:31-46 + :817-847 (multi-channel install: brew, curl script, PowerShell, source); no SECURITY.md in root (only docs/SECURITY_DEPENDENCIES.md)
one_why: pi 9's bar is 30+ docs matching code; jcode has 82 docs whose checkable claims do match (agentgrep adaptive truncation, cache-cold warning at README.md:684 vs kv_cache_monitor.rs), but a self-referentially broken index plus a completely undocumented flagship interop surface is exactly the 'matching code' failure the pi rung docks for -- cline 8's dock for dual-tree confusion is the closest precedent.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Host state is partitioned by lifetime into four named structs - turnRuntime replaced wholesale each Run, taskRuntime spanning one delivery scope, sessionRuntime spanning one conversation, pendingTurn for what outsiders arm - and because atomics/mutexes make whole-assignment illegal for sessionRuntime, a test cross-checks every field against explicit reset/carry-over lists
evidence: internal/runtime/agent/turnruntime.go:11-13,78-82; internal/runtime/agent/sessionstate.go:13-19,55-58; internal/runtime/agent/sessionstate_test.go:14-49 (sessionReset/sessionCarryOver/windowReset/windowCarryOver vs AST field list); tools/repolint/structstate.go:8,64 (scalar-count ratchet; perTurnState grouping pattern)
one_why: Forgotten-reset and cross-turn-contamination are the classic bug class in long-lived agent loops; making lifetime the partition axis, then testing the field lists a struct assignment cannot cover, turns an omission into a failing list-diff instead of a user report.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Eight in-house AST linters encode the boundaries the Go compiler cannot check inside one package - closed utility layer, frontends-only-import-controller, windowState owner list, scalar-state ratchet, coded-refusal-path, error-text-match ban, frontend/wire parity - and run as a required CI job
evidence: tools/repolint/layers.go:13-20 (frontends set), :22-30 (closed leaf layer); tools/repolint/windowstate.go:16-23 (owners), :26-49 (sess.win read check); tools/repolint/structstate.go:64; tools/repolint/refusal.go:14-41; tools/repolint/main.go:38 (error-text); .github/workflows/ci.yml:457 (go run ./tools/repolint)
one_why: No anchor subject gates architecture beyond compile boundaries and a handful of tests; here the layering contract is executable, CI-required, and carries its own ratchet semantics, which is what makes a 132-file package survivable - but it is post-hoc scanning, not the compiler (see c8).

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: 21 effect tests run one prompt through the real boot.Build assembly against a scripted recording provider and assert what actually reaches the provider request, sink, or trajectory - 'component correctness is not system effectiveness' is a codified repo rule, not a slogan
evidence: internal/assembly/boot/effect_test.go:1-4,31-60 (effectRecordingProvider, effectRun); 21 effect_test files in internal/assembly/boot/; REASONIX.md:29-32 (rule text)
one_why: Most suites test components that could each pass while the assembled system silently drops the feature (wiring regressions); asserting at the final boundary through the real assembly is the cheapest gate that catches 'built correctly, never reached'.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Inside the loop's own package, the context window is a peer owner with a bidirectional narrow interface: the loop reaches the window only via a.window(), the window reaches the loop only via a windowHost interface, and any other read of sess.win fails the window-state lint
evidence: internal/runtime/agent/context_window_host.go:12-15 (windowHost), :43-47 (window() built per entry); internal/runtime/agent/sessionstate.go:21-22 (win field, owner comment); tools/repolint/windowstate.go:16-23 (four named owners)
one_why: Codex and pi separate loop from product surfaces; this applies the same discipline to a subsystem *inside* the loop package, so compaction/cache-window invariants have exactly one lock-owner set - the pattern would transplant to any agent with tangling context-management state.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Session leases fence one transcript against four frontends: acquire with holder identity, same-runtime reclaim, cross-runtime detection, plus a parent-guard on recovery branches and idle covered recovery branches trashed by GC rather than left to collide
evidence: internal/state/sessionstore/session_lease.go:84,126,180,225 (TryAcquire/TryReclaimCurrentProcess/HeldByOtherRuntime); internal/state/sessionstore/recovery_gc.go:92 (TryAcquireRecoveryParentGuard), :173 (ReclaimableRecoveryBranches), :221 (TrashCoveredRecoveryBranch)
one_why: crush's 8-rung datadir lock guards the data dir; this guards the session identity itself across CLI/serve/desktop/ACP, with reclaim semantics for a crashed holder - the multi-surface version of the same fence, including what happens to the orphaned recovery branch.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Rewind is coverage-honest: checkpoints are content-addressed per user turn with after-write fingerprints, restore is transactional with compensation, and restoring files under partial coverage is refused unless the user explicitly confirms the named gaps
evidence: internal/state/checkpoint/checkpoint.go:1-14 (schema v2: blob storage, fingerprints, coverage gaps, transactional restore with compensation); internal/session/control/rewind.go:18-28 (ErrRewindCoverageConfirmationRequired, RewindPlanRequiresConfirmation)
one_why: Every checkpoint-revert in the corpus (git-stash or snapshot) silently promises more than it captured; making partial coverage a typed refusal that the frontend must surface and the user must confirm converts a trust leak into an explicit choice.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Runtime-fatal output (panic on any goroutine, fatal runtime error) is mirrored into a per-PID 0600 file via debug.SetCrashOutput and queued for reporting on next start - plus a doctor suite (billing/session/runtime/quality/catalogs subcommands) and zero log.Printf across non-test internal/
evidence: internal/platform/crashreport/fatal.go:10-40 (InstallFatalOutput, debug.SetCrashOutput at :38); internal/frontend/cli/doctor.go:41-60 (subcommand dispatch); measured: grep log.Printf internal --include=*.go minus tests = 0 hits, slog ~206 call sites
one_why: crush's 8-rung recover middleware cannot see runtime fatals that bypass deferred recovery entirely; mirroring the crash descriptor is a ten-line trick that closes the last observability hole, and the zero-log.Printf census means errors reach a structured sink or nowhere visible.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Two packages hold ~46k non-test LOC of the kernel - internal/runtime/agent (132 files, 23.1k) and internal/session/control (102 files, 22.8k) - where intra-package boundaries are enforced by post-hoc AST lint with explicit scope exemptions, not by the compiler
evidence: measured: find internal/runtime/agent -name '*.go' ! -name '*_test.go' | xargs wc -l = 23107; internal/session/control = 22759; tools/repolint/refusal.go:24-27 (adapter exemption keyed to one file); contrast largest non-test files: agent.go 1995, controller.go 1394 - files are split, packages are not
one_why: This is the sole reason the architecture scores 8 not 9: codex's 127 crates make illegal states unimportable at compile time, whereas here any careless PR inside the package can reach across a conceptual boundary and only CI's scan - with its own exemption list - catches it; the discipline is real but one config edit from diffusion.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: An error a caller must distinguish carries identity - errors.Is sentinel inside Go, dotted code through refuse() across HTTP - and two linters enforce it: refusal-path fails any new http.Error in the serve frontend, error-text fails any new match against an error message
evidence: REASONIX.md:49-58 (rule + two live historical defects: catalog.go answering 400 for an unwritable disk; ServerRow classifying auth by regexing /401|403|unauthorized/ over prose an MCP server wrote); tools/repolint/refusal.go:14-41; tools/repolint/main.go:38
one_why: Failure-misattribution is how agents learn wrong lessons (a truncated response reaching the model as 'invalid arguments' trains it to stop batching); the lint pair makes prose-matching a build failure rather than a code-review preference, and the doc records which defects earned each rule.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Bash OS-sandbox defaults ON (not opt-in): empty/unknown config normalises to enforce, per-command Seatbelt/bwrap wrap, and enforce-without-backend refuses the command instead of running it unwrapped
evidence: internal/contract/config/config.go:1004-1017 (BashModeForGOOS: case "" and default -> "enforce"), internal/contract/config/config.go:1578-1583 (default comment: "macOS/Linux jail bash by default"), internal/assembly/boot/tool_environment.go:61-79 (Spec wired from cfg.BashMode(); warn when enforce && !Available), internal/safety/sandbox/sandbox.go:9-12 (fail-closed doc), internal/safety/sandbox/seatbelt_darwin.go:18-23 (sandbox-exec -p wrap), internal/safety/sandbox/prepare_linux.go (bwrap args)
one_why: This is the exact axis that separates codex (10) from nanocoder (5): real machinery AND the right default - nanocoder jails only opt-in and fail-opens to plain sh, Reasonix refuses to run bash at all if the backend is missing.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: If the jail fails to start, running unconfined is a separate, per-escape human decision: a nil approver is fail-closed, typed-nil context values are normalized to absent so the `!= nil` idiom cannot authorize unconfined execution
evidence: internal/safety/sandbox/escape.go:11-24 (EscapeRequest, "Nil means fail closed"), :37-56 (WithEscapeApprover nilutil.IsNil guard + why), internal/tools/builtin/bash_sandbox_escape_test.go:33,65,85 (escape-with-approval / stays-closed-without-approver / denial-blocks-unconfined)
one_why: Most harnesses treat sandbox-unavailable as either silent degradation or hard stop; here degradation is itself an approval surface with tests for the fail-closed direction, and the typed-nil footgun is closed on both the stamping and the reading side.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Network egress is three separate decisions - external network (allow-listed domains via host egress proxy, with per-host ask outside the list), host services (HostAuthorities, default ssh_agent only), and loopback - so one transport flag cannot answer both "may I reach the internet" and "may I reach this daemon socket"
evidence: internal/safety/sandbox/sandbox.go:53-66 (Network/HostAuthorities/Egress/ClosedLoopbackPorts fields + "transport and authority are separate questions"), internal/safety/permission/write_fence.go:14-16 (NetworkEgress subject-sensitive const), internal/session/control/approval.go:693-695 (NetworkEgressApprovalTool needs fresh human even in YOLO), internal/safety/sandbox/host_authority_test.go:100,130,145 (separation + docker-socket denied while network allowed + granted daemon reachable), internal/safety/egress/policy.go:13-17, internal/safety/egress/address.go:9,17-38 (metadata-NET blocking incl. IPv6-embedded IPv4)
one_why: codex's separate network approval (seatbelt_network_policy.sbpl + tools/network_approval.rs) is the anchor 10 marker; Reasonix generalizes it: docker socket as a host authority is denied even with network on, and a domain not on the list asks a per-host human instead of failing or silently passing.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Permission judgement reads shell structure: compound commands are split top-level with quoting/substitution treated as opaque, unparseable shapes (heredocs, unbalanced quotes, leading operators) fall back to whole-string match, and the destructive-command glob table is explicitly labelled UI-warning-only
evidence: internal/safety/permission/bash_decompose.go:3-35, internal/base/shellparse/bash.go, internal/safety/permission/bash_readonly.go:53-56 ("dangerousBashPatterns ... Used only for a UI warning - the deny list is the actual enforcement mechanism"), internal/safety/permission/bash_destructive_git_test.go
one_why: This is the anti-pattern the anchors dock nanocoder for (regex deny-list gating, execute-bash.tsx:189); Reasonix inverts it - structure parses for matching, the regex table exists only to warn, and the file says so.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Full-access has a floor: plan approval, memory write/forget, sandbox escape, managed-config write and network-egress approvals survive YOLO/auto/plan-window and non-interactive nil approvers - bypassAllowsLocked refuses before consulting the posture
evidence: internal/session/control/approval.go:688-700 (RequiresFreshHumanApprovalTool list), :591-596 (requiresFreshApprovalTool checked first in bypassAllowsLocked), :258-260 ("Fresh user decisions ... are never answered by YOLO/full-access"), :61-63 (promptMu serializes to one in-flight decision)
one_why: The usual yolo implementation is a boolean that skips everything; here the bypass path itself has a deny-list of approval classes, which is what makes the posture defensible at all.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Headless Ask defaults to DENY: every explicit non-interactive mode wires a denyPermissionApprover (with an honest refusal reason so the model stops asking for a user who was never there), the CLI default mode maps to ask-fails-closed, and subject-sensitive questions return "needs a person" when unattended
evidence: internal/session/control/approval.go:103-131 (BuildHeadlessApprovalGate: yolo/auto/dontask/ask all get denyPermissionApprover or explicit Allow, one construction point shared by every sub-agent gate), internal/session/control/approval_bridge.go:23-31 (denyPermissionApprover + reason), internal/frontend/cli/cli.go:239-240,494-503 (default ask; "Default/ask fails closed because no UI can answer"), internal/safety/permission/write_fence.go:36-47 (unattendedAsk: "A question with nobody to answer it is a no")
one_why: The classic headless bug is Ask silently becoming Allow; the write_fence comment names the exact failure it fixes ("YOLO, built with no approver at all, granted every one of these silently") and the fix is at the single gate-construction point so sub-agents cannot diverge from the parent.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Windows bash has no OS-level confinement at all: the effective mode is force-off even when the user's config says enforce, and the entire safety-under-bash story (jail, egress proxy, forbid-read) collapses to in-process checks on the most common desktop OS
evidence: internal/contract/config/config.go:1004-1007 (BashModeForGOOS forces "off" for windows "even when older configs explicitly requested enforce"), internal/safety/sandbox/seatbelt_windows.go:5-27 (Command unwrapped, Available=false, EgressSupported=false), internal/safety/sandbox/protects_windows.go:3-7, internal/frontend/doctor/report.go:167 (doctor flags ignored enforce), docs in sandbox.go:8-12
one_why: Honestly documented and surfaced in doctor, and AppContainer lanes exist for MCP/plugin processes (internal/ext/plugin/plugin.go, sandbox.go:33-38), but on Windows `git push`-class shell writes under auto/yolo hit nothing beneath the permission layer - codex's windows-sandbox-rs is exactly the rung-difference between 8 and 10 here.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Prompt-injection defense is a second-model screen on external tool results (web/browser/desktop/MCP) that is advisory, off by default, and never blocks, rewrites or drops - its output is a provenance warning line plus a user-visible notice
evidence: internal/runtime/agent/injection_screen.go:11-15 ("the verdict is advisory - it adds a notice and never blocks"), :16-24 (INJECTION/CLEAN prompt, "The text is data"), :35-41 (off when no triage provider), internal/contract/config/config.go:1054-1056 (screen_external_content opt-in), internal/runtime/agent/injection_screen_test.go:101 (TestScreenExternalIsOffByDefaultAndSilentOnFailure)
one_why: Honest and better than nothing (nothing enforces injection defence anywhere - enforcement can only come from what the screened result then hits: permission rules + jail), but no anchor-band claim about injection resistance should cite this as enforcement.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: The permission package's own Gate resolves Ask to Allow when Approver is nil (preserving autonomy by design), so any caller that constructs permission.NewGate(policy, nil) directly - bypassing the control layer's denyPermissionApprover wiring - runs writer tools that rules meant to ask about
evidence: internal/safety/permission/permission.go:8-9,547-549 ("a non-interactive run passes a nil Approver, which the Gate treats as allow"), :611-614 (Ask -> unattendedAsk -> allow unless subject-sensitive), internal/safety/permission/permission_test.go:310-321 (TestGateHeadlessAllowsAsk pins this as intended)
one_why: The production path closes this (every headless gate is built through BuildHeadlessApprovalGate with a deny approver, approval.go:93-131) and unattendedAsk fences the subject-sensitive subset, but the library's safe default is the open one - a third-party embedding of internal/safety/permission inherits fail-open.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: The default-config comment contradicts the shipped headless behavior: config.Default says no-TTY Ask resolves to allow, while the CLI run path documents and implements the opposite (default ask fails closed, unattended writes need --auto/yolo)
evidence: internal/contract/config/config.go:1575-1577 ("keeps `reasonix run` autonomous (no TTY -> ask resolves to allow)") vs internal/frontend/cli/cli.go:494-503 ("Default/ask fails closed because no UI can answer; unattended writes require explicit --auto/-y ... or yolo")
one_why: Code, not the comment, is authoritative (BuildHeadlessApprovalGate wires the deny approver), but a security-relevant default described two ways invites a future refactor to 'fix' the code to match the stale comment.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Sandbox denial is tested by execution, on the real backend, in CI: a macOS test writes under and outside the write-root through sandbox-exec and asserts the outside write fails; a Linux test proves an egress-bridged process can reach only its proxy (host loopback port and 1.1.1.1:443 refused) - and CI installs and self-verifies bwrap with userns sysctls so these run rather than skip
evidence: internal/safety/sandbox/seatbelt_darwin_test.go:206-263 (TestSandboxEnforcesWrites), :267-300 (go build under sandbox - toolchain not broken), internal/safety/sandbox/seatbelt_egress_linux_test.go:14-77 (TestBwrapEgressConfinesToTheBridge), .github/workflows/ci.yml:97-99 (3-OS matrix), :112-126 (install+verify bwrap, warning not silence when userns denied)
one_why: This is codex's violation_tests pattern reappearing on a second subject - the anchors' 6-rung ('tested approval, nothing underneath') is precisely the subjects that only test profile strings; here the profile's behavior is executed and the denial asserted.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Real-provider model evals run inside CI as a comment-triggered job with a two-fold anti-grader design: the benchmark harness and suite always check out from the default branch (a PR cannot weaken its own grader), only the agent is built from PR head, gated on author association plus a deployment environment that can require human approval per run
evidence: .github/workflows/e2e-bot.yml:21-31 (author_association gate + environment: e2e-bot), :44-52 ('this is where the harness ... live'), :56-66 (install and verify bubblewrap before running the agent), :68-77 (build base agent + e2ebench from default branch, "so a PR can't weaken its own grader or tests"), :79 (PR head checkout)
one_why: No anchor had in-CI model evals at all - that is the stated ceiling on verification 8 (errata); this clears it as evidence, though as an on-demand report rather than a required gate, which is why it lifts the score to 9 and not past it.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: TestExternalActionsAlwaysReachApproval is weaker than its name: it feeds the mode strings "auto"/"yolo" into permission.New, whose ParseDecision maps everything unrecognised to Ask - so it never exercises the Allow-mode policy the real yolo posture uses
evidence: internal/safety/permission/permission_test.go:396-416 (loop over modes into New), internal/safety/permission/permission.go:45-53 (ParseDecision: default -> Ask), internal/session/control/approval.go:111-113 (real yolo sets policy.Mode = permission.Allow)
one_why: The underlying claim (external actions always reach a human) is NOT true of the real yolo posture at policy level - fresh-human floors are only the approval.go:693-695 tool list, and network is allowed inside the jail by default; the test's ParseDecision coincidence lets the stronger-sounding claim pass review unchallenged.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: The default jail's security boundary is writes, not network: sandbox.network defaults true so a permitted command under the default posture has full external egress (domain allow-listing and per-host asks only engage when allowed_domains is set), and file-writer built-ins are confined in-process separately from the shell jail
evidence: internal/contract/config/config.go:902-903 ("Network allows network egress ... Defaults true so module/package downloads keep working; the boundary is then writes"), :1582 (SandboxConfig{Network: true, HostAuthorities: [ssh_agent]}), internal/safety/sandbox/sandbox.go:14-15 ("Confining the in-process file-writer built-ins is handled separately"), internal/tools/builtin/confine.go:18-36 (ConfineBash overrides the unconfined init-registered bash)
one_why: Defensible product trade-off and stated plainly, but it means data-exfiltration-shaped commands are unconstrained by default on every platform - the jail stops destruction and host writes, not disclosure; reviewers scoring this against codex should note codex splits network approval separately.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: CI is required-gate dense: 3-OS matrix with -race (targeted sweep per-PR, full sweep on push, incl. the safety/sandbox package set), in-house repolint architecture linters and a sensitive-path covergate as required jobs, govulncheck, CodeQL, goleak leak-detection wired into 15 package test mains, and 21 boot effect tests asserting what actually reaches the provider request
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:97-99,265-275 (race matrix), :457 (go run ./tools/repolint), :462 (go run ./tools/covergate), :510-513 (govulncheck), .github/workflows/codeql.yml, goleak in 15 files (internal/runtime/agent/main_test.go, internal/session/control/main_test.go, ...), internal/assembly/boot/*_effect_test.go (21 files)
one_why: Beyond the anchor 8-rung's 'real test corps', these gates assert structure (layering, coverage of safety paths, goroutine hygiene) rather than just behavior - the corpus's strongest verification culture after codex.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Two independent compaction boundaries - capacity (window x ratio, default 0.85) and economics (ContextSoftLimitTokens, an explicit cost override) - and the live trigger is the lower of the two, decided once in one function that frontends consume verbatim; every sizing decision is measured against the provider projection, not the stored history
evidence: internal/runtime/agent/compact.go:92-107 (capacityCompactTrigger), :111-123 (economicCompactTrigger: 'what a prompt costs to replay'), :131-141 (compactTrigger picks the lower; comment: a panel that renders the settings alone cannot say which); internal/runtime/agent/compact_projection.go:216-218 ('Priced on the request this produces, not the history it stores'); internal/runtime/agent/context_breakdown.go:9-27 (gauge reports CompactAt + which boundary fired)
one_why: pi's 8-rung headline is the projected-context trigger; this keeps that and adds a second boundary that fires on replay cost before capacity is threatened - no anchor compacts because the prompt got expensive, and the single-decision-point design means no UI can render a trigger that is not in force.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Prompt-cache discipline with forensic attribution: PrefixShape hashes system/tools and a cumulative BodyChain hashes each message, CompareShape merges provider usage with session-drained rewrite reasons, and an undeclared body rewrite mints a 'body_unreported' identity - so every cache miss names its cause, including causes the session did not declare
evidence: internal/runtime/agent/cache_shape.go:14-24 (PrefixShape), :78-90 (BodyChain 'a rewrite in the carried region moves every entry after it'), :103-137 (CompareShape, body_unreported at :120-123); internal/runtime/agent/preflight.go:342,356 (warm/cold/unknown label); internal/runtime/agent/cachehit_e2e_test.go, cache_body_test.go; benchmarks/tool-surface-cache/main.go; REASONIX.md:25-27 (cache-first rule: never mutate the prefix, 'ride the turn tail')
one_why: codex gates reuse by cache key (client.rs:354-390) but a miss is silent; here the byte-stability rule is paired with an observation apparatus that tells the user which of system/tools/body/rewrite caused the miss - turning cache economy from a hope into a measurable per-turn property, which is the precondition for ever fixing regressions.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Compaction bills itself: a context-carried spend accumulator sums every summarizer call's usage ('a discarded answer is still a charge'), foldEconomics refuses folds whose savings do not cover the round-trip, candidates are accepted below the 50% checkpoint ceiling without padding, and a summarizer failure degrades to a mechanical fold instead of hanging
evidence: internal/runtime/agent/compact_accounting.go:13-31 (compactionSpend, withCompactionSpend); internal/runtime/agent/compact.go:212-216 (foldEconomics, minFoldTokens=100), :22-27 (defaultCompactRatio 0.85, checkpointCeilingRatio 0.50, exceptionalMinSavingsRatio 0.25), :53-55 (summaryTimeout -> 'then a mechanical fold'); internal/runtime/agent/compact_fold_input.go:147-149 (degradeFoldSummary)
one_why: No anchor prices its own maintenance: compaction is an API call that costs tokens, and a summarizer that fails or a fold that saves nothing are both money spent - gating on fold economics and billing discarded output is the rung where context management becomes cost-aware rather than size-aware.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Folded content stays addressable: each fold leaves an index, a recall tool reads folded canonical positions or searches them, and one per-generation token budget (max(2000, 10% of window)) covers read and search together so 'the fold that freed the window cannot be undone by the turns after it'
evidence: internal/runtime/agent/compact_recall.go:13-15 (comment), :17-27 (recallBudget), :31-36 (both operations spend one budget: 'two would let a search refill what a read was refused'); internal/runtime/agent/compact_index.go; internal/runtime/agent/compact_recall_test.go
one_why: Compaction's two failure modes are information loss and immediate re-expansion; anchors pick one (cline folds foreign history with no way back). An addressable fold with a hard anti-recall-loop budget defuses both, and the refusal errors name the recovery path.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: The fleet tool dispatches 2-64 sub-agent tasks as a declared dependency graph with disjoint write_path claims checked in preflight ('preflight failure starts nothing'), and adopt_ref lets a re-issued fleet stand completed children's persisted answers in for re-running them - crash recovery is part of the tool contract, not an operator ritual
evidence: internal/runtime/delegation/fleet.go:24-27 (min/max), :30-31 (write_paths preflight), :41-74 (schema: depends_on, write_paths, fail_fast semantics, 'An item may pass adopt_ref... which is how a fleet a restart interrupted is re-issued without paying twice'); internal/runtime/delegation/fleet_adopt.go:44-53 (mutual-exclusion validation); internal/runtime/delegation/fleet_graph.go; internal/runtime/writeclaim/
one_why: codex's 9-rung gets daemon recovery + journals at the session layer; here the interrupted-fleet reissue is priced into the API ('without paying again for the items that finished') and write conflicts are refused before any task starts - the orchestration failure modes (double-spend, clobbered writes) are preflighted rather than debugged.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: A durable session-level instruction queue returns a receipt only after disk write, with its own recovery and idempotency store and an explicit post-crash 'inbox is paused' policy; background jobs persist and rebuild after restart, and recovered mutation evidence is deliberately restored as opaque 'so restart cannot downgrade the security-review requirement'
evidence: internal/session/control/controller.go:195 ('inbox is the durable session-level instruction queue'); internal/session/control/inbox.go:283-285 (EnqueueInbox receipt-after-disk); internal/state/sessioninbox/recovery.go, idempotency_store.go; docs/GUIDE.md:742 (after crash recovery the inbox is paused); internal/tools/jobs/jobs.go:612-637 (opaqueRecoveredTaskMutation), :1420-1445 (persisted-Running ownership probe, tombstone suppression), :1467-1474 (recovery-failure notice)
one_why: This is codex's queue-plus-journal rung reached independently, and the restart path is thought through further than any anchor: crush/pi at 7 resume state; here a restart can neither lose a queued instruction nor launder a pending security review into a trusted one.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Task budgets bound cost, wall-clock, and tokens with every axis shipped off by default, chosen because 'tokens is the one that generalizes - money is not portable across models'; sub-agents inherit the compaction budget shape and the planner runs under a host-owned research budget
evidence: internal/runtime/agent/run_budget.go:12-20 (TaskBudget + design comment), :37-41 (runBudget: rounds are a poor proxy; an unpriced round still counts so the axis 'never reads cheaper than the turn actually was'); internal/runtime/delegation/task.go:74,911 (CompactionBudgets to children); internal/runtime/coordinator/coordinator.go:74-77 (planner research budget that must not strand an ordinary task)
one_why: nanocoder's 6-rung gap is 'no budgets'; the axis argument (a fast empty loop and a slow expensive one both accumulate tokens, neither wall clock nor dollars catches both) is the correct generalization and the unpriced-round-still-counts rule closes the accounting hole that budgets usually leak.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Four concurrent interop contracts: full-spec MCP client (stdio/streamable-http/SSE, OAuth with PKCE + protected-resource metadata + token rotation, registry browse/install), an ACP v1 server, a versioned in-house Extension Protocol with generated schema, a conformance suite and a published Go SDK, and a headless CLI contract (--output-format json/stream-json, events-jsonl, --metrics)
evidence: docs/SPEC.md:130-160 (MCP transports, OAuth/PKCE, 0600 token binding), :193-195 (readOnlyHint mapping, containment against malicious servers); docs/ACP.md:9-10 (ACP v1 NDJSON JSON-RPC); internal/ext/extension/protocol/protocol.go:9 ('such change requires a new major protocol version'), dto_lifecycle.go:35 (ProtocolVersion validate nonempty); internal/ext/extension/conformance/; sdk/go/sdk.go:1-19; docs/CLI.md:132-136,204-210; internal/ext/extension/protocol/schema.generated.json
one_why: Beyond cline's 8 (MCP client + SDK + four surfaces, no ACP): the ACP surface plus a versioned own protocol with generated wire docs and conformance tests approaches codex's 9; it stops short because there is no MCP-server mode and the SDK is Go-only (extension sidecars), not a multi-language client SDK.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Claude Code's actual storage is ingested, not just its advertised format: ~/.claude.json per-project and user-wide MCP scopes (the file 'claude mcp add actually writes'), .mcp.json, and hooks/hooks.json with a full Claude event-name map - precedence-merged under the project file and fail-soft so a typo in another tool's config never stops startup

one_why: Migration friction is the cheapest interop win and no anchor has it - the comment shows the discovery work (finding the one location the rival CLI does not write); the fail-soft precedence rule is the right trust posture for config that belongs to another tool.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Documentation is a governed corpus with a machine-checked standard: every path matches a CODEOWNERS primary+backup rule, every doc carries an owner/status/reviewed-date header, the standard itself is DOCS_STANDARD.md, and repolint enforces headers, prose width and classification by path as a required CI job - 35+ docs, with the bilingual set pinned to a named three-file list
evidence: docs/DOCS_STANDARD.md:1-4 (owner/backup/status/reviewed header), :12-21 (O1-O4 CODEOWNERS rules, areas table); tools/repolint/docs.go:1-3 ('the part of it a machine can hold'), :36-58 (class-by-path, translatedDocs whitelist); .github/workflows/ci.yml:442,457 (repolint required job, also scans desktop/ and sdk/); docs/ ls: 35+ markdown pages incl. GUIDE.zh-CN.md, CLI.zh-CN.md
one_why: pi's 9 is '30+ docs matching code' by diligence; this makes matching code a CI-enforced property with named owners and drift detection, which is the only way doc-accuracy survives at 300k+ LOC and 11k PRs.

subject: deepseek-reasonix
title: Error and onboarding UX consistently names the remedy and degrades honestly: MCP timeout errors print the config key that fixes them, an invalid user config falls back to a last-known-good copy 'in memory without modifying the original file' with a warning, a broken project file is quarantined from later merges, failed MCP launches get a structured Failure ledger (stage, stderr, HTTP status, re-authorization flag), and repolint's errortext gate bans matching on rendered error text so identity travels as typed codes
evidence: internal/ext/plugin/client_session.go:140 ('increase mcp_call_timeout_seconds or call_timeout_seconds'); internal/contract/config/load.go:103-113 (last-known-good degradation), :141-147 (project file ignored + dropped from merge sources); internal/ext/plugin/failures.go:13-36 (Failure ledger, blocked-launch errors); tools/repolint/errortext.go:9-19 ('a message is where that knowledge dies'); docs/CLI.md:252,498 (doctor billing/catalogs); reasonix.example.toml (13,136-byte annotated config)
one_why: The 9-rung docs claim needs an enforcement story on the other side of the screen too; the lint that forbids string-matching errors is what makes 'the message names the fix' stable across refactors instead of folklore.

subject: orca-agent
title: runtime_host.rs holds ~23.3k product LOC (39,726 total; tests start :23301) fusing host, supervisor, thread actor and hosted-operation runner in one file with 125 impl blocks
evidence: crates/orca-runtime/src/runtime_host.rs:4208 (struct RuntimeHost), :11734 (struct ThreadActor), :16272 (impl ThreadActor), :22294 (fn run_hosted_operation), :23301 (mod tests); children only partially offloaded via #[path] mods at :110-121; orca-runtime crate is 292,829 of 544,356 LOC (54%)

subject: orca-agent
title: RuntimeHost/ThreadActor control plane enforces six ownership properties (one admitter, fresh cancel scope, stale-command fencing, completion independent of subscribers, shutdown-join-reclaim, actor-owned state) for TUI, server and headless alike
evidence: docs/architecture/adr/0005-runtime-host-operation-control-plane.md:14-45 (property list, codex-derived); crates/orca-tui/src/hosted_submission.rs:8 and crates/orca-tui/src/agent_runtime.rs:5 (TUI drives RuntimeHostHandle, no TUI loop); root run_agent_loop called only from controller.rs:823 and recursive child path agent_loop.rs:244; tests/runtime_lifecycle_contract.rs
one_why: This is the anti-nanocoder pattern taken seriously: the ADR names its pre-P0.3 failure mode (TUI-only loop + duplicate turn assemblers) as an architecture defect and replaces it with one admitted mailbox per thread -- evidence there is no parallel entry-path loop, unlike nanocoder's React-hook loop at 5.

subject: orca-agent
title: Core loop is small and factored into typed-context steps: run_agent_loop (724) -> run_agent_turn_loop (1127) -> iteration/kernel (142/134), with children reusing the identical loop
evidence: crates/orca-runtime/src/agent_loop.rs:35, :244 (execute_child_agent_loop recurses into run_agent_loop); runtime_turn_loop.rs:292-410 (loop body over RuntimeTurnIterationResult::{ContinueLoop,Return,Suspended}); runtime_turn_kernel.rs:17-38; lifecycle.rs AgentLoopContext/RuntimeTurnContext, step_context.rs:1-345
one_why: Same-kernel recursion for subagents plus borrowed/moved typed contexts means continuation, budget and journal semantics cannot diverge between root and child -- the property crush's fused agent.go:2393 lacks; the loop itself is codex-grade, the mass around it is not.

subject: orca-agent
title: Per-operation append-only journal enforces ordering invariants on append and crash-recovers atomically: torn final line, non-contiguous ordinals, unflushed tool.started restored as indeterminate, terminal append-once
evidence: crates/orca-runtime/src/execution_journal.rs:1-15 (invariant doc), :369 (append reject), :395/:403 (durable/atomic flush); tests crates/orca-runtime/tests/execution_journal.rs:135,169 (fault-injected flush), :353 (torn mid-write reopen), :435 (ordinal gaps), :461 (regressive budget rejection); agent_loop.rs:64-73 (OperationContext::open; journal is source of truth for the terminal fact)
one_why: Codex's rollout journal persists; orca's journal additionally refuses illegal histories at append time and is tested against armed write faults and half-written files -- a stronger crash-semantics posture than any anchor's journal evidence in the excerpts.

subject: orca-agent
title: Crate-boundary direction is CI-tested via cargo metadata: thin root dependency graph, orca-runtime must not depend on orca-tui, provider not on tools, TUI not on provider, plus compile-time facade checks
evidence: tests/dependency_architecture_contract.rs:57-65 (root deps == clap/orca-core/orca-runtime/orca-tui), :66-78 (runtime!->tui, provider!->tools), :80-89 (tui!->provider), :110-120 (public facade types compile)
one_why: Real and cheap boundary enforcement -- but only four direction assertions plus facades, not a kode-cli/kolkrabbi-style zone DAG with a shrinking-violations ratchet; it guards crate edges while the runtime_host god-file sits unguarded inside one crate.

subject: orca-agent
title: orca doctor: read-only versioned-schema diagnostics (config, trust, sandbox readiness) with JSON/text output and credential redaction, contract-tested
evidence: src/cli.rs:62,128-135,805-811 -> crates/orca-runtime/src/diagnostics.rs; tests/doctor_cli_contract.rs:21 (stable schemaVersion=1, exit code 1 on fail), :67 (redacts env credentials and reports source), :106 (never prints API key from config)
one_why: Field-supportable debugging is a 9-rung operability marker (codex debug prompt-input, pi diagnostics); a doctor that can't leak the very keys it inspects is the version most harnesses get wrong.

subject: orca-agent
title: Two event-sourced layers coexist: per-operation execution journal and a session-wide runtime_surface commit ledger (commit ~12.9k + reducer ~9.4k product LOC) still carrying legacy task-adoption migration shims
evidence: execution_journal.rs:1-15 vs crates/orca-runtime/src/runtime_surface/commit.rs:10-13 (LegacyActiveTaskAdoption*/LegacyTerminalTaskReconciliation* imports), runtime_surface/reducer.rs (~9.4k non-test), runtime_surface/mod.rs export surface of hundreds of ledger types
one_why: The scopes are stated and defensible (operation terminal facts vs session/surface fold), but two journals plus in-flight legacy reconciliation is where 'journal says one thing, actor does another' bugs live -- authority is documented in comments, not enforced by a shared invariant.

subject: orca-agent
title: orca storage prunes only explicitly archived, unlocked, unchanged sessions and previews by default; retention refuses symlinks and non-regular files
evidence: src/cli.rs:115-123 ('Apply the explicit policy. Without this flag, only preview candidates'); crates/orca-runtime/src/thread_store/retention.rs:1,90,99,107,133,141; archive/delete tested at tests/thread_store_contract.rs:485
one_why: Disk cleanup that deletes the wrong transcript is unrecoverable; dry-run-default plus file-kind guards is the small, copyable discipline most agents ship rm-by-age instead of.

subject: orca-agent
title: Every hosted generation runs inside catch_unwind and surfaces as a typed GenerationTaskOutcome::Panicked with usage accounting preserved around it
evidence: crates/orca-runtime/src/runtime_host.rs:20699-20724 (catch_unwind around run_hosted_operation, Panicked variant, usage delta still computed); runtime_actor/operation_recovery.rs:10-36; tests/subagent_recovery_contract.rs, tests/signal_contract.rs:1-3 (SIGINT/SIGTERM cancel, not die, mid-turn)
one_why: One panicking tool turn must not take the host, the journal accounting, or the sibling subagents with it -- panic typed into the same outcome channel as errors keeps recovery on one code path, the crush recover()-middleware rung done in Rust.

subject: orca-agent
title: Sandbox-by-default posture: AutoEdit maps bash to WorkspaceWrite no-network; Plan is a read-only hard ceiling rules cannot lift; host shell only via explicit FullAuto

one_why: Direct inversion of the nanocoder 5-rung failure (real machinery, wrong default): autonomous execution happens inside the sandbox, and extensions go through the runtime permission path (policy.rs:82-84).

subject: orca-agent
title: Single process-launch choke point (ExecutionBroker) rejects non-dangerous launches when enforcement is Unavailable/Advisory; RemoteSandbox refused, not run locally; target claims without a target-aware backend refused, not widened

one_why: Broker-level fail-closed is platform-independent and tested in every CI; cwd bound to an opened dir identity closes TOCTOU path-swap (execution_broker.rs:186-190). This is the SECURITY.md refuse-launch claim enforced in code, the exact rung nanocoder's fail-open falls below.

title: No CI job on any platform ever proves the OS sandbox blocks anything: negative enforcement tests are macOS-only behind a macOS-gated probe with no macOS test job, and the two Linux fail-closed tests self-skip when bwrap is installed (exactly CI)

subject: orca-agent
title: SECURITY.md's runtime-boundary claims match the code at HEAD (refuse-launch, diagnostics-only denials, non-authoritative project config, advisory-only danger-full-access); honesty defects are cosmetic: advisory URL still names pre-rename blade-deepseek, marketing could over-read 'pinned-user trust'

subject: orca-agent
title: Three-tier compaction: window-ratio soft/hard triggers -> no-LLM cache-aware micro-compaction -> incremental remote summary -> local-truncation fallback, plus one-shot prompt-too-long recovery
evidence: crates/orca-provider/src/context.rs:21,30 (COMPACTION_THRESHOLD 0.90, SOFT 0.80 with codex/grok/claude alignment comments :19-38), :42-46 (fixed 48k COMPACTION_TARGET_TOKENS with 0.60-soft small-window cap, explicitly anti-window-scaling), :704-755 (compact_with_summary_inner: micro pass to 90% soft, then summarize_collapsed_messages, then local_compaction), :1778+ (cache_aware_micro_compaction truncates backwards stopping early so 'everything before the first changed turn remains an exact, useful cache prefix'); crates/orca-runtime/src/compaction.rs:241-266 (decide_for_pressure single-trigger line; decide_for_provider_error one-shot prompt-too-long compact-and-retry)

subject: orca-agent

subject: orca-agent

subject: orca-agent

subject: letta-code
title: The reasoning loop and conversation state are not in the harness at all: the default backend is a stream-consumer over the Letta API, with the backend plane swap behind a CI-enforced boundary
