one_why: This is the cleanest loop/product separation in the anchor set -- stronger than cline's 8-rung SDK-core because even transcript, compaction and turn state leave the client process -- at the cost of making the default mode useless without the vendor server, which is why the repo carries a second full local plane (see c10) instead of a thin offline mode.

subject: letta-code
title: Six client-side turn while(true) loops across three hosts (headless.ts alone has six), with verbatim-copied behavior blocks and a proven semantic divergence between paths
evidence: src/headless.ts:1769,2183,3372,3851,3952,4280; src/cli/app/use-conversation-loop.ts:746; src/websocket/listener/turn.ts:315; AGENTS.md:35-37 admits 'separate orchestration paths'; identical 15-line skill-content-injection block copy-pasted 5x (use-conversation-loop.ts:764, headless.ts:1819,2202,3413,4290) vs centralized listener (turn.ts:60 imports skill-injection.ts); max-turns runaway cap enforced in headless (headless.ts:2145) and listener (turn.ts:349) but absent from the TUI loop (grep for maxTurns/max_turns in use-conversation-loop.ts: no match)
one_why: This is the nanocoder failure mode (per-host loop reimplementation) at institution scale -- shared stream drain and shared verdicts keep it from being fatal, but the max-turns gap shows drift is not hypothetical: an interactive runaway turn has no client-side step cap.

subject: letta-code
title: All turn-recovery verdicts (pre-stream conflict class, retry-vs-rethrow, approval-recovery eligibility, denial rebuild) extracted into one pure module consumed by all three loop hosts, with an 851-line spec including an explicit cross-host determinism test
evidence: src/agent/turn-recovery-policy.ts:1-6 ('Pure, framework-agnostic... Both TUI and headless consume these helpers... identical conflict inputs always produce the same recovery action'); consumed by use-conversation-loop.ts:825,843, headless.ts:2260,4337, websocket/listener/recovery.ts:7-17; 851-LOC src/agent/turn-recovery-policy.test.ts with 'same inputs always produce same action (determinism)' at :201
one_why: The right antidote to multi-host loop drift: make the three orchestrators unable to disagree on verdicts even while they keep separate control flow -- the verdict layer is where parity is defined and tested, and it costs one leaf module.

subject: letta-code
title: Runs default to server-side background execution with client-side stall detection, timed run re-discovery, and stream resume that replays the missed tail across the reconnect boundary
evidence: src/agent/message.ts:293,327 (background: true default; SDK retries deliberately disabled, message.ts:350-352, 'retries would violate idempotency'); src/cli/helpers/stream.ts:110 (stallReconcilerFired 'stream went silent mid-run; reconciler aborted the dead read to reconnect'), :425 ('Stream went silent, reconnecting to recover the missed tail'), :538 (drainStreamWithResume); src/cli/helpers/stream-resume.ts:30,82 (FALLBACK_RUN_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS=5000, discoverFallbackRunIdWithTimeout via runs.list); used by all three hosts (stream.ts consumers: use-conversation-loop.ts, headless.ts, listener/turn-stream.ts, listener/recovery.ts)
one_why: Killing the client mid-turn loses nothing: the run keeps executing server-side and any host can reattach by run id -- a crash-recovery property no anchor has (codex journals locally; letta makes the run itself crash-independent). Local-backend-only builds degrade to stream-resume.test.ts-level behavior.

subject: letta-code
title: TUI host layer dwarfs the loop it drives: AppCoordinator.tsx 5,109 LOC, use-submit-handler.ts 3,804, and the turn loop itself is a 2,887-LOC React hook with zero direct tests
evidence: wc -l: src/cli/app/AppCoordinator.tsx 5109, use-submit-handler.ts 3804, use-conversation-loop.ts 2887, src/headless.ts 4788; no test file imports useConversationLoop (grep -rl over src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}: empty); 43 files baseline-exempted from the 1000-LOC cap in scripts/source-file-size-baseline.json, headless.ts frozen at exactly 4788
one_why: The frozen-LOC baseline means these numbers are a permanent, CI-enforced ceiling rather than transient debt; per the pi errata (product files >5k dock placement) this is the same docking factor that held cline at 8, and the untested loop-hook shape is nanocoder's, mitigated only because the verdict logic lives elsewhere (c3).

subject: letta-code
title: CI-enforced size ratchet that freezes each god-file at its exact current LOC, layered on layer-boundary, module-ownership, cycle, and mock-isolation checkers that the repo's own meta-test guards
evidence: scripts/check-source-file-size.js:7-9 (MAX_LINES=1000, baseline file), :31-38 (a baselined file shrugging below MAX or a new file above it both fail); scripts/source-file-size-baseline.json (43 entries; src/headless.ts capped at exactly 4788); package.json:184-191 (check:cycles/boundaries/file-size/module-ownership/test-mock-isolation); src/maintainability-checks.test.ts tests the checkers themselves
one_why: Ratchet-with-baseline is the honest way to live with god files: growth is a CI failure, the exception list is auditable, and the ratchet may only shrink -- unlike cline/crush, which have no equivalent import or size contract at all.

subject: letta-code
title: Fatal crash path sets the process exit code synchronously before any async work, drains telemetry under a 3s bound, and is verified by subprocess-level tests asserting exit code 1
evidence: src/telemetry/fatal-error-handler.ts:69-71 ('Set this synchronously so another listener or an early event-loop exit cannot turn the fatal failure into a successful process result'); :20-30 (EPIPE/429-noise suppression); :33-52 drainWithTimeout; :94-106 uncaughtException/unhandledRejection wiring; src/telemetry/fatal-error-handler.test.ts:77-129 spawns a real process and asserts exitCode===1
one_why: Crash posture is exactly what separates the 8-rung (crush recover middleware) from nanocoder's 6 ('no visible crash-recovery posture'): the failure semantics are specified -- never exit 0 on a fatal -- and tested at process level, not just try/catch hopes.

subject: letta-code
title: On restart into a conversation with server-pending approvals, every host denies the stale tool calls with an explicit recovery reason instead of hanging or replaying them
evidence: src/agent/check-approval.ts getResumeDataFromBackend (642 LOC, own specs check-approval-resume-data.test.ts, check-approval-prepare-message.test.ts); headless.ts:1765-1810 resolveAllPendingApprovals loops until none pending, denies via buildFreshDenialApprovals(..., STALE_APPROVAL_RECOVERY_DENIAL_REASON) at :1795, treats 404/422 as 'no approvals' rather than fatal; same getResumeDataFromBackend imported by listener turn.ts:13 and the TUI path
one_why: The unglamorous half of crash-resume: a run paused on an approval whose executor died must resolve deterministically, and the harness guarantees forward progress by denying with a reason visible to the model -- every anchor that resumes sessions leaves this state underspecified.

subject: letta-code
title: The repo's one named tri-loop parity test simulates neither loop: it drives QueueRuntime with a hand-written script that mirrors the two hosts' queue wiring
evidence: src/queue/listener-tui-queue-parity.test.ts:11-14 ('Mirrors listen-client arrival + turn-start/turn-end queue wiring'), :15-77 simulateListenerScript builds a fake arrival/turn-start sequence against QueueRuntime directly; no test drives useConversationLoop (zero importers in test files) or headless.ts's approvalLoop (:4280) against the listener's turn.ts:315
one_why: The name claims the mitigation for c2 but only the queue plane is actually parity-checked; verdict-level parity exists via the pure policy (c3) while control-flow parity -- max-turns being the demonstrated gap -- is asserted by comment and convention (AGENTS.md:38-41 tells PR authors to run per-path behavior tests) rather than executed.

subject: letta-code
title: The offline/local backend is a second complete execution plane -- own turn executor on pi-ai, own transcript store (3,301 LOC), own compaction -- not a degraded mode of the hosted plane
evidence: src/backend/local/local-backend.ts:178 (class LocalBackend extends HeadlessBackend); src/backend/dev/provider-turn-executor.ts:565 (client-side loop on @earendil-works/pi-ai, imports at :7); src/backend/local/local-store.ts 3301 LOC; src/backend/local/local-transcript.ts:24-28 (own schema-versioned JSONL: pi-session-entry-jsonl, v1->v2 migration-required error with backup_path); selection via src/backend/backend-mode.ts:22-27 env flag
one_why: Doubles the semantics surface every core change must hold (loop, compaction, transcript, resume now exist twice with different guarantees), but the local transcript's versioned manifest + migration-required-with-backup error is the most careful on-disk session-format discipline found outside codex's rollout journals.

subject: letta-code
title: The shipped default permission mode auto-allows every tool: approval machinery is real and well-tested but switched off out of the box
evidence: src/permissions/mode.ts:10 (DEFAULT_PERMISSION_MODE = "unrestricted"); mode.ts:109-112 (case "unrestricted": return {decision:"allow"} for everything except earlier deny rules); src/permissions/startup.ts:58 (no CLI/settings override falls through to the default); src/permissions/permissions-mode.test.ts:85-101 (test literally named "unrestricted mode - allows all tools", asserts reason "Permission mode: unrestricted")
one_why: The 6-rung anchor (cline/pi/crush) is defined by tested approval as the default gate; here the default interactive session never asks -- this is the nanocoder "real machinery, wrong default" signature, except the wrong default is more wrong (auto-allow-all vs regex-gated ask).

subject: letta-code
title: Two guards evaluate before any mode/rule logic and survive even unrestricted mode: the workspace sandbox and the cross-agent memory guard, the latter with symlink-escape tests against real filesystems
evidence: src/permissions/checker.ts:278,299 (workspace + cross-agent guards run as decision steps before deny rules and before the mode override at :403); src/permissions/cross-agent-guard.ts:19-21 ("The guard runs BEFORE any other permission logic... unbypassable by modes and rules"); cross-agent-guard.ts:236-246 (realpath pass so a symlink into another agent's memory is caught); src/permissions/cross-agent-guard.test.ts:390,402,414 ("unrestricted mode does NOT let you write another agent's memory", "reads... denied across all modes"), :618-700 (symlink-escape suite using real temp dirs and symlinkSync)
one_why: This is what separates letta-code from nanocoder-5: even in the worst default mode there is a non-empty, behavior-tested enforcement floor -- and the guard honestly documents that it only covers in-process file tools, pointing spawned shells at the kernel instead.

subject: letta-code
title: Fail posture is split by context: unattended memory-subagent confinement throws when no kernel backend exists, but every other sandbox entry point warns and continues unconfined, and Windows has no backend at all
evidence: src/permissions/memory-confinement-launcher.ts:74-76 (throw "Memory confinement is unavailable"); src/agent/subagents/sandbox.ts:106-110 (same missing-backend case: warnSandboxBackendUnavailable then return null = spawn unconfined); src/sandbox/availability.ts:98-113 ("We intentionally continue rather than fail closed"); availability.ts:129-135 (probe returns backend null on anything not darwin/linux -- so the default-on subagent jail is silently absent on Windows); src/permissions/workspace-sandbox.ts:41-45 (fail-closed throw -- the third, different posture)
one_why: Three different fail-postures for the same missing-backend condition in one codebase; the fail-open majority plus the Windows no-backend gap means 'default-on confinement' is true only on macOS and namespace-capable Linux.

subject: letta-code
title: The cross-agent shell sandbox is opt-in (agent shells run unconfined by default), even though the machinery itself is first-rate: bwrap tmpfs-masks peer memory, seatbelt uses -D parameterized paths, and the old bypassable static shell scanner was deliberately deleted
evidence: src/permissions/sandbox-gate.ts:37-38 ("by default... agent shells run unconfined", opt-in via LETTA_FS_SANDBOX=1); src/sandbox/availability.ts:79-94 (opt-in rationale: kernel denials broke legitimate workflows); src/sandbox/bwrap.ts:64-67 (denied roots masked with --tmpfs, unreadable and unenumerable); src/sandbox/seatbelt.ts:33-38 (-D params, no SBPL string escaping); cross-agent-guard.ts:10-14 (static shell scanner removed: 'bypassable by symlinks, command substitution, globbing, and subprocesses'); bwrap.ts:22 ("No --unshare-net: network stays open") + seatbelt.ts:12-15 ("allow default... threat model is filesystem scoping for memory isolation, not general untrusted-code confinement")
one_why: Deleting a bypassable static scanner in favor of kernel enforcement is the architecturally correct call (codex-10 direction), but shipping it off-by-default for the main agent reproduces nanocoder's exact docking reason; and there is zero network egress control by explicit design -- the jail walls one agent's memory off, nothing else.

subject: letta-code
title: PermissionRequest hooks (the user's deny hatch, e.g. the shipped block-rm-rf.sh example) only run when the decision is already "ask", so they are dead code under the default unrestricted mode; meanwhile the Skill tool is unconditionally auto-allowed and injects untrusted SKILL.md content into the transcript unauthenticated
evidence: src/permissions/checker.ts:864-893 (hooks only fire inside if (result.decision === "ask")); hooks/block-rm-rf.sh (example rm -rf blocker, exit 2 -- never consulted when mode auto-allows); checker.ts:437-447 ("Skill tool is always allowed (read-only)"); src/tools/impl/skill-content-registry.ts:23-25 (queueSkillContent -- any SKILL.md read is queued); src/websocket/listener/skill-injection.ts:22-41 (queued content appended as a user-role message with no trust gating)
one_why: The only user-extensible policy surface cannot defend against the default posture, and the injection story is the inverse: skill files (project-local, attacker-writable in a cloned repo) reach the model verbatim with no approval and no trust gate -- prompt-injection payload rides a zero-permission tool.

subject: letta-code
title: Honest, documented non-enforcement plus real hardening at the remote surfaces: non-loopback listener refuses to start without auth, HMAC/timing-safe capability tokens with a 32-byte secret floor, PATH-planting defense on sandbox-exec
evidence: src/websocket/app-server.ts:172 ("refusing to start non-loopback websocket listener... without auth"); src/websocket/app-server-auth.ts:1,8 (timingSafeEqual; MIN_SIGNED_BEARER_SECRET_BYTES = 32); src/sandbox/seatbelt.ts:20-22 (hardcoded /usr/bin/sandbox-exec, "never resolved via PATH, to defend against a planted sandbox-exec"); src/sandbox/seatbelt.ts:12-15 and cross-agent-guard.ts:1-25 (explicit statements of what is and is not enforced); note: no SECURITY.md at repo root (docs/ = nix.md + examples + plans)
one_why: Closest thing to pi's exemplary SECURITY.md honesty in the anchor set, but embedded in code comments instead of a policy document -- the model's limits are stated precisely ("memory isolation, not untrusted-code confinement"), which is what earns the honesty credit even as the missing doc caps it.

subject: letta-code
title: Nothing ever executes the kernel sandbox: seatbelt/bwrap tests assert generated profile text and argv order, no test spawns sandbox-exec or bwrap, and no CI job installs bubblewrap -- the safety layer's last mile is unverified end-to-end
evidence: src/sandbox/seatbelt.test.ts:33-79 (asserts profile contains/contains-after-ordering only); src/sandbox/wrap.test.ts (43 LOC, argv composition); src/memory-confinement.test.ts:23-36 (asserts result.launcher[0] === "/usr/bin/sandbox-exec", never runs it); grep bwrap|bubblewrap|sandbox-exec across .github/workflows = no matches (nanocoder's CI does install real bubblewrap and run the jail spec, anchor nanocoder.md :63-95); unit matrix ci.yml:137-176 runs the same string tests on 4 OSes
one_why: A wrong deny/allow emission order in seatbelt.ts or bwrap.ts (the comments themselves call last-mount-wins ordering a HAZARD at bwrap.ts:57-63) would pass the entire 229k-LOC test corps and CI -- the exact property a real-jail test would catch, and a capability the lower-scoring nanocoder has.

subject: letta-code
title: Gating CI runs full tool-calling agent scenarios against live models -- 4 hosted models and 4 local-backend provider models, each across text/json/stream-json outputs, with behavioral assertions -- the first evals-in-CI evidence in the anchor set
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:376-408 (headless job, matrix [gpt-5.4-mini-medium, sonnet-4.6-low, haiku, gemini-3.6-flash], LETTA_API_KEY, no continue-on-error); ci.yml:410-442 (headless-local with OPENAI/ANTHROPIC/GOOGLE keys); src/test-utils/headless-scenario.ts:157,169 (scenarios require sentinel "BANANA" iff every tool step succeeded), :368-382,408-427 (assertContainsAll over text, json, stream-json outputs), :359 (memFS memory-task marker check); ci.yml:509 (local ollama smoke) -- caveats: ci.yml:383-384 models excluded for provider flakiness, ollama-smoke :451 and reflection-headless :518 are continue-on-error, assertions are sentinel-level
one_why: The frozen errata says do not award verification 9+ without evals-in-CI or fuzzing; this is evals-in-CI in the literal sense (real models, behavioral assertions, PR-gating), so the 8-ceiling that bound codex/cline/pi is genuinely broken here -- but sentinel smoke is a long way from scored or adversarial evals.

subject: letta-code
title: A meta-checker proves every test file is claimed by a CI shard, and the checkers themselves have tests -- closing the silent-untested-file hole that a shard list alone leaves open
evidence: scripts/check-test-coverage.cjs:116 ("all N test files are covered by CI" gate), :53 (forbidden-directory rule), :122-131 (lists uncovered files); src/maintainability-checks.test.ts (tests the meta-checkers); ci.yml:137-176 (unit matrix 4 OS x 4 shards + 4 extra Windows shards), ci.yml:188-217 (integration shards against live Letta Cloud); ~869 src/**/*.test.ts files, ~228.9k LOC (scout census errata, census test_loc 1126 wrong); bypass-style FIX regressions like src/permissions/read-only-shell-security.test.ts:8-26 (cd-bypass, sensitive-path auto-approve regressions)
one_why: Cheap CI plumbing with a real guarantee: with 869 test files the failure mode isn't 'no tests', it's 'a test nobody runs' -- this makes that a build error, which none of the anchor CI configs claim to do.

subject: letta-code
title: Two permission engines ship simultaneously with v2 flipped default-on by env-absence and the v1/v2 differential check gated behind an opt-in flag
evidence: src/permissions/checker.ts:75-79 (isPermissionsV2Enabled: unset env returns true -- v2 default-on, LETTA_PERMISSIONS_V2=0 reverts to v1); checker.ts:159-196 (LETTA_PERMISSIONS_DUAL_EVAL shadow-evals the other engine and only console.errors on decision/matchedRule mismatch); checker.ts:706-711 (matcher semantics differ per engine: canonicalizeToolNames on for v2, off for v1) -- permission-rule semantics therefore depend on an env var, and rule-matching divergences are surfaced only when someone opts into dual-eval
one_why: Migration-era security logic with two live semantics for the same settings file: a deny rule that matches under v1 but not v2 (or vice versa) behaves silently differently per host environment -- the differential harness exists but is not the default, so the divergence window is uncovered by default.

subject: letta-code
title: Local-backend compaction triggers pre-request on a usage-anchored context estimate honestly ported from pi, with the pi-ai max_tokens clamp subtlety documented and enumerated deviations from upstream
evidence: src/backend/dev/provider-turn-executor.ts:225-240 (comment: 'Context pressure must be handled before the provider request, not only after an overflow. pi-ai first makes an oversized request valid by shrinking its output allowance... a near-full request can therefore finish with length instead of throwing'); :241-260 contextCompactionThreshold with 16,384-token reserve capped at 20% for small windows, pinned upstream pi line refs in comment; :262-273 shouldCompactForContextPressure; src/backend/dev/pi-stream-adapter.ts:562,751-769 (hook fires both pre-request and post-turn); src/backend/local/local-context-estimate.ts:4-22 (ported-from-pi header with three enumerated intentional deviations, incl. a timestamp-based post-compaction staleness guard so pre-compaction usage anchors are ignored)
one_why: This is pi-8's 'projected-context trigger measures what the model would actually receive' -- it literally re-derives pi's calculateContextTokens semantics (usage anchor + trailing estimate) and fixes two undercount bugs pi has; the deviation list is exactly how a port should look, and the pre-request placement beats crush/nanocoder-6's reactive summarize-on-overflow.

subject: letta-code
title: Two compaction strategies (all / sliding_window 30% default) with escalating eviction steps, a ten-rung transcript-shrink ladder on summary overflow, and a model-specific summary fallback for a known provider refusal path
evidence: src/backend/local/compaction.ts:43-44 (sliding_window, 0.3 default); :604-627 planLocalSlidingWindowCompaction grows evictionPercentage by 0.1 until kept messages fit goalTokens and cutoff lands on a valid assistant boundary; :31-41 TRANSCRIPT_FALLBACK_MAX_CHAR_STEPS 120k->2k, consumed at :487-510 (retry each rung only on isContextWindowOverflowError, else rethrow); :380-444 claude-fable-5 swapped to a fallback summary model because its summaries trip Anthropic's refusal path surfaced as an opaque error; src/backend/dev/context-window-overflow.ts:37-53 (13-marker overflow detector across providers)
one_why: Two strategies plus degradation ladders put this at cline-7's 'two strategies behind one threshold' rung and above crush/nanocoder-6's single auto-summarize; the refusal-path swap is the kind of provider-idiosyncrasm handling codex-9 earns credit for, but it is hard-coded model-id string matching, not a tier system.

subject: letta-code
title: Zero client-side prompt-cache handling in either backend: cache is only pass-through reporting; hosted discipline is opaque (Letta server), local discipline is pi-ai's, so nothing between harness and provider is this repo's decision
evidence: grep -rE 'cache_control|cacheControl|prompt_cache|promptCache' src/ returns no non-test, non-cost-field hits; src/backend/dev/provider-turn-executor.ts:312-339 only maps usage.cacheRead/cacheWrite into usage_statistics chunks; src/backend/dev/pi-local-endpoint-provider.ts:119 'fingerprint cache' is a provider-instance memo, not prompt caching; no cache warming, no cache-key pinning anywhere; hosted compaction/cache entirely server-side (src/agent/create-agent-request.ts:93,215 only sends compaction_settings:{model})
one_why: This is the exact feature that separates codex-9 (client.rs:354-390 cache-key-gated reuse) and pi-8 (cache-warmer.ts) from cline-7 ('no cache discipline') in the anchors; delegation to a server or a library may be correct engineering, but the anchors score observable discipline and the harness has none of its own -- token-economy cannot leave 7 on this lane.

subject: letta-code
title: Reflection subagent startup context hard-capped at ~16k estimated tokens with graceful degradation: parent-memory section shrinks to the file-tree first, hard truncation last, and the truncation is announced inside the prompt
evidence: src/agent/subagents/context-budget.ts:12-16 (16_000-token limit at conservative 4 chars/token, explicitly dependency-free); :30-48 buildMinimalParentMemorySection / shrinkParentMemorySection keeps <memory_filesystem> tree when dropping preview; :64-93 buildSubagentPrompt final guard; getReflectionStartupNotice :25-27 injects a human-readable notice telling the agent to read files from MEMORY_DIR
one_why: nanocoder-6 is docked 'no budgets'; here the one orchestration budget that exists is honestly heuristic (chars/4, self-documented) and self-announcing to the model, which is the cheap correct shape -- but it is the only budget in the orchestration plane (see e8).

subject: letta-code
title: Rival harnesses are wrapped as first-class subagent tools: Claude Code driven over its stream-json stdout contract and Codex driven over `codex app-server --stdio`, with session resume and MCP-server inheritance reminders
evidence: src/tools/impl/external-coding-agent.ts:13 EXTERNAL_CODING_AGENT_TYPES = ['claude-code','codex'], :34 resumeSessionId option, :9-10 imports; src/tools/impl/claude-stream-session.ts:119-121 builds --output-format stream-json args, :142 spawnSubagentProcess('claude',...); src/tools/impl/codex-app-server.ts:100 nodeSpawn('codex', ['app-server','--stdio']), :253 threadId-keyed agent ids; src/reminders/engine buildMcpServersReminderText imported at external-coding-agent.ts:5-8
one_why: No anchor does this: codex-9 delegates to itself (codex_delegate.rs), cline-8 teams are same-runtime; consuming competitors' machine contracts as orchestration leaves is a genuinely original interop-orchestration hybrid -- and it doubles as a live compatibility probe of those contracts.

subject: letta-code
title: Cron schedules are durable in ~/.letta/crons.json with atomic flush-to-temp-then-rename writes, a cross-process owner lock token, mtime hot-reload, and an explicit guarantee that pausing a task cannot smuggle an agent past the persisted schedule limit
evidence: src/cron/cron-file.ts:2 ('Persistent cron task storage backed by ~/.letta/crons.json'), :121-123 (crons.json + owner.json), :205 writeFileSync(tmp, {flush:true}), :221-229 owner-token lock read/write, :428 ('Pausing a task must not let an agent exceed the persisted schedule limit'), :987 mtime change detection; src/cron/run-log.ts + runner.ts + 17-file package with per-file tests
one_why: Meets cline-8's durable-cron rung (theirs sqlite, here fsync+owner-lock, arguably the more paranoid write path); below codex-9's daemon-recovery in one respect the anchor cares about: there is no attempt-before-dispatch ledger with unknown-no-retry reclaim here, so a crash mid-run leaves no honest 'unknown' record.

subject: letta-code
title: The message/task-notification/cron/approval queue that all three turn hosts share is purely in-process: coalescing, soft/hard caps and user-interrupt pause are well-designed, but a crash silently drops every pending turn and there is no journal
evidence: src/queue/queue-runtime.ts:186 QueueRuntime (plain class, no fs/sqlite import anywhere in src/queue -- grep persist|sqlite|crash across the dir returns nothing); :170-182 maxItems soft-drop / hardMaxItems reject; :40-45 paused items skipped by every dequeue path, system-originated items never paused; :102-109 isCoalescable by kind; src/queue/listener-tui-queue-parity.test.ts pins TUI/listener parity but only within one process lifetime
one_why: codex-9's queue is first-class with journals; cline-8's hub has an event journal; here the queue is the single most stateful object in the interactive plane and it has zero crash semantics -- the nanocoder-6 descriptor 'unproven crash semantics' applies exactly, mitigated only by the hosted backend keeping turn state server-side.

subject: letta-code
title: Subagents spawn as full headless `letta` child processes with maxTurns plumbing but no concurrency cap, semaphore, or cost budget anywhere in the fan-out path -- parallel-fanout stdout loss is already an observed production failure that was patched with a retry instead of a limiter
evidence: src/agent/subagents/manager.ts:448 spawnSubagentProcess per execution; grep -i 'max_concurrent|concurrent|semaphore|pLimit' across src/agent/subagents/ and src/tools/impl/task.ts: no matches; manager.ts:582 and :698-706 ('lost stdout before its result envelope; retrying once' / '#3257 observed under high parallel fan-out' -- one-shot retry gated by looksLikeTruncatedStreamJson); src/tools/impl/task.ts:104,926 maxTurns is per-child turn count, no depth or aggregate limit found
one_why: The anchor's 6-vs-8 discriminator includes budgets; a model-driven agent can spawn unbounded parallel headless processes each with its own provider spend, and the fix pattern (detect truncation, respawn) treats the symptom -- hermes-style concurrency caps and per-child budgets are the missing layer; credit given, though, that the retry is scoped to unambiguous truncation only because side effects may already have happened (manager.ts:695-697 comment).

subject: letta-code
title: The headless stream-json contract deliberately converges on Claude Code/Codex wire conventions (timestamp field/format) so downstream normalizers treat all three CLIs uniformly, funneled through one writer that reports stdout drops instead of pretending success
evidence: src/stream-json-writer.ts:1-24 (module docstring: 'Field name and format match Claude Code and Codex stream-json output so downstream normalizers can treat all three CLIs uniformly'; single choke point enforcing the timestamp invariant); :39-60 writeWireMessageAsync returns false when stdout destroyed -- 'callers emitting a message that downstream consumers depend on (e.g. the final result envelope a subagent parent parses) must check the return value'; src/cli/args.ts:150-195 (--output-format text|json|stream-json, --input-format stream-json bidirectional, --no-wait receipt mode, --include-partial-messages)
one_why: This is codex-9's headless exec --json surface plus something none of the anchors do: explicit wire-compat targeting of competitors' formats as an interop strategy -- pi-6 earns its headless credit on its own rpc docs, letta earns it on being droppable-into-elsewhere's-pipelines, which is the more useful contract for a third-party integrator.

subject: letta-code
title: Agents are re-exposed as an OpenAI Responses-compatible HTTP endpoint (/v1/responses) with a versioned protocol package and shipped typed client bundles consumed by the desktop app and chat.letta.com, plus a PyPI wheel packaging path
evidence: src/websocket/app-server-openai-responses.ts:33 RESPONSES_PATH = '/v1/responses' with previous_response_id/store/stream request shape :37-45; src/websocket/app-server.ts 461 LOC; src/app-server-client.ts 772 LOC; package.json:47-77 exports map: './app-server-protocol' types, './app-server-client' browser+import+require triple, './protocol' types, './mcp-client' dist; :20-28 files list ships the dist bundles; python/wheel_backend.py + pyproject.toml PyPI packaging
one_why: The codex-9 vs cline-8 discriminator in the anchor is 'versioned app-server protocol + published SDKs' -- letta has the versioned protocol and shipped client types (matching codex's shape) AND an OpenAI-compat surface neither codex nor cline exposes, which is the single strongest third-party integration hook in this lane.

subject: letta-code
title: MCP support is client-side and real (stdio/SSE/streamable-HTTP + OAuth) with server-side tool management gated on backend capability, but the harness never exposes itself as an MCP server and has no ACP at all
evidence: src/mcp-client.ts:6-11 (stdio, SSE, streamableHttp transports), src/mcp-oauth.ts 369 LOC; src/cli/subcommands/mcp.ts:174-178 serverMcpAvailable -> getBackend().capabilities.serverSideToolManagement; @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0 package.json:138; grep -rni 'acp|agent-client-protocol' src/ package.json: zero hits (llamacpp false-positives only); no vscode/jetbrains extension directory anywhere in tree; IDE-ish surfaces are the closed desktop app and chat.letta.com via the SDK exports
one_why: codex-9 exposes MCP both directions; nanocoder-7's whole interop score is its ACP commitment; letta's surfaces are wide (CLI, desktop, web, four messaging channels, app-server) but no editor can speak a standard protocol to it -- cline-8 sits at the same 'no ACP' line and this is why the lane tops out at 8.

subject: letta-code
title: User documentation lives entirely off-repo at docs.letta.com (docs/ holds only nix.md, examples, plans) -- the exact codex-7 shape -- while error-message engineering in-code is genuinely strong: a 976-line classified formatter with actionable links and a single-source denial formatter born from 10+ inconsistent call sites
evidence: ls docs/ -> examples, nix.md, plans; README.md links to docs.letta.com for every feature and onboarding flow (:38-56 npm install -g, first-run cloud/local choice, letta setup, /connect, personality tutorial); src/cli/helpers/error-formatter.ts 976 LOC with per-error-class handling and run/agent deep-links (:837-838 createAgentLink); src/permissions/format-denial.ts:1-5 ('Callers previously open-coded this formatter in 10+ places... with subtle inconsistencies... single source of truth lives here'); contributor docs: AGENTS.md 968 lines + per-dir AGENTS.md
one_why: On the anchors' own criterion pi-9 (30+ in-repo docs) vs codex-7 (in-repo = pointers) is decided by repo-local docs and letta's fail that test identically to codex; the failure-copy layer deserves noting as the docs-dx idea the anchor set never scored -- but honest placement stays 7, docked for off-repo docs and cloud-optional onboarding that still nudges sign-in as the default.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Dual-backend migration: full agent stack exists twice behind a 9,519-LOC adapter, and CI exercises only the legacy leg
evidence: vibe/app_server/_unified_harness_backend_adapter.py (9,519 LOC, 443 defs, translates every app-server RPC to the Rust Unified Harness); docs/adr/0011-unified-harness-backend.md ('the invocation selects one Host... no shared catalogue'); tests/conftest.py:96 (backend_contract selects ONE backend via --experimental-harness CLI flag); .github/workflows/ci.yml:99 (the only test job runs 'uv run pytest --ignore tests/snapshots' with no --experimental-harness); no cargo/nextest job in any .github/workflows/*.yml (cargo test exists only at Makefile:70); vibe/_experimental_harness.py:15 (rollout key vibe_cli_unified_harness_rollout lets GrowthBook switch users onto the unified backend)
one_why: A remote rollout can move users onto a backend whose Python-side translation seam never runs in CI, so behavior drift between the two implementations is discoverable by users before it is discoverable by tests; the contract suite's own conftest comment (tests/app_server/backend_contract/conftest.py:88-92) shows the authors know backend selection is a footgun but still run one leg per invocation

subject: mistral-vibe
title: AgentLoop is a 3,966-LOC, 142-method god class with a 30-kwarg constructor, explicitly noqa'd past complexity rules
evidence: vibe/core/agent_loop/_loop.py:528 (class AgentLoop, noqa: PLR0904), :529 (__init__ noqa: PLR0913, PLR0915, ~30 kwargs including session_lease, cache_store, experiment_state, harness_files); 142 method defs in the class body (static count :528-end); 89 imports; the class owns turn lifecycle, approvals, compaction triggers, titles, teleport, checkpoints, config reload; vibe/cli/textual_ui/app.py:673 (VibeApp, 6,669 LOC, also noqa: PLR0904) is the anchor-errata >5k-LOC product-surface docking factor
one_why: Every cross-cutting change (approval semantics, title cadence, overflow self-heal) lands in one file, which is how codex-shaped cores stay at 9 and how this caps near 7-8 despite good external boundaries

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Session journal: per-step append-only fsynced JSONL plus atomic rewrite, owner-only modes, corrupt-tolerant loader
evidence: vibe/core/session/session_logger.py:386-408 (O_APPEND|O_CREAT 0o600, flush + os.fsync, rationale comment 'Session logs hold raw tool results'); :413-438 (_overwrite_messages_sync via NamedTemporaryFile + os.replace); :64-66 (asyncio save lock so concurrent saves cannot interleave appends); vibe/core/agent_loop/_loop.py:2105 (save after every LLM step, comment 'so the on-disk log stays fresh') and :2137 (finally-save on turn teardown); vibe/core/session/session_loader.py:235-262 (explicit corrupted-metadata / empty-messages / invalid-JSON recovery paths)
one_why: Crash loss is bounded to at most one in-flight step and a half-written log degrades to a diagnosable '(corrupted session)' entry instead of an exception on /resume - a cheap durability posture worth copying in any CLI agent

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Session lease: OS byte-range lock with symlink refusal, pid/timestamp diagnostics beside (not inside) the lock, explicit busy error
evidence: vibe/core/session/session_lease.py:42-96 (acquire: symlink check on both parent dirs, 0o700 dir, 0o600 lock file, non-blocking _acquire_file_lock raising SessionBusyError); :63-64 comment ('The diagnostic sits beside the lock, not inside it: Windows byte-range locks make the lock file unreadable while held'); :81-89 (BaseException-wide rollback releasing the OS lock even when non-OSError code fails); session id regex-validated at :11,:27 before path construction
one_why: Two processes opening the same session is the classic resume-corruption race; this makes it a typed SessionBusyError with a readable pid diagnostic on both POSIX and Windows, including the descriptor-close-releases-lock Windows subtlety

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Rewind engine is an append-only event log (turns, manual edits, keep/revert decisions) re-projected into file state, with dependency-closed per-hunk revert
evidence: vibe/core/checkpoints/checkpointer.py:32-60 (class docstring: 'append-only log... resolved into file states through a pure History'; truncating at a turn boundary re-projects the earlier state; 'every projection is a dependency-closed drop and never a merge'); :47-52 manual edits captured by reconcile 'against the live projection, so it is idempotent and needs no side caches'; vibe/core/checkpoints/history.py:703 LOC pure projection; vibe/core/rewind/manager.py:18-21 ('Impure shell over the shared Checkpointer')
one_why: Modeling file history as a pure log plus projections rather than git-stash snapshots gives per-hunk revert with correct dependent-hunk semantics and idempotent drift capture - materially stronger than the anchor 8-rung (cline git-stash checkpoints) in design, marred only by c6

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Checkpoint log is memory-only: rewind and file-restore die at process exit, so a resumed session cannot rewind any prior turn
evidence: vibe/core/agent_loop/_loop.py:741 (checkpointer = Checkpointer() - fresh empty log at every loop construction; sole construction site repo-wide); checkpointer.py:46-47 docstring states 'The log never touches disk'; zero persistence calls under vibe/core/checkpoints/ (grep for persist/jsonl/write hits only projection-logic lines) and zero 'checkpoint' references under vibe/core/session/ (session_logger, session_loader, resume_sessions all clean)
one_why: Messages survive restart but the ability to undo the edits those messages describe does not; cline at the 8-rung keeps checkpoints on disk (checkpoint-hooks) so rewind survives restart, which is exactly the operability gap here - unless the Rust harness store compensates, which nothing in the Python tree indicates

subject: mistral-vibe
title: No faulthandler or native-crash hook anywhere despite a native-Rust second backend; Python-level observability is otherwise solid
evidence: grep for faulthandler|excepthook across vibe/, cli-rust/, harness/ returns nothing; what exists instead: vibe/observability/logging.py:57-108 (RotatingFileHandler subclass with owner-only creation, structured formatter, harness logger), vibe/cli/stderr_guard.py:39-58 (fd-2 dup guard so native writes cannot corrupt the TUI), vibe/observability/sentry.py
one_why: A segfault in the pyo3 harness binding or libc dies without a stack trace on disk; faulthandler.enable() plus a Rust panic hook is a three-line backstop that the stderr_guard's own existence (native writes are expected here) argues for

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Explicit turn-vs-mutation exclusion inside the loop: act() refuses while any session 'holder' runs, with the TOCTOU window documented
evidence: vibe/core/agent_loop/_loop.py:1619-1627 (act rejects when _active_turn set, then rejects when self._holders non-empty, with comment 'A holder is not a turn, so the check above cannot see one. A move refuses while a turn is active and then awaits twice; without this a turn could begin in that window'); :1457-1471 (_take_session/_release_session); :1696,:1712 teleport takes/releases the session around a git-pushing operation; vibe/core/types.py:686-708 (MessageList reset hooks keep RewindManager consistent when the list is replaced under it, reset_preserving_system locked against deferred-init interleaving)
one_why: Long-running session operations (teleport, relocate, rewind) and turns share mutable state; naming that mutual-exclusion domain explicitly, at both ends of each await, is the kind of race-hardening most CLI agents only discover through bug reports

subject: mistral-vibe
title: vibe/core/loop.py is not the agent loop - the name squat redirects every reviewer and ADR-ignorant contributor away from agent_loop/_loop.py
evidence: vibe/core/loop.py is the ScheduledLoop cron manager (MAX_LOOPS_PER_SESSION per scout, distinct from AgentLoop); the real loop is vibe/core/agent_loop/_loop.py:528 (class AgentLoop, act() at :1594); docs/adr/0003-event-driven-agent-loop.md describes the latter without disambiguating the former
one_why: Pure naming cost, but it is the first file any contributor or automated reviewer opens, and the scout of this very repo had to flag it as a red herring

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Shell gating parses bash with tree-sitter and fails closed the moment the extract stops describing what runs: syntax errors, line continuations, heredoc bodies, env-assignment prefixes and unreadable identity tokens all flip invalidates_scope, which strips every pattern grant and forces the literal command as the only honest scope
evidence: vibe/core/tools/builtins/_shell_permission_analysis.py:287-303 (analyze_shell_command: '\\\n' line continuation and tree.root_node.has_error both add approval reason + invalidates_scope), :193-215 (_identity_survives: unreadable token before the arity boundary invalidates the pattern), :316-323 (heredoc/redirect bodies never reach command_parts so 'python <redirect> *' would grant every script); vibe/core/tools/builtins/bash.py:369-410 (scoped_command_parts/needs_exact_command_scope: no part is offered once the extract lies); per-binary option guardrails vibe/core/tools/builtins/_shell_command_policy.py:312-330 (find -exec/-delete/-ok/-fprint all require approval), :576+ (git --ext-diff/--output/--textconv), :831-862 (dispatcher + has_option_guardrails); tests: tests/tools/test_bash.py:3446-3470 (grant on 'git log $REF' does NOT cover 'git log --ext-diff' or '--output=/tmp/stolen', legacy AND managed shells), :3532 ('cat $FILE' grant does not cover 'cat notes.txt > /etc/cron.d/pwn'), :3274 ('&&' -> 'a syntax error')
one_why: This is the same mechanism class the grok-build anchor earned with, and it closes the corpus-wide regex-denylist anti-pattern class: approval is owed for the syntax the extractor cannot read, and a grant can never widen over tokens that were dropped - the denylist itself (bash.py:104-135) is only a second layer under the parser.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Grant algebra is explicitly anti-widening: a literal flag keeps command-text grants out of glob reach, path grants are encoded with a 'vibe-path:' prefix so no command wildcard can ever authorize a path, and sensitive-file grants are scoped to the exact filename so approving one .env does not licence the next
evidence: vibe/permissions.py:44-58 (literal flag docstring names the threat: 'cat *' would otherwise cover 'cat notes > /etc/cron.d/pwn'), :71-134 (path_grant_pattern encode/_parse + _is_legacy_path_grant_pattern: command wildcards like '*' or 'npm *' must not clear outside-workdir checks), vibe/core/tools/permissions.py:39-51 (covers(): literal rules match text-only, scope+tool_name must both match); vibe/core/tools/utils.py:36-44 (DEFAULT_SENSITIVE_PATTERNS .env/.envrc), :217-227 (grant scoped to glob.escape(file) - 'a different sensitive file re-prompts'), :148-165 (resolve_path_permission: denylist checked before allowlist, NEVER wins); tests: tests/test_permissions.py:12-55 (12 path-glob rows incl. relative-'tmp/*' must not match /var/tmp/secret; 'cat *' must not authorize /etc/passwd), tests/test_permission_store.py:95-144 (outside-path scopes do not overgrant; traversal and windows-case normalization)
one_why: Most subjects let approve-always silently generalize; here every grant records the narrowest honest scope and the code comments state the escape class being closed - the widening attack ('innocent grant earned, escalated command covered') is treated as the design center, and it is tested as pairs.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Uncertainty lands on deny or a prompt everywhere on the enforcement path: no bound approval UI returns an immediate NO, programmatic mode never prompts and treats the folder as untrusted, the trust store is created owner-only, rerooting a session re-resolves trust instead of carrying the old verdict, and git operations against untrusted checkouts reject user config inside the worktree
evidence: vibe/core/agent_loop/_request_broker.py:49 (events is None -> ApprovalResponse.NO 'Tool execution not permitted.' - no UI, no execution); vibe/core/config/layer.py:149,314 (layers untrusted by default, UntrustedLayerError - project .vibe/config.toml refused in untrusted dirs), vibe/core/config/layers/project.py:47-60 (reroot re-resolves trust: 'without this the verdict earned by the old root would decide the new one'); vibe/core/git/fetch.py:48,347 (untrusted-repository fetch policy, reject user config files resolving inside the checkout); vibe/core/trusted_folders.py:21-40 (trust decisions incl. decline persisted); vibe/core/tools/base.py:144 (every tool defaults to ASK, incl. MCP tools which carry no resolve_permission); tests: tests/cli/test_approval_app_grace_period.py:53-127, tests/core/test_trusted_folders.py:35 (owner-only trust store file mode), :93-105 (untrusted path -> false/none), tests/acp/test_trust.py:20-155 (trust RPC rejects foreign cwd, non-string cwd, and accepts symlink to session cwd - 8 boundary tests)
one_why: The inverse of the corpus's recurring failure (nanocoder's fail-open-to-sh): there is no code path where a missing UI, a moved workspace, or an unreadable trust file results in execution - the default for unknown tools is ASK and the default for unknown folders is untrusted.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: No OS-level enforcement exists anywhere in either backend, and --yolo is a total waiver that short-circuits even the denylist: if a parse is wrong or bypass is on, an approved command runs with full user privileges and nothing beneath can veto it
evidence: repo-wide grep for bwrap|seatbelt|seccomp|landlock|RLIMIT over vibe/ and harness/ returns zero hits (harness 'sandbox' hits are the v8 code-mode eval isolate and tool-name namespacing only: harness/core/src/core/features/programmatic_tool_calling/code_mode/v8.rs:51-112 heap/timeout terminate, harness/core/src/core/tools/resolved/assembly.rs:92 sandbox_name); vibe/core/agent_loop/_loop.py:2943-2948 (bypass_tool_permissions returns EXECUTE before resolve_permission is ever consulted - NEVER/denylist/sensitive all skipped on the legacy path); vibe/cli/entrypoint.py:140-145 (--auto-approve/--yolo single flag, no floor, no managed pin); vibe/core/tools/builtins/bash.py:700-760 (run() never re-checks policy at execution time; enforcement is decided-then-executed); network: per-origin URL_PATTERN approval only (vibe/core/tools/builtins/web_fetch.py:115-135) with cross-origin redirect re-check (:244-248) but no SSRF/metadata screening and no codex-style separate egress approval
one_why: This is the fixed ceiling the anchors call 'tested approval, nothing underneath' (the 6 rung): unlike grok-build there is no opt-in kernel layer and no floor surviving bypass - the whole safety story rides on the correctness of one tree-sitter extraction plus the human in the loop; SECURITY.md (disclosure-only) never states this ceiling.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Injection tagging is partial and spoofable: vibe_warning wraps only harness-authored advisories (AGENTS.md injection, plan-mode reminder, context events, empty-file warnings) while raw file bodies, bash stdout, web_fetch content and every MCP tool result enter the transcript untagged, with no escaping of a forged closing tag in the wrapped payloads
evidence: vibe/utils/__init__.py:9 (VIBE_WARNING_TAG='vibe_warning'); wrapped sites: vibe/core/tools/builtins/read_file.py:48-49,137 (warnings + discovered AGENTS.md only - the file content itself at :173-215 is line-numbered but unwrapped), vibe/app_server/_agents_md_hooks.py:141, vibe/core/middleware.py:129,165-176 (plan-mode 'MUST NOT' is prompt text, not a tool gate), vibe/core/agent_loop/_loop.py:2445-2447,3635-3638; NOT wrapped: vibe/core/tools/builtins/web_fetch.py:157-163 (fetched content returned raw), vibe/core/tools/remote.py:24-30 (MCPToolResult.text unwrapped; grep shows no vibe_warning anywhere under vibe/core/tools/), bash stdout via bash.py:735-760; no escaping/sanitizing of '<'+tag sequences in any wrapped content (vibe/core/utils/tags.py:15-16 only parses known tags for outbound projection); the two *injection* test files test the @-mention and /skill injection FEATURES, not containment: tests/agent_loop/test_agent_file_injection.py:46-96, tests/agent_loop/test_agent_skill_injection.py:45-96
one_why: With no sandbox (s4), the approval prompt is the containment layer and injection is its main attack path; the corpus norm (this study's 'injection-screening' concept) is to mark untrusted content and screen for tag forgery - vibe marks the cheapest surfaces and left the highest-volume untrusted channels (bash output, web, MCP) unmarked, and nothing tests that a file reading '</vibe_warning>' cannot break the framing.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Behavior-shaping surfaces are all gated behind a persisted folder-trust decision with a repo-root/cwd/session/decline grain, and the trust gate is exercised at the RPC boundary against spoofed cwd shapes
evidence: vibe/core/trusted_folders.py:21-26 (trust_repo/trust_cwd/trust_session/decline), :71-83 (find_trustable_files = AGENTS.md + local config dirs), :49-68 (repo-root detection excludes home and fs root); vibe/core/config/layers/project.py:13-16 (project config walks up only to a TRUSTED .vibe/config.toml); vibe/core/plan_session.py + vibe/core/middleware.py:165-176 (plan mode narrows the model to read-only via prompt guard before approval, cline-style); vibe/core/hooks/_pre_tool.py:48-113 (hooks can deny/allow per call, deny reason surfaced to model); tests: tests/acp/test_trust.py:20-155 (trust decision rejected without session, for unknown session, for foreign cwd, non-string cwd), tests/agent_loop/test_approve_always_permanent.py:33-258 (permanent grant persists to config and session rules, session-only grants never persist, typed path grants survive)
one_why: Same shape as pi's project-trust gate but wired deeper: hooks, project config, AGENTS.md and MCP-provided behavior all sit behind the one trust decision, and the trust RPC itself is tested as a trust boundary rather than assumed.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: The two highest-adversarial-fidelity suites never run in CI: the 367-scenario PTY golden client-e2e suite (incl. tool-approval and trusted-folders-gate scenarios) is Makefile-only and explicitly excluded from the main pytest, and the Rust harness has zero cargo-test invocation in any workflow
evidence: pyproject.toml:304-305 ('client-e2e is a standalone harness... --ignore=client-e2e'); Makefile:29 (golden suite target) and Makefile:69-70 (test_rust: cargo test) - grep over .github/workflows/*.yml finds no 'client-e2e', no 'cargo test', no nextest; the CI pytest job is ubuntu-only with a 2-retry flake tolerance (.github/workflows/ci.yml:97-104 'pytest failed; retrying last-failed tests'); client-e2e safety scenarios exist and are real: client-e2e/scenarios/conversation/tool_approval*.py (6 files), client-e2e/scenarios/trusted_folders/gate.py, decline.py, options_selection.py (trust-gate keystrokes against scripted handshake)
one_why: The property tests that carry the verification score DO run in CI (tests/tools, tests/app_server) - but the layers that could catch approval-UI regressions and Rust-harness semantic drift (the dual-backend risk the scout flagged) have no gate, so 'CI is green' under-claims what is actually verified.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Honesty about the enforcement ceiling is minimal: SECURITY.md is pure disclosure policy, README claims only 'Features tool execution approval', and the only accurate description of the trust system's limits lives in a model-facing skill file rather than user docs
evidence: SECURITY.md:1-51 (reporting/coordination only - no statement of what is or is not enforced, contrast pi's SECURITY.md:50 'intentionally does not have a sandbox'); README.md:110 ('Safety First: Features tool execution approval' - true but silent on no-sandbox and on --yolo being unconditional); vibe/core/skills/builtins/vibe.py:1243-1262 (accurate trust-system + sensitive-file rules, injected into the model's context, not user documentation); no docs/adr or docs/ page describes the threat model of the permission layer
one_why: Not misleading (nothing is over-claimed, so no phantom-safety-control), but the anchors' honesty exemplar documents its ceiling for users; vibe leaves users to discover that approval is the entire boundary.

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Compaction primary deliberately rides the live prompt-cache prefix; the fallback breaks cache on purpose for reliability; prior user messages survive the fold in a token budget
evidence: vibe/core/compaction/manager.py:137-138 (comment 'Cache-friendly: the request rides on the live conversation's token prefix', primary call sends conversation + one appended request message with live tools); manager.py:157-158 (fallback comment 'Breaks the prompt cache on purpose - a reliable summary is worth it', fresh system prompt, thinking off, no tools, flat transcript render at :207-229); compaction/context.py:12 (_PREVIOUS_USER... 20k-token preservation budget), :191-247 (collect_prior_user_messages walks newest-first, drops injections/prior summaries, middle-truncates the spill, re-parses previously preserved messages from the old envelope at :113-127 so user intent survives chained compactions); context.py:86-91 escapes reserved tags inside preserved user content against envelope spoofing
one_why: The two-pass structure (cheap cache-hugging primary, expensive transcript fallback) plus cross-compaction user-message folding is a concrete, copyable pattern; cline's 7-rung has the fold but explicitly 'no cache discipline', and vibe's cache-hugging primary is a real increment over that rung

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Auto-compact triggers on the previous turn's API-reported usage, not a projected request; overflow is caught reactively once per turn
evidence: vibe/core/agent_loop/_loop.py:3363 (stats.context_tokens = usage.prompt_tokens + usage.completion_tokens - set only after an API response); vibe/core/middleware.py:100-106 (AutoCompactMiddleware compares that stale counter to auto_compact_threshold before the next turn); _loop.py:2091-2098 (ContextTooLongError caught in-loop, self-heals via _run_compaction, gated once-per-turn by _should_self_heal at :1929-1935); manager.py:186-205 (PTL retry loop inside compaction drops oldest round, _COMPACTION_PTL_RETRIES=3)
one_why: pi's 8-rung measures the projected request before sending (compaction.ts:289 'what the model would actually receive'); vibe's turn-heavy growth between the last API call and the next request always overshoots the threshold by one turn, and the reactive backstop only fires once - a second overflow in the same turn raises. Correct, but strictly more tokens wasted and fewer recovery chances than the 8-rung

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Prompt-cache discipline exists only on the Anthropic/Vertex leg, and mid-session system-prompt refreshes silently bust it from at least 8 app_server call sites
evidence: vibe/core/llm/backend/anthropic.py:251-273 (cache_control ephemeral on the system block and the last user message only - two breakpoints, no tool-block or history breakpoints); vertex.py:62,121 (inherits adapter, adds last-user-message control); mistral.py:104-115,511,604 (Mistral path only *counts* usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, zero client-side cache-key control); openai_responses.py:203 and generic.py:202 (same, count-only); cache-bust surface: _loop.py:894-901 (_refresh_system_prompt_unless_reloaded rewrites the cache_control'd system message with no cache gating after skill sync), _legacy_session_backend.py:310,324,464,506,519,524,537 and _resources.py:830 (refresh_system_prompt on config/skill/tool changes), _loop.py:1189 (refresh after experiment-layer sync)
one_why: No cache warming (pi's cache-warmer.ts is the 8-rung marker) and no attempt to defer or coalesce the refreshes that rewrite a cached system block; on the flagship Mistral backend all cache behavior is opaque server-side. The discipline is real but one-sided exactly as the scout flagged

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Turn, dollar, and token session budgets as separate one-method middleware, plus a 50 percent context warning injection and cost accounting that prices cached tokens
evidence: vibe/core/middleware.py:49-96 (TurnLimitMiddleware / PriceLimitMiddleware / TokenLimitMiddleware each a before_turn STOP with a human-readable reason string); _loop.py:1833-1834 (max_turns wired into the pipeline); app_server/protocol.py:807-812 (max_turns/max_tokens are protocol-level session params); middleware.py:112-134 (ContextWarningMiddleware injects a VIBE_WARNING_TAG-wrapped percent-used notice once at 50 percent of threshold); core/types.py:70-72,110-121 (input/output/cached-input price per million, session_cost); llm/backend/anthropic.py:179-190 (cache_read/cache_creation folded into prompt_tokens so budgets see true spend, with the Anthropic-excludes-cached rationale commented)
one_why: Cheap, composable runaway protection that the anchors mostly lack at this granularity (nanocoder's 6-rung explicitly has 'no budgets'; crush has none in-loop); the cached-token price axis makes dollar caps honest under prompt caching

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Subagents are real child sessions with their own lease, saved under the parent's session dir, linked into parent history, with typed cancel-cleanup and resume_child
evidence: vibe/app_server/_runtime.py:1000-1056 (create_child: child session_logging rooted at parent_session_dir/agents, own SessionLease acquired, share_permissions=True; lease released on any BaseException; resume_child reloads a crashed/finished child's messages); vibe/app_server/_sessions.py:317-395 (run(): persist_empty_session + record_child_session before the turn; BaseException rollback unlinks, deletes saved child, closes runtime; on CancelledError/GeneratorExit interrupts the child turn and awaits completion); tools/builtins/task.py:97-106 (depth limit 1 enforced with an explanatory ToolError; only AgentType.SUBAGENT spawnable 'security constraint to prevent recursive spawning'), :77-87 (per-agent-name fnmatch deny-then-allow list, default allowlist=['explore'])
one_why: Durability of delegation is above the 6-rung ('unproven crash semantics'): a parent resume can rediscover children as sessions, and cancel paths are exhaustively rolled back - but the ceiling is intentional depth 1 and no inter-agent messaging, which is why this stays at 7, not cline's 8 (teams-as-tools)

subject: mistral-vibe
title: The first-class turn queue (enqueue/steer/replace/resume, idempotency keys) is in-memory only - queued input dies with the process
evidence: vibe/app_server/protocol.py:216-221 (session/turn/enqueue, queue/read, queue/remove, queue/replace, queue/steer, queue/resume are named RPCs); app_server/_turn_queue.py:49 (docstring: 'Own queued turns and idempotency receipts for one live Session'), :17-34 (typed full/idempotency-conflict/not-found errors); app_server/models.py:1177 (TURN_QUEUE_MAX_ITEMS=32); _turns.py:269-270 (new turn refused while queue non-empty - 'Resume queued turns before starting a new turn'); zero hits for turn_queue persistence in vibe/core/session/session_logger.py (grep)
one_why: The API shape is codex-9-rung ('queue' as first-class with steer and idempotency receipts) but the backing store is nanocoder-6-rung; cline's 8-rung durable sqlite cron and crush's sqlite resume both survive the crash this queue does not - a small persistence layer would lift the shape to its own promise

subject: mistral-vibe
title: No loop/runaway detector anywhere; only the optional max_turns counter stands between an agent and infinite tool-calling
evidence: repo-wide grep for loop.detect/runaway/repeated-tool patterns in vibe/ (non-test) returns nothing; the only circuit-breakers are TurnLimitMiddleware (middleware.py:49-57, opt-in via --max-turns/protocol param, default None per protocol.py:359) and the once-per-turn overflow self-heal; scheduled loops cap at MAX_LOOPS_PER_SESSION=50 with MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS=30 (vibe/core/loop.py:26-27) but a fired prompt that itself loops is unguarded
one_why: The anchors record crush as the only subject with a loop-detection breaker (loop_detection.go:11-40) and treat that as what separates its 7 from nothing; vibe's budgets are stricter than crush's but they bound total spend, not repetition - a 40-tool-call identical-edit loop is legal until the dollar cap fires

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Full ACP server surface plus five-platform prebuilt vibe-acp binaries, headless -p/--output text|json|streaming, a GitHub Action, and an MCP client with sampling - strongest interop spread in the corpus
evidence: vibe/acp/agent.py:452-1127 (initialize, authenticate, new/load session, prompt, cancel, close, list_sessions, set_session_mode, set_config_option, fork_session, resume_session, ext_method with voice/config-schema/project-links extensions); distribution/zed/extension.toml (published Zed agent_server for darwin/linux aarch64+x86_64 and windows - prebuilt vibe-acp archives per release); docs/acp-setup.md:1-40+ (Zed and JetBrains setup, pinned agent-client-protocol==0.11.0 at pyproject.toml:29); vibe/cli/entrypoint.py:65,114 (-p/--prompt, --output) + programmatic.py:39-43 (TEXT/JSON/STREAMING built on the same LocalHarness app-server session as the TUI); action.yml (composite GitHub Action); tools/mcp/registry.py:454 (per-server sampling_enabled); _sessions.py SessionRuntimeRegistry implements SubagentRunnerPort behind the same app-server
one_why: Exceeds cline's 8-rung on protocol breadth (ACP fork/resume/list where cline has none; plugin-import where nobody else imports rivals) but stops short of codex's 9: no MCP server side, no published typed SDK - the app_server protocol is internal, version-skew-tolerated (ADR 0014) rather than shipped as a product

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Foreign plugin-format adapters detect and translate claude-code, codex, kimi_code, opencode, and agent-plugins.org packages - including rival skill directories - with ambiguity detection and path-traversal checks
evidence: vibe/core/plugins/_compatibility.py:24-31 (DetectedPluginFormat enum: AGENT_PLUGINS_1_0, CODEX, CLAUDE_CODE, KIMI_CODE, OPENCODE, UNKNOWN, AMBIGUOUS), :157-176 (marker-file detection, ambiguous when multiple formats match), :258-298 (_opencode_markers: scans .opencode/plugins+tools for code files, keyword-gated package.json with explicit 'package.json must resolve inside the plugin root' traversal guard at :293); plugins/_foreign.py:354 (imports root/.claude/skills as a skill source); _foreign.py:53 + app_server/models.py:683 (format tags only - no foreign prompt or code vendored, matching the scout's provenance verdict)
one_why: Nothing in the anchor set imports a competitor's plugin ecosystem as a first-class input; it is a distribution strategy disguised as an interop module - each marker check is also a migration funnel, with format ambiguity handled explicitly rather than first-match-wins

subject: mistral-vibe
title: ADR 0011 links a design doc that does not exist in the repo; product docs are off-tree and the 1,062-line README carries everything else
evidence: docs/adr/0011-unified-harness-backend.md:34 ('See docs/design/resume-cross-harness-session-listing.md for the full ...') - docs/design/ does not exist (ls confirms; find for design docs returns only the .vibe/skills authoring template); docs/ contains exactly README.md (9 lines), acp-setup.md, proxy-setup.md, adr/ (17 files, 1,654 lines total incl. the 606-line 0009); README.md is 1,062 lines covering install, proxy, Git-on-Windows, update policy, feature reference
one_why: The ADR culture is genuinely 9-rung (agent-facing routing table in AGENTS.md:1-57, decision records with amendments), but pi's 9-rung is 30+ in-repo docs that match code, and cline's 8-rung is a full feature-doc tree; a dangling reference inside the single most consequential ADR is exactly the drift gate that docs exist to prevent

subject: mistral-vibe
title: Onboarding and error UX are specific and actionable: one-line installer plus uv/pip/brew paths, self-update prompt, argparse help that states safety semantics, typed errors with examples in the message
evidence: README.md:27-54 (curl one-liner, uv tool install, pip), :984-986 (daily PyPI check with in-app update-or-continue prompt, vibe --check-upgrade); vibe/cli/entrypoint.py:180-185 (--trust help explicitly states 'not persisted to trusted_folders.toml. Skips the trust prompt. Use this for non-interactive automation.'); vibe/core/loop.py:66-79 (LoopError messages embed the expected grammar with an example 'e.g., 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d'); config/layer.py:86-88 (config layer wraps OSError 'e.g. a read-only config.toml' rather than crashing raw); session_lease.py:15-18 (SessionBusyError carries the session id); tools/builtins/task.py:98-113 (each ToolError states the violated constraint and the remedy)
one_why: No anchor docking factor here: errors name the constraint and the fix, and the CLI help doubles as safety documentation - matches codex's install ergonomics and beats crush's docs-dx 6 baseline

subject: dexto
title: Turn loop is an explicit phase state machine with strict-zod serializable checkpoint states that refuse to snapshot mid-flight
evidence: packages/core/src/llm/executor/turn-executor.ts:199-247 (TurnDriverStateSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('phase', ready-for-model | model-step-prepared | model-step-complete | stopped), all .strict()); :619-627 getState() throws 'cannot checkpoint during model preparation / a model step / tool execution'; :917-922 checkpoint() = getState + dispose; turn-executor.integration.test.ts:70 (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify) roundtrip via parseTurnDriverState) and :507, :632, :671, :714, :1174, :1196 (checkpoint after prepare / after model step / after tool calls, rehydrate and continue), :554, :788, :1188, :1435 (transient-phase and finished-driver refusals asserted)
one_why: This is the strongest anchor-level architecture signal found: the loop's continuation state is a validated closed union, so illegal states are unrepresentable and mid-flight snapshot corruption is refused at runtime and pinned by tests - beyond pi's in-memory loop and crush's non-serializable agent.go.

subject: dexto
title: Checkpoint/resume machinery is fully built and tested but has zero production callers; server admits restart-survival is unimplemented
evidence: grep for createTurnDriver callers outside packages/core/src/llm and chat-session.ts returns only chat-session.test.ts (:680, :824, :869) - no host, route, or A2A path constructs ChatSessionTurnDriverInput{kind:'resume'} (packages/core/src/session/chat-session.ts:61-62); checkpoint() is invoked only by the wrapper chat-session.ts:798-801 and tests; packages/server/src/hono/routes/messages.ts:319-321 TODO: 'This only preserves resumability while the current agent process stays alive. To survive agent/server restarts, persist a resumable run checkpoint for approval-blocked turns and resume from storage after approval.'
one_why: The flagship durability feature (kill -9 mid-turn, resume from the last phase boundary) exists as a tested seam with no consumer - process restart loses the in-flight run (history survives, driver state does not), which is exactly the gap codex/pi's rollout journals close; approval-blocked runs die with the server.

subject: dexto
title: TurnExecutor.execute drives the loop through the same public step-callback interface its 4,456-LOC integration suite drives, so the real loop is exercised step-by-step without mocking the loop itself
evidence: turn-executor.ts:536-558 (execute() = while(!stopped){ runNextModelStep(); if tool-calls executeToolCalls(); decideNextStep(); }) built on the TurnDriver interface :390-397; turn-executor.integration.test.ts (4,456 LOC) calls driver phases directly across every branch, e.g. :578 retry-after-preparation-failure, :797 checkpoint does not clear queued steer messages, :3503/:3561 retry-budget exhaustion with llm:retrying events asserted
one_why: Loop-internal invariants (step ordering, tool-before-decide, queue preservation) become directly addressable by tests instead of being inferred from end-to-end runs - the nanocoder lesson inverted: the loop seam is why the largest test file in the repo can be an honest loop spec.

subject: dexto
title: Model-request retry is refused unless the persisted conversation history is byte-for-length unchanged, preventing duplicate tool side effects on replay
evidence: turn-executor.ts:1692-1726 runModelStepWithRetry snapshots (await this.contextManager.getModelHistory()).length before the call and compares after failure; canRetryModelRequest :1728-1733 returns false if history length changed, step aborted, or error is not an APICallError with isRetryable; MODEL_REQUEST_MAX_RETRIES=2 (:80); tested at turn-executor.integration.test.ts:3503 (retryable failure retried with llm:retrying event) and :3561 (budget exhausts to terminal failure)
one_why: Direct counter to the retry-blind-backoff anti-pattern (auto-code-rover): a retryable provider error that arrives after the history was already mutated would replay tool calls, and dexto's guard makes 'history untouched' a precondition of replay.

subject: dexto
title: Two-tier mid-task input queues (late-steer coalesced into the next model step, follow-ups only after natural stop) decided inside the loop against DB-backed queue stores with an ephemeral fallback
evidence: turn-executor.ts:1122-1160 decideNextStep: tool-calls branch does hard-cancel check (abort + empty steer queue => cancelled), non-tool branch tries steerQueue.hasPending() as 'late-steer' then followUpQueue unless executionControl.followUpQueueMode==='host-run'; :1166-1193 injectQueuedMessages coalesces into one user message with originalMessageIds metadata; message-queue.ts:182 store.append persists position; checkpoint preserves steer queue (turn-executor.integration.test.ts:797) || persistence half (from dexto-e5): packages/core/src/storage/stores/backend.ts:533 (DatabaseBackedSessionMessageQueueStore implements SessionMessageQueueStore); packages/core/src/session/message-queue.ts:8-45 (EphemeralMessageQueueStore fallback with deep-clone isolation on every read/write); ChatSession wires separate steer+followUp stores (session/chat-session.ts:186-187, session-manager.ts:161-162); HTTP surface at packages/server/src/hono/routes/queue.ts (425 LOC)
one_why: Mid-turn steering is a loop-policy decision with its own cancel semantics and end-of-turn fallback, not a bolt-on (core), AND the queue is server-side durable rather than a UI-side buffer (econ) - the late-steer path ('missed the pre-request injection point') is the subtle case most harnesses drop, and codex's first-class `codex queue` remains the only 9-rung benchmark; no other anchor persists queued input at all, missing only CLI first-class-ness and crash-resume of a parked queue mid-run (cf. dexto-c2).

subject: dexto

subject: dexto
title: DextoAgent.ts is 3,724 LOC with ~100 methods but delegates the loop: no provider call inside the file, stream() is event fan-in plus one session.stream() call

one_why: The scout's top god-file suspect turns out to be a wide but honest facade - the crush failure mode is absent - though at 3.7k LOC with ~15 inline event listeners it sits close to the errata's 5k docking line and should be split along its existing manager seams.

subject: dexto
title: context/utils.ts is a 2,224-LOC module of 34 exports mixing token estimation, blob resolution, MIME matching, tool-result sanitization, and display formatting
evidence: packages/core/src/context/utils.ts (2,224 LOC; :estimateStringTokens, estimateMessagesTokens, estimateContextTokens, expandBlobReferences, filterMessagesByLLMCapabilities, normalizeToolResult, persistToolMedia, sanitizeToolResultToContentWithBlobs, filterCompacted, formatToolOutputForDisplay, ... 34 exports)

subject: dexto
title: Every loop phase emits an OTel span with result attributes, and a CLI (dexto span list <runId>, dexto trace) fetches and formats run traces on demand
evidence: turn-executor.ts:711-727, :804-815, :843-866 (recordOperationSpan wrappers 'turn.prepare_model_step' / 'turn.run_model_step' with resultAttributes llm.finish_reason, tool.count / 'turn.decide_next_step' with turn.next_action); llm/services/vercel.ts:166-176 and :181-190 (createTurnDriver span carries 'turn.resume' attribute); packages/core/src/telemetry/telemetry.ts:139 (enabled unless config.enabled===false), :208 (NodeSDK), OTLP HTTP exporter :105-113; packages/cli/src/cli/commands/span/register.ts:9-16 ('Inspect hosted run spans from Dexto Cloud', --json); otel-collector-config.yaml at repo root
