subject: dexto
title: Cancellation persists the partial assistant response and synthesizes failed/cancelled tool results into history, then recovers the partial text from history for the caller
evidence: packages/core/src/llm/executor/stream-processor.ts:209 (addAssistantMessage created during streaming, content updated), :492 persistFailedToolResults, :502/:546 persistCancelledToolResults (:826); chat-session.ts:572-597 on AbortError reads back the last assistant message from conversation history and returns its text; chat-session.ts:548 busy-guard per run; turn-executor.ts:494-500 comment: external signal linked per-step, not permanently, so soft cancel aborts the current step while queued messages continue with a fresh controller
one_why: A cancelled run leaves no orphaned tool-call blocks in history (the classic broken-context-after-cancel bug) and the user keeps partial output - cancellation is a persisted, history-consistent operation rather than a dropped future.

subject: dexto
title: Typed error taxonomy maps to HTTP status with recovery guidance rendered in the TUI, but an in-file TODO admits four route families still return ad-hoc error shapes
evidence: packages/server/src/hono/middleware/error.ts:14-36 (ErrorType -> 400/402/403/404/408/409/429/500/502 map), :47-100 handleHonoError adds endpoint/method context, hides stacks outside development; :4-11 TODO: routes incl. mcp.ts, webhooks.ts, sessions.ts, queue.ts, a2a-tasks.ts return { error } / { ok:false } shapes outside the standard; packages/tui/src/services/processStream.ts:38-46 (recovery guidance lines rendered under errors); custom lint gates eslint-rules/require-openapi-json-error-responses.js
one_why: The taxonomy and lint enforcement are above the crush 8-rung posture, but the self-documented inconsistency on exactly the MCP/A2A/queue surfaces means machine clients must still branch per-route until that TODO lands.

subject: dexto
title: Session fork copies persisted history with lineage and parent-sessionId, and best-effort rolls back partial forks; no rewind or tree navigation anywhere
evidence: packages/core/src/session/session-manager.ts:318-394 (forkSession: maxSessions check, generateForkSessionId, parentSessionId lineage :341, copySessionHistory, catch => deleteSession + clearMessages + in-memory cleanup via Promise.allSettled); packages/server/src/hono/routes/sessions.ts:196-198, :700-703 (POST /sessions/{id}/fork); grep -ri rewind across packages/tui|cli|webui returns only text-buffer undo (:487-827), no turn-level rewind; no session-tree command surface comparable to pi's /tree
one_why: Fork-with-rollback beats crush's plain sqlite resume for branch workflows, but history is append-only forever - recovery from a bad turn is 'fork earlier and replay by hand', which caps operability below codex/pi's 9.

subject: dexto
title: Pattern approval keys are derived from whitespace-split tokens with shell metacharacters ignored, so an approved 'git push * ' key also covers 'git push x && <arbitrary-command>' - and remember-choice persists to storage by default
evidence: packages/tools-process/src/command-pattern-utils.ts:49-59 (generateCommandPatternKey: head + first non-flag token, no metachar handling), :34-39 (dangerous check only on head token); packages/core/src/tools/tool-manager.ts:1303 (rememberChoice -> 'session' key); packages/core/src/tools/schemas.ts:10 (DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS_STORAGE='storage' - remembered keys survive restart); packages/tools-process/src/command-validator.ts:387 (compound '&&' rejected only in strict mode, default is moderate per tool-factory-config.ts:15)
one_why: One-time approval of a benign command silently blesses every future compound command sharing its first two tokens, with the blessing persisted to disk; the second layer that was supposed to catch this (CommandValidator.requiresApproval) is dead code (see dexto-s3) - the exact 'pattern grants wider than the user intended' rug-pull.

subject: dexto
title: Schema default is auto-approve while docs state 'manual (Default)'; the shipped agent scaffold template also sets auto-approve
evidence: packages/core/src/tools/schemas.ts:9 (DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS_MODE='auto-approve'); packages/core/src/tools/approval/tool-approval-policy.ts:59 (auto-approve -> kind ready before any tool-authored policy); docs/docs/guides/configuring-dexto/permissions.md:35 ('### manual (Default)'), docs/docs/guides/configuring-dexto/agent-yml.md:359 ('Default: manual'); agents/agent-template.yml:79 (mode: auto-approve) vs agents/default-agent.yml:87 (mode: manual)
one_why: Same failure mode that put nanocoder below the 6-rung ('real machinery + wrong default'), aggravated by a security-relevant docs/code contradiction pointing the wrong way - the opposite of pi's exemplary honesty at that rung; mitigation exists only on the curated default-agent path, not for anyone scaffolding from the template or omitting the block.

subject: dexto
title: CommandValidator still computes requiresApproval after 'command-level approval removed', but no consumer anywhere reads it; the regex deny-list itself is untested and inherits the full process env into every child
evidence: packages/tools-process/src/process-service.ts:131-134 ('Command-level approval removed' comment; validation.isValid consumed, validation.requiresApproval discarded); grep 'requiresApproval' over all of packages/ - zero consumers outside command-validator.ts:363-368 itself; command-validator.ts:275 ('TODO: Add tests for this class'), no command-validator test file exists; command-validator.ts:35-37 ('curl | python intentionally NOT blocked'); process-service.ts:148-156 (child env = full process.env spread)
one_why: The only backstop under auto-approve is an untested regex list that documents its own holes, and the second decision channel it produces is wired to nothing - an approval flow that rotted out but left the machinery in place, plus every API key in the host env reaches any command that passes the regex gate.

subject: dexto
title: Approval is bound in-loop against durable, identity-scoped records: deterministic approval ids keyed on run/turn/step/toolCall, replay-rejects conflicting details, and caller fields cannot override request-owned session scope
evidence: packages/core/src/llm/executor/turn-executor.ts:1919-1935 (executePreparedModelToolCall: prepareToolCall -> recordApprovalRequest -> requestApprovalDecisionWithAbort -> applyApprovalDecision -> execute, execution gated on applied.kind!=='terminal'); packages/core/src/approval/manager.ts:33-38 (ApprovalRecordIdentity runId/turnId/modelStepId/toolCallId); packages/core/src/approval/manager.test.ts:174,236,341,583,626 (replay idempotency, conflicting-detail rejection, scope-override rejection); packages/core/src/tools/approval/tool-approval-policy.test.ts:211 (approval-context session mismatch throws)
one_why: This is the strongest approval plumbing among the T3 subjects reviewed: crush's 6-rung grants are per-call-id but not durable-record-replay-tested at this depth; the semantics asserted ('denied means not executed', 'replay with different details throws') are exactly cline's agent-runtime.test.ts:2355 approval-iff-policy quality.

subject: dexto
title: No prompt-injection defense of any kind: the 'security' hooks are a profanity/PII policy and an opt-in redactor, nothing marks tool output as untrusted in the system prompt
evidence: packages/core/src/hooks/builtins/content-policy.ts:23-25 (ABUSIVE_PATTERNS = profanity regex; whole hook is abusive-language + email/api-key redaction), :19-22 (redactEmails/redactApiKeys default false); packages/core/src/hooks/builtins/response-sanitizer.ts:17-21 (all defaults off); grep -ri 'prompt injection|untrusted' over packages/core/src/systemPrompt and hooks - zero hits
one_why: With auto-approve defaults (dexto-s2), the regex deny-list (dexto-s3) and the pattern-key bypass (dexto-s1) are the entire containment story for content that arrives via MCP, webui, A2A and MCP-server surfaces - injected instructions need no bypass at all, they just ask the agent nicely, and no layer exists to notice.

subject: dexto
title: The filesystem half of the boundary is real and tested (realpath canonicalization, traversal rejection, directory-approval callback for external paths), while the MCP policy matcher's suffix rule widens alwaysAllow across every server, session-less approvals land in a shared global scope, and the server is unauthenticated by default in dev mode
evidence: packages/tools-filesystem/src/path-validator.ts:132-134 (realpath canonicalize), :278-280 (containment via path.relative), path-validator.test.ts:168-191 (traversal tests), directory-approval.ts:82-88 (needsApproval for external dirs); packages/core/src/tools/tool-manager.ts:2063-2073 + packages/core/src/tools/approval/session-tool-policy.ts matchesToolPolicyPattern ('mcp--read_file' matches mcp--<any-server>--read_file); packages/core/src/approval/manager.ts:27,130 (GLOBAL_APPROVAL_SCOPE for session-less approvals); packages/server/src/hono/middleware/auth.ts:46 (dev default: next() with no auth), packages/server/SECURITY.md:225 (reporting contact exists)
one_why: Dexto's boundary is asymmetric: FS paths get crush-plus treatment with actual traversal tests, but a wildcard-suffix alwaysAllow entry silently covers future malicious MCP servers' same-suffixed tools, approvals recorded without a session leak into one global bucket, and the server fronting all of it is open by default outside NODE_ENV=production.

subject: dexto
title: Next-input token estimate is anchored on the previous call's real usage (lastInput+lastOutput+newMessages) with pure-estimate fallback and logged calibration drift
evidence: packages/core/src/context/manager.ts:1287 and :1392-1417 (getEstimatedNextInputTokens: `lastInput + lastOutput + newMessagesEstimate` when actuals exist, `estimateContextTokens` pure fallback at :1414); formula and no-double-count rationale documented at :1356-1378; overestimation-after-pruning explicitly argued as safe at :1376-1378; calibration log `Context token calibration: pureEstimate=..., lastActual=..., diff%` at :1321-1330; post-call actuals captured in turn-executor.ts:1760-1772
one_why: This is pi@8's 'measure what the model would actually receive' projected-trigger in miniature: it gates compaction on real API numbers instead of a length/4 guess, and the calibration log makes estimator error an observable quantity - crush/nanocoder (6 rung) have neither.

subject: dexto
title: A second economy tier below compaction: per-step tool-output pruning with 40K protect / 20K minimum-savings thresholds, read-time placeholder substitution, history left intact
evidence: packages/core/src/llm/executor/turn-executor.ts:2258-2259 (PRUNE_PROTECT=40_000, PRUNE_MINIMUM=20_000), :2273-2318 (pruneOldToolOutputs: backwards scan, stops at `isSummary` boundary, marks via markMessagesAsCompacted, emits `context:pruned` with savedTokens); packages/core/src/context/manager.ts:734-781 (markMessagesAsCompacted sets compactedAt), :553-580 (transform to PRUNED_TOOL_PLACEHOLDER at format time only); separate write-side cap in llm/executor/tool-output-truncator.ts:4 (120K chars ~30K tokens)
one_why: Tool outputs dominate long-session tokens; pruning them losslessly-for-audit (DB keeps originals, model sees placeholders) reclaims far more than summarizing chat text and is why dexto clears the crush@6 'one auto-summarize' rung - the scout's hypothesis that pruning is the real workhorse is confirmed by the thresholds and the per-step call at turn-executor.ts:1347.

subject: dexto
title: Both compaction gates are the same reactive 0.9-threshold strategy; no proactive tier and no recovery path when the provider itself rejects an oversized request
evidence: packages/core/src/context/compaction/strategies/ - only noop.ts (58 LOC) and reactive-overflow-compaction.ts (496) exist; both executor gates call the same strategy.shouldCompact: turn-executor.ts:1424 (pre-call estimate) and :1775 (post-call actual), threshold default 0.9 in compaction/overflow.ts:30-38 with target 0.7 at :52-58 and strategy default at reactive-overflow-compaction.ts:104; grep for context-length/overflow provider-error handling in packages/core/src/llm/errors.ts returns zero hits - no 'prompt too long' -> compact -> retry loop anywhere; image/file parts get a flat 1000-token estimate (turn-executor.ts:2337-2339)
one_why: One steady-state context-size blowup (one huge tool result that lands under both checks but over the API's acceptance) has no graceful degradation, and a 90%-of-window trigger on long-turn tool chains is late; codex's token-budget fresh-window tier (compact_token_budget.rs) is precisely the missing third leg.

subject: dexto
title: Prompt-cache discipline is deliberate but minimal: one static ephemeral breakpoint on the system prompt, plus cache-read/write tokens that are measured and priced but never acted on
evidence: packages/core/src/llm/formatters/vercel.ts:191-205 (only per-message cacheControl in the repo: system prompt, gated on anthropic/bedrock-claude/vertex-claude by name match at :193-199); call-level `anthropic: {cacheControl: {type:'ephemeral'}}` in llm/executor/provider-options.ts:30,98,116,130,140,154, pinned by provider-options.test.ts:56,150-243; cacheRead/Write parsed from provider metadata in llm/executor/stream-processor.ts:628-641 and folded into pricing at core/llm/usage-metadata.ts:26-27; grep 'cacheControl|ephemeral' across packages/ finds no other breakpoint site, no warming, no cache-stats surface
one_why: Better than cline@7 ('no cache discipline') - the breakpoint placement is centralized, model-gated and tested - but with history carrying no breakpoint, everything after the system prompt re-reads at full price every turn; pi@8's active warming + cache-stats and codex@9's cache-key-gated reuse are the missing rungs, and the cacheRead/write telemetry already present is the natural foundation.

subject: dexto
title: Subagent spawning ships real governance: self-spawn block, per-parent concurrency cap, iteration cap, allow-list, and automatic reasoning-variant downgrade for cost containment
evidence: packages/agent-management/src/tool-factories/agent-spawner/runtime.ts:261-267 (workspace agent cannot spawn itself, blockedReason at :265), :396-400 (maxConcurrentAgents refusal in spawnAndExecute at :378), :403-410 (allowedAgents allow-list error listing allowed ids), :76-104+ :1075 (applySubAgentLlmPolicy caps subAgentMaxIterations and selects the lowest supported reasoning variant via REASONING_VARIANT_FALLBACK_ORDER :33-43); schema limits in agent-spawner/schemas.ts:26,:41; approvals for spawned agents get their own test file runtime.approvals.test.ts
one_why: nanocoder@6's docking reason was 'no budgets'; dexto has concurrency + iteration + model-cost (reasoning downgrade) budgets and an allow-list at the spawn seam itself - this is the governance bundle cline's teams-as-tools grew, enforced pre-spawn rather than post-hoc.

subject: dexto
title: The orchestration plane that survives nothing: TaskRegistry is an in-process Map with Math.random ids and 5-minute result TTL, sitting next to a sqlite-everywhere session layer
evidence: packages/orchestration/src/task-registry.ts:31-41 (class, `tasks = new Map`, maxTasks 20, resultTTL 5 min), :47-50 (`task-${Math.random().toString(36)...}` id generator); SignalBus is a bare EventEmitter (signal-bus.ts:24-26); wait/check/list tools are built over this registry in agent-spawner/factory.ts:111 (ConditionEngine) and :303-305 (createWaitForTool/createCheckTaskTool wiring); contrast the DB-backed layers: storage/stores/backend.ts:533, tools-scheduler/src/manager.ts:77-79
one_why: Server restart silently destroys in-flight background tasks, their wait-for continuations, and task results (crush@7 at least resumes sqlite state; cline@8 keeps a hub event journal) - and Math.random ids make even log correlation across restarts impossible; this single module is why dexto's orchestration tops out at the 7 rung.

subject: dexto
title: Scheduler is a genuine persistent-cron with write-compensation: schedules reload from the toolState store at boot and a failed delete rolls the list entry back
evidence: packages/tools-scheduler/src/manager.ts:31 ('Persistent schedules (survive agent restarts)'), :77-79 (listSchedules at startup, count logged); storage.ts:113-146 (deleteSchedule: removeFromList -> deleteState -> deleteExecutionLogs, with addScheduleToList restore on partial failure and logged restoreError); server route packages/server/src/hono/routes/schedules.ts; execution logs per schedule (storage.ts:125)
one_why: Direct analogue of cline's sqlite-cron-store (part of its 8-rung orchestration), and the compensating-delete is more transactional hygiene than any anchor's cron was shown to have; what keeps it from counting as 8-rung overall is that in-flight scheduled *runs* share the ephemeral plane of dexto-e7.

subject: dexto
title: Interop breadth is the densest observed since codex: MCP client with all three official transports plus a dual-transport MCP server exposing any agent as a tool
evidence: packages/core/src/mcp/mcp-client.ts:161 (StdioClientTransport), :226 (SSEClientTransport with fallback builder), :318 (StreamableHTTPClientTransport), behind manager.ts (1,238 LOC); server side packages/server/src/mcp/mcp-handler.ts:22 (StdioServerTransport) and :30-35 (StreamableHTTPServerTransport), registering the agent as `chat_with_agent` with ephemeral per-call sessions and guaranteed cleanup at :52-80; CLI mode `dexto --mode mcp` (cli/src/index-main.ts:555); IDE use documented via .cursor/mcp.json (docs/docs/guides/dexto-in-cursor.md)
one_why: codex@9 has MCP both ways, cline@8 client-only; dexto matches the codex shape on the MCP axis and adds an explicit ephemeral-session lifecycle in the server tool (mcp-handler.ts:66-80) that avoids the session-leak failure mode remote MCP wrappers commonly ship.

subject: dexto
title: No anchor ships an A2A protocol server, and the only foreign-harness touchpoint is protocol-level: dexto drives the external Codex app-server over stdio JSON-RPC with zero imports from rival codebases
evidence: packages/server/src/a2a/jsonrpc/methods.ts:4 ('Implements A2A Protocol v0.3.0 RPC methods by calling DextoAgent'), ~1,429 LOC across a2a/ (jsonrpc/server.ts:271, adapters/, types.ts:262); AgentCard surfaced via mcp-handler.ts:37-46; foreign-harness check: grep for @anthropic-ai/claude|@openai/codex|@zed-industries|opencode|@google/gemini-cli across packages/*/package.json returns zero, and llm/providers/codex-app-server.ts:1243 spawns the external `codex app-server` binary (ENOENT handled with actionable error at :234-242) - adapter, not vendored code
one_why: The lane contract asked for rival-harness import paths: none exist (supports the scout's original-provenance verdict); A2A + the Codex driver mean dexto positions itself as an interop *hub* between agent ecosystems, which is beyond both 8-rung anchors and the nanocoder ACP@7 rung (dexto still has no ACP).

subject: dexto
title: `dexto run` - the primary headless entry - emits only prose `[tag]` lines to stderr with no machine-readable event stream, while --json exists only on the span/trace diagnostics commands
evidence: packages/cli/src/cli/commands/run/headless.ts:26-44 (writeHeadlessLine/TaggedLine/TaggedBlock: '[tag]' and '| line' formatting to process.stderr, 376 LOC of it) and :18-22 (result is {finalMessage,totalTokens,fatalError} in-process only); run/register.ts:12-25 (options: --model and prompt/stdin only, no format flag) while grep for '--json' in packages/cli/src finds it exclusively in commands/span/register.ts:13 and commands/trace/register.ts:17,40,66
one_why: This is the gap that keeps interop from 9: codex's `exec --json` and pi's rpc mode are the rungs, pi earns its whole 6 even with no MCP at all; every CI/script consumer of dexto must regex prose or go through the server HTTP API instead of the CLI - and the JSON plumbing (event bus, StreamingEvent types already imported at headless.ts:7) is one serializer away.

subject: dexto
title: The HTTP contract is drift-gated in CI from both ends: OpenAPI spec sync check, CLI README sync, and custom ESLint rules that force every route to declare JSON error responses
evidence: workflows: .github/workflows/sync-openapi-docs.yml (spec sync gate) and sync-cli-readme.yml ('Ensure CLI README is in sync', runs on README/ sync-script paths); custom rules eslint-rules/require-openapi-route-contract.js + require-openapi-json-error-responses.js (+ require-zod-describe.js); spec rendered live at docs/docusaurus.config.ts:65 (spec: 'static/openapi/openapi.json'); typed client ships as @dexto/client-sdk v1.12.1, private:false, dual-format exports (client-sdk/package.json:2-16), released via .changeset + changesets-publish.yml
one_why: No anchor was observed linting route contracts let alone gating doc/spec drift in CI; this is the mechanism-level answer to 'docs match code', and combined with the private:false versioned SDK it is the strongest docs-contract discipline in the study so far.

subject: dexto
title: The token-economy control surface (thresholdPercent, maxContextTokens, preserveLastNTurns, strategy choice) is schema-validated but absent from user docs, which live only in an internal feature-plan
evidence: knobs exist in packages/agent-config/src/schemas/compaction.ts and core types compaction/types.ts:11-22; strategy registry keyed by name at packages/image-local/src/index.ts:335 ('reactive-overflow' -> factory); grep for thresholdPercent|maxContextTokens across docs/docs/ returns zero hits; the 949-line token-math write-up sits in feature-plans/context-calculation.md, not docs/; user-facing 'compact' mentions limited to docs/docs/guides/cli/interactive-commands.md, configuring-dexto/memory.md, tutorials/sdk/config-files.md; SECURITY.md absent at repo root (ls: No such file)
one_why: cline's 8-rung docs include a feature reference for auto-compact (docs/features/auto-compact.mdx); dexto ships the knobs, the DI seam for new strategies, and a 949-line internal design doc, then leaves users to read source - the cheapest docs-dx fix found, and the pi@9 bar is exactly 'in-repo docs matching code'.

subject: roo-code
title: Task.ts at 4,619 LOC / ~86 members fuses the agent loop, state model, persistence, checkpoints and condense triggers in one class
evidence: src/core/task/Task.ts:158 (class Task extends EventEmitter), :2427 (initiateTaskLoop while-loop), :2460+ (recursivelyMakeClineRequests with hand-rolled retry stack), grep count of private/public/protected members = 86; webview god-object pair src/core/webview/webviewMessageHandler.ts 3,230 LOC + ClineProvider.ts 3,149 LOC
one_why: Worse fused surface than crush's 7-scoring agent.go (2,393) + coordinator.go (1,877) combined, and per the pi errata a >5k fused loop/product file is a docking factor; loop semantics are only testable via mock-heavy specs (7,191 LOC in src/core/task/__tests__ with heavy fakes), unlike codex's StepContext/TurnContext separation.

subject: roo-code
title: CLI ships no second agent loop: it loads the VS Code extension headlessly via a vscode API shim and drives it over the existing webview-message protocol
evidence: apps/cli/src/agent/extension-host.ts:26 (import createVSCodeAPI from @roo-code/vscode-shim), :535 (resumeTask sends showTaskWithId); apps/cli/src/commands/cli/list.ts uses readWorkspaceTaskSessions against the shim's storage; packages/types/src/vscode-extension-host.ts 792 LOC IPC contract shared by both surfaces
one_why: The anti-pattern it avoids is nanocoder's entry-path-loop-duplication (loop inside React hooks re-implemented per surface); one engine, one persistence format, zero loop-fork drift - at the cost of a vscode-shaped neck, but the direction (make the engine host-agnostic rather than clone the loop) is the right port.

subject: roo-code
title: CLI reconstructs the agent loop's state machine by heuristics on the tail of the presentation message stream
evidence: apps/cli/src/agent/state-store.ts:5 ("clineMessages array (source of truth for agent state)"), apps/cli/src/agent/agent-state.ts:48-120 (AgentLoopState enum; STREAMING detected via partial===true or last api_req_started text lacking a cost field), apps/cli/docs/AGENT_LOOP.md (loop-stops-when-last-message-is-non-partial-ask rule)
one_why: Coupling a state machine to the rendering schema's incidental fields (a cost key's absence means "streaming") means any webview message-format change can misclassify RUNNING/IDLE/RESUMABLE in the headless host; an explicit loop-event protocol (as packages/types already partially defines for IPC) would make the same fact a contract instead of an inference.

subject: roo-code
title: Condense and sliding-window truncation are non-destructive tag-hides (condenseParent/truncationParent + marker messages), so rewinding past a compaction restores the original messages
evidence: src/core/condense/index.ts:459 ("NON-DESTRUCTIVE CONDENSE" tagging comment + map :426-448 per f-econ), :534-596 (getEffectiveApiHistory filters by existing summary/truncation ids and strips orphan tool_result blocks), :657-695 (cleanupAfterTruncation reactivates messages whose summary was rewound away); src/core/task-persistence/apiMessages.ts:27-37 (condenseId/condenseParent/truncationId/truncationParent/isTruncationMarker fields), src/core/context-management/index.ts:50-64 (truncateConversation tags hidden instead of deleting, "restored if the user rewinds past the truncation point"); specs src/core/condense/__tests__/rewind-after-condense.spec.ts (567 LOC), nested-condense.spec.ts (211 LOC), index.spec.ts:358 (orphaned-condenseParent restore on rewind); integrator verified the NON-DESTRUCTIVE comment at condense/index.ts:459 and the 567-LOC spec in-tree
one_why: Cline's anchor compaction deletes ranges, so its checkpoint/compaction interaction is lossy by construction; roo decouples logical visibility from physical storage so the checkpoint timeline, condense, and truncation compose - the dedicated rewind-after-condense specs exist because this property is enforced, not hoped for. Evidence base taken from f-econ (stronger: line-ranged impl citations + spec LOC counts); f-core's context-management tag-hide citation merged in.

subject: roo-code
title: MessageManager declared the SINGLE entry point for all conversation-message deletion, consolidating splice sites that the god-class had scattered
evidence: src/core/message-manager/index.ts:37-48 (class MessageManager, rewindToTimestamp "SINGLE entry point for all message deletion operations" incl. orphaned summary/truncation-marker cleanup), src/core/message-manager/index.spec.ts 852 LOC; checkpointRestore routes through it (src/core/checkpoints/index.ts:267-270)
one_why: In a 4.6k-LOC Task where any code path could splice clineMessages, funneling every deletion through one tested function is how rewind/condense/truncation stay mutually consistent without an invariant framework - the cheap interim guard for a pre-split codebase.

subject: roo-code
title: Session JSON writes go through an advisory-locked temp-file + backup + rollback helper, and the history index self-reconciles
evidence: src/utils/safeWriteJson.ts:20-27 (proper-lockfile inter-process advisory lock, temp file, backup-before-replace, rollback on error), used by src/core/task-persistence/apiMessages.ts:118 and taskMessages.ts:54; src/core/task-persistence/TaskHistoryStore.ts:47-65 (writeLock serialization, 2s debounced index writes, FSWatcher + 5-min periodic reconciliation)
one_why: JSON-per-task storage is the obvious cheap choice, and this is the minimum engineering that makes it survivable across crashes and multiple editor windows; the read side then never trusts the file (apiMessages.ts:47-71 returns empty-with-warning on malformed content and migrates legacy claude_messages.json)

subject: roo-code
title: Checkpoints silently disable themselves for the rest of a task on any init timeout or restore error (11 enableCheckpoints=false sites), so rewind coverage decays without user action
evidence: src/core/checkpoints/index.ts:58,66,100,125,142,191,201,206,223,296,384 (enableCheckpoints = false on missing workspace/storage, git-absent, init timeout, checkpoint-save error, restore error, diff error), :287-293 comment admitting the inherited double-cancelTask hack: "hacky solution to a problem that I don't fully understand"
one_why: Revert-ability is the headline operability feature (shadow-git per task), but a single transient git hiccup permanently downgrades the task to no-checkpoint with only a webview toast; a retried re-init or per-operation degradation would keep the recovery promise instead of fail-open-by-exhaustion.

subject: roo-code
title: CLI crash posture and demonstrated resumability: classified exceptions, expected-control-flow filtering, flush-then-exit shutdown, signal-only park mode, and lock-protected per-task JSON resume
evidence: apps/cli/src/commands/cli/run.ts:343 (emitRuntimeError), :423-429/:444-450 (uncaughtException/unhandledRejection -> emit event then idempotent shutdown, isExpectedControlFlowError suppresses stdin/shutdown races), :465-484 (shutdown detaches handlers, disposeHost, jsonEmitter.flush, flushStdout), :452-460 (parkUntilSignal keep-alive mode for --signal-only-exit); resume substrate: src/core/task-persistence/TaskHistoryStore.ts:22-30 (per-task history_item.json + _index.json, proper-lockfile via safeWriteJson), apps/cli/src/commands/cli/run.ts:518 (host.resumeTask), :409-491 (onSigint/onUncaughtException/onUnhandledRejection -> shutdown)
one_why: crush's recover-at-trust-boundaries and gemini-cli's listener discipline equivalent for a json-stream headless agent: errors become emitted events on the wire before exit so scripted consumers see why the run died, instead of a truncated stream; gap kept honest: no crash journal or auto-restart, and no in-CI crash fuzzing. Evidence base kept from f-core (more precise line-ranged crash-handler citations); f-econ's resume/TaskHistoryStore citations merged in - crash semantics are demonstrated, not assumed (above nanocoder-6).

subject: roo-code
title: Single in-loop approval router with fail-closed defaults: every ask passes checkAutoApproval; absent state or falsy autoApprovalEnabled means ask, and an empty command allowlist auto-approves nothing
evidence: src/core/task/Task.ts:1321 (checkAutoApproval call inside ask), :1323-1327 (approve/deny branches), src/core/auto-approval/index.ts:62-64 (default ask), src/core/auto-approval/commands.ts:130-133 (no allowlist => nothing approved)
one_why: Defaults fail closed everywhere I could check, but unlike the cline anchor's agent-runtime.test.ts:2355 there is no spec proving the loop honors the router end-to-end; the binding is real in code, unproven in tests (see roo-code-s9).

subject: roo-code
title: Shell-substitution anti-bypass layer: bash/zsh expansion classes (${var@P}, ${!v}, =(...), *(e:...:), <<<$(...)) demote any auto_approve to ask_user, never to deny, and survive prefix allowlists
evidence: src/core/auto-approval/commands.ts:22-58 (pattern classes), :280-284 (gate applied after sub-command decisions), __tests__/commands.spec.ts:70-84 (true positives), :43-68 (false-positive regressions for node -e / arrow fns)
one_why: Nuance vs nanocoder's regex-denylist rung-5 finding: same regex shape but opposite failure direction - a miss here only costs an approval prompt, and the spec guards both bypass and false-positive sides, which is anti-bypass research cline lacks.

subject: roo-code
title: Self-poisoning guard: writes to agent-own config (.rooignore, .roorules*, .clinerules*, .roomodes, .vscode/**, AGENTS.md) force an approval even under alwaysAllowWrite
evidence: src/core/protect/RooProtectedController.ts:14-26 (pattern list), src/core/auto-approval/index.ts:173-178 (isProtected requires the separate alwaysAllowWriteProtected toggle), src/core/tools/WriteToFileTool.ts:58,130 (flag threaded into askApproval), __tests__/RooProtectedController.spec.ts:12-58
one_why: Attacker-controlled prompt rewriting .roorules or AGENTS.md is the cheapest persistent injection; making those writes un-auto-approvable by default closes the loop the ignore/protect pair exists for - but the error path returns not-protected while the comment claims caution (RooProtectedController.ts:55-59, a comment/behavior mismatch).

subject: roo-code
title: .rooignore read gating with realpath symlink resolution, path-traversal specs, fail-closed filterPaths, and a separate outside-workspace permission tier
evidence: src/core/ignore/RooIgnoreController.ts:102-110 (realpathSync), :113 (fail-open catch), src/core/ignore/__tests__/RooIgnoreController.security.spec.ts:143-168 (traversal), :186 (paths outside cwd allowed by design), :302-311 (filterPaths fails closed), src/core/auto-approval/index.ts:164-178 (outside-workspace needs its own toggles)
one_why: Converges with the study's context-overflow-failopen family: validateAccess returns true on error and for anything outside cwd, so .rooignore is a within-project politeness, not a fence - the spec even asserts /etc/hosts is accessible; outside-workspace approval is what actually carries the weight.

subject: roo-code
title: Terminal-side ignore check is a 12-command whitespace-split base-name match: bash -c, cp, or redirection bypass .rooignore in two tokens, and the spec codifies the gaps in comments
evidence: src/core/ignore/RooIgnoreController.ts:123-167 (split on /\s+/, baseCommand whitelist), __tests__/RooIgnoreController.security.spec.ts:76,128 ('implementation doesn't handle quoted paths as expected')
one_why: Mitigated only by the fact that un-allowlisted commands still prompt (src/core/tools/ExecuteCommandTool.ts:66), so this bypass matters precisely when the user has enabled command auto-approval - the population the docs warn hardest about.

subject: roo-code
title: skill tool is auto-approved unconditionally while project skills load from the cloned repo's .agents/skills and .roo/skills: a malicious repository ships untrusted instructions into context with no approval
evidence: src/core/auto-approval/index.ts:148-155 (approve regardless of state), src/services/skills/SkillsManager.ts:601-603 (project dirs .agents/skills then .roo/skills), src/core/protect/RooProtectedController.ts:20 (.roo/** protected from agent writes but not from git clone)
one_why: The code comment claims skills are 'explicitly installed/defined by the user', which holds for global skills and fails for project-sourced ones; zero other injection defense exists in the repo (grep 'untrusted' in src: 0 hits), so the approval layer is the only injection control and this path skips it by design.

subject: roo-code
title: Auto-approval docs are unusually honest - explicit data-loss warning banner plus per-category risk ratings (Write High, MCP Medium-High, Command High) - but SECURITY.md is a disclosure policy with no sandbox statement

subject: roo-code

subject: roo-code

subject: roo-code

Evidence base kept from f-safety (wiring lines + spec size); f-econ's SkillsManager citations merged in - among anchors only crush had a loop breaker, and skills parallel nothing except codex delegate-style extensions.
